The letter cites the continued detention of two online journalists, prison sentences over Facebook posts after the December 2025 coup attempt, and repeated suspensions imposed by the media regulator HAAC.

2026-09-01-ben-gouvernance-ia-transforme.summary: Benin placed third in the first Africa AI Governance Index, which scores all 54 African states across eight domains. The accompanying argument is that a governance lead has yet to become anything citizens can point to.

2026-09-01-bfa-cil-formulaire-autorisati.summary: Burkina Faso's data protection authority, the CIL, publishes the form for applying to transfer personal data abroad. It asks for the foreign recipient, whether the destination country has a data protection authority, and the purpose, consent and security arrangements behind the transfer.

2026-09-01-bfa-facture-electronique-cert.summary: Certified electronic invoicing systems go on sale in Burkina Faso from 7 September 2026 for large and medium enterprises, under the general tax code — the point at which the invoicing regime becomes equipment a business has to buy.

2026-09-01-biometricupdate-semlex-congo-.summary: Fourteen defendants in the case of Semlex, the Belgian firm that made the Democratic Republic of Congo's biometric passports from 2015 to 2025, have been sent to a Brussels criminal court on bribery, money laundering and tax fraud charges. Investigators allege about $60 of each $185 passport went to a Dubai firm, nearly $60 million in all; 51 Congolese citizens are civil parties.

2026-09-01-businesstimesug-uganda-nin-re.summary: Uganda's cabinet approved phasing out the standalone taxpayer identification number for individuals, replacing it with the national identification number already printed on the identity card. Nothing states a commencement date or a transition arrangement for the roughly nine to ten million Ugandans not yet on the register.

2026-09-01-ca-kenya-draft-safeguards-dea.summary: The Communications Authority of Kenya published draft guidelines (CA.G.520:2026) on deactivating and recycling inactive phone numbers, open for comment until 11 September 2026 with a proposed start date of 19 September. The draft sets up a central database of deactivated and recycled numbers, quarterly reporting by operators, a *106# status check, and whitelisting for prisoners and incapacitated subscribers.

2026-09-01-camerounlink-car-submarine-ca.summary: A fibre cut in Cameroon disrupted internet service in the Central African Republic last week, prompting an assessment of the landlocked country's options for reaching submarine cable capacity by another route.

2026-09-01-capitaltimes-ura-crawford-cap.summary: The Capital Times reports that Uganda's and Kenya's revenue authorities still enforce e-Permit collections at border points for Crawford Capital, a firm the United States sanctioned on 12 May 2026 over diverting South Sudanese public funds. The UK-registered company collects a dollar charge on imports bound for South Sudan; documents cited show the Uganda Revenue Authority shares customs data with South Sudan's revenue authority but do not show a direct contract.

2026-09-01-cisd-computer-support-central.summary: Mauritius runs a central offsite backup service for government electronic media out of the central information systems division, alongside technical support and equipment commissioning for ministries and departments. It is the state's standing backup arrangement; the page publishes no capacity, retention period or restoration-test record.

2026-09-01-civ-artci-neutralite-du-net-c.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's regulator ARTCI consulted on draft net-neutrality guidelines from 6 July to 6 August 2026 and published operators' responses in September. The draft allows zero rating only where it is unpaid and non-discriminatory, and would have internet providers declare their traffic-management practices each year; Moov Africa argued that strict non-discrimination would slow 5G services.

2026-09-01-cmr-cameroons-water-utility-t.summary: Cameroon's state water utility Camwater awarded China's Hangzhou Laison Technology a CFA721.76 million contract on 17 August 2026 for 3,000 smart water meters, an IT platform and a payment-system interface, in pilot areas of Douala and Yaoundé. The offer is 27.8% below Camwater's CFA1 billion estimate, and the meters are the first 7.5% of 40,000 planned under the World Bank-backed IMPACT programme.

2026-09-01-cod-cartographie-recensement-.summary: The cartography phase of the DRC's second population census is being operationalised with digital tools and satellite imagery, the central census bureau's technical coordinator said — 42 years after the country's only previous census, in 1984.

2026-09-01-compcom-cost-of-living-report.summary: South Africa's Competition Commission published its August 2026 cost-of-living report, tracking prices of food, water, electricity, transport, internet and other essentials for the lowest-income households. Between January and July 2026, wired internet prices rose 3.5% and wireless 4.1%, against headline inflation of 3.8%; the internet figures cover fixed services only, not mobile data.

2026-09-01-connectingafrica-nokia-lozano.summary: A Nokia executive's account of African infrastructure investment accelerating on artificial intelligence and data growth. Vendor commentary.

2026-09-01-dict-policy-standards-researc.summary: Seychelles' Department of Information Communications Technology sets out the mandate of its Policy, Standards and Research Section: technical and coding standards for interoperable e-government services, integration of government applications and databases, and management of Gov Mail, the government intranet and the e-services portal. The page is undated.

2026-09-01-digitalmag-uemoa-monnaie-elec.summary: Senegal held 29.7% of electronic money outstanding in the West African Economic and Monetary Union at the end of 2025, and 26.5% of large microfinance institutions' assets, according to the union's Banking Commission. E-money outstanding across the union rose 35.2% to CFAF 1,923.2 billion, and 64.9% of its 172.9 million e-money accounts were inactive.

2026-09-01-djibouti-etats-unis-cooperati.summary: Djibouti's communications minister, Mohamed Abdoulkader Moussa Helem, received the US ambassador, Cynthia Kierscht, on 31 August 2026. They discussed US investment in new technologies and telecommunications, and training for journalists and media staff. No agreement, figure or timetable was announced.

2026-09-01-dni-frogfoot-vox-fibre-billio.summary: The DNI consortium subscribed R1.6 billion, about US$99 million, for 34.8% of the fibre network operator Frogfoot and the internet provider Vox, valuing the two at R14.4 billion. The stated purpose is township fibre.

2026-09-01-e-gouvernance-rwanda-etudes-g.summary: Rwanda Cooperation said it hosted eight government delegations from seven countries in one week in late August 2026: Liberia, Kenya, Nigeria, Benin, Gambia, Gabon and Guinea. A delegation from Gabon's interior ministry spent nearly two weeks studying e-government, AI policy, digital civil registration and identification, cybersecurity, data protection and system interconnection.

2026-09-01-eduspots-digital-champions-ma.summary: EduSpots launched a nine-month Digital Champions Programme on 1 September 2026 to train and certify 60 community leaders across 52 Ghanaian communities, under the Mastercard Foundation EdTech Fellowship. Participants attend a three-day residential academy in Elmina, followed by monthly modules on online safety, AI for educators and use of the EduSpots App.

2026-09-01-egypt-masrawy-environmental-d.summary: Egypt's Environmental Affairs Agency and the General Organization for Export and Import Control signed a protocol on 1 September 2026 to exchange data on industrial facilities through the unified environmental data registry. The two bodies will study linking their systems electronically and agree which data are shared, from what source and how often. It was signed at the launch of the IDEIA digital environmental impact assessment system.

2026-09-01-egypt-mcit-cisco-letter-of-in.summary: Egypt's prime minister witnessed the signing of a letter of intent between the communications ministry and Cisco Systems. A letter of intent carries no value, scope of works or delivery date.

2026-09-01-egypt-medical-professionals-e.summary: Egypt's Ministry of Health and Population put an electronic system for medical professionals' assignment-modification requests into full use at the start of September 2026, after a pilot from mid-August. Requests linked to a staff member's health previously meant repeated trips between offices and results sent by post; documents and examination results are now exchanged electronically between the bodies involved.

2026-09-01-egypt-pandemic-fund-health-da.summary: Egypt's Pandemic Fund steering committee, chaired by the deputy health minister, named surveillance systems and data exchange as the mechanism for joining the public-health and animal-health sectors under a One Health approach. It is a stated project priority rather than a system in service.

2026-09-01-egypte-ideia-evaluation-impac.summary: Egypt's Minister of Local Development and Environment, Manal Awad, launched IDEIA, a digital system for environmental impact assessments, on 1 September 2026. It moves applications, review, approval and follow-up off paper and lets applicants track their files. It is the digital component of the Green Sustainable Industry programme, financed by the EIB, the EU, AFD and the Egyptian government at a total of EUR 271 million.

2026-09-01-egypte-parquet-service-electr.summary: Egypt's Public Prosecution opened an online service on 1 September 2026 for looking up family-case data and the judgments issued in them, through its electronic portal. Working with the communications ministry, it restricts access to users verified by the Digital Egypt portal's digital identity, so that only the parties concerned can see their records.

2026-09-01-gha-gss-rebased-gdp-quarterly.summary: The Ghana Statistical Service's September 2026 quarterly GDP bulletin carries final rebased estimates from 2006 to 2023, revised figures for 2024 to the first quarter of 2026 and provisional figures for the second quarter of 2026, at constant 2013 prices. In its provisional second-quarter figures, information and communication made up 3.48% of GDP and grew 30.9% year on year in real terms.

2026-09-01-gha-imf-tar-26-78-regulation-.summary: An IMF technical assistance report on Ghana, dated September 2026, found that the crypto guidelines of the Bank of Ghana and the Securities and Exchange Commission fall short of full oversight, ahead of a licensing regime under the Virtual Asset Service Providers Act 2025 due to start in December 2026. It puts annual crypto transactions at about US$21bn and recommends activity-based rules, final stablecoin rules and transitional licensing.

2026-09-01-ghanaiantimes-afcfta-digital-.summary: An editorial on what the AfCFTA Digital Trade Corridor has to get right to matter, following the joint venture agreement signed in Accra. See the corridor entry above.

2026-09-01-gis-mauritius-digital-service.summary: Mauritius will develop a Digital Service Framework setting mandatory principles and standards for every government digital service, from planning through operation, binding all services developed, procured or maintained by ministries. Cabinet noted it on 28 August; no compliance date is set.

2026-09-01-govmu-justice-info-page.summary: The government's justice portal sets out the constitutional and institutional frame — separation of powers, a single-structure judiciary, a human rights action plan — and is the public face of a sector whose digital systems sit in the 2026-2031 investment programme rather than in service. It describes the aim; no court case-management system is named on it.

2026-09-01-guinee-afpif-2026-ixp-partici.summary: Guinea's internet exchange point, IXP-Guinée, attended the 15th African Peering and Interconnection Forum in Kigali on 17–20 August 2026, represented by its executive secretary Abdoulaye Sivory Sakho with backing from the digital economy ministry's WARDIP programme. Sessions covered exchange-point governance, network performance measurement, access to content delivery networks and peering.

2026-09-01-inatro-sistema-licenciamento-.summary: Mozambique's road transport institute, INATRO, launched a digital licensing system at the Maputo International Fair on 1 September 2026. Applications for special transit licences for oversize and overweight vehicles, and certificates for emergency lights and sirens, can now be made and issued fully online.

2026-09-01-independent-uganda-ucc-smartp.summary: Uganda's communications regulator launched a study of smartphone penetration, device cost and usage, against a stated target of full national network coverage by 2030.

2026-09-01-investment-authority-launches.summary: Sudan's National Investment Authority activated a service on its electronic One-Stop Platform that lets investors submit and track project requirements lists online without attending in person. Secretary-General Ahlam Madani said it implements government directives on digital transformation and is being integrated with other institutions. No launch date, user numbers or supplier is given.

2026-09-01-isoc-pulse-ixp-tracker-gabon.summary: The Internet Society's Pulse tracker lists one active internet exchange point in Gabon as of September 2026, with eight members, drawing on PeeringDB data. The country has nine active networks and an internet resilience score of 52 out of 100, with international connections rated fair.

2026-09-01-isoc-pulse-ixp-tracker-hubsix.summary: The Internet Society's IXP tracker records HubSIX, an internet exchange point in Dakar, Senegal, with 260 Gbps of capacity and six member networks as of September 2026, all six having joined in the previous 12 months. The figures are self-declared in PeeringDB; no traffic volumes are given, and the exchange does not take part in the MANRS routing-security programme.

2026-09-01-itweb-africa-airtel-nigeria-p.summary: Airtel Nigeria opened two premium experience centres in Lagos, taking its nationwide retail total past 350.

2026-09-01-itweb-africa-egypt-ai-trainin.summary: Egypt is expanding artificial-intelligence and cybersecurity training inside its judiciary under a cooperation agreement between the National Telecommunications Institute and the State Lawsuits Authority.

2026-09-01-itweb-africa-japan-malawi-inn.summary: Japan's ambassador to Malawi met the communications regulator's director general with a Japanese delegation, exploring stronger digital and innovation ties. Nothing was signed.

2026-09-01-itweb-digital-finance-consume.summary: South Africa ran Money Smart Week from 24 to 30 August, an initiative of the committee the Treasury and the conduct authority established to co-ordinate financial literacy, as digital finance growth widens the consumer-protection question.

2026-09-01-itweb-hungry-lion-data-breach.summary: Customer credentials for the fast-food chain Hungry Lion were exposed for about nine months through its consumer-facing web portals, on analysis of stealer-log data finding 23 records tied to its South African domain, 13 of them customer accounts.

2026-09-01-itweb-shoprite-fintech-inform.summary: Shoprite finalised the acquisition of an initial 51% of R&A Cellular, whose point-of-sale platform is used by informal retailers to sell prepaid airtime, electricity, gaming and entertainment — extending the retailer's financial services into South Africa's informal economy.

2026-09-01-karnataka-hosts-african-union.summary: The Indian state of Karnataka hosted officials from the African Union, Ethiopia, Malawi, Rwanda, Sierra Leone and Zambia on 1 September 2026, on a UNDP-supported visit to study digital public infrastructure. State officials and the Centre for e-Governance briefed the delegation on digitising public services and interoperability between government systems.

2026-09-01-ken-senate-ict-committee-repo.summary: The Kenyan Senate's ICT committee report on the Artificial Intelligence Bill, 2026 (Senate Bills No. 4 of 2026) recommends that the Senate does not proceed with the Bill. The 170-page report draws on written submissions from 143 stakeholders and asks for a national AI policy to be published first.

2026-09-01-kenya-data-centre-licence-con.summary: The Communications Authority of Kenya published a consultation in September 2026 proposing a standalone licence for co-location data centres, which are now licensed as Tier 2 network facilities providers. Proposed fees are KSh5,000 to apply, KSh100,000 initially and KSh80,000 or 0.4% of gross turnover a year, for a 15-year term; existing NFP and ASP licensees would need no separate licence.

2026-09-01-kenya-manufacturing-summit-tr.summary: Kenya's Principal Secretary for Medical Services met Africa CDC and African Union Commission officials on 1 September to prepare the Extraordinary Summit on African Manufacturing, set for 3–5 December 2026 in Nairobi. He cited work to digitise the health-products supply chain through the Track and Trace system. No cost or timetable for the system is given.

2026-09-01-kictanet-budapest-convention-.summary: Kenya plans to accede to the Council of Europe's Budapest Convention on Cybercrime, and Parliament is inviting public views by 11 September 2026, according to a 1 September post to the KICTANet mailing list by lawyer Victor Kapiyo. The parliamentary notice itself is not quoted.

2026-09-01-kictanet-ict-regulations-vali.summary: Kenya's Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital Economy is holding a virtual validation forum on 15 draft Kenya Information and Communication Regulations, 2026, from 15 to 17 September. The drafts cover licensing, broadcasting, spectrum, tariffs, interconnection, consumer protection, domain names and the Universal Service Fund. Registration is required.

2026-09-01-liberia-financial-inclusion-d.summary: A Liberian Observer editorial argues that Liberia's newly launched Enhanced Collateral Registry, which lets borrowers pledge inventory, equipment and livestock, needs clear loan terms and real-time credit reporting alongside it. It cites a non-performing loan ratio of 19.1 per cent in 2024 and 12.9 per cent in 2025, ahead of a national conference on bad loans on 9–11 September.

2026-09-01-malawi-us-specimen-data-not-s.summary: The US Embassy in Lilongwe said Malawian biological specimens will go to the United States only during public health emergencies and outbreaks, and that no personally identifiable information is shared. The agreement, signed on 11 February 2026 within a five-year US$936 million health package, requires Malawi to supply requested specimens within seven days. Malawian health advocates criticised the clause giving Malawi access to resulting products only after US domestic needs are met.

2026-09-01-mcit-egypt-nti-sla-cooperatio.summary: Egypt's National Telecommunication Institute and the State Lawsuits Authority signed a cooperation protocol on 31 August 2026 covering training in digital transformation, artificial intelligence and cybersecurity for the authority's counsellors. It continues the AI Ambassadors Program, whose second cohort is now under way. No protocol number, cost or date of effect is given.

2026-09-01-mdg-fdtic-2024-rapport-etats-.summary: Madagascar's telecoms regulator ARTEC published the 2024 financial statements of the Telecommunications and ICT Development Fund, the universal-service fund it manages. The four-page statements show Ar 62.9bn in contributions received, Ar 91.3bn granted and a deficit of Ar 27.95bn for the year. Whether an auditor's opinion accompanies them is not stated.

2026-09-01-mdg-fdtic-2025-rapport-etats-.summary: Madagascar's telecoms and ICT development fund (FDTIC), the universal-service fund managed by the regulator ARTEC, published its financial statements for 1 January to 31 December 2025. The fund took in Ar 100.1 billion in contributions and granted Ar 100.4 billion, close to break-even after a 2024 deficit. The file does not show whether an auditor's opinion accompanies the four pages of statements.

2026-09-01-mli-agefau-renforcement-capac.summary: Mali's universal-access fund agency AGEFAU is paying for a programme to train 504 elected officials and staff of 126 communes, launched on 1 September 2026 at the local-government training centre. The first session, on office software and collaborative tools, drew 84 participants from Koulikoro and Bamako; the agreement behind it is worth 200 million FCFA.

2026-09-01-mli-anthropic-threat-intellig.summary: Anthropic reported in September 2026 that a Claude user, likely a Bamako-based consultant working for Mali's state security agency ANSE, used the model to build Lakana 360, a platform monitoring about 25 million SIM cards on all three national mobile operators. It collects call records, texts and voice traffic, and the warrant requirement was removed from its dossier-writing component. Anthropic said it disrupted the activity.

2026-09-01-mli-cooperation-bilaterale-la.summary: Ivorian and Malian customs project teams met in Abidjan on 24-25 September 2026 to review SIGMAT, the interconnected transit-goods system on the Abidjan-Bamako corridor, now in its operating phase. They adopted a joint roadmap with an action matrix to correct the difficulties that persist.

2026-09-01-moov-africa-niger-offre-noctu.summary: Moov Africa Niger advertised a night-time mobile data bundle of 3.5GB for 500 CFA francs, usable from 23:00 to 06:00 and activated by dialling *157*7#, in a LinkedIn post on 1 September 2026. That is about 143 CFA francs per gigabyte.

2026-09-01-mozambique-intic-facim-ict-re.summary: Mozambique's ICT institute INTIC told a panel at the 61st FACIM fair in Maputo that digital platforms and intermediaries, including foreign operators serving Mozambicans, must register and declare where their data are stored. Its legal head Edson Psico said enforcing the ICT legal framework needs money, technology, staff and inspection capacity.

2026-09-01-mus-dpo-advice-to-management-.summary: The Data Protection Office updated its guidance in September 2026. Every Management Company must register as a controller, and also as a processor where it handles personal data for managed entities. Each must name its own Data Protection Officer, and managed entities get no blanket exemption but may ask for a case-by-case assessment.

2026-09-01-mydailynewsonline-afcfta-dtc-.summary: The AfCFTA Secretary-General set out the case for the Digital Trade Corridor: cutting the cost and complexity of intra-African business by ending the routing of African payments through third countries.

2026-09-01-myjoyonline-misinformation-de.summary: Ghana's National Commission for Civic Education said misinformation, hate speech and deepfakes threaten democratic stability, its chair Kathleen Addy telling a media event in Accra that fabricated images and audio mean seeing and hearing no longer count as proof. The EU's deputy ambassador announced support for a new African Media Integrity and Resilience Programme on verification skills.

2026-09-01-nam-nbc-bon-cran-launch-ai-pr.summary: The Bank of Namibia and the communications regulator CRAN have launched a programme to build shared AI infrastructure for public agencies and find uses in advisory services, procurement, licensing and scam reporting. Agencies are to buy AI hardware and software jointly rather than separately, and the roadmap includes AI in indigenous languages.

2026-09-01-nam-the-ongiini-eval-ow-bench.summary: A concept paper on arXiv announces Ongiini-Eval-OW, a planned 600-item benchmark for English to Oshindonga and English to Oshikwanyama translation, with references from two independent native-speaker translators, a 30% blind split and scoring on chrF++, BLEU and COMET-22 plus a 50-item human evaluation. The authors say no machine-translation evaluation benchmark exists for either standardised Oshiwambo variety, which major commercial services, NLLB-200, MADLAD-400 and the Masakhane checkpoints do not cover; first public release is targeted for Q4 2026 under CC-BY-4.0 for data and MIT for code.

2026-09-01-nam-usf-annual-report-2025-co.summary: The Communications Regulatory Authority of Namibia published the Universal Service Fund's 2025 integrated annual report, which carries the Fund's first financial statements, covering the 18 months to 31 December 2025. It also reports the Fund's Phase 1 (2024/25) and Phase 2 (2025/26) mobile radio access network deployments.

2026-09-01-national-payment-system-bill-.summary: South Africa's Reserve Bank governor said the National Payment System Bill will soon go out for public comment, moving payment regulation from an entity-based model to an activity-based one — the change that would open payment licensing beyond banks.

2026-09-01-newvision-uganda-nira-registe.summary: Uganda's identification authority holds 36.15 million people on the national register, close to 77% of a population the 2024 census put at 45.9 million, leaving nine to ten million unregistered. The figure matters because cabinet has just made that register the basis of tax identity.

2026-09-01-nga-kpmg-orange-nigeria-smart.summary: KPMG Nigeria and Orange Group's smartphone study, published in September 2026 from 13,251 respondents in 12 cities, puts smartphone ownership at 75% in 2025, up from 64% in 2023. Android runs on 96% of smartphones and WhatsApp on 95%; OPay is installed on 69% and PalmPay on 29%, and over a third of mobile subscribers were still on 2G in May 2026.

2026-09-01-nilepost-arrests-fake-news-pe.summary: Kampala police confirmed on 1 September 2026 that three men are held at Jinja Road Police Station over alleged fake news and unlawful obtaining or disclosure of personal data on social media in July. The case rests on Uganda's Computer Misuse Act, whose offences carry up to 10 years in prison. Police have not named the posts, platforms, victims or charges.

2026-09-01-nsia-kasi-100mw-ai-data-centr.summary: Nigeria's sovereign wealth fund announced plans for KASI, a 100MW artificial-intelligence-ready hyperscale data centre campus in Lagos offering co-location, cloud, storage and high-performance compute. It is framed as import substitution for compute currently bought abroad; no construction start or cost is stated.

2026-09-01-observer24-namibia-diginam-pk.summary: Namibia's National Root Certification Authority, operated by the communications regulator at the top of the country's digital trust chain, is technically live after a key-signing ceremony; the electronic signature provisions of the transactions act took effect on 15 June 2026.

2026-09-01-reuters-us-hands-off-ai-regul.summary: The United States pressed G20 members against creating new artificial-intelligence oversight bodies at a technology meeting in North Carolina, a position that would leave the largest American model developers unregulated by any new international body. African states negotiating continental AI governance are on the other side of that argument.

2026-09-01-sanews-manamela-sadc-computin.summary: South Africa's higher education minister, Buti Manamela, told a meeting of SADC university vice-chancellors in Johannesburg on 31 August 2026 that the region must build its own computing capacity, datasets, African-language technologies and cybersecurity. He set five priorities, including agreement on a regional higher education data system, to show results by the SADC ministers' meeting in June 2027.

2026-09-01-senegal-national-cybersecurit.summary: Senegal's National Assembly adopted the bill on protecting critical information infrastructure and digital security, creating a national cybersecurity authority with legal personality and a special status, backed by a national response team. Adopted is not promulgated.

2026-09-01-seneweb-cdp-donnees-personnel.summary: Senegal's personal data protection commission (CDP) handled 195 files between April and June 2026, 154 declarations and 41 authorisation requests, and issued 153 declaration receipts and 39 authorisations. It deferred two files, rejected one processing operation, heard two data controllers, and dealt with eight complaints and one report.

2026-09-01-shoprite-ra-cellular-techcent.summary: The group's results disclose that the R&A Cellular acquisition closed with effect from 14 August 2026 and that the initial stake is 51%. Financial terms remain undisclosed and the initial accounting for the combination is incomplete.

2026-09-01-ssd-radioyei-boss-emoney-rule.summary: The Bank of South Sudan's amended electronic money rules have taken effect, setting three customer-verification tiers with daily limits of SSP 1.625 million, 6.5 million and 13 million. Every digital payment platform must connect to the National Payment System through a licensed switch, keep customer funds in trust accounts spread across banks, and resolve complaints within seven days.

2026-09-01-techafricanews-egypt-fra-fint.summary: Egypt's Financial Regulatory Authority granted preliminary approval for two further projects to enter its regulatory sandbox for non-banking financial technology.

2026-09-01-techafricanews-gabon-makokou-.summary: Gabon's national digital infrastructure and frequencies agency, ANINF, installed two public Wi-Fi spaces in Makokou, at the Place de l'Indépendance and the Alexandre Sambat Stadium. It also fitted the town's digitised driving-licence enrolment centre with a local network, dedicated internet connection and backup power equipment, as part of Liberation Day activities.

2026-09-01-techafricanews-ghana-million-.summary: Ghana's communications ministry began a five-day training of trainers in datacom and access network technologies under the One Million Coders Programme on 31 August 2026, running to 4 September at the Ghana-India Kofi Annan Centre of Excellence in ICT. Huawei experts deliver the course, and each certified trainer is expected to train at least 20 members of the public.

2026-09-01-techafricanews-mtn-uj-taef-me.summary: MTN Group, the University of Johannesburg and The African Editors' Forum welcomed the first cohort of the MTN Pan-African Media Innovation Programme on 1 September 2026. The six-week course takes 42 journalists, editors and media practitioners from 10 countries, including South Africa, Nigeria, Rwanda, Ghana and South Sudan; the university chose the participants.

2026-09-01-techafricanews-safaricom-ethi.summary: Safaricom Ethiopia Foundation and the Federation of Ethiopian Associations of Persons with Disabilities signed a three-year memorandum of understanding, reported on 1 September 2026, covering digital inclusion, accessible technology, education, economic empowerment, healthcare and disability-rights advocacy. No funding amount is given.

2026-09-01-techafricanews-wiocc-300m-inv.summary: A third account of the same WIOCC subscription agreement, adding no new terms. See above.

2026-09-01-techcabal-chipmango-raises-1-.summary: ChipMango, a California-headquartered chip design and engineering training company, closed a US$1.9 million seed round led by Atlantica Ventures to expand its engineering work and workforce platform across Africa.

2026-09-01-techcabal-grey-yuan-payments-.summary: The cross-border payments startup Grey launched direct yuan payouts into Chinese bank accounts from dollar, euro, sterling and stablecoin balances, aimed at African importers trading with China.

2026-09-01-techcabal-mtn-momo-south-afri.summary: MTN sees the overhaul of South Africa's payment infrastructure as its opening for MoMo in a market where cash still dominates everyday payments and where its mobile money product has not taken hold.

2026-09-01-techcabal-nokia-ai-africa-tel.summary: Nokia's account of a shift in what African networks are expected to do — from moving data to processing and acting on it — as artificial intelligence workloads change network design. It is the vendor's framing of its own market.

2026-09-01-techcabal-tanzania-kimambi-su.summary: The Tanzanian activist and influencer Mange Kimambi filed a 36-page complaint against Meta in a California court on 21 August, alleging her accounts were disabled under pressure from Tanzanian authorities during a period of political unrest. The allegation is untested.

2026-09-01-techcabal-tim-cook-apple-afri.summary: An assessment of Apple's African position as Tim Cook departs: no retail store on the continent, limited reach for its payment service, and a market served largely through third parties and grey imports.

2026-09-01-techcity-nigeria-nin-healthca.summary: Field reporting from May 2026 documented how national identification number registration barriers were blocking access to Nigeria's Basic Health Care Provision Fund; this account follows the community-level responses that resulted.

2026-09-01-techreviewafrica-world-bank-b.summary: The World Bank opened a five-day implementation support mission on Malawi's US$150 million Digital Acceleration Project, to review progress and set priorities for the next phase. No disbursement or results figure accompanies it.

2026-09-01-techtrends-ai-rewiring-legal-.summary: An account of artificial intelligence entering routine legal work for African small businesses, most of which never see a lawyer until something goes wrong.

2026-09-01-tgo-mfb-srmt-2027-2031-strate.summary: Togo's finance ministry published its medium-term revenue mobilisation strategy for 2027-2031 in September 2026. Of its FCFA 10.5 billion cost, FCFA 5,995 million goes to digital transformation, including e-invoicing, links between the revenue authority and treasury systems, AI-assisted risk analysis for tax and customs, and sovereign data hosting. The measures target FCFA 481 billion in extra revenue, with 80% of the cost expected from partners.

2026-09-01-thecitizen-tanzania-digital-h.summary: Electronic medical records, interoperable health information systems, digital primary-care tools and artificial intelligence are moving onto Tanzania's health procurement agenda, changing what suppliers are being asked for.

2026-09-01-thecitizen-tanzania-korea-ai-.summary: Tanzania and South Korea discussed using artificial intelligence, hospital information systems and other digital tools to connect health facilities and share patient records. The talks produced no named instrument.

2026-09-01-thecitizen-tanzania-mobile-mo.summary: Active mobile money subscriptions in Tanzania reached 87.05 million in June 2026, up 7.5%, on the communications regulator's figures.

2026-09-01-thepoint-gambia-id-card-passp.summary: The Gambia's Ministry of Public Service said on 28 August it has cut steps from ID card and passport procedures and built their workflows into the MyGov platform, developed with JICA and partners in Bangladesh. MyGov has not launched because of contractual issues over passport issuance; rollout is hoped for before the end of 2026. A mass registration drive, including mobile teams in Spain and Italy, is issuing 10-year ID cards.

2026-09-01-thestar-monari-when-itax-fail.summary: A column on Kenya's tax portal failing on the evening of the 30 June filing deadline, when the revenue authority itself notified a traffic surge and intermittent delays. The penalties for late filing continued to run.

2026-09-01-togoofficiel-fsrp-agri-numeri.summary: A Chadian delegation from the West African food system resilience programme visited Lomé to study Togo's deployment of digital solutions in agriculture. The account is the host government's.

2026-09-01-tza-nfif3-mid-term-evaluation.summary: The Tanzania Economic Research Institute, TICGL's research arm, analysed the Bank of Tanzania's mid-term evaluation of the Third National Financial Inclusion Framework (2023–2028), covering December 2023 to December 2025. Access points grew 60.7% to 2,266,706 and active account use rose from 60% to 72.5% of adults. The institute finds service quality and household financial health improving more slowly.

2026-09-01-tza-online-child-safety-commi.summary: Tanzania has set up a National Advisory Committee on Online Child Protection and Safety and reached 1,811,212 children with online-safety education across all 26 mainland regions, Deputy Minister Maryprisca Mahundi told the National Assembly on 31 August 2026. The committee includes the ministry responsible for ICT and will advise on strategies against online risks to children.

2026-09-01-tza-statistical-abstract-2025.summary: Tanzania's National Bureau of Statistics published the Statistical Abstract 2025 in September 2026. It is an annual compendium of official tables, largely drawn from ministry administrative records.

2026-09-01-undp-funguo-tza-2026-funguo-c.summary: The UN Development Programme's FUNGUO innovation programme gave TZS 1.3bn to a fifth cohort of 14 Tanzanian businesses at the closing ceremony of Innovation Week Tanzania 2026. UNDP says FUNGUO has supported more than 100 businesses and channelled over US$3m to innovators since 2021. The 14 recipients are not named.

2026-09-01-undp-malawi-police-digital-fo.summary: Malawi Police officers were trained to identify, preserve and analyse digital evidence, as offences committed through digital platforms grow more complex.

2026-09-01-virtual-reality-primary-schoo.summary: Mauritius is putting immersive virtual reality into Grade 4 to 6 classrooms in state primary schools, across mathematics, science, history and geography and health and physical education. The digital promotion agency implements it for the technology ministry with the education ministry, the Rodrigues Regional Assembly and a university immersive media laboratory. No school count or pupil reach is published.

2026-09-01-wearetech-madagascar-actualis.summary: Madagascar is overhauling its 2014 cybercrime law, with judicial cooperation across borders the central problem where offenders and evidence sit in several countries at once.

2026-09-01-wiocc-300m-techcentral.summary: WIOCC Group signed a shareholder subscription agreement with the Africa Finance Corporation and Saudi Arabia's Vision International Investment Company for a combined US$300 million — by some distance the largest capital raise in the carrier-neutral infrastructure operator's history. The agreement was signed at a technology exhibition in Riyadh.

2026-09-01-wiocc-afc-vision-invest-inves.summary: WIOCC's own announcement of the US$300 million subscription agreement sets out that the money is to accelerate its digital infrastructure expansion across Africa. See the entry above for the transaction.

2026-09-01-wits-sadc-vc-meeting-regional.summary: University leaders, government representatives, the SADC Secretariat and the Southern African Regional Universities Association met at Wits University on 31 August–1 September 2026. They discussed the SADC higher education strategy, a proposed SADC University of Transformation, a regional higher education data system and micro-credentials. No design, cost or timetable for the data system is given.

2026-09-01-wmc-tunisia-germany-financing.summary: Five agreements worth more than EUR100 million were signed between Tunisia and Germany, with about EUR40 million more under discussion for the green economy. The piece asks the question the announcements do not answer: which Tunisian firms will be able to reach the money, in what form and at what cost.

2026-09-01-xaf-giz-ai-made-in-africa-exe.summary: GIZ's survey of 85 African AI businesses, run from April to July 2026 alongside a mapping of 311 firms, finds that 65% name cloud and compute as their largest cost, while 56% price their products under USD 2,500 a year per customer. The firms mapped have raised USD 1.3 billion since 2014, at a median ticket of USD 225,000, and three in four respondents treat AI products as core to their business.

2026-09-01-xaf-ria-datacipation-data-pol.summary: Research ICT Africa's project page describes DataCipation, under which it worked with GIZ and AUDA-NEPAD as an implementation partner on the continental rollout of the AU Data Policy Framework. RIA says it helped deliver validated national data policies and strategies for The Gambia, the Comoros and Somalia, supported drafting of Zambia's National Data Policy and developed South Africa's Open Data Policy Framework. As the project closes, a knowledge exchange among participating countries is to feed a Data Policy Implementation Toolkit and a network sustainability roadmap.

2026-09-01-zaf-atain-global-business-ser.summary: Atain, a company selling AI-driven customer experience and business process services, opened a R70 million global business services centre in Cape Town that will take its South African workforce from about 1,500 to 2,100. South Africa's deputy trade minister John Steenhuisen spoke at the opening. No date for the investment decision is given.

2026-09-01-zaf-national-treasury-digital.summary: A draft National Treasury deck dated September 2026, prepared for a GTAC-EU e-procurement dialogue, sets out how the Office of the Chief Procurement Officer plans to modernise procurement systems. It presents the Central Supplier Database, with about 900,000 registered suppliers, as the base, verifying suppliers against SARS, Home Affairs and the banks, and plans an e-procurement system and a digital marketplace on top of it.

2026-09-01-zaf-ocp-registry-south-africa.summary: The Open Contracting Partnership's data registry lists the National Treasury's eTenders feed in the Open Contracting Data Standard, covering February 2017 to September 2026 under a public-domain licence and retrieved monthly. It holds 35,309 tenders, 9,551 awards and 1,691 contracts, and excludes municipalities and state-owned entities unless they share data voluntarily.

2026-09-01-zmb-auditor-general-report-20.summary: Zambia's Office of the Auditor General issued its report on the accounts of the Republic for the year ended 31 December 2025; the document prints no issue date. The 258-page report covers ministries, provinces and agencies, and finds that the PMEC payroll has workflow controls on only 8 of 29 SAP infotypes.

2026-09-02-afdb-axian-digital-finance-wo.summary: The African Development Bank and AXIAN Group launched a programme on 2 September 2026 to offer digital loans and financial services through AXIAN's Mixx and MVola mobile money platforms to 34,000 women-led small businesses in Madagascar, Tanzania and Senegal. A second component will train 25,000 women in those countries plus Togo and the Comoros. No committed amount is stated.

2026-09-02-ago-governo-pretende-estender.summary: Angola's telecommunications minister Mário Oliveira said on 2 September 2026 in Lobito that the government is preparing a domestic submarine cable linking the networks of coastal cities, as part of extending fibre-optic services nationwide. He spoke at the launch of ZAP Fibra in Benguela province and said links to neighbouring countries and an earth-observation satellite are also planned. No cost or timetable is given.

2026-09-02-algerie-aapi-diar-dzair-datac.summary: Algeria's investment promotion agency (AAPI) handed over land concessions on 2 September 2026 for four projects, including a site at El Affroun in Blida wilaya for a data centre by the company Diar Dzair, expected to create 340 jobs. The other three are food-industry projects in Bordj Bou Arreridj. No investment sum is given.

2026-09-02-aljazeera-us-eu-ai-regulation.summary: At a G20 innovation ministerial in Chapel Hill on 1 September, the United States urged other governments to adopt the Carolina Principles, a framework arguing that regulation should not single out particular technologies. The European Commission moved the other way in the same week, sending information requests to more than 30 AI companies worldwide under the AI Act. The two positions are the choice most African governments drafting AI rules will be asked to pick between.

2026-09-02-anats-tchad-site-officiel-nni.summary: Chad's secure documents agency, ANATS, set up by Ordinance 001/PR/2016, issues identity cards, passports, residence cards, driving licences and civil status records. Its website says its population management system assigns everyone enrolled, including refugees and foreign residents, a unique national identification number (NNI) after deduplication, and lists 29 enrolment centres. The page carries no date.

2026-09-02-aps-css-paiement-prestations-.summary: Senegal's social security fund (Caisse de Sécurité Sociale) announced on 2 September 2026 that beneficiaries can receive social benefits directly into a Wave mobile-money account. Recipients sign up with a form available at CSS branches or on its website. No beneficiary numbers or start date are given.

2026-09-02-arcep-tchad-registre-des-lois.summary: The register of laws on the website of Chad's electronic communications and postal regulator, ARCEP, lists eight statutes from 2014 and 2015. They include Law 007/PR/2015 on personal data protection, Law 008/PR/2015 on electronic transactions and Law 009/PR/2015 on cybersecurity and cybercrime. The page is undated, and its links to the texts of the laws do not work.

2026-09-02-assabahnews-pm-circular-publi.summary: Tunisia's head of government issued a circular directing ministers, secretaries of state, heads of public enterprises and state controllers to adopt strategic action plans on the governance and performance of public establishments. Among its legal bases is the 2020 decree-law on electronic data exchange between public bodies.

2026-09-02-auda-nepad-africa-prosperity-.summary: The Africa Prosperity Network said on 2 September 2026 that its next Africa Prosperity Dialogues will run in Accra from 27 to 29 January 2027, with registration opening on 7 September. Organisers recalled that regional economic communities committed in July 2024 to a continent-wide mobile money interoperability framework by 2027; payments and digital infrastructure are two of the four themes.

2026-09-02-auda-nepad-harmonised-standar.summary: Amine Idriss Adoum, a director at the African Union Development Agency (AUDA-NEPAD), said African institutions have adopted more than 1,000 decisions and declarations on regional integration but implemented fewer than 15%. Speaking at the launch of the Africa Prosperity Dialogues 2027, he blamed unaligned national laws, regulations and technical standards, citing transport rules along the proposed Abidjan–Lagos highway.

2026-09-02-beac-registre-instructions-ci.summary: The Bank of Central African States' register of payment-system instruments lists the CEMAC rules that apply in Chad: Regulation 03 of 21 December 2016 on payment systems, means and incidents, and Regulation 04 of 21 December 2018 on payment services. It also lists a 2018 instruction on interoperability and a 2025 instruction adopting the ISO 20022 standard for payments.

2026-09-02-ben-compte-rendu-du-conseil-d.summary: Benin's Council of Ministers approved on 2 September 2026 the construction of 35 integrated economic, social and digital centres in 26 communes, each combining a social protection one-stop shop, a post office and a community digital point. The same session approved a digital platform to identify and geolocate farmers and plots, and appointed technical advisers on artificial intelligence in several ministries.

2026-09-02-ben-decret-2026-579-comite-na.summary: Benin issued Decree No. 2026-579 on 2 September 2026 creating the National Digital Committee and setting its functions, organisation and operation. The item gives the decree only as an attached PDF and states no further details.

2026-09-02-businessday-africa-ai-governa.summary: Roseline Ilori of Bridge57 Solutions argues that Africa cannot scale AI faster than it can govern it, and that the question worth asking is not how quickly the continent adopts the technology but whether the systems being deployed are safe, fair, transparent and accountable. The gap she names is institutional rather than technical: regulators unable to supervise automated systems, businesses that do not understand the risks, and citizens with no way to challenge an algorithmic decision.

2026-09-02-bwa-weaving-the-slip.summary: A Botswana Gazette investigation published on 2 September 2026 reports that Botswana keeps no gambling statistics as it moves to lower the legal betting age. Unregistered betting influencers draw 4,000 to 15,000 responses to a single slip and refer followers to bookmakers, while parents in Mathethe and Digawana describe children funding bets from household mobile-money and bank accounts.

2026-09-02-cmr-bridging-digital-dividend.summary: Civic Watch and the Club des Jeunes Aveugles Réhabilités du Cameroun held a workshop in Yaoundé on 2 September 2026, with German Embassy support, on protecting disabled people online and offline. Cameroon's Ministry of Social Affairs described national disability cards carrying tax exemptions under the 2026 Finance Law and a 50% higher-education fee waiver. Civic Watch's founder warned of targeted cyberbullying on TikTok and Snapchat.

2026-09-02-cmr-camerounlink-plan-directe.summary: Cameroon is commissioning a national master plan to digitise its public-procurement information system; the African Development Bank published the contract award on 31 August 2026. The six-month study went to the NC Consulting and Eyra International grouping for FCFA 241.36 million, funded under the AfDB-backed public-finance governance project PAGFIP.

2026-09-02-cmr-tchad-cameroun-le-bnft-fo.summary: Chad's national land freight bureau (BNFT) began training transporters, freight forwarders and drivers in Douala, Cameroon, on 1 September 2026 to use its e-BNFT digital platform, covering account creation, file entry and tracking. The bureau says it has been extending digitised procedures since February 2026 to offices including Douala, Kribi, Ngaoundéré, Moundou, Bongor and N'Djamena.

2026-09-02-cod-lancement-officiel-de-la-.summary: DR Congo's transport minister Jean-Pierre Bemba launched SYGREM, a freight-charge management platform built by the freight office Ogefrem with PADS Corporation, in Kinshasa on 1 September 2026. It digitises the FERI, AD and FERE freight-tracking documents and adds geolocation and online payment, with receipts paid into dedicated Ogefrem bank accounts.

2026-09-02-cod-rdc-jean-claude-mputu-den.summary: Jean-Claude Mputu, spokesman for the Congo Is Not For Sale coalition (CNPAV), said the Democratic Republic of Congo's passport contract with Semlex, renewed in 2020 when the original five-year deal expired, has never been published. The renewal, meant to last a year, ran until 2025; the only concession won was a passport price cut from $185 to $100.

2026-09-02-comision-europea-guinea-ecuat.summary: The European Commission's country page states that the EU has no delegation in Equatorial Guinea; cooperation is supervised from its delegation in Yaoundé, Cameroon. Equatorial Guinea received no bilateral allocation under the 11th EDF and has no multiannual indicative programme for 2021-2027, but takes part in thematic civil-society and human-rights programmes and in regional programmes through ECCAS.

2026-09-02-connectingafrica-egypt-cisco-.summary: Egypt's National Telecommunication Institute and Cisco signed a memorandum of understanding to train 3,000 certified technology instructors in support of the national AI strategy: 1,000 university faculty members and independent lecturers a year for three years, in data networks, cybersecurity, operating systems and AI. The target is the supply of people qualified to teach those subjects rather than the students directly. Cisco says its programmes have trained or mentored nearly 670,000 Egyptian students; no signing date is given.

2026-09-02-cote-divoire-mtnit-mistral-pa.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's Ministry of Digital Transition published its own communiqué on the strategic partnership it signed with the French AI company Mistral on 17 August in Abidjan. The work is a study and strategic audit of the national AI ecosystem, mapping the actors and resources available, and sits inside the Feuille de Route Numérique 2026-2028 and its forty structuring projects. No sum is stated and no financier of the audit is named.

2026-09-02-crasa-cspc-committee-meeting-.summary: The Communications Regulators' Association of Southern Africa held the first in-person meeting of a committee for its 2026/27 financial year in Gaborone, Botswana, from 2 to 4 September 2026. The meeting was convened to advance the committee's 2026/27 workplan; no agenda items or outcomes are given.

2026-09-02-damongo-university-additional.summary: Ghana's Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu said on 2 September 2026 that a US$30 million Chinese government grant will not be enough to complete and equip the University of Science and Technology at Damongo, which he put at more than US$100 million. The Savannah Region university is planned as a centre for science, robotics, digital sciences and artificial intelligence.

2026-09-02-dayoo-guangzhou-cross-border-.summary: Guangzhou launched a national pilot for international data cooperation, opening a service that lets foreign firms send data in for local model processing and export the resulting tokens, alongside a federated research platform that already links Portuguese, Brazilian and Macau institutions by exchanging encrypted model parameters rather than data. No African place is named; the pilot sets terms that others will have to work within.

2026-09-02-digital-skills-open-new-oppor.summary: Eswatini's Ministry of Information, Communications and Technology ran a digital skills workshop series at the 58th Eswatini International Trade Fair in Manzini, held from 28 August to 6 September 2026. Speakers from the University of Eswatini, the Royal Science and Technology Park and the private sector covered digital careers, coding and digital marketing.

2026-09-02-dji-djibouti-unveils-ai-tools.summary: Djibouti's Ports and Free Zones Authority showed AI applications at the country's first national AI forum, among them DPCS Foresight, which predicts when customers will collect containers so terminals can stack them to cut re-handling and dwell time. It also showed DPCR Vision AI, a camera system launched in 2024 that detects potholes and cracks on regional corridor roads.

2026-09-02-djibouti-electronic-single-wi.summary: Djibouti's customs administration plans an electronic single window bringing customs and trade procedures onto one platform, discussed at a preparatory workshop at the People's Palace on 1 September 2026. It is working with the commerce ministry, the AfCFTA Secretariat and Korea's CUPIA, and says the system will go beyond the SYDONIAWORLD system now in use. No cost or timetable is given.

2026-09-02-eca-unfpa-digital-monitoring-.summary: The UN Economic Commission for Africa and the UN Population Fund announced a meeting in Abidjan, with Côte d'Ivoire's National Population Office, to validate a digital platform for monitoring the African Union roadmap on the demographic dividend. Representatives from eight West African pilot countries, including Benin, Mali, Niger and Senegal, will test the platform and produce national monitoring reports.

2026-09-02-egypte-hisham-setit-menzouma-.summary: Egypt's Unified Procurement Authority presented its national medical-stock system to the prime minister on 2 September 2026. Its head, Hisham Steit, said the system covers 38,000 users, 11,000 health facilities and 2,000 suppliers, with stocktaking on a mobile scanning app and real-time balances. The prime minister said about EGP 90 billion is budgeted this year for medicines and medical supplies.

2026-09-02-eritrea-technology-education-.summary: UNESCO's education profile for Eritrea describes technology in education under the 2018–2022 National Education Sector Plan, which uses terms such as ICT, e-learning and distance learning without defining them. The 1997 Constitution mentions technology only in connection with science, arts and sports. The profile is on a legacy site that is no longer updated.

2026-09-02-fg-moves-to-enhance-nigeria-s.summary: Nigeria's finance ministry and its budget and economic planning ministry set up a Standing Committee on Macroeconomic Data and Assumptions and agreed to build a central government data repository, according to a statement reported on 2 September 2026. A validation workshop found wide gaps between past budget assumptions and outcomes, especially for oil output and revenue. The workshop's date is not given.

2026-09-02-gabon-programme-citoyennete-p.summary: Gabon's director general of social welfare visited Mouila on 1 September 2026 to review a programme issuing birth certificates to people without civil status and enrolling them in the national health insurance fund, CNAMGS. Across Ngounié province 500 files were registered, 486 sent to the Mouila court for substitute judgments, and 100 birth certificates are ready for collection.

2026-09-02-gbc-ghana-cid-interpol-ai-cyb.summary: Ghana's police CID put Interpol's 2026 African Cyber Threat Assessment on the record at the awareness month launch: AI now enables 55% of reported cybercrime in Africa, with related losses of $484 million. CID director-general COP Lydia Yaako Donkor described generative AI supplying convincing phishing messages, cloned voices and synthetic images and video, with cryptocurrency, mule accounts and fraudulent investment schemes moving the proceeds — an industrialised, borderless ecosystem rather than isolated offending. She tied Ghana's exposure directly to the spread of mobile money, internet banking and instant transfers.

2026-09-02-ghana-burkina-faso-flood-data.summary: At an AV-STEC project meeting in Bolgatanga, Ghanaian and Burkinabe officials proposed a Bagre-Kompienga release protocol based on real-time data sharing and agreed spill thresholds. Burkina Faso's power utility SONABEL said letters to Ghana's Volta River Authority since October 2025 had gone unanswered. Participants cited slow warnings, weak data sharing between forecasters and responders, and false alarms; the project is funded through Canada's IDRC.

2026-09-02-guinea-ecuatorial-estrategia-.summary: Equatorial Guinea's Ministry of Transport, Telecommunications and Civil Aviation opened a four-day working session in Malabo on 2 September 2026 with eight World Bank Group specialists. Its aims are to finish and validate the national digital economy strategy, complete the sector's legal framework and prepare a World Bank-financed project, which would be the Bank's first operation in the country in 35 years.

2026-09-02-guinee-penurie-actes-naissanc.summary: Guinea's digital birth certificates have not been printed for about two weeks because of a nationwide shortage of secure paper, the civil-registry officer for Conakry's Ratoma commune said on 2 September 2026. Registration continues and new stock is expected within a week. The relocation of the data centre from the Maison centrale has also disrupted the system.

2026-09-02-hcn-blida-deuxieme-centre-nat.summary: Algeria's High Commission for Digitalisation said on 2 September 2026 that the second national data centre, at Blida, has received Uptime Institute Tier III Design certification, after the first centre at El Mohammadia in February 2026. The certificate covers the design, not the built facility; the commission says it is still seeking Tier III certification of the constructed centres.

2026-09-02-here-is-our-ai-plan-to-reach-.summary: Rwanda's ICT minister Paula Ingabire set out a plan to bring AI-based farming advice to 2.5 million farmers, speaking at the Africa Food Systems Forum in Kigali on 1 September 2026. She cited the e-Soko price platform, Smart Nkunganire's 1.5 million farmers registered for subsidised inputs, and Tunga, a Kinyarwanda voice assistant on trial at the agriculture ministry's call centre.

2026-09-02-inseed-anad-politique-dacces-.summary: Chad's national statistics institute, INSEED, sets the access conditions for microdata in its National Data Archive (ANAD). Users must keep respondents anonymous under the 2019 statistics law, may not copy or pass the data to others without INSEED's written consent, must cite a prescribed source line and must send INSEED two copies of any resulting report.

2026-09-02-inseed-tchad-textes-reglement.summary: Chad's national statistics institute, INSEED, lists the legal basis of the national statistical system: Law No. 026/PR/2019 of June 2019, which makes INSEED the system's central body with legal personality and management autonomy, and four application decrees of July 2019. The system also includes a statistics development fund, a national statistics council, sectoral statistical units and a statistics school.

2026-09-02-itweb-africa-ghana-digital-fi.summary: A second account of the same National Cyber Security Awareness Month launch, adding the Financial Industry Command Security Operations Centre as standing infrastructure for threat-intelligence sharing among Ghana's regulated financial institutions. See the Cyber Security Authority's launch entry for the campaign itself.

2026-09-02-itweb-africa-mtn-nigeria-flyx.summary: MTN Nigeria launched FlyX, a 5G fixed-wireless home broadband service for locations where indoor reception is weak or its FibreX fibre product is unavailable, at ₦30,000 for 30 days at 50Mbps and ₦45,000 at 100Mbps, both unlimited. The operator holds a target of eight million Nigerian homes on fibre within three years and names lengthy approvals, the physical demands of cable installation and slow cost recovery as what stands in the way. Fixed wireless is the faster-to-deploy substitute rather than the plan.

2026-09-02-itweb-co-za-icasa-concourt-po.summary: ICASA has asked the Constitutional Court to settle whether it may condone a late licence-renewal notice from a class licensee, having lost the question in both the Pretoria High Court and the Supreme Court of Appeal to Open Heaven, a Hammanskraal community radio station that filed two weeks late. The regulator reads section 11(9) of the Electronic Communications Act as granting that power only for individual licences, and section 19(2) as deliberately withholding it for class licences; Open Heaven argues the Act leaves latitude where good cause is shown. The court heard the matter on 27 August and has not ruled.

2026-09-02-itweb-co-za-microsoft-eastern.summary: Microsoft and implementation partner NKUSI-IT Siyasebenza ran a three-day Power Apps skills-transfer programme for 20 IT specialists of the Eastern Cape Department of Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs, at the Steve Biko Centre in Ginsberg, Qonce, covering Power Apps, Power Automate, Power Pages and Dataverse. The partner's recommendation is a province-wide skills and adoption framework around AI and Copilot, cyber security and Azure, which is where a three-day course turns into a procurement position.

2026-09-02-itweb-co-za-mtn-chairman-fint.summary: The chairman of a pan-African operator told its fintech summit that more than $2 trillion flowed through mobile money globally in 2025, of which sub-Saharan Africa accounted for about $1.4 trillion, across 2.3 billion registered accounts and 593 million active in any 30 days. He argued the next frontier is financial health rather than inclusion.

2026-09-02-itweb-co-za-popia-grace-perio.summary: South Africa's Information Regulator called the compliance grace period the data protection Act's key weakness: a public body that remedies a violation within the stated timeframe cannot then be fined. Its chair said the high-value fines issued since enforcement powers commenced in July 2021 have largely not materialised, with bodies either complying in time or challenging in court.

2026-09-02-itweb-co-za-sa-online-retail-.summary: South African online retail crossed 10% of national retail turnover in June 2026 and is forecast at R159 billion in sales for the year, growth of 22.5%, according to Online Retail in South Africa 2026 by World Wide Worx with Mastercard, Peach Payments and Ask Africa. The R29 billion added is close to the whole 2020 online market of about R30.2 billion. Takealot is used by 35.3% of online shoppers, Shein by 21.5% and Checkers Sixty60 by 15%, and PayInc processed an average 934 transactions a minute on Black Friday 2025.

2026-09-02-kenya-cofek-high-court-rideha.summary: Kenya's High Court struck down a National Transport and Safety Authority rule requiring ride-hailing platforms to retain passenger and driver data for three years and hand it over on demand, finding it breached the right to privacy and the Data Protection Act 2019, the Consumers Federation of Kenya reported on 2 September 2026. The court, on a petition by Bolt, also blocked an 18% commission cap and suspended its declaration for 12 months so the government can redo the regulations.

2026-09-02-kenya-ecitizen-sh36-5bn-colle.summary: Kiambu gubernatorial aspirant Bonnie Mwangi called on 2 September 2026 for Parliament to investigate Kenya's eCitizen payment platform, citing Auditor-General findings for 2023/24. Reported collections were about Sh100.84 billion but bank statements supported only Sh64.30 billion, a gap of Sh36.5 billion, and four transfers worth Sh127.85 million went from the government paybill to private entities without supporting approvals.

2026-09-02-kictanet-youtube-tax-pushback.summary: Kenyan creators are contesting the withholding tax on video-platform earnings, which sits alongside the digital services tax, value-added tax on digital marketplace supply and the digital asset tax. The civil-society network carrying the campaign published its own brief on digital-tax reform in 2024.

2026-09-02-ko-funda-signaler-une-irregul.summary: The Republic of Congo's Ministry of State Control runs KO FUNDA, an online portal where citizens can report corruption, embezzlement, favouritism, absent officials, poor public service and excessive delays. The ministry says reports are handled confidentially and each is examined before any decision. The page carries no publication date.

2026-09-02-lanation-djibouti-forum-natio.summary: Djibouti opened its first national forum on artificial intelligence at the Palais du Peuple on 2 and 3 September, organised by the ministry for the digital economy and innovation under the president's patronage. The framing is explicitly sovereignty: AI as a lever of independence, innovation and development rather than a technology to be received. The forum sits against Vision Djibouti 2035 and UNESCO's readiness assessment.

2026-09-02-lequotidien-reunion-nouveau-c.summary: The Réunion to South Africa cable is scheduled to enter service in 2028, adding route diversity before an older system retires from 2027. Marine surveys run in 2026, with manufacture and laying to follow.

2026-09-02-madagascar-cybercrime-bill-fa.summary: Madagascar's National Assembly was due to vote on a bill reforming the 2014 cybercrime law. Article 17 sets two to five years' prison and fines of Ar5m to Ar50m for running fake-account networks or deceiving people with fake identities, doubled for organised groups. Article 52 makes group administrators and resharers liable for manifestly illegal content they knowingly leave online.

2026-09-02-mauritania-leegoud-land-regis.summary: Mauritania's technical committee on rural land and developer plots in Nouakchott called on holders of rural land concessions inside the capital's urban zone to register on the Leegoud platform by 18 September 2026. Help desks are to open in Nouakchott's three moughataas. The exercise follows a declaration to the Council of Ministers on 28 April 2026.

2026-09-02-mozambique-absa-mpesa-digital.summary: Absa Bank Mozambique and M-Pesa signed a memorandum of understanding at the FACIM 2026 trade fair in Maputo, reported on 2 September 2026. It links M-Pesa's Paga Fácil merchant service to Absa accounts so merchants can move receipts into the bank at no cost, usually within minutes. No value is given.

2026-09-02-mozambique-intic-facim-ict-re.summary: Officials of Mozambique's National Institute of Information and Communication Technologies (INTIC) said at a panel during the 61st Maputo International Trade Fair that applying the country's ICT laws needs money, technology, staff and cooperation across sectors. Legal head Edson Psico named enforcement of data-protection rules, incident response and supervisory capacity as the main challenges, and said Mozambique depends on external technology.

2026-09-02-mozambique-misau-tender-healt.summary: Mozambique's health ministry is seeking ten operators to help its ICT staff install data networks at 15 health centres in Maputo city and province, under a Global Fund grant for 2024–2026. The work lasts three months at a daily rate of 600 meticais per operator, and expressions of interest close on 18 September 2026.

2026-09-02-mpten-architecture-numerique-.summary: The Republic of Congo's digital economy ministry set out a national digital public infrastructure architecture built on MOSIP for digital identity, X-Road for data exchange between ministries, and Mojaloop for a payments switch linking MTN MoMo, Airtel Money, banks and the Treasury. Services would run through an e-Citizen portal hosted at the national data centre. The page describes plans; no adopting decree, cost or timetable is given.

2026-09-02-nation-africa-ruto-fibre-opti.summary: Kenya's ICT Cabinet Secretary William Kabogo said 37,000km of the government's 100,000km fibre target has been laid, leaving 63,000km before the 2027 deadline. The network, funded through the Universal Service Fund, is meant to serve 53,000 government facilities; Kenya Power had been paid Sh940.6m by June 2025. Broadband subscriptions reached 52.85 million by March 2026.

2026-09-02-newvision-starlink-launch-uga.summary: Starlink began commercial service in Uganda, ending the regulatory process that followed a memorandum and a five-year operating licence signed with the communications regulator in May 2026. The licence requires a national gateway and physical point of presence, an operational office, and registration of every device activated in the country.

2026-09-02-nga-sanwo-olu-80bn-digital-ec.summary: Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu, represented by his deputy Obafemi Hamzat, told the GITEX Nigeria Official Tour on 2 September 2026 that the state has more than $80 billion in technology commitments. About 3,000km of a planned 6,000km fibre network was laid between 2019 and 2025, and the state plans to secure 200–400MW of state-procured electricity.

2026-09-02-niger-onc-media-crisis-commun.summary: Niger's communications minister Adji Ali Salatou and the national communication observatory (ONC) met media chiefs in Niamey on 2 September 2026 after the events of 28-29 August at the capital's air base. The ONC presented its monitoring of broadcast, online and platform content from 28 August to 1 September, citing an information vacuum, conflicting descriptions of the events and disinformation on social networks.

2026-09-02-nigeriainfo-npf-vigilant-app-.summary: The Nigeria Police Force launched the NPF Vigilant App on 1 September at its conference centre in Jabi, Abuja, a public channel for reporting suspected financial fraud, uploading evidence and tracking a case through to feedback. It was built by the Force ICT Department with financial-sector stakeholders and is meant to coordinate police handling with banks; the Central Bank of Nigeria, NIBSS, banks and fintechs attended. Inspector-General Olatunji Disu said the technology must be deployed lawfully and ethically, with respect for privacy and data protection.

2026-09-02-nimc-digital-sovereignty-gite.summary: The head of Nigeria's National Identity Management Commission, Abisoye Odusote, told GITEX Nigeria in Lagos on 2 September 2026 that Africa must train its own cryptographers and digital trust specialists, and called for aligned certificate policies, data privacy and legal frameworks. At the same event the AfCFTA secretary-general, Wamkele Mene, urged faster implementation of the Protocol on Digital Trade.

2026-09-02-nra-begins-nationwide-distrib.summary: Sierra Leone's National Revenue Authority began distributing Smart GST machines to 10,000 GST-registered businesses nationwide, announced on 31 August 2026. Commissioner-General Abu Martin Kanneh said the machines complement the existing electronic cash register system and will let businesses issue valid receipts. No cost or supplier is given.

2026-09-02-opinion-internet-tariffs-has-.summary: In an opinion column, a member of South Sudan's SPLM-IO political bureau says MTN and Zain raised internet tariffs by about 15%. He asks the information and communications minister, Ateny Wek Ateny, to explain who approved the increase and whether the ministry regulates tariffs.

2026-09-02-orange-free-reunion-south-afr.summary: Two French operators will fund the €93 million cable between Réunion and South Africa, one acting as landing party and its marine subsidiary laying infrastructure designed by a French manufacturer. The cable is scheduled to enter service in 2028, replacing a system commissioned in 2002; the partners did not disclose their respective shares.

2026-09-02-premiumtimes-osinbajo-cairo-d.summary: African lawyers meeting in Cairo reviewed and prioritised six pillars of a proposed declaration on children's rights and design accountability, covering safety-by-design requirements, restrictions on exploitative targeting and manipulative practices, and age-appropriate design standards. The session chair argued companies cannot engineer risk into products and then leave children and parents to manage it.

2026-09-02-reunion-submarine-cable-la-re.summary: The Réunion regional authority launched RéuNION, a submarine cable from Saint-Paul to Durban costing €93.1 million and carrying 16 fibre pairs at 20 Tbps each. It is funded by €30m from the EU's regional development fund, €20m from the Connecting Europe Facility and €43.1m from the consortium, and must be built within three years under the European funding terms.

2026-09-02-rights-officials-accuse-gover.summary: South Sudan Human Rights Commission officials told a Juba panel on 2 September 2026 that the government treats civil society organisations as enemies or political opponents. Deputy chair Ezekia A. Gibson rated transparency and participation weak and accountability very weak; participants said the National Revenue Authority does not consistently publish the revenue data it is required to release.

2026-09-02-rwandas-new-ekash-payment-sys.summary: The National Bank of Rwanda reported that its eKash payment and transfer system has carried more than 10.5 million transactions worth over 960 billion Rwandan francs since its national launch on 14 July 2026, with 98.6% completed. Users of interoperable payments rose from 740,787 to 1,971,522 by end-July; some users report failed or delayed transfers, which the central bank says it is tracking daily.

2026-09-02-sdn-zakat-chamber-banking-hr-.summary: Sudan's Zakat Chamber signed a contract with the National Technical Company, formerly the Nile Centre, to complete an enterprise resource planning system linking its disbursement, human-resources and finance functions. Work on the system had stopped because of the war. No cost or timetable is given.

2026-09-02-ssd-sudanspost-nec-rejects-bi.summary: South Sudan's National Elections Commission has ruled out biometric voter registration, its chairperson saying on 2 September 2026 that registration will be on paper and later computerised, because most of the population cannot read. General elections are set for 22 December 2026.

2026-09-02-standard-gm-grcs-digital-volu.summary: The Gambia Red Cross Society launched a digital Volunteer and Membership Management System at its Kanifing headquarters on 31 August 2026, replacing branch paper registers. It handles registration, profiling, branch assignment, validation and deployment of volunteers, which officials say cuts mobilisation from days to minutes. No cost, supplier or volunteer count is given.

2026-09-02-starlink-launches-uganda-pric.summary: Prices published with the Ugandan launch put a residential 100 Mbps package at Shs203,704 a month against an estimated Shs2.3 million to start, plus a Shs437,036 regulatory charge — against fibre offers from the two mobile incumbents advertised at Shs110,000 and Shs99,000 for the same speed.

2026-09-02-syc-information-commission-tr.summary: Seychelles' Information Commission held its second 2026 induction session for information officers newly appointed by public bodies, led by chief executive Diana Benoit. The commission runs two such sessions a year.

2026-09-02-tcd-tgo-agriculture-digital-k.summary: A four-member delegation from Chad's West Africa Food System Resilience Program visited Lomé on 28 August to study three digital agriculture tools built by its Togolese counterpart: SIHAM, TG-ALERTE+ and e-Agri conseil. Togo reported more than 80,000 agrometeorological bulletins in 2024, reaching over 122,000 people. The Togo programme has $96.37 million in World Bank financing.

2026-09-02-techafricanews-ghana-csa-awar.summary: Ghana's Cyber Security Authority launched the 2026 National Cyber Security Awareness Month on 2 September, themed on securing the country's digital finance ecosystem and observed each October. Director-general Divine Selase Agbeti pressed banks, fintechs, payment service providers, insurers and merchants to treat cyber resilience as a core governance responsibility rather than a regulatory box, warning that lost trust in digital payments would undermine the wider digital economy. CSA figures put reported incidents at 2,008 in the first half of 2025 against 1,317 a year earlier, a 52% rise, with reported losses of GH¢14.94 million, more than 90% of it online fraud and impersonation.

2026-09-02-techafricanews-ghana-nca-5g-s.summary: Ghana's National Communications Authority closed applications for 700MHz, 2.3GHz and 3GHz mobile-broadband spectrum on 2 September with four applications received, and opened Envelope A under the published Selection and Award Procedure. Envelope B, holding the Best Price Offer, stays sealed. The authority was careful to say that opening Envelope A determines nothing about the eligibility, compliance or completeness of any application.

2026-09-02-techafricanews-instarc-125m-s.summary: Instarc, a Tallinn-based regulatory-technology firm, raised a €1.25 million strategic investment from HFO Investments to commercialise its compliance platform for South African accountable institutions under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act. The platform covers client onboarding, identity and ownership verification, configurable workflows, document management, retrievable audit records and APIs into existing systems, and the company says it is built to adapt to other regulatory regimes. The date the investment was agreed is not stated in the reporting held.

2026-09-02-techafricanews-kenya-lesotho-.summary: Kenya's Communications Authority is hosting a Lesotho Communications Authority delegation to benchmark Kenya's National Addressing System and the legal framework behind it.
