2026-09-06-gabonreview-gabon-cnt-biometr.summary: Gabon's national transport company, CNT, is preparing a personalised biometric card for Libreville buses and has consulted the data protection authority on the rules for collecting passengers' personal data, reported on 6 September 2026. The cards could be tailored to pupils, students and workers. No launch date or cost is given.

2026-09-06-ghana-needs-6000-new-cell-sit.summary: Ghana's communications minister, Samuel Nartey George, said on 6 September 2026 that the country needs about 6,000 new cell sites. About 1,100 are being rolled out, roughly 800 by MTN Ghana, of which nearly 180 are complete, and about 350 by Telecel, with completion expected in the first half of 2027. He also directed that all rural telephony sites be upgraded to at least 4G.

2026-09-06-ghana-sam-george-inspects-rur.summary: Ghana's Communications Minister Samuel Nartey George inspected rural telephony sites in the Eastern Region on 4 September 2026 and directed that all rural telephony sites nationwide be upgraded to at least 4G. He said rural communities are still being given 2G and 3G. No cost or timetable for the upgrade is given.

2026-09-06-lesechos-congo-etat-civil-cir.summary: Congo-Brazzaville's territorial administration issued a circular on 1 September 2026 tightening control of civil registration. It bars antedating records, altering identity, parentage or date of birth without a court decision, and issuing several records for one person, and requires agents to check each document against the original register. Agents involved in document fraud face administrative and judicial sanctions.

2026-09-06-liberia-iic-cental-foi-compli.summary: Liberia's Independent Information Commission and the anti-corruption group CENTAL ran a Freedom of Information Act compliance campaign from 11 August to 2 September 2026 at the national identification registry, the statistics institute LISGIS, LACE and the water corporation. Agencies were told to appoint information officers, set up request review bodies and publish budgets and contracts proactively. Three more agencies were scheduled for 8-10 September.

2026-09-06-libya-gia-national-informatio.summary: Libya's High Technical Committee for the National Information System met in Tripoli on 1 September 2026 and ruled that permanent membership belongs to the director of each ministry's information and documentation centre, with proxies accepted only by official letter in emergencies. The finance ministry's information centre presented national financial-sector indicators and how they are produced.

2026-09-06-papss-ceo-mike-ogbalu-intervi.summary: PAPSS chief executive Mike Ogbalu III told journalists in Lagos that the payment system is live in 30 countries with 24 central banks and settles in seven seconds on average. It stores encrypted transaction data but no personal or KYC records, attempted attacks more than doubled in six months, and links to China's and India's payment systems are targeted for early 2027.

2026-09-06-senegal-arm-enabel-market-inf.summary: Senegal's market regulation agency (ARM) and the Belgian development agency Enabel held a workshop in Dakar on 4 September 2026 on rebuilding the agricultural market information system. ARM's director-general, Babacar Sembène, said the new system should show production, harvests, stocks and areas of need so that price movements can be anticipated.

2026-09-06-seneweb-senegal-pylones-telec.summary: Senegalese MP Thierno Alassane Sall sent written questions to several ministers about telecoms masts being built close to homes, citing a mast under construction in Ngaparou, Mbour department. Residents say they complained to the regulator ARTP, the commune and the sub-prefect without reply. He asks whether safety and health impact studies were carried out and permits issued.

2026-09-06-sudan-bayan-civil-service-dig.summary: Columnist Al-Samani Awadallah, writing in Al-Hakim News on 6 September 2026, backs Sudan's Bayan digital platform for the civil service, which is to hold state employees' records from appointment to retirement, including promotions, transfers and leave. He presents it as a remedy for job manipulation and favouritism. The piece gives no launch date, cost or supplier.

2026-09-06-tanzaniainvest-e-delivery-150.summary: Tanzania's National Planning Commission has registered 150 development projects on its e-Delivery system since the platform launched on 1 July 2026, against a target of more than 500. Deputy Executive Secretary Sosthenes Kewe urged ministries in Dodoma to speed up registration, saying the system will help rank projects for the Vision 2050 plan.

2026-09-06-techtrends-remittance-startup.summary: Sending US$200 to sub-Saharan Africa cost an average of 8.46% in the third quarter of 2025, against a global average of 6.36%, according to World Bank figures cited by TechTrends Africa. Apps such as LemFi and Sendwave now run the London to Lagos corridor at about 2-3%, against around 7.8% in 2023.

2026-09-06-thisday-orogun-national-socia.summary: A ThisDay column by Weneso Orogun discusses Nigeria's Auditor-General's 2024 report, which found the National Cash Transfer Office paid N33.75 billion to 3,295,207 households in 35 states in 2023 without records reconciling recipients against the National Social Register. The report says office staff obstructed auditors' requests for the Remita statements.

2026-09-06-togo-atd-guide-architecture-e.summary: Togo's government enterprise-architecture guide, and with it the common interoperability framework it defines, is still a draft on the digital agency's own live status page: version 1.0, status Brouillon, with the version date, reviewer and review date fields blank and the revision table carrying only its column headers. The framework exists as a published normative text and has not been given force of law.

2026-09-06-ubc-ubos-mou-bugwe-tieng-adho.summary: The Uganda Bureau of Statistics signed memoranda of understanding with the Samia Bugwe and Tieng Adhola cultural institutions to collect and share community data, with a focus on births and deaths. The bureau will help the institutions set up statistics units and train staff. No cost or timetable is given.

2026-09-06-waemu-ai-strategy-tor-uemoa.summary: The West African Economic and Monetary Union's Commission invited expressions of interest from consultancies to draft a regional artificial intelligence strategy, funded from its 2026 budget. The firm is to review member states' AI data, strategies, infrastructure and skills and identify risks, including ethics, regulation and data security. The assignment runs 90 days; submissions closed on 11 September 2026.

2026-09-07-afrinic-afpub-2026-v6-001-dra.summary: A draft AFRINIC policy proposal would require any IPv4 request to come with an IPv6 request and a deployment plan, with IPv6 reachability targets rising from 25% at 12 months to 75% at 48 months. It cites Africa's IPv6 capability at 6%, against 44% worldwide, after 3 million IPv4 addresses were recovered under Soft Landing without a measurable gain in IPv6.

2026-09-07-afrinic-ipv6-for-ipv4-control.summary: A draft AFRINIC policy would tie any new IPv4 request to IPv6 eligibility, a deployment plan and percentage targets over 12, 24 and 48 months. The registry's own impact assessment says the evidence standard and the top-25 measurement method are not defined and warns smaller operators may face a disproportionate burden; AFRINIC 37 reached no consensus and the proposal returned to the mailing list.

2026-09-07-alchourouk-ai-in-vocational-t.summary: Tunisia’s employment minister said artificial intelligence is being added to vocational training, with twelve laboratories to be created in training centres from the new training year.

2026-09-07-angola-worldbank-test-project.summary: The World Bank's appraisal document for Angola's Tertiary Education, Science and Technology Project describes a US$150m IBRD loan and a US$50m Global Partnership for Education grant, approved in December 2023 as the first phase of a US$550m programme. The project became effective in December 2024 and runs to 2028.

2026-09-07-aps-algeria-second-meeting-un.summary: Algeria's digitalisation high commission and the domestic trade ministry held a second joint meeting on a unified digital mechanism for regulating the national market, taking the data sources themselves as the subject — how they are produced, updated and kept consistent.

2026-09-07-aps-cdp-seminaire-autorites-a.summary: Senegal's personal data protection commission (CDP) opened a seminar in Dakar for African and international data protection authorities, running from 7 to 10 September 2026. It is meant to strengthen cooperation and share experience on data governance, digital transformation and artificial intelligence.

2026-09-07-aps-parlementaire-senegalais-.summary: A Senegalese parliamentary committee chair called in Dakar for African data-protection authorities to be given stronger means of action.

2026-09-07-aslm-ebola-laboratory-systems.summary: A multi-country laboratory assessment completed before the current Ebola outbreak covered 26 countries, finding every one with a functioning surveillance system and core diagnostic capacity and 3,964 laboratories mapped across fourteen. It named digital interoperability between laboratories and surveillance platforms, alongside specimen referral, workforce surge and domestic financing, as the weak points — the seams the response has since had to improvise at.

2026-09-07-atu-apm27-3-draft-agenda-spec.summary: The African Telecommunications Union published the draft agenda and working-group schedule for the third African Preparatory Meeting for the 2027 World Radiocommunication Conference, held in Tunis on 7–11 September 2026 alongside the 11th African Spectrum Management Conference. The agenda covers the ITU's preparatory work plan, other regions' positions and the WRC-27 agenda items.

2026-09-07-au-archives-repository-projec.summary: The African Union Commission received a South African delegation in Addis Ababa on 7 September 2026 to restart the project to digitise the African Union's archives and build a common repository system. The delegation, led by an official of South Africa's African Renaissance and International Cooperation Fund, is to stay until 19 September 2026. No cost or timetable for the project is given.

2026-09-07-auc-itu-mou-digital-transform.summary: The African Union Commission and the International Telecommunication Union signed a memorandum of understanding in Geneva on 7 September 2026 setting a framework for cooperation on Africa's digital transformation. Priority areas include artificial intelligence, digital public infrastructure, skills, connectivity, cybersecurity, space technologies, regulation and standardisation. No funding commitment is stated.

2026-09-07-bfa-ecofin-video-verbalisatio.summary: Burkina Faso's video-verbalisation cameras recorded 19,910 road offences over August 2026, generating CFA146.559m in fines of which CFA16.1m had been recovered at the 4 September review. A motorised police brigade was created on 2 September specifically to trace drivers who evade the camera-issued fines.

2026-09-07-botswana-bera-bpc-tariff-cons.summary: Botswana Power Corporation's tariff application for 2026/27, put to consultation by the regulator BERA, seeks a 46% increase from 1 April 2026. BPC puts its revenue requirement at P9.585bn against current revenue of P6.108bn excluding subsidy, a gap of P3.477bn.

2026-09-07-burundi-iwacu-cam-protection-.summary: A ministerial ordinance of 7 February 2025 requires every Burundian adult and every household outside a health mutual to hold a Carte d'Assurance Maladie, which the revenue office has priced at 3,000 BIF. Iwacu's editorial welcomes the measure but recalls the card's troubled record since its creation in 1984.

2026-09-07-businessexplainer-oosthuysen-.summary: An industry argument that South Africa is not positioning itself as future-ready cites employer survey findings that about 55% of workers show little or no proficiency in mathematics or data skills, 52% of businesses find it difficult to hire anyone prepared for digital transformation and 70% rate workforce technology skills poor or very poor, against 118,500 unfilled ICT vacancies of which 36% are junior roles.

2026-09-07-businesstoday-abc-bank-papss-.summary: Kenya's African Banking Corporation (ABC Bank) has gone live on the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System, letting customers send and receive payments across 28 African countries. Customers can pay accounts at more than 190 participating banks, sending either in Kenyan shillings or in the recipient's currency.

2026-09-07-cadreco-umoa-mobile-money-202.summary: Mobile payments and transfers in the West African Monetary Union reached FCFA 164,169 billion in 2025, up 31.4 per cent, according to the UMOA Banking Commission's 2025 annual report. Electronic money accounts rose to 172.9 million, of which 60.6 million were active, and electronic money institutions posted a provisional net profit of FCFA 16.9 billion.

2026-09-07-capacity-telecom-egypt-red-se.summary: Telecom Egypt named the contractor for a 200km subsea cable between Sharm El Sheikh and Taba, extending its Red Sea festoon into a continuous Suez-to-Taba route designed for about 5 petabits per second.

2026-09-07-civ-aip-fenacci-observatoire-.summary: Four days after nationwide checks on electronic standardised invoicing began, Côte d'Ivoire's traders' federation created a National Observatory on Electronic Standardised Invoicing, announced at a press conference in Adjamé. The observatory has no published mandate, membership or reporting arrangement, and the federation's earlier demand that the checks be suspended is not withdrawn on the record.

2026-09-07-cmr-businessincameroon-cybast.summary: A United States firm plans US$75m, about FCFA 42.25bn, for a Douala data centre designed in part for artificial-intelligence workloads with dedicated power generation. The planning ministry describes it as an intention presented at the first bilateral economic forum rather than a commitment; the same vendor's Ivorian project was underwritten by a US$66.14m export-credit guarantee.

2026-09-07-cote-divoire-us-exim-cybastio.summary: The US Export-Import Bank's board approved a guarantee of about US$66.1m to Citibank on 21 August 2025 to finance Côte d'Ivoire's national data centre, with the finance ministry as borrower and Washington-based Cybastion as exporter. EXIM describes it as the first data centre it has backed in sub-Saharan Africa.

2026-09-07-digital-realty-nairobi-nbo2-d.summary: A second facility on the operator's Nairobi campus adds 6.4MW of capacity, opened alongside the retirement of the iColo brand in Kenya and Mozambique in favour of the parent's. The figure is critical IT load rather than delivered live load, and no occupancy or campus total is published.

2026-09-07-drc-qr-code-product-traceabil.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo's standards control office plans a national QR-code system letting consumers scan a product — medicines included — to verify its certification status, with consumer checks stated as opening within weeks and resting on 88 laboratories across 29 sites. No launch date, register or enforcement route is published.

2026-09-07-egypt-unhcr-mpca-pdm-report-2.summary: UNHCR gave multipurpose cash to an average of 24,335 refugee and asylum-seeker households in Egypt during 2024, paid every two months through Egypt Post offices, and raised transfer values by about 32% over the year. Its December survey reached 393 households, and 99% said the cash let them buy items or services they could not afford before.

2026-09-07-elmoudjahid-algerie-zones-hor.summary: An editorial in Algeria's El Moudjahid on 7 September 2026 states that areas without telecoms coverage are to be connected within 18 months, in an operation covering about 3,000 remote rural zones and funded entirely from the state budget. It gives no operator, cost or start date.

2026-09-07-eswatini-auditors-ai-inter-sa.summary: Eswatini's audit office hosted a week-long peer programme at which supreme audit institutions across the region weighed the use of artificial intelligence in government audit. No tool, pilot, audit methodology or procurement is named.

2026-09-07-eta-egypt-homepage.summary: The Egyptian Tax Authority's own portal carries the state of its digital systems: electronic invoicing with registration guidance and online training for businesses joining it, an e-receipt system defined as an electronic document proving business-to-consumer transactions, and value-added tax return automation. A consumer-incentive scheme rewarding shoppers for taking a receipt or invoice is in trial operation at five shopping malls.

2026-09-07-ethiopia-fayda-proof-of-ident.summary: The national identity programme's own page lists the 33 documents accepted as proof of identity for registration, from the local administration card and passport to birth, education, marriage and business records. The page carries no publication date of its own.

2026-09-07-falana-serap-n33-75bn-cash-tr.summary: The Auditor-General's 2024 report states that the government could not provide auditors with sufficient evidence that ₦33.75bn of cash transfers intended for more than 3.29 million vulnerable households reached genuine beneficiaries, the payment platform's statements not having been supplied. A rights lawyer has asked the financial crimes commission to investigate and a civil-society organisation puts over ₦78.8bn across social protection programmes as diverted, unaccounted for or irregularly spent.

2026-09-07-gab-agp-cgi-agents-communicat.summary: The Centre Gabonais de l'Innovation introduced about forty staff of the communication ministry to AI tools for administrative work on 7 September 2026. It is the first step of a programme meant to train 500 civil servants by December 2026 and 1,000 more in the first half of 2027.

2026-09-07-gabonactu-digitalisation-titr.summary: A Gabonese commentary places the digitalisation of transport titles and documents among the state's modernisation projects, and puts the open question as who governs it and whether local suppliers are used. No contracting authority, supplier, scope, cost or timetable for the project is on the record.

2026-09-07-gauteng-egovernment-annual-re.summary: The Gauteng provincial department's 2025/26 annual report records 96 public Wi-Fi hotspots offering up to 500MB of free internet a day, 33 e-services live, 99% provincial network uptime and 7,271 cameras on the provincial safety network. The figures are the department's own, with no audited outturn or prior-year comparison in the account.

2026-09-07-gdn-dpi-inclusivity-survey-de.summary: The Global Development Network has begun fieldwork on a five-country DPI Inclusivity Survey covering Sierra Leone and Ghana alongside Chile, Bangladesh and Indonesia, with partner teams at the Institute for Development and the University of Ghana. Running to April and engaging more than 5,000 households, it asks whether digital identity and digital payment systems leave people feeling more economically, socially and politically included, rather than measuring registration and access.

2026-09-07-gha-myjoyonline-5g-deployment.summary: Ghana expects to complete 5G spectrum assignment and begin deployment by December 2026, its communications minister said.

2026-09-07-gha-myjoyonline-digitisation-.summary: Ghana signed a contract to digitise 3.5 million public records held by the archives department, presented as records-management modernisation and better access to official information.

2026-09-07-gha-myjoyonline-mobile-data-p.summary: Ghana’s communications minister said households and businesses are getting more data for less money after government engagements with the mobile operators.

2026-09-07-gha-myjoyonline-mous-11-unive.summary: Ghana signed memoranda with eleven universities to embed digital certifications into degree and diploma programmes.

2026-09-07-gha-myjoyonline-one-million-c.summary: Ghana’s coders programme held 141,954 registered accounts and 27,782 actively engaged learners at the start of August.

2026-09-07-gha-myjoyonline-sam-george-ch.summary: Ghana’s communications minister was unanimously confirmed as the next chair of the African Union technical committee on communication and ICT, for two years.

2026-09-07-gha-myjoyonline-sovereign-vir.summary: Ghana is building a government-owned virtual meeting platform for secure high-level operations, the deputy chief of staff said.

2026-09-07-ghana-biometric-sim-verificat.summary: Ghana's communications minister said Parliament has passed the legislative instrument governing SIM registration and the biometric verification phase will be introduced before the end of 2026. The same account puts completion of the 2021–2023 exercise it replaces at 44.28% of subscribers.

2026-09-07-ghana-marrify-digital-marriag.summary: A privately operated platform launched in Accra on 28 August lets users search and verify registered marriage and divorce records drawn from the registrar-general's department, the courts, district assemblies and the Gazette. No data-sharing agreement, fee schedule, coverage figure or record count is published.

2026-09-07-ghana-nca-public-education-te.summary: Ghana's communications regulator took radio-frequency exposure messaging to traders, transport operators and commuters at Koforidua Central Market, after opposition to a mast at a lorry station. It is the consent side of a build the same week's ministerial account puts at about 6,000 sites short.

2026-09-07-ghana-sam-george-government-a.summary: Ghana's communications ministry gave a full public account of its January–August delivery, and the arithmetic is the interesting part: 141,954 registered accounts against 5,812 logged completions on the national coders programme, 8,578 fibre cuts projected for 2026 at roughly US$2,045 a repair, and a dig-once policy still awaiting Cabinet. It also records voice over LTE rising from about 7% of traffic to 22.43% and smartphone penetration at 71.8% in June 2026.

2026-09-07-ghana-seevcash-visa-card.summary: A Ghanaian remittance startup moving money from the United States to Ghana raised US$333,000 from a blockchain foundation's community fund, to launch an international payment card usable online and in stores. The commitment date is not stated in the account.

2026-09-07-ghana-unesco-ai-readiness-ass.summary: UNESCO has completed its AI Readiness Assessment for Ghana, one of 77 countries assessed, after three rounds of consultation convened by the communications ministry. The findings are meant to guide implementation of Ghana's national AI strategy.

2026-09-07-gitex-mint-africa-lagos-finan.summary: A financial-innovation platform was unveiled in Lagos with backing from governments and financial-sector regulators, its full debut deferred to the 2027 edition of the technology week. No participants, funding or programme of work is published with the announcement.

2026-09-07-gmb-standard-gamcel-9-digit-m.summary: Three Gambian operators moved to nine-digit mobile numbers at midnight, with the fourth to follow in a second phase on a reserved prefix, the regulator confirmed.

2026-09-07-gnb-ang-bissau-municipal-digi.summary: Bissau city council announced the launch of a modernisation and digital transformation programme for the institution, on a plan approved at its first strategic retreat.

2026-09-07-graphic-ghana-customs-valuati.summary: An industry commentary traces Ghanaian customs valuation from manual assessment through pre-shipment inspection to an artificial-intelligence-assisted future.

2026-09-07-graphic-ghana-hunger-project-.summary: A development organisation opened an ICT centre at a rural development centre in Ghana’s Eastern Region.

2026-09-07-guinea-bissau-baboudottir-ado.summary: A University of Iceland doctoral thesis on inequality among adolescents in Bissau draws on a survey of 2,039 pupils aged 14 to 19 in 16 schools, followed by interviews and focus groups. It finds parental education and income decide access to private schooling, and that access to computers and the internet is limited, more so for girls and public-school pupils.

2026-09-07-hespress-adaptvote-blockchain.summary: Researchers at Mohammed I University in Oujda and Abdelmalek Essaâdi University in Tétouan tested AdaptVote, an e-voting model combining facial recognition and blockchain, with 300 people in Nador over 12 hours. The network was available for only 35% of the trial; 95.7% passed identity checks first time and voting took 2.1 minutes against 4.5 on paper. It is a research platform, not an official system.

2026-09-07-highstreetjournal-ghana-stran.summary: Ghana's communications minister, Samuel Nartey George, said on 7 September 2026 that equipment from earlier rural connectivity projects, installed at sites with no line of sight or backhaul, is being relocated. He also said AirtelTigo has been given spectrum, a provisional licence and access to parts of the GIFEC core network after its own licences expired.

2026-09-07-independentnews-eswatini-ers-.summary: Eswatini’s national business body backed the revenue service’s move to electronic invoicing while asking that it be made affordable and workable across existing technologies before national rollout.

2026-09-07-ippmedia-vodacom-bridge-for-b.summary: The leading Tanzanian mobile operator entered a three-year partnership with a global entrepreneurship network to reach 1,000 entrepreneurs and 40 ventures, with a first cohort of entrepreneur-support organisations due in October 2026. No commitment amount is stated, so the agreement carries targets and no measurable resource behind them.

2026-09-07-isoc-live-afigf-road-to-ghana.summary: The Africa Internet Governance Forum secretariat announced an online session on 9 September 2026, the first in a series ahead of the 15th Africa IGF, which Ghana hosts in Accra on 2-5 November 2026. The session covers how national, regional and youth IGF initiatives can implement the WSIS+20 outcomes and the Global Digital Compact in Africa.

2026-09-07-ken-government-welcomes-digit.summary: Kenya's ICT principal secretary John Tanui told investors the government is working on policy to keep the country attractive, speaking at the launch of the NBO2 data centre in Nairobi, where Icolo rebranded as Digital Realty. The company's Africa managing director Marcel Louw said it runs more than 17 data centres in Africa, with over 200 megawatts of capacity going live.

2026-09-07-kenya-cofek-high-court-quashe.summary: Kenya's High Court quashed as unconstitutional the Attorney-General's advisory opinion of 1 October 2024 clearing a former Communications Authority chairperson of conflict of interest over two Digital Superhighway tenders awarded to Nightigale, according to the Consumers Federation of Kenya, which brought the case. The court did not void the contracts, and said the anti-corruption commission is the forum to investigate.

2026-09-07-kenya-ict-authority-kdeap-cyb.summary: Kenya's technology authority put the National Information Security Framework's audit, risk-management and certification mechanisms to a Nairobi stakeholder workshop, to establish whether they are practical for national implementation ahead of certifying critical information infrastructure. The framework text and the certification criteria are not published.

2026-09-07-ktpress-east-africa-universit.summary: Rwanda's Education Minister Joseph Nsengimana opened the 15th East African Higher Education Quality Assurance Network forum in Kigali on 7 September 2026, saying the region must rethink how it defines and assures quality in higher education as artificial intelligence changes teaching and work. The Inter-University Council for East Africa said a regional AI network has been launched.

2026-09-07-lanation-benin-indabax-langue.summary: The Beninese edition of a continental machine-learning meeting opens a track on large language models and low-resource African language corpora, at Cotonou from 10 to 12 September.

2026-09-07-lanation-djibouti-premier-con.summary: Djibouti's ministry for the digital economy ran the country's first national AI prototyping competition ahead of its first National Forum on Artificial Intelligence. Of 126 applications, 56 were eligible and 17 reached the pitch stage; the winner, Tech Genius, received 2,000,000 Djibouti francs, with 1,000,000 and 500,000 francs for second and third place.

2026-09-07-lby-lana-qarar-449-2026-tanzi.summary: Libya's economy and trade minister Suhail Bushiha issued Decision No. 449 of 2026 on 7 September, banning the import of goods for trade outside banking channels from 30 September 2026. Customs may release commercial shipments only once banking, trade and customs requirements are met and the shipment's true value is documented; licensed individual traders get an annual import ceiling.

2026-09-07-lby-zero-cash-initiative-halt.summary: Libya’s banking sector development forum said it has stopped pursuing its cashless initiative in the form submitted to the central bank, because the executive framework it needed was never issued.

2026-09-07-liberia-ul-ebu-tripartite-mou.summary: A tripartite memorandum signed on 27 August has a foreign online university covering 97% of online tuition for more than 200 students of the national university, with three smart classrooms due in 2027. No commitment amount is stated.

2026-09-07-libya-cbl-governor-financial-.summary: Libya's central bank governor launched a link to the Arab regional payments platform, a study track on a central bank digital currency and stablecoins, and a cyber-skills programme, and put a pilot for accession to China's cross-border interbank system at early 2027. None of the four carries an instrument, budget, participant list or delivery date.

2026-09-07-linfodrome-cepici-e-licences.summary: Côte d’Ivoire’s investment promotion centre is taking investor licences, permits and authorisations onto an online platform, with ministry focal points trained to keep it current.

2026-09-07-mtn-ghana-commits-1-1bn-netwo.summary: The dominant Ghanaian operator's US$1.1bn three-year commitment is restated against the site build behind it: 800 new cell sites of which 180 are already active, and a second operator targeting 2,698 sites in 2026. The communications minister dates the regulator board's removal of wholesale 5G exclusivity to 15 July 2026.

2026-09-07-myjoyonline-accra-africa-inte.summary: Ghana is to host the fifteenth Africa Internet Governance Forum in Accra in November.

2026-09-07-myjoyonline-ghana-cert-gh-336.summary: Ghana’s national incident response team handled 3,363 cybersecurity incidents in the first half of 2026.

2026-09-07-myjoyonline-ghana-dpc-regulat.summary: Ghana’s data protection commission increased its regulatory activity by 51.5 per cent in the first half of 2026, alongside a rise in data-controller registrations.

2026-09-07-myjoyonline-ghana-ministry-st.summary: Ghana’s communications minister directed his ministry’s senior staff and those of its agencies to enrol on the national coders programme by the end of the week.

2026-09-07-namibia-eta-2019-accreditatio.summary: CRAN's regulations on the accreditation of security products, services and certification service providers under the Electronic Transactions Act of 2019 came into force on 15 June 2026. They set out which products and services need accreditation and how providers apply, and are the instrument under which the home affairs ministry later became Namibia's first accredited certification service provider.

2026-09-07-namibian-nampost-social-grant.summary: Retired Namibian MP Elifas Dingara called on the government and Namibia Post Limited, which pays social cash grants, to address failures in the grant payment system. He said elderly beneficiaries had travelled long distances and queued only to find their names missing at payment points. He asked for answers on missing beneficiaries, delayed and unpaid grants, and complaint timeframes.

2026-09-07-nassit-mobile-app-pensioners-.summary: Sierra Leone's social security trust is to launch a self-service application for pensioners and contributors, with a short-code fallback for feature phones, biometric verification and integration with the three mobile-money services. It is announced rather than launched, with no date published.

2026-09-07-newvision-ucc-explains-intern.summary: Uganda’s communications regulator published the text of its suspension directive: public internet, new SIM sales and outbound data roaming stopped, mobile VPNs disabled, a whitelisted exclusion list from referral hospitals to railway signalling, and restoration only on written notice.

2026-09-07-nigeria-efina-a2f-2023-survey.summary: EFInA's eighth Access to Financial Services in Nigeria survey, based on 26,930 interviews, puts formal financial inclusion at 64% in 2023, against 57% in 2020. The full report was published in July 2024.

2026-09-07-nigeria-nin-62-5-million-gap-.summary: Nigeria had issued national identification numbers to 117.5 million people out of 134.6 million enrolments at 30 June 2026, against a target of 180 million by December. Closing the gap would need monthly enrolment to rise from 1.5–1.8 million to about 7.4 million.

2026-09-07-nigeria-police-vigilant-app-f.summary: The police fraud-reporting app launched on 1 September is the fourth police reporting platform in a decade, and it arrives over a cybercrime centre already logging about 146,000 reports and about ₦58bn in recovered assets. Nothing published says how the new channel routes against the centre already running, or what became of the earlier platforms.

2026-09-07-nigeria-worldbank-id4d-isr-au.summary: The World Bank's August 2026 status report on Nigeria's digital ID project counts 117.5m people with a National Identification Number at 30 June 2026, against a target of 180m by December. Monthly enrolment would have to rise from under 2m to about 7.4m to reach it, and the NIMS 2.0 integrator contract was due to be signed by end-July.

2026-09-07-nigeriaworks-papss-ogbalu-bri.summary: Mike Ogbalu, chief executive of the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System launched by Afreximbank in 2022, briefed journalists in Lagos on its move to a second strategic plan from 2027. He said Afreximbank's settlement guarantee has grown from $500 million to $3 billion, that 15 central bank governors sit on its governing council, and that PAPSS has launched a currency marketplace and a card scheme.

2026-09-07-nilepost-mpigi-national-id-de.summary: Residents of a Ugandan district report waiting more than a year for identity cards, making repeated trips to registration centres and losing access to services tied to the number.

2026-09-07-nilepost-nira-national-id-exp.summary: Uganda’s identity authority is to hold a national ID expo, with millions still outside the register and the number framed as the gateway to services.

2026-09-07-nilepost-ura-nin-replace-tin.summary: Uganda's revenue authority says the move from taxpayer numbers to national identification numbers will not automatically make every citizen a taxpayer, the purpose being a single more secure identifier for government services and more accurate taxpayer records. It follows the finance minister's statement four days earlier that the two numbers must be interoperable rather than one replacing the other.

2026-09-07-novojornal-paga3-standard-ban.summary: The founders of an Angolan payments startup accuse a commercial bank of using information shared in a pilot to build a similar product; the case has run about a year and the bank calls the claim abusive.

2026-09-07-openserve-third-fibre-route-s.summary: The state-affiliated wholesale operator completed a third long-haul fibre route from Cape Town to Pretoria via Springbok and Mahikeng, built so the network stays up through major breaks. It sits inside a wholesale network of about 180,000km carrying just under R3bn of capital expenditure a year.

2026-09-07-papss-ai-fraud-detection-cryp.summary: The continental payment system's chief executive put transaction volume growth above 1,000% and value growth at 125% since 2022, with settlement averaging seven seconds against an original 120-second design target and an artificial-intelligence layer screening for suspicious activity before value is released. He declined to give the absolute volume and value, saying disclosure is still being agreed and a report will follow in early 2027.

2026-09-07-papss-canex-creative-economy-.summary: The continental payment system is being extended towards creative-economy payments, with third-party rails for royalties and licensing described and a Lagos creative-industries event in November set as the pilot occasion. No design, timetable or participant list is published.

2026-09-07-sa-internet-costs-competition.summary: Wired internet prices rose 3.5% and wireless 4.1% over the first half of 2026, both ahead of cumulative headline inflation of 3.8%, on the competition authority's cost-of-living report. Over the six years to July 2026 the two rose 18.6% and 6.4% against headline inflation of 36%, so the recent move reverses the longer pattern for a service the authority treats as essential.

2026-09-07-saps-ai-generated-police-imag.summary: Provincial police in the Free State have warned that creating and sharing artificial-intelligence face-swap images of oneself in police uniform can breach section 68 of the South African Police Service Act 68 of 1995, which makes impersonating a police official an offence. It is an existing statute asserted against a new practice, not a new rule.

2026-09-07-shabait-eritrea-afro-verse-vi.summary: An Eritrean project is rendering traditional housing, household objects and landscape in three-dimensional virtual reality.

2026-09-07-socialnetlink-cdp-senegal-eco.summary: The head of Senegal’s data protection commission told a Dakar workshop that personal-data protection is a condition of digital transformation rather than an obstacle to innovation.

2026-09-07-south-africa-ai-inclusion-sum.summary: A deputy minister framed artificial-intelligence inclusion as three frontiers — connection, capability and command — arguing that youth, women and people with disabilities should build and shape the technology rather than only use it, at a first national summit on youth, artificial intelligence and the future of work. No programme, budget or date accompanies the framing.

2026-09-07-south-africa-dbsa-npc-digital.summary: A study by the DBSA and the National Planning Commission estimates that universal high-speed broadband in South Africa will need R108bn to R142bn of additional investment by 2035, in 2025 terms. An annex surveys the data-centre market, which it puts at nearly 500MW of potential IT load, concentrated in Gauteng.

2026-09-07-suna-sudan-animal-resources-m.summary: Sudan’s animal resources and fisheries ministry launched an official website for producers, breeders and investors, presented as a step in digital transformation.

2026-09-07-tanzania-ict-competency-stand.summary: Tanzania's education ministry and UNESCO's Dar es Salaam office set out ICT competency standards for teachers in 2015, adapting UNESCO's global framework across its six modules and two knowledge stages. The 2015 text revised a first version piloted in 2011 with World Bank and GESCI support, and its annexes add an implementation strategy for pre- and in-service teachers.

2026-09-07-techafricanews-nitda-students.summary: Nigeria’s technology development agency and a state startup agency finished a coding and emerging-technology bootcamp for primary and secondary pupils.

2026-09-07-techafricanews-samsung-wallet.summary: A QR-code payment feature was added to a handset maker’s wallet application for South African users.

2026-09-07-techafricanews-ttcl-tanzania-.summary: The state operator scored highest on the regulator’s quality measurement for the quarter to June 2026, at 98.1 per cent against 97.7 and 97.1 for the two larger operators.

2026-09-07-thecitizen-bot-creditinfo-loc.summary: Tanzania’s central bank backed a credit bureau’s locally operated fraud detection, identity verification and know-your-customer services for lenders.

2026-09-07-thisday-nerd-academic-reposit.summary: Nigeria’s education repository passed 400,000 theses and dissertations and 115,000 verified credentials.

2026-09-07-thisday-nitda-national-innova.summary: Hub operators, founders and investors met in Lagos to validate Nigeria’s draft standard framework for national innovation hubs.

2026-09-07-timeslive-icasa-ott-inquiry-n.summary: South Africa’s communications regulator said it will inquire into the effect of over-the-top services on consumers, against licensed broadcasters losing audience and revenue.

2026-09-07-togopresse-alphabetisation-nu.summary: Togo’s solidarity minister set out a literacy initiative and digital tools as the country’s route to reducing illiteracy, ahead of International Literacy Day.

2026-09-07-wearetech-3c-coding-school-eg.summary: An Egyptian coding school raised US$3 million to expand, entering Saudi Arabia and building a virtual assistant that paces learning to each child; it says it has reached 120,000 pupils.

2026-09-07-wearetech-africinvest-spoon-c.summary: A pan-African investment fund took a minority stake in a Mauritian digital transformation firm, with no sum disclosed.

2026-09-07-wearetech-uber-indemnisation-.summary: Uber is paying active Nigerian drivers about N40,000, over US$30, on ending its operations in the country; the drivers move to other booking apps.

2026-09-07-who-regional-health-data-hub-.summary: The regional health data hub launched at Addis Ababa carries 53 datasets and 7,965 indicators, about 65% of them ingested against a target of 80% by the end of 2026, and its governance framework is still in development. It is intended to bring maternal, newborn, child and adolescent health together with noncommunicable disease data across all 47 member states of the region.

2026-09-07-xaf-afrinic-pdp-wg-guidelines.summary: A second draft of a proposal to rewrite the rules of AFRINIC's policy development working group was submitted on 7 September 2026 and is under discussion. The authors say the registry's recent lack of a board quorum left adopted policies unratified and committees unrenewed; the draft would need changes to AFRINIC's bylaws.

2026-09-07-youm7-egypt-idsc-ai-awareness.summary: An Egyptian government survey puts those who have heard of artificial-intelligence applications at 65 per cent in 2026 against 22 per cent in 2023, with work the leading use.

2026-09-07-youm7-egypt-telecom-sector-gr.summary: Egypt’s communications minister said the telecommunications and technology sector grew 24.3 per cent in the fourth quarter of the 2023-24 financial year, the highest rate in its history.

2026-09-07-zambia-npki-digital-trust.summary: The communications regulator has operationalised the National Digital Trust Anchor as national root certification authority, under the electronic communications and transactions statute. The framework is to issue and verify the certificates and signatures that establish who a person or organisation is online. No certificate count, list of subordinate authorities or accreditation route accompanies the launch.

2026-09-07-zwe-potraz-dtprp-call-for-pol.summary: Zimbabwe's telecommunications regulator, POTRAZ, with the Research Council of Zimbabwe and the Scientific and Industrial Research and Development Centre, invited policy research proposals under a National Digital Technologies Policy Research Programme. Priority areas include AI governance, data governance and sovereignty, platform regulation, connectivity and innovation policy; proposals close on 3 October 2026 and applicants are notified by 23 October.

2026-09-08-africanenda-central-bank-paym.summary: Notes from a central bank payments conference in Istanbul argue for rethinking how instant payment systems are regulated.

2026-09-08-ago-angop-bai-bank-of-china.summary: Angola's Banco Angolano de Investimentos (BAI) signed a memorandum of understanding with Bank of China in Xiamen on 8 September 2026 on renminbi clearing. It provides for an RMB clearing account and for BAI's indirect membership of China's Cross-Border Interbank Payment System (CIPS) through Bank of China. No sum is stated.

2026-09-08-ago-mercado-bai-renminbi.summary: Angola's Banco Angolano de Investimentos signed a memorandum with Bank of China's Luanda branch on 8 September 2026 to open a renminbi clearing account and develop renminbi settlement services. Bank of China will support BAI's indirect access to China's Cross-Border Interbank Payment System, aimed at Angolan firms trading with China. No value, start date or expected volume is given.

2026-09-08-ami-onm-ai-agro-hydro-early-w.summary: Mauritania's national meteorological office ran a two-day workshop in Nouakchott from 8 September 2026 for regional administrators and its own staff on an AI-based agricultural and hydrological early warning system using the AGRIFEMIA platform. The training aims to improve forecasting of climate risks to agriculture and water resources.

2026-09-08-anacao-cabo-verde-sir-delegac.summary: Cabo Verde's prime minister delegated coordination of the intelligence service SIR to the interior minister by despacho no. 15/2026 in the Boletim Oficial. The opposition MpD calls it unconstitutional, arguing the SIR law gives the prime minister exclusive authority, and says it will challenge it. The government cites its general power of delegation; President José Maria Neves declined to comment publicly.

2026-09-08-au-commissioner-ai-for-good-g.summary: The African Union's commissioner for infrastructure and energy took a seat among more than 40 founding members of the ITU-convened AI for Good Global Commission, meeting for the first time in Geneva. The commission, co-chaired by Rwanda's president, has named closing the divide that leaves an estimated 2.2 billion people offline as a principal priority.

2026-09-08-bog-notice-29-unlicensed-digi.summary: The Bank of Ghana named 20 more unlicensed mobile loan apps on 8 September 2026, including CreditGo, Cash Cedi, Sika Credit and Zoom Advance, five weeks after listing a different 20 in August. It said they breach its September 2025 directive on digital credit providers and warned banks and payment service providers not to process their transactions.

2026-09-08-caribou-dpi-adoption-governan.summary: Two development organisations argue that digital public infrastructure fails on governance rather than technology, drawing on Ethiopian and South African examples.

2026-09-08-cipesa-uganda-digital-economy.summary: A rights organisation maps Uganda’s digital-economy growth against the gaps it finds in biometric-data, artificial-intelligence and platform-work safeguards.

2026-09-08-cisa-china-ai-distillation-ca.summary: US security agencies issued a joint advisory alleging that China-based AI companies are extracting proprietary capabilities from US frontier models through industrial-scale knowledge distillation, described as the core of their development strategy rather than a supplement, and recommending mitigations.

2026-09-08-citinewsroom-ghana-npp-rural-.summary: Ghana's opposition gave the communications ministry 30 days to publish a full status report on the Rural Telephony and Digital Inclusion Project, asking for sites constructed, connected, operational and built but out of service. The project runs on a EUR155 million China Eximbank facility against a target of 2,016 sites, with 1,961 stated as constructed at the January 2025 handover and 46 disputed as unconnectable.

2026-09-08-citizen-anc-candidate-lists-u.summary: South Africa's ANC secretary-general Fikile Mbalula said on 8 September 2026 that some branch-submitted candidate lists for the local government elections carried inaccurate and unverified identity numbers. The party has opened an internal review of its nomination process, and has gone to the Electoral Court over the Electoral Commission's refusal to reopen list submissions.

2026-09-08-citizenza-gauteng-wifi-digita.summary: Gauteng’s e-government department reported progress on free public Wi-Fi sites, digital-skills training and smart-safety technology across the province.

2026-09-08-cmr-leconomie-plan-directeur-.summary: The African Development Bank awarded the NC Consulting/Eyra International grouping a six-month, FCFA 241.36 million contract to draw up Cameroon's master plan for digitalising public procurement. The plan is to cover the whole procurement cycle and the gaps that limit use of COLEPS, the e-procurement platform run since 2018. No award date is given.

2026-09-08-connectingafrica-gulf-crisis-.summary: Instability in the Gulf has put redundancy, data-sovereignty rules for cross-border failover and the physical resilience of data centres back at the centre of cloud investment decisions, the piece argues, with availability zones in small coastal states hard to separate and maritime insurance costs for cable-laying vessels spiking. It reads the disruption as an opening for African markets.

2026-09-08-cpv-expressodasilhas-correios.summary: Cabo Verde's postal operator, Correios de Cabo Verde, warned on 8 September 2026 that people impersonating its staff are sending messages asking recipients to click a link named 'Correios.ink/cv'. The operator said the link is not its own and advised the public not to click it or share personal or banking details.

2026-09-08-dji-lobservateur-strategie-na.summary: Djibouti presented its first national artificial intelligence strategy for 2026–2030, built on six areas: data and AI governance, cybersecurity, training, research, innovation and inclusion. A readiness assessment carried out with UNESCO rates the country 'emerging', at about 24.5 out of 100, against an ICT development index of 61.6. No budget is given.

2026-09-08-dza-anp-algerie-telecom-conve.summary: Algérie Télécom signed agreements in Niamey on 8 September 2026 with Niger Télécom and Niger's telecoms and postal school ESCEP-Niger. They cover a skills centre at the school, training for Niger Télécom staff, and donated transmission equipment for a fibre link between Ngezam and Agadez with an initial 100 Gbps capacity on Niger Télécom's national backbone. No value is given.

2026-09-08-dza-elwatan-dme-deadline-15-n.summary: Algeria's health minister has set 15 November 2026 as a final deadline for every public health establishment to switch on the electronic medical record, built on a single national patient number. Each facility must name a lead and report progress weekly; extra funding was allocated but not quantified.

2026-09-08-dza-mesrs-premiere-reunion-co.summary: Algeria's higher education minister, Kamel Baddari, chaired an inter-ministerial meeting on 8 September 2026 on implementing the national artificial intelligence strategy, following a first session on 5 August. It created five thematic commissions, approved a national research centre for AI and data, planned an AI-based tax administration system and set a target of 50,000 AI specialists trained by 2030.

2026-09-08-elmoudjahid-algerie-a-l-ere-d.summary: An El Moudjahid editorial on Algeria's Algérie Numérique 2030 strategy cites the opening of the national digital services centre at Mohammadia, with Tier III data centres, and ministries joining the Dzair Digital Services portal. It lists a product-traceability system in commerce, electronic medical records in hospitals, a national agricultural information system and the Takwin vocational training platform.

2026-09-08-etradeforall-koafec-ministeri.summary: The African Development Bank co-hosts the 8th Korea-Africa Economic Cooperation ministerial conference in Seoul from 8 to 11 September 2026, with Korea's finance ministry and Export-Import Bank. The theme is harnessing artificial intelligence and digital infrastructure for Africa's transformation, and African finance ministers attend. No financing commitments are stated.

2026-09-08-fraternite-dividende-demograp.summary: Benin and seven other West African states (Burkina Faso, Côte d'Ivoire, Guinea, Mali, Niger, Senegal and Togo) are testing a platform to monitor progress on the demographic dividend at a meeting in Abidjan from 7 to 9 September 2026. The tool aims to harmonise indicators against African Union commitments on health, education, jobs and governance before wider rollout.

2026-09-08-gab-gabonreview-aninf-900000-.summary: More than 900,000 intrusion alerts were recorded in Gabon over 60 days, some rated very critical, after several attacks on national bodies. Digital economy minister Mark-Alexandre Doumba said on 7 September 2026 that the government had raised its vigilance level and called on administrations, firms and citizens to treat cybersecurity as a permanent duty.

2026-09-08-gha-myjoyonline-npp-challenge.summary: Ghana's opposition New Patriotic Party said on 8 September 2026 that the Ghana Rural Telephony and Digital Inclusion Project began in 2020, financed by a EUR155 million China EXIM Bank facility, and left 1,961 sites built by January 2025. It called on the communications ministry and GIFEC to publish a full status report on the project within 30 days.

2026-09-08-gha-theoverseer-nhia-digital-.summary: Ghana's National Health Insurance Authority said all scheme claims are now processed electronically and a national digital health platform is running in 502 facilities across eight regions. Chief executive Victor Asare Bampoe said patients' visits are tied to one-time attendance codes, biometric checks are used in busy facilities, and data analytics flag duplicate claims. Active membership reached 70% in August 2026 against an 80% end-year target.

2026-09-08-gnb-inm-nova-estacao-climsa-p.summary: Guinea-Bissau's meteorological institute installed a CLIMSA/PUMA2025 satellite receiving station between 21 and 25 August 2026, supplied by the African Union with EU support. It receives Meteosat Third Generation imagery in near real time, at intervals of up to ten minutes and 1 km resolution.

2026-09-08-govstack-mkulima-bora-kenya-a.summary: Kenya is piloting a digital agricultural marketplace across five Rift Valley counties, built on reusable components and open standards, with identity-verified onboarding and more than a thousand users.

2026-09-08-graphic-ghana-fibre-cuts-grid.summary: Ghana’s communications minister said fibre cuts and an unstable power grid are causing prolonged outages and undermining network quality.

2026-09-08-itweb-multichoice-piracy-regu.summary: A South African broadcaster called for stronger rules against pirate streaming, its chief executive telling a briefing that technology alone cannot stop unauthorised distribution.

2026-09-08-journaldesnations-ceeac-cadre.summary: Experts from member states of the Economic Community of Central African States met in Douala, Cameroon, from 31 August to 4 September 2026 to draft a common framework for cross-border data governance. They reviewed countries' readiness and worked to harmonise technical contributions; GIZ, AUDA-NEPAD, UNECA and the African Union Commission were involved.

2026-09-08-ken-digital-realty-nbo2-data-.summary: Digital Realty opened its Nairobi Two (NBO2) data centre in Karen, adding 6.4 MW to its Nairobi campus, which now has more than 14 MW of IT power over 34,000 square metres. NBO2 has six data halls. The launch also marked the rebranding of icolo to Digital Realty; the source's date for the event is inconsistent.

2026-09-08-ken-odpc-guidance-notes-cross.summary: Kenya's Office of the Data Protection Commissioner published Guidance Notes for Cross-border Data Transfers in September 2026, with a foreword by Data Commissioner Immaculate Kassait. The 63-page document includes a compliance checklist, an application form for binding corporate rules and standard clauses for controller-to-controller and controller-to-processor transfers. It prints no issue date.

2026-09-08-kictanet-south-sudan-audpf-da.summary: The African Union Commission, AUDA-NEPAD, GIZ and KICTANet convened a three-day workshop in Juba from 8 to 10 September on domesticating the African Union Data Policy Framework in South Sudan. This is a forward notice of the convening; no outcome or workplan is on record.

2026-09-08-lanation-fongbe-ia-donnees-la.summary: Benin's 'J'aime Ma Langue' project, run by the state digital agency ASIN with the Institute for Inclusive Digital Africa, collected 700 hours of Fongbe speech from 2,400 contributors in more than 20 localities to train AI in Beninese languages, reported on 8 September 2026. ASIN paid contributors more than 5.8m CFA francs. The article asks how consent, reuse and access to the data will be governed.

2026-09-08-lbr-nir-oesd-digital-id-conce.summary: Liberia's US$54.7 million concession with Austria's OeSD International to rebuild the national identification system has been signed but cannot be implemented until the legislature ratifies it, National Identification Registry director Andrew Peters said. The project covers biometric enrolment and deduplication, digital and physical credentials and a digital identity platform. No signature date is given.

2026-09-08-lbr-west-african-government-f.summary: A named analyst's column in the Liberian Observer contrasts Kenya's Government Vehicle Management System, announced on 6 August 2026 by head of public service Felix Koskei to track every state vehicle's driver, fuel, mileage and maintenance, with Liberia's handover of 56 untracked vehicles and motorbikes to agriculture officers.

2026-09-08-lby-north-africa-bank-alipay-.summary: A privately owned Libyan bank said it will launch a direct mobile payment service to China, capped at US$5,000 a transaction and US$50,000 a year.

2026-09-08-lefaso-bclcc-studio-sensibili.summary: Burkina Faso's central anti-cybercrime brigade, the BCLCC, has set up an audiovisual studio to produce public awareness content on online risks. Short videos will debunk false information and explain how to verify it, and other content will cover protecting personal data and accounts. No cost or launch date is given.

2026-09-08-lequotidien-bankily-digital-p.summary: A commentary in Le Quotidien de Nouakchott defends Bankily, the mobile banking app Banque Populaire de Mauritanie launched in 2020, after complaints about a faulty update that was temporarily rolled back. Citing the central bank's 2025 annual report, it says Bankily handles about 1.1 million transactions a day, nearly 80% of bank-wallet transactions by number and 73.5% by value.

2026-09-08-lequotidien-education-inspect.summary: Mauritania's Ministry of Education opened a ten-day training course on 8 September 2026 for 20 secondary-school inspectors in documentation, archiving, librarianship and electronic document management. Secretary-general Sedfi Sidi Mohamed called for a modern documentation centre in the secondary inspectorate to store, classify and digitise its records.

2026-09-08-lesoleil-rentree-numerique-so.summary: A Senegalese daily's digital-season piece sets out Africa's technological sovereignty problem: dependence on foreign infrastructure, platforms and cloud services against the cost of building domestic alternatives. It is commentary rather than a record of any instrument.

2026-09-08-mar-haddad-pegasus-sanchez-cl.summary: A Moroccan academic and politician rejected as overstated the July 2026 consortium findings tying Moroccan bodies to the compromise of the Spanish prime minister’s phone.

2026-09-08-mar-hespress-hijaoui-pegasus-.summary: A Moroccan analysis asks why Spanish prosecutors have taken no action against a former intelligence officer since 2010, and whether the spyware row now reopens that file.

2026-09-08-mar-mmsp-instituts-jazari-ass.summary: Morocco's four JAZARI artificial intelligence institutes held their general assemblies in Rabat on 8 September 2026, chaired by the digital transition minister, Amal El Fallah Seghrouchni. Their founding conventions were approved in the Bulletin officiel in August 2026. JAZARI ROOT covers digital infrastructure, data centres, computing and national AI capability; the others cover education, industry and smart cities.

2026-09-08-mar-mmsp-maroc-ia-2030-etat-a.summary: Morocco's minister for digital transition, Amal El Fallah Seghrouchni, chaired a review in Rabat on 8 September 2026 of the Maroc pour l'intelligence artificielle 2030 roadmap. Its targets are 100 billion dirhams added to GDP, 50,000 jobs and 200,000 certified people by 2030; progress was reported on sovereign cloud and data centres, a Data Factory, a Software Factory and a shared AI platform.

2026-09-08-maroc-ia-2030-avancees-presen.summary: Morocco's digital transition ministry presented the main advances of the Maroc IA 2030 roadmap in Rabat, framing it as the move from design into implementation. The minister-delegate said the national AI conference had been the founding stage and that the AI Made in Morocco roadmap now enters a phase of concrete delivery.

2026-09-08-maspero-vodafone-elsewedy-cas.summary: Egypt’s communications minister attended a Cairo signing at which three companies undertook to establish a large data centre venture and the country’s first sovereign artificial-intelligence data centre.

2026-09-08-mdg-newsmada-paositra-pilote-.summary: Madagascar's microfinance institution Paositra Finances launched a scheme at Ankatso letting 1,400 master's students at the universities of Antananarivo and Fianarantsoa buy laptops on 12-month credit. Students pay a 20% deposit of about 210,000 ariary, then 75,000 ariary a month. The scheme draws on part of the World Bank-financed DECIM digital and energy connectivity project.

2026-09-08-mdg-tiatanindrazana-mndpt-sta.summary: Madagascar's digital development and telecoms ministry obtained 300 Starlink kits with free internet service under a cooperation with Starlink, reported on 8 September 2026, to connect remote areas. It follows free internet installed at the main public universities. No duration or cost of the free service is given.

2026-09-08-moz-brasil247-atdi-portal-uni.summary: An official of Mozambique's Agency for Digital Transformation and Innovation (ATDI), set up in March 2026, said 23 million of the country's 35 million people are unidentified and only about 200,000 of some 2 million annual births are registered. He said the single public services portal already offers 21 services, including identity cards, driving licences and passports.

2026-09-08-mwi-nrb-public-statement-nzik.summary: Malawi's National Registration Bureau announced that it would launch the Nzika Digital ID Wallet on 16 September 2026 at the Bingu International Convention Centre in Lilongwe, with Homeland Security Minister Peter Mukhito presiding. The bureau says the wallet adds a digital ID to the physical card and will cut printing costs and the time taken to obtain an ID.

2026-09-08-mwi-nyasatimes-macra-social-m.summary: The Malawi Communications Regulatory Authority installed a social media monitoring system in January 2025 under a $1.5 million contract awarded to Hashcom Ghana Limited 15 days earlier. More than a year on, no published document shows whether it ran during the September 2025 election, what data it collected or who had access. MACRA declined to comment pending an audit.

2026-09-08-nam-disability-grant-system-d.summary: Namibia is putting new guidelines and digital systems behind the medical assessment of persons with disabilities and their access to social grants.

2026-09-08-nam-healthpolicywatch-us-hiv-.summary: The United States will stop funding Namibia's HIV programme after 2027, providing $45m for fiscal 2027 for transition, after Namibia rejected US terms for sharing health data and pathogen information. Namibia has received about $1.1bn from PEPFAR over 22 years and already funds most treatment for around 220,000 people. It said the US terms conflict with constitutional privacy rights and its sovereignty over biological resources.

2026-09-08-namibian-mohss-digital-disabi.summary: Namibia's health ministry has launched a digital disability assessment system. On 8 September 2026 the Namibian Organisation of Youth with Disabilities welcomed the change but warned that poor rural connectivity, inadequate equipment and limited digital skills could make the system a new barrier outside the main towns.

2026-09-08-nga-punch-nitda-naccima-msme-.summary: Nigeria's IT agency NITDA and the chambers of commerce body NACCIMA signed a memorandum of understanding on the sidelines of GITEX Nigeria to support digital adoption by small and medium enterprises. It covers a shared digital platform for businesses, capacity building and the institutionalising of the Digital Nigeria International Conference. No funding is attached.

2026-09-08-novojornal-brigadas-moveis-re.summary: Angola's territorial administration ministry put mobile brigades into service from late August 2026 to speed up updating of the electoral register, and more than 1.6 million citizens have updated their data, reported on 8 September 2026. Of 634 planned one-stop service desks, 362 are installed and 272 operating; the update runs from 15 June 2026 to 31 March 2027.

2026-09-08-paradigm-initiative-world-lit.summary: A digital rights organisation marks International Literacy Day by arguing what technology owes African education, against a projection of 830 million African young people by 2050.

2026-09-08-premiumtimes-nitda-unified-re.summary: Nigeria's IT development agency called for a unified regulatory approach across Africa and a single interface through which technology companies engage government, arguing that approvals spread across several agencies delay projects and deter investment.

2026-09-08-pti-angola-ai-platform-world-.summary: Angola authorised US$6 million of World Bank money for an artificial-intelligence platform for the public sector under Presidential Order no. 342/26. The funding runs through the Projecto de Aceleracao Digital de Angola and sits in a sequence of recent authorisations covering public digital infrastructure, interoperability, digital skills and government cybersecurity.

2026-09-08-pulse-kenya-ca-nnai-data-cent.summary: Kenya's Communications Authority issued an enhanced framework for numbering, naming, addressing and identification resources and opened consultations on network equipment specifications and on deactivating and recycling inactive numbers. Short codes move to allocation on a services basis rather than per operator, and the same set of notices carries the Authority's separate proposal for a standalone data centre licence category.

2026-09-08-sada-ai-governance-trust-digi.summary: The Smart Africa Digital Academy held a two-day executive programme on AI governance, trust and digital sovereignty in Yasmine Hammamet, Tunisia, for more than 40 senior policymakers and regulators, with RealTyme and Université Laval. Sessions covered risk-based regulation, AI standards, sovereign infrastructure and adding AI to existing digital public infrastructure.

2026-09-08-sajim-digital-negligence-tert.summary: A survey of 289 South African tertiary students finds weak awareness of their own digital footprint driving exposure to cyberbullying.

2026-09-08-sen-primature-declaration-pol.summary: Senegal's prime minister, Ahmadou Alhaminou Mohamed Lo, delivered his general policy statement to the National Assembly on 8 September 2026. On digital matters it commits to securing public data and digital identities, a sovereign cloud to host the state's sensitive data on Senegalese soil, and an accelerated strategy for sectoral uses of artificial intelligence.

2026-09-08-sen-socialnetlink-dpg-cloud-s.summary: Senegal's prime minister, Ahmadou Alhaminou Mohamed Lo, set out the government's digital priorities in his general policy statement of 8 September 2026, naming a sovereign cloud to host sensitive state data on national territory and artificial intelligence as main strands of the New Deal Technologique. Digital projects must now show feasibility, financing and impact before implementation.

2026-09-08-shorouk-egypt-remote-criminal.summary: Egypt's Ministry of Justice opened lawyer registration on its remote criminal litigation platform, and Al Shorouk reported its charges on 8 September 2026: EGP 500 a year to register, EGP 500 for remote attendance at felony hearings, EGP 100 for a detention-renewal hearing and EGP 10 per copied page of case files. Remote litigation is provided for in the new criminal procedure law taking effect on 1 October 2026.

2026-09-08-som-dawan-digital-system-nati.summary: Somalia's Ministry of Planning launched a digital system on 8 September 2026 to monitor the National Transformation Plan across all 26 federal ministries, inaugurated by Deputy Prime Minister Salah Ahmed Jama. Planning Minister Mahmoud Abdirahman Beenebeene said every project will be assessed against performance indicators. The plan has so far reviewed 153 donor-funded projects.

2026-09-08-som-pfm-smart-signs-contract-.summary: PFM Smart signed a contract with Somalia's finance ministry to upgrade the SFMIS financial management system and roll it out to Jubbaland, South West, Galmudug and Hirshabelle, migrating them off the BISAN platform. The upgrade covers budgeting, commitments, procurement, treasury, revenue and reporting, and links SFMIS to the HRMIS and the ITAS tax system.

2026-09-08-ssd-radiotamazuj-uganda-cross.summary: South Sudan and Uganda's health ministers signed a memorandum of understanding in Juba on cross-border health security, reported on 8 September 2026. It provides for real-time sharing of epidemiological information, mutual outbreak notification, joint contact tracing and surveillance, biospecimen transfer and harmonised screening at points of entry.

2026-09-08-tcd-lesfaitsdici-tchad-connex.summary: Seventeen companies presented investment agreements with Chad worth about US$790.5 million in N'Djamena on 4 September 2026, under the Tchad Connexion 2030 plan. That is about 3.9% of the US$20.5 billion pledged at the Abu Dhabi forum in November 2025; the deals cover agro-industry, livestock, construction and telecoms and are expected to create 7,500 direct jobs.

2026-09-08-techafrica-eg-ix-egypt-peak-t.summary: Egypt's main internet exchange EG-IX peaked at 722.19Gb/s over the preceding day across 18 member networks holding about 3Tbps of provisioned ports over 31 connections, every one running IPv6. Only five members are Egyptian; the exchange is owned by the state-controlled incumbent and run on a vendor platform, where most large African exchanges are member-owned or neutrally run.

2026-09-08-techafricanews-dcspay-kotani-.summary: A stablecoin payments platform partnered a local payout provider to widen stablecoin payout and settlement across African markets.

2026-09-08-techafricanews-egypt-8bn-outs.summary: Egypt's communications minister put outsourcing exports at US$5.1 billion at the end of 2025 and set a US$8 billion target for 2028, opening the sixth Tech Invest Egypt conference in Cairo, and gave ICT sector growth of 24.3 per cent for the fourth quarter of the 2025/26 financial year as the highest on record. It is the third ministerial figure for the same 2025 outturn — US$4.8 billion and US$5.2 billion are also on the record — and no statistical release stands behind any of them.

2026-09-08-techafricanews-egypt-vodafone.summary: Two data centre partnerships announced in Cairo project about US$1 billion of investment between them. The first establishes Africa Data Centres Egypt, combining Vodafone Business, Elsewedy Electric and Cassava Technologies, starting at 20MW over three years on a targeted path to 200MW; the second, between Vodafone Business and Cassava, is described as Egypt's first sovereign AI data centre, offering GPU-as-a-Service locally so that AI workloads run without moving data out of the country. The sums are projections stated at announcement rather than committed capital.

2026-09-08-techafricanews-ghana-girls-in.summary: Ghana’s communications minister opened a five-day programme bringing together a hundred beneficiaries of the country’s girls-in-ICT initiative.

2026-09-08-techafricanews-kenya-data-cen.summary: The Communications Authority of Kenya has proposed a standalone Data Centre licence for co-location operators, taking them out of the Network Facilities Provider-Tier 2 category they currently sit under, and opened comment for thirty days from its public notice. The Authority gives visibility over data-centre operations, support for investment and proportionality with comparable jurisdictions as its reasons; the notice itself is not held, so the closing date is unestablished.

2026-09-08-techafricanews-kopo-kopo-k2-c.summary: A Kenyan payments company released a second version of its API, adding payment reversals from point-of-sale systems and new payout features.

2026-09-08-techafricanews-m-pesa-ethiopi.summary: M-PESA Ethiopia has extended cardless ATM withdrawals to Awash Bank's machines, letting wallet holders draw cash without a bank card by authorising the withdrawal in the app. The service has been live with Bank of Abyssinia since August; the date it started with Awash Bank is not stated.

2026-09-08-techafricanews-south-africa-s.summary: South Africa's operator association has asked the Competition Commission for a five-year exemption letting Vodacom, MTN, Telkom, Cell C, Rain and Liquid share limited infrastructure planning information through an independent third party, to find connectivity gaps and avoid duplicated build. The communications minister, who called the proposal encouraging for rural areas and townships, also argued that disruption to Middle East routes gives the country an opening as an alternative submarine cable hub.

2026-09-08-techafricanews-vodacom-400000.summary: The operator says it has trained more than 400,000 young people in digital skills since 2024, and argues that connectivity without skills is not enough.

2026-09-08-techafricanews-zaru-absa-stab.summary: The rand-backed stablecoin ZARU added a second large South African bank to the network that bridges it to the currency.

2026-09-08-techcabal-flowt-kenya-550k-pr.summary: A Kenyan fintech raised US$550,000 to lend to small climate-focused businesses, turning bank and mobile-money records into lender-ready data against a target loan book of US$1 million.

2026-09-08-techcabal-kenya-payment-platf.summary: The cross-border routes Kenyans use to be paid narrowed one by one over the past year: an international payments provider restricted accounts, a dollar-banking service closed, a remittance wallet paused and a streaming platform ended creator monetisation.

2026-09-08-techcabal-mansa-ai-1000-afric.summary: A research lab founded in 2020 is building training data covering a thousand African languages, after finding what exists both scarce and poor.

2026-09-08-techcabal-nigeria-data-sovere.summary: With Nigerian financial firms facing a January 2027 data-localisation deadline, the sovereignty argument is moving past where servers sit to backups, access rights and where data is analysed.

2026-09-08-techtrends-africa-pension-tec.summary: Nigerian pension assets passed N31 trillion in mid-2026, about US$22.8 billion and up by half in two years, against just over 11 million contributors — the frame for an argument about why African retirement saving stays offline.

2026-09-08-thecitizen-congo-locks-down-g.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo is vesting its geological data in the state and charging for access, extending state control over mining; a resource-governance institute questions whether release will be even-handed.

2026-09-08-thesun-papss-nigeria-fintechs.summary: The chief executive of the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System, Mike Ogbalu III, told journalists in Lagos that the system lets businesses settle cross-border trade in local currencies and is drawing informal trade into the formal economy. He described its fraud controls, currency exchange arrangements and aim of covering the whole continent, and placed Nigeria's fintech sector at the centre of that effort.

2026-09-08-times-eswatini-online-scams-e.summary: Eswatini’s communications regulator warned of increasingly sophisticated scams run through messaging apps, social media, mobile money, online banking and video calls.

2026-09-08-timeslive-data-centre-boom-wa.summary: A ratings agency rates South Africa’s water resilience relatively low and names energy and water as the risks to a data-centre pipeline, suggesting operators may need modular energy that bypasses the grid.

2026-09-08-togo-conseil-ministres-commis.summary: Togo's Council of Ministers on 7 September 2026 adopted a bill to ratify the revised convention governing the West African Monetary Union's Banking Commission. The revision extends the Commission's supervision to all regulated institutions, not only credit institutions, and covers resolution and depositor protection. The Council also adopted a bill on banking regulation in Togo.

2026-09-08-tun-leconomistemaghrebin-dgi-.summary: Tunisia's tax directorate added functions to its TEJ tax data exchange platform from September 2026, announced on 8 September. Taxpayers can check their filing status in real time and delegate tasks to other users, public enterprises can check suppliers' tax standing, and all withholding-tax certificates now go through TEJ.

2026-09-08-tun-letemps-psim-plateforme-s.summary: Tunisia's health ministry and UNICEF held a national workshop in Tunis, reported on 8 September 2026, to prepare PSIM, a digital platform for maternal, newborn and child care. The workshop reviewed a benchmarking study of existing practice and identified priority needs. No launch date, cost or funding source is stated.

2026-09-08-tun-tunisienumerique-dgi-tej-.summary: Tunisia's tax directorate announced on 8 September 2026 new functions on its Tej tax-exchange platform from September. Taxpayers can check their filing status in real time, subscribers can delegate functions to other users, and public bodies can check their suppliers' tax position. Tej now also carries all withholding-tax certificates, and public bodies still on the older e-sit-fisc system were told to register.

2026-09-08-undp-aa4dpi-south-south-dpi-m.summary: Delegations from Ethiopia, Malawi, Rwanda, Sierra Leone and Zambia, with African Union representatives, concluded a two-week South-South learning mission to India on digital public infrastructure. Convened under UNDP's newly launched Africa Accelerator for Digital Public Infrastructure, it took delegates through New Delhi, Pune and Bengaluru to examine India's digital identity, payment and data exchange systems.

2026-09-08-undp-africa-accelerator-digit.summary: UNDP has published the standing description of its Africa Accelerator for Digital Public Infrastructure, led jointly by the Regional Bureau for Africa and the Digital and AI Hub, which supports countries to assess digital readiness, strengthen governance, build implementation capacity and develop investment-ready programmes across digital identity, digital payments and data exchange.
