Its first published cohort session ran on 2 and 3 September with delegations from Ethiopia, Malawi, Rwanda, Sierra Leone and Zambia; no budget, duration or deliverable set is published for the accelerator itself.

2026-09-08-vanguard-inec-voter-register-.summary: Nigeria’s voter register is approaching 100 million ahead of the 2027 elections, the commission recording 10,772,421 new registrants in the latest continuous registration exercise.

2026-09-08-vanguard-nrs-reform-tax-data-.summary: An account of Nigeria’s tax reform argues the authority is entering a phase where the quality of the information it holds matters as much as the revenue it collects.

2026-09-08-wearetech-benin-paludisme-ia-.summary: Benin's health ministry has contracted the South Korean firm Noul to put twenty AI-assisted malaria diagnostic devices into the main public referral hospitals, moving the miLab MAL system from individual facilities into the national malaria control programme, which has classified it as a point-of-service diagnostic. The device automates blood-smear preparation, digitisation and image analysis; the supporting evidence is the vendor's account of a 2025 evaluation in 211 children, and the award date is not established.

2026-09-08-wearetech-burkina-faso-amenag.summary: Burkina Faso is revising its digital territorial development plan to a 2030 horizon, against an international union figure putting about 70 per cent of the population off the internet in 2024.

2026-09-08-wearetech-samrawit-tarekegn-s.summary: An Ethiopian engineer's Addis Ababa venture, founded in 2021, runs an online platform for booking home care and domestic help, listing skills, languages, coverage areas and rates before booking. It is extending its network to nursing, social work and psychology profiles with continuing training for its workers.

2026-09-08-wearetech-tanzanie-formation-.summary: Tanzania is training girls for work in information and communications technology, presented as the answer to a wide gender gap in access.

2026-09-08-wearetech-workke-kennedy-moka.summary: WorkKE, a Kenyan platform launched in 2024, matches businesses to freelancers and uses local cybercafes as access relays, releasing escrow-held payments as project stages are validated and settling over mobile money. It reports more than 1,650 registered users, over 500 of them freelancers, and 200 partner cybercafes, and is extending into Uganda, Tanzania, Nigeria, South Africa and Ghana; the counts are the company's own.

2026-09-08-zaf-electoral-commission-intr.summary: South Africa's Electoral Commission said it promulgated its Disinformation Code on 4 September 2026, ahead of the 4 November 2026 local government elections. Parties and candidates must retract and correct false information within 36 hours of becoming aware of it and clearly label AI-generated content.

2026-09-08-zaf-no-completion-date-for-sa.summary: SARS told Freight News it cannot give a completion date for South Africa's National Single Window, which is being phased in across the agencies that regulate cross-border trade, nor list the agencies already integrated. An electronic inspection workflow shared with the Border Management Authority has run since September 2023, with selected plant importers testing it.

2026-09-08-zaf-sars-vat-connect-21-vat-m.summary: The South African Revenue Service confirmed in VAT Connect Issue 21 on 8 September 2026 that the VAT Act now defines e-invoice, e-credit note, e-debit note, interoperability framework and e-reporting, in force from 1 April 2026 under the Tax Administration Laws Amendment Act 4 of 2026. The finance minister may prescribe a voluntary e-reporting system by regulation. No commencement date for those regulations is given.

2026-09-09-afcfta-quest-ghana-digital-tr.summary: The AfCFTA Secretariat and Ghanaian technology company Quest Ghana signed a joint venture agreement in Accra on 31 August 2026 to set up a continental Digital Trade Corridor. It is to build digital infrastructure for payments, commodity trading, marketplaces and logistics. The US$5.17 billion figure reported is Quest Ghana's own valuation, not a stated commitment.

2026-09-09-ahram-papss-instapay-egypt-cr.summary: The Pan-African Payment and Settlement System plans to connect to Instapay, Egypt's central-bank-licensed instant payment app, its chief executive Mike Ogbalu said at a Cairo conference held 7-9 September 2026. He said six Egyptian banks are awaiting central bank approval to join PAPSS, which operates in 30 African countries.

2026-09-09-algeria-tender-mobile-coverag.summary: Algeria's Postal and Electronic Communications Regulatory Authority launched a competitive tender on 7 September to extend mobile wireless coverage to 3,000 sparsely populated areas, under its universal service mandate in Law no. 18-04 of 10 May 2018.

2026-09-09-apc-alinet-solar-community-ne.summary: The Association for Progressive Communications reported on 9 September 2026 that the ALINET community network in Sipili, Kenya, run by the Arid Lands Information Network (ALIN East Africa), uses solar power as its main supply to withstand outages and voltage surges. ALIN obtained a licence for the network in 2023; Sipili's surrounding population is put at over 100,000, mostly farmers.

2026-09-09-assabahnews-tunisia-ai-summit.summary: The Arab ICT Organisation and Tunisia's communication technologies ministry opened the 'AI towards the Future 2026' summit in Yasmine Hammamet on 9 September 2026. Participants include the ITU, UNESCO, the Council of Europe, Smart Africa, ESCWA and the GSMA; sessions cover turning AI's technical potential into economic and social value.

2026-09-09-atu-tunis-apm27-3-wrc27-commo.summary: African governments and telecoms regulators opened four days of talks in Tunis on 8 September 2026 to build common spectrum positions ahead of the 2027 World Radiocommunication Conference. Hosted by Tunisia's National Frequency Agency and coordinated by the African Telecommunications Union, it is the third such preparatory meeting, after Maseru in 2024 and Nairobi in 2025.

2026-09-09-biometricupdate-african-deleg.summary: Delegations from Ethiopia, Malawi, Rwanda, Sierra Leone and Zambia completed a two-week mission to India under the UNDP's Africa Accelerator for Digital Public Infrastructure programme, visiting Delhi, Pune and Bengaluru. They met India's identity authority, UIDAI, and its national payments corporation, NPCI, and studied digital ID, payments and data systems used in agriculture, health and social protection.

2026-09-09-cioafrica-nobus-nairobi-avail.summary: Nobus Cloud Services, a Nigerian public cloud provider operated from Lagos, went live with a Nairobi availability zone designated Nobus-EA-AZ1, letting Kenyan organisations provision workloads locally. It opened alongside a programme offering free cloud credits and technical support to African startups and enterprises.

2026-09-09-civ-communique-conseil-des-mi.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's Council of Ministers on 9 September 2026 adopted a communication on a public-private partnership, signed in December 2025, with Zipline to build and run ten drone hubs delivering medical products, including blood, to hard-to-reach health facilities. Phase one, over 27 months, covers Daloa, Biankouma, San Pedro and Kouto; a US government grant funds the infrastructure and the state pays for services. No contract value is given.

2026-09-09-cmr-journalducameroun-villes-.summary: Cameroon's housing and telecoms ministries and UN-Habitat launched a national action plan for smart cities on 8 September 2026. It rests on three pillars: digital tools for urban management, innovation and inclusion, and stronger municipal and regional governance with dedicated funding. Orange, MTN and CAMTEL are named for infrastructure, FEICOM for municipal finance and ANTIC for regulation; no cost is given.

2026-09-09-cod-numerico-pact-telecoms-co.summary: A workshop in Kinshasa on 9 September 2026, under the World Bank-supported connectivity and transport project PACT, presented two studies on the Democratic Republic of Congo's telecoms sector: one on infrastructure sharing, roaming and the .cd domain, the other on taxation. Recommendations include requiring operators to give the regulator current infrastructure data and a central infrastructure database updated twice a year.

2026-09-09-comesa-aricea-agile-digital-r.summary: COMESA assistant secretary-general Mohamed Kadah called for more predictable and agile regulation of digital technologies at the 14th annual general meeting of ARICEA, the Eastern and Southern African ICT regulators' association, in Livingstone, Zambia, on 9 September 2026. He cited data privacy, cybersecurity, AI and cross-border enforcement, and named universal high-speed internet as a priority.

2026-09-09-consumerconnect-nitda-cloud-e.summary: The director-general of Nigeria's National Information Technology Development Agency, Kashifu Inuwa Abdullahi, told ITW Data Cloud Africa 2026 in Nairobi that federal bodies generate nearly US$1 billion a year in IT demand, which a Cloud-First Policy will direct to cloud and shared infrastructure. He said 326 ministries and agencies spent N3.89 trillion on technology between 2023 and mid-2026, and local data capacity runs at nearly 90% utilisation.

2026-09-09-dcd-ivory-coast-state-owned-d.summary: Cote d'Ivoire is targeting 2027 for the opening of its first state-owned data centre, built by Cybastion at an estimated US$66 million under an Export-Import Bank of the United States financing package. The facility is specified at 1.73MW of IT capacity within 3MW of total power, 228 racks and 10 petabytes of storage.

2026-09-09-dcmag-free-cable-sous-marin-r.summary: Free, through Telco OI, joined the EUR93 million ReuNION consortium led by La Reunion Connectee to build a submarine cable linking La Reunion directly to South Africa. The 16-fibre-pair system is planned for service in 2028 as successor to SAFE, in service since 2002 and at end of life.

2026-09-09-digital-parks-africa-nigeria-.summary: Digital Parks Africa announced Nigeria Data Centre 1, a carrier-neutral facility in Lagos and its first outside southern Africa, at ITW Africa. The developer frames the build as an extension from power and technical services into data centre operations, aimed at financial institutions, cloud and connectivity providers; no investment value is stated.

2026-09-09-dza-aps-government-meeting-pe.summary: Algeria's prime minister, Sifi Ghrieb, chaired a government meeting on 9 September 2026 that took up the Penal Code, damage from recent fires and a unified digital system for regulating and supplying the national market, his office said. No detail of the digital system is given.

2026-09-09-dza-mesrs-deuxieme-reunion-co.summary: Algeria's Minister of Higher Education and Scientific Research, Kamel Baddari, chaired the second coordination meeting on the national AI strategy, reported on 9 September 2026. Five thematic commissions were installed, a national AI and data research centre was decided, and the meeting set a target of training 50,000 AI specialists by 2030.

2026-09-09-egy-almanassa-e-court-platfor.summary: Egypt's justice ministry launched an E-Court platform on 31 August 2026 that lets lawyers and litigants attend first-instance criminal hearings remotely. Lawyers must pay 500 pounds a year to register, 500 more per remote felony hearing and 10 pounds a page for case-file copies. The Egyptian Lawyers Syndicate says the fees have no legal basis.

2026-09-09-egy-maspero-digital-egypt-pla.summary: Egypt's Digital Egypt platform was shortlisted among the top 15 entries in the digital government category of the ITU and UNDP Digital@UNGA 2026 awards, announced on 9 September 2026. The communications ministry says the platform offers more than 240 services to 12.9 million registered users and is linked to 109 government bodies, with 270 services targeted by the end of 2026.

2026-09-09-equatorial-guinea-starlink-la.summary: Equatorial Guinea's vice-president, Teodoro Nguema Obiang Mangue, announced on 9 September 2026 the official launch of SpaceX's Starlink satellite internet service. Sales will be centralised, requests handled by the telecoms regulator Ortel, and earlier connections made with foreign details deactivated. The government also plans talks with Meta on charging fees for use of its applications in the country.

2026-09-09-ericsson-ghana-nca-5g-cyberse.summary: An Ericsson delegation called on Ghana's National Communications Authority to discuss 5G deployment, quality of service, cybersecurity and network resilience. The Authority's deputy director-general said 5G licence conditions require 70 per cent population coverage by March 2027 and that compliance monitoring would be strengthened.

2026-09-09-eth-shega-mobile-money-diagno.summary: A diagnostic report by Ethiopia's Team Shega, published on 9 September 2026, finds that more than 135 million mobile wallets have been opened, yet fewer than one adult in ten holds a mobile money account and 0.4% rely on one alone. Drawing on Global Findex 2025, UNCDF and central bank data, it finds most inclusion gains were bank-led and makes eight recommendations.

2026-09-09-ethio-telecom-4g-expansion-11.summary: Ethio Telecom is to expand its 4G network from 6,924 to 11,014 sites in 2026/27 under the Year II plan of its Next Horizon strategy. It is a published target, not an outturn.

2026-09-09-gha-gna-bog-20-unlicensed-dig.summary: The Bank of Ghana published a list of 20 mobile loan apps operating without a licence on 9 September 2026, among them Cash Cedi, CreditGo, Quick Cedi and Zoom Advance. It said they breach customer data privacy and consumer protection rules under its September 2025 directive on digital credit providers. Banks and payment service providers were told not to process transactions for them.

2026-09-09-gha-myjoyonline-nca-5g-spectr.summary: Ghana's National Communications Authority said on 9 September 2026 that MTN Ghana, Telecel Ghana and Goal Telecom qualified for the next stage of its licensing process for the 700 MHz, 2.3 GHz and 3 GHz bands. A fourth applicant, Infrava, was disqualified. The next stage opens and ranks the qualified applicants' price offers; no date is given.

2026-09-09-ghana-france-telecoms-coopera.summary: Ghana's communications minister met the French ambassador to discuss expanding access to affordable connectivity, French investment in digital infrastructure and approaches to digital disinformation, and to exchange views ahead of the Internet Governance Forum in November.

2026-09-09-gin-webguinee24-data-center-n.summary: Guinea's prime minister, Amadou Oury Bah, visited the National Data Centre on 9 September 2026, a year after its inauguration, to review progress towards full operation. He told the teams concerned to finalise and send the technical and administrative documents needed to speed up its commissioning. No date for full operation is given.

2026-09-09-gmb-thepoint-nine-digit-numbe.summary: The Gambia's regulator PURA has moved telephone numbers from seven to nine digits, with old and new numbers running in parallel until the seven-digit format is retired on 28 February 2027. PURA worked with Meta and the ITU so systems abroad recognise the new format, and monitored Africell, QCell and Comium networks during the switch.

2026-09-09-gnq-meta-tax-starlink-ortel-c.summary: Equatorial Guinea's vice-president, Teodoro Nguema Obiang Mangue, gave the state operator ORTEL sole legal authority to sell Starlink satellite internet, under the state secretariat for artificial intelligence, and ordered contracts made outside official channels cancelled. He also tasked a commission with discussing payments to the state with Meta, which he said has done business in the country without paying.

2026-09-09-hapijournal-egypt-digital-pla.summary: Egypt's communications minister Raafat Hendy put the Digital Egypt platform at about 245 live services and set a target of more than 400 by 2030, and said a digital identity platform has launched so that transactions requiring personal verification — powers of attorney, notarisation — can be completed without attending an office. He also said an integrated data centre strategy is being prepared for launch by the end of 2026, and that outsourcing exports reached $5.1bn in 2025 against an $8bn target for 2028; ITIDA put outsourcing employment above 195,000, from about 90,000 in 2021. The report is of the minister's remarks to a business delegation, and none of the targets carries a published implementation document.

2026-09-09-incm-relatorio-defesa-consumi.summary: Mozambique's communications regulator, INCM, reported 391,723 telecoms complaints in 2025, up about 44% from 271,993 in 2024, with 95.2% of closed complaints resolved; postal complaints fell from 276 to 258. Vodacom logged 115,100 complaints and Movitel 87,428. INCM named Tmcel, Teledata, TMT and StarTimes for closer follow-up, and two postal operators filed no returns.

2026-09-09-itweb-africa-bank-of-uganda-s.summary: Bank of Uganda's governor told Parliament's Public Accounts Committee that the central bank has strengthened its internal security systems after a physical break-in and allegations of system manipulation at its headquarters. He said the incidents involved a physical breach and fraudulent payments rather than an external cyberattack.

2026-09-09-itweb-africa-kenya-cross-bord.summary: Kenya's Office of the Data Protection Commissioner issued guidance on cross-border transfers of personal data, setting out the legal, regulatory and operational obligations of every entity that transfers personal data abroad or receives it from abroad, the safeguards required and the mechanisms for ensuring adequate protection in the recipient country.

2026-09-09-itweb-africa-malawi-exam-resu.summary: Malawi's education ministry and the national examinations board released the 2026 school certificate results online on 7 September, candidates and examination centres reading them through e-results portals rather than waiting for printed results delivered to districts. The board introduced e-registration in 2022 and the results portals in 2024, and examination fees are now paid through banks and mobile wallets by candidates or parents directly, which it says removes the risk of fees collected by teachers on students' behalf going astray. Of 188,169 candidates, 111,510 passed, a 59.26 per cent pass rate.

2026-09-09-itweb-africa-zambia-digital-t.summary: Zambia and Altron Security have launched a National Public Key Infrastructure, intended as a sovereign root of trust for digital identity, electronic signatures and secure online government, with certificates carrying legal validity under the country's electronic communications and transactions law. The master cryptographic keys were generated under independently audited conditions in a purpose-built facility and are held offline, split among several custodians so that no single body controls them. The Smart Zambia Institute's national coordinator said the launch is only the beginning and its value depends on whether government can sustain the infrastructure, fund it and get public institutions to adopt it.

2026-09-09-itweb-co-za-iec-election-disi.summary: South Africa's Electoral Commission has gazetted a Disinformation Code for the local government elections on 4 November, binding political parties, candidates and anyone acting on their instruction or for reward across all election-related communication, online or offline, paid or unpaid. Parties and candidates must check information before sharing it, publicly retract and correct anything false within 36 hours of becoming aware of it, label AI-generated content and political advertising, and report online disinformation to Real411 within 36 hours; fake accounts, bot networks, coordinated inauthentic behaviour, doxing and cyberbullying are prohibited, as is disinformation targeting the commission or its staff. Contravention carries the sanctions applying to the Electoral Code of Conduct under the Municipal Electoral Act 27 of 2000, and parties will undertake to comply at the signing ceremony on 23 September; the source gives no gazette number or date for the final code.

2026-09-09-itweb-co-za-sa-ai-infrastruct.summary: A column by Johan Steyn on the Africa AI Governance Index, published in July by the Nairobi-based Lawyers Hub, which ranks South Africa eleventh in Africa on its capacity to govern AI, scoring 2.10 out of four against Rwanda's 3.25, Nigeria's 2.81 and Benin's 2.58 — the only three the index classifies as having established AI governance. The index scores all 54 states across eight pillars and 80 indicators per country, and finds every African sub-region scoring highest on strategy and lowest on implementation. The argument is that South Africa built the infrastructure first: its draft national AI policy was withdrawn on 26 April 2026 after several cited academic sources were found not to exist, leaving no dedicated policy until revised documents reach Cabinet in November 2026.

2026-09-09-itweb-coalition-warns-crypto-.summary: A South African crypto industry coalition asked National Treasury and the Reserve Bank to redraft proposed cross-border crypto asset regulations, warning of job losses, effects on millions of holders and lost tax revenue. Its members say they support regulation, transparency and financial-crime measures but not rules that discriminate against the activity.

2026-09-09-itweb-shein-temu-sa-ecommerce.summary: South Africa's crackdown on low-value imports has significantly slowed cross-border e-commerce growth and pushed the two largest platforms from tax arbitrage towards local fulfilment and supply chains, on the Online Retail in South Africa study.

2026-09-09-journalducameroun-beac-papss-.summary: The Bank of Central African States (BEAC) and the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS) held a webinar on 9 September 2026 to bring commercial banks of the CEMAC zone onto the continental payment system, following BEAC's own accession. The session covered terms of participation and next steps; no timetable or number of banks is given.

2026-09-09-kbc-kenya-digital-infrastruct.summary: Kenyan ministers opening the ITW and Datacloud Africa Conference in Nairobi named route diversity, cybersecurity, reliable power, data governance and infrastructure resilience as the conditions for further investment, and positioned connectivity as the foundation for Africa's participation in the global digital economy. No new instrument or commitment was announced.

2026-09-09-ken-techweez-nemis-kemis-migr.summary: Kenya's switch from the NEMIS school data system to KEMIS ran into failed logins, lost submissions and outdated learner records during the 2026 Grade 10 selection for nearly 1.2 million pupils, Techweez reported on 9 September 2026. Education PS John Ololtuaa told MPs in late August that the latest capitation payment used neither system but manually verified data.

2026-09-09-kenya-us-cooperation-ai-cyber.summary: Kenya and the United States discussed deepening cooperation on artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, digital infrastructure and investment on the sidelines of the AmCham Business Summit. The talks covered university and research partnerships and positioning Kenya for US foreign direct investment; no instrument was signed.

2026-09-09-kictanet-kenya-alternative-me.summary: The Kenya ICT Action Network launched a report, Many Microphones, Little Accountability, at a webinar on 9 September 2026, finding that Facebook, TikTok, YouTube and X are reshaping political news and spreading misinformation ahead of the 2027 general election. The study drew on three months of platform monitoring, a national survey and interviews.

2026-09-09-kictanet-sheconnects-empowerh.summary: Kenya's ICT policy network KICTANet held a three-day workshop in Tana River County from 9 to 11 September 2026 to train 100 women as trainers in its digital skills curriculum for women micro-entrepreneurs. Under its EmpowerHer project, 300 such trainers in Nairobi, Tana River and Nyandarua counties are to reach 15,000 women.

2026-09-09-koica-moz-2026-mozambique-ing.summary: The UN Development Programme, with funding from the Korea International Cooperation Agency, handed over ICT equipment worth more than US$300,000 to Mozambique's National Institute for Disaster Risk Management and Reduction in Maputo on 9 September 2026. The equipment is meant to improve information management, communication and coordination in disaster risk management at national, provincial and district level.

2026-09-09-lanation-djibouti-horizon-fib.summary: Djibouti Telecom, Ethio telecom and Sudatel presented their Horizon terrestrial fibre project to Google, Meta, Microsoft, Amazon and other carriers and vendors in Addis Ababa on 7 September 2026. The multi-terabit link would connect cable landing stations in Djibouti and Port Sudan through Ethiopia, reducing reliance on Red Sea submarine cables. No cost or launch date is given.

2026-09-09-lbr-newdawn-iaa-goes-digital.summary: Liberia's Internal Audit Agency was due to launch its own custom software for planning, running and tracking internal audits across government on 10 September 2026 at Monrovia City Hall, Information Minister Jerolinmek Matthew Piah announced. It is the agency's first in-house digital system. No cost is given.

2026-09-09-lby-british-council-benghazi-.summary: The British Council signed a memorandum with the University of Benghazi giving more than 70,000 students access to its Digital Library of over 80,000 resources, the British Embassy announced on 9 September 2026. The university lost much of its library collection during the war. No cost is stated.

2026-09-09-lby-unified-economic-number-p.summary: Libya's National Council for the Unified Economic Number began pilot electronic issuance of a single identifier for economic, commercial and investment entities on 9 September 2026, under Cabinet Decision No. 348 of 2026. Applicants' National Number must match the phone number registered to it. The number is issued free through the Dawlati government services platform.

2026-09-09-lesahel-niger-telecom-algerie.summary: Niger's telecoms and post college ESCEP signed a convention with Algérie Télécom's Skills Centers network in Niamey on 8 September 2026, at a meeting chaired by the communication ministry's secretary-general. The agreement provides for a Skills Center at ESCEP with Algérie Télécom's support, aimed at training and the capacity of Niger's telecoms infrastructure. No cost is given.

2026-09-09-mar-panorapost-ia-nouvelle-ph.summary: Morocco's Ministry of Digital Transition and Administrative Reform presented progress on its "Maroc IA 2030" roadmap in Rabat, including a sovereign AI marketplace, an AI assistant for the Idarati portal and a national e-wallet proof of concept. The roadmap targets 100 billion dirhams of added GDP, 50,000 jobs and 200,000 trained people by 2030.

2026-09-09-mk-korea-45-african-countries.summary: South Korea agreed to cooperate with 45 African countries on artificial intelligence, tying AI solutions, AI data centres and power supply facilities to projects financed by its Economic Development Cooperation Fund. No commitment sum is stated.

2026-09-09-mli-maliweb-dnen-kabakoo-prem.summary: Mali's digital economy directorate and Kabakoo Academies launched the first cohort of 1,000 young people under a three-year agreement signed on 31 January 2026 to train 15,000 in digital and entrepreneurial skills, announced at Mali's digital week of 28 July to 1 August 2026. The four-month course is open to 18- to 35-year-olds and fees are covered by bursaries.

2026-09-09-moz-cedsif-seeks-artificial-i.summary: Mozambique's Centre for Development of Financial Information Systems (CEDSIF) issued an open call for expressions of interest for artificial intelligence consultancy services, reported on 9 September 2026. The consultancy would support its digital transformation and information systems development; no value or deadline was given.

2026-09-09-mwi-linkedin-longwe-ctn-ai-ed.summary: Converged Technology Networks' chief executive, Brian Munyao Longwe, wrote on 9 September 2026 that the company is upgrading its Lilongwe edge data centre, live since February 2026, for AI workloads with support from the EU D4D Hub, and plans further sites in Blantyre, Mzuzu and Zomba alongside 150 new 4G sites. He puts Malawi's fixed broadband connections at about 15,000.

2026-09-09-ner-niger-is-transforming-for.summary: Webb Fontaine, which built it, says Niger's foreign-trade single window, GUCE-Niger, now connects customs, the finance, trade, agriculture, livestock and health ministries, the chamber of commerce and every bank, through e-Forex for foreign-exchange operations. Stamp duties are now calculated and paid through the platform.

2026-09-09-ner-nigerdiaspora-enrolement-.summary: Niger's interior ministry said mass enrolment for the Alliance of Sahel States biometric passport opens on 15 September 2026, at the territorial surveillance directorate in Niamey and regional police offices elsewhere. The passport costs 45,000 FCFA, or 29,750 FCFA for minors and students. Passports bearing the ECOWAS logo stay valid until they expire.

2026-09-09-newzimbabwe-cabinet-e-hailing.summary: Zimbabwe's Cabinet granted e-hailing platforms including Bolt, InDrive and Tap & Go a five-month moratorium, Information Minister Soda Zhemu announced on 9 September 2026. During it the government will develop a self-regulating framework for drivers and passenger safety and register the businesses, with a view to bringing platforms and drivers into the tax net.

2026-09-09-nga-developmentdiaries-eprocu.summary: Nigeria's Bureau of Public Procurement has made its Digital Submission Portal mandatory for procurement requests from federal ministries, departments and agencies, Development Diaries reports. The outlet notes that the government has not said it will publish contract awards, amounts or delivery records, and cites duties under the Public Procurement Act 2007 to maintain a contractor database and keep procurement records.

2026-09-09-nga-naltf-shettima-112-emerge.summary: Nigeria's Vice-President Kashim Shettima directed a committee of the police, the Nigerian Communications Commission, the National Emergency Management Agency and the Federal Road Safety Corps to finalise a roadmap and operating procedures for the nationwide 112 emergency number, at a meeting in Abuja on 8 September 2026. The plan goes to the National Economic Council, which has approved 112 as the single emergency number. No budget is given.

2026-09-09-nga-ncc-industry-statistics-i.summary: The Nigerian Communications Commission's monthly statistics, updated 9 September 2026, show 157,706,496 active internet subscriptions in July 2026, almost all on mobile, up from 138,749,365 a year earlier. Data usage in July 2026 was 1,662,021.45 terabytes, against 1,131,255.90 terabytes in July 2025.

2026-09-09-nga-techeconomy-bcg-digital-g.summary: Boston Consulting Group's eighth biennial Digital Government Citizen Survey, covering 44 countries, found 91% of Nigerian respondents use AI weekly, the highest of any market surveyed. Nigeria's adoption of digital government services stands at 50%, and net satisfaction with them fell five points since 2024 to 64%.

2026-09-09-nga-thestar-nysc-learner-iden.summary: Nigeria's education minister Tunji Alausa said on 8 September 2026 that his ministry and the National Youth Service Corps are discussing an API to exchange education records and verify certificates. He also proposed a national Learner Identification Number and standard name-recording across education and identity databases, to be developed with JAMB, the identity commission and others.

2026-09-09-nga-thisday-dms-implementatio.summary: Mobile device manufacturers asked the Nigerian Communications Commission to extend the timetable for its Device Management System, which checks each device's IMEI against registers of stolen or counterfeit handsets before activation. The commission plans to charge about N670 per IMEI and over N3,700 for high-end devices, with free onboarding of existing stock closing on 7 September. Manufacturers said the window was too short and the appeal procedure unclear.

2026-09-09-nigeriacommsweek-uk-dap-siun-.summary: The UK Digital Access Programme inaugurated the Siun Community Self-Built Connectivity Hub in Obafemi Owode, Ogun State. It is one of ten community-centred hubs the programme supports in Nigeria on a model that places ownership and management with local communities and pairs affordable access with digital skills; how many of the ten are open is not stated.

2026-09-09-nitda-trust-transparency-digi.summary: Nigeria's IT development agency told a multi-stakeholder meeting on digital governance in Abuja that the question must shift from what technology can do to how it should be governed, raising accountability when digital systems fail, transparency in algorithmic decision-making and a route for citizens to challenge automated decisions. It used AI-driven grant disbursement as the worked example.

2026-09-09-ntra-egypt-mobile-wallets-usa.summary: Egypt's National Telecom Regulatory Authority reported 57.01 million mobile wallets in the first half of 2026, up 23% on a year earlier, with penetration at 45%. Wallets carried 2.22 billion transactions worth EGP 2.96 trillion. Vodafone Cash held 53% of wallets and 77% of transaction value.

2026-09-09-onecitizendaily-south-sudan-y.summary: The Central Equatoria branch of the Union of Journalists of South Sudan trained more than 20 people from civil society, security bodies and the media in Yei River County on cybercrime, the Cybercrime and Computer Misuse Act 2026 and election preparedness. The session also covered responsible use of digital platforms and protection of personal information.

2026-09-09-radionationale-ai-forward-sum.summary: The AI Forward Summit 2026, organised by the Arab Information and Communication Technologies Organisation and Tunisia's communication technologies ministry, opened in Tunisia on 9 September 2026. Secretary of State Mohamed Ben Ayed told the opening session that Tunisia wants international cooperation on capacity-building, technology transfer and finance so developing countries produce AI rather than only consume it.

2026-09-09-rwa-newtimes-cybersecurity-tv.summary: Rwanda is introducing cybersecurity courses in technical and vocational education and training schools. The first cohort of 24 TVET teachers has completed a ten-day training-of-trainers programme to support the rollout. No cost, number of schools or start date for the courses is given.

2026-09-09-sadc-exchange-gateway-aim-con.summary: The Southern African Development Community and the Committee of SADC Stock Exchanges attended AIM Congress 2026 in Dubai from 7 to 9 September, promoting Southern Africa as an integrated investment destination. A joint investment forum presented regional capital-market integration as a way to finance infrastructure, industrialisation and energy. No deals or sums are reported.

2026-09-09-sadc-nsds-south-africa-consul.summary: The SADC Secretariat issued a call on 9 September 2026 for an individual consultant to draft South Africa's National Strategy for the Development of Statistics over 180 days. The work is funded by a World Bank IDA grant to the Regional Statistics Project (P175731).

2026-09-09-safaricom-ethiopia-government.summary: Safaricom Ethiopia put itself at 15 million 90-day active customers and more than 3,600 sites in five years of operation, at a meeting with the innovation and technology minister. Its chief executive raised infrastructure and supply-chain constraints on further rollout, including the timely customs clearance of telecommunications equipment and fibre cable.

2026-09-09-sdn-akherkhabar-bankak-boycot.summary: A social-media campaign in Sudan urged Bank of Khartoum customers to boycott its Bankak app, withdraw their money and move to Family Bank, Savings Bank or Omdurman National Bank, citing repeated app outages. Posts also claimed the bank had stopped transfers to other banks and alleged Emirati shareholding; the report notes neither claim carries independent documentation or official confirmation.

2026-09-09-sdn-sudan4news-public-service.summary: The head of Sudan's police public service complexes, Major General Tariq al-Rih, said on 9 September 2026 that the Omdurman and Bahri complexes, which house passport, civil registry and traffic services, are fully running and Khartoum's will partly reopen. Transactions rose from 206,362 in 2025 to 522,225 in 2026, and he set a three-month plan to put all complexes online.

2026-09-09-sidwaya-carte-identite-biomet.summary: Burkina Faso's national identification office ONI began special operations to issue the Alliance of Sahel States biometric identity card, CIB-AES, at Koudougou on 9 September 2026, ahead of International Identity Day on 16 September. No enrolment figures or costs are given.

2026-09-09-som-somalidigest-nira-id-behi.summary: Somalia's deputy prime minister, Jibril Abdirashid Abdi, asked the information ministry on 7 September 2026 to require social media accounts to carry the holder's NIRA identity number in the media regulations being drafted. He spoke at a communication forum in Mogadishu; the report also records dozens of disputed takedowns of Puntland broadcasters' posts between January and August.

2026-09-09-sonatel-starlink-senegal-lice.summary: Senegal's Supreme Court on 7 September 2026 provisionally suspended the licence granted to Starlink Senegal for fixed satellite internet, on an application by the incumbent operator Sonatel. Sonatel is challenging ministerial order no. 038974 of 6 November 2025, which authorised the SpaceX subsidiary for five years, arguing that its own concession obligations and investments were not taken into account.

2026-09-09-swz-observer-standard-bank-un.summary: Standard Bank Eswatini will close its Unayo wallet platform on 31 December 2026, the Eswatini Observer reported on 9 September 2026. Unayo has more than 200,000 registered retail customers and about 5,000 business clients, of whom about 30% transact regularly; the bank says the Eswatini Payment Switch now provides the real-time transfers between banks and wallets that Unayo was built to offer.

2026-09-09-syc-nation-repair-cash-transf.summary: Seychelles' finance ministry and the Agency for Social Protection signed a performance agreement under the regional REPAIR programme, reported on 9 September 2026, to make rapid cash transfers to households after floods, landslides or tsunamis. The agency will pay through its existing beneficiary registry and payment systems and add newly affected households. No value is stated.

2026-09-09-syc-statehouse-cabinet-digita.summary: Seychelles' Cabinet, chaired by President Patrick Herminie on 9 September 2026, approved a multi-stakeholder Digital Economic Transformation Forum to agree a national digital architecture, priority pilot projects and an implementation roadmap. The same meeting approved a Hydrographic Office within the Maritime Safety Authority to manage marine data.

2026-09-09-techafricanews-gabon-four-dig.summary: Gabon set out four public-administration digital projects at the sixth steering committee of the e-Gabon-SIS project and the Gabon Digital programme on 8 September 2026, chaired by digital economy minister Mark-Alexandre Doumba: migration of the Single Master File to an integrated human resources management system, a government interoperability platform for exchanging data between institutions, a National Digital Identity System, and a government messaging system due before the end of 2026. No budget or delivery date is published for the first three.

2026-09-09-techafricanews-ghana-ai-robot.summary: Ghana's communications ministry has launched a five-day AI and robotics summer bootcamp for 100 students from 19 schools, split into four age cohorts covering coding, robotics and AI from ages 6 to 18. Younger participants work through visual and block-based activities and older ones through programming and design exercises.

2026-09-09-techafricanews-kenya-child-on.summary: The Communications Authority of Kenya and the University of Nairobi's Institute for Development Studies have begun reviewing preliminary findings from a joint national survey on children's online experiences and safety, agreeing the report structure and thematic areas ahead of validation. The authority says the findings are intended as the evidence base for regulatory interventions on child online protection; nothing has been published yet.

2026-09-09-techafricanews-mtn-south-suda.summary: MTN South Sudan opened the Rumbek ICT Hub in Lakes State on 8 September 2026, a digital learning and innovation centre offering ICT training, learning resources and capacity-building for young people. It was launched with the Lakes State Government and endorsed by the national ICT minister; no cost, duration or intake figure is published.

2026-09-09-techcabal-africa-ai-race-not-.summary: An analysis arguing that the consequential AI adoption in Africa is enterprise and industrial rather than consumer-facing — systems processing invoices, optimising energy use and running mines rather than chatbots. It draws on 4Sight Holdings, which frames its work as automating routine business processes rather than adding assistants, and ABB, whose South African process automation manager describes mining's problem as islands of automation that do not operate as one connected system. The case made is that the continent's constraints — unreliable power, cost pressure, dangerous working environments — raise the return on automation rather than lowering it, and that the obstacle is organisational: structured data, mapped processes and change management, not the technology.

2026-09-09-techcabal-dlocal-ghana-epsp-l.summary: dLocal Ghana, the subsidiary of the Uruguayan payments company, has secured an Enhanced Payment Service Provider licence from the Bank of Ghana, letting it provide local collections, merchant acquiring, mobile-money acceptance and payouts in its own name where it had previously routed Ghana flows through its global platform and regulated third-party partners. It will roll the services out on operational readiness rather than at once. Paystack and Flutterwave hold comparable licences and Fincra was licensed in the enhanced category in May 2026; Bank of Ghana data put mobile money at GH¢4.54 trillion in 2025, up 50.8 per cent on 2024.

2026-09-09-techcabal-mtn-nigeria-100-mil.summary: MTN Nigeria became the first Nigerian operator to pass 100 million subscribers, ending July 2026 with 100.86 million on regulator data, up from 98.64 million in June and 51.76 per cent of the market. It spent NGN620.5 billion on capital expenditure excluding lease additions in the first half of 2026 on spectrum, fibre backhaul and other network infrastructure.

2026-09-09-techtrendske-lulu-coastal-cab.summary: A consortium unveiled the LuLu Coastal Cable System at ITW Africa 2026, presented as the first fully protected submarine cable dedicated to Kenya's Indian Ocean coastline: 500km linking five landing points from Mombasa to Lamu, including Vipingo Special Economic Zone, Kilifi and Malindi, pairing a seabed cable with a parallel protected terrestrial route. It is specified at 144 fibres and up to 60Tbps per fibre pair over a 25-year design life, with service targeted for the second quarter of 2028 subject to contract execution, and the Mombasa landing connecting it to cables already landed at the port. The co-developers named are INDOI of Mauritius, Blue Trade Investments as the Kenya-registered landing party, ARISE IIP, AfriTrade Consulting Group and Kingdom Bank; no project value or financing structure is stated.

2026-09-09-techtrendske-paratus-east-afr.summary: Paratus said its 2,000km Goma-to-Mombasa terrestrial fibre route is live and carrying traffic, announced at the ITW and Datacloud Africa conference in Nairobi. The route links eastern DRC to the Kenyan coast through Kigali, Kampala and Nairobi, with access to subsea capacity landing at Mombasa. Starlink services have launched in Uganda alongside it, and the company is introducing a Layer 2 connectivity service over low-earth-orbit satellite for the East African market.

2026-09-09-terrapay-alipay-cross-border-.summary: TerraPay and Alipay+ announced a partnership to enable cross-border QR payments for African digital wallets. In the initial phase 15 African wallets connected to TerraPay's Xend interoperability network would be able to pay at more than 150 million merchants, extending the network from account-to-account transfers into in-store payments.

2026-09-09-thisday-fg-digital-training-a.summary: Nigeria's education ministry admitted 16,000 people to the first cohort of its free Digital Training Academy, from 72,850 applications received between 17 August and 1 September 2026, of which 19,699 met entry requirements. Training is delivered through Coursera and Pluralsight under the Nigeria Education Digital Infrastructure programme, with a national launch on 14 September.

2026-09-09-thisday-uk-fcdo-community-con.summary: A community-owned connectivity hub was inaugurated on 2 September 2026 at Siun in Obafemi Owode, Ogun State, Nigeria, under the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office's Digital Access Programme. It is one of ten community hubs the programme supports in Nigeria, built with local materials and residents' labour. No cost or connection capacity is given.

2026-09-09-thisdaylive-eu-eib-boost-afri.summary: The European Union and the European Investment Bank have invested €108 million through the Boost Africa initiative for African entrepreneurs, attracting a further €400 million and creating up to 15,000 jobs, the EU ambassador to Nigeria, Gautier Mignot, said in Abuja on 9 September 2026. He spoke ahead of the Boost Africa Impact Forum.

2026-09-09-times-eswatini-ers-e-invoicin.summary: Business Eswatini brought its retail and wholesale members together with the Eswatini Revenue Service to explain the revenue service's Electronic Invoicing Solution and prepare for its introduction. A number of businesses volunteered for the pilot phase, in which invoices are to be generated, sent and validated electronically in real time or near real time.

2026-09-09-ttcl-bbs-tanzania-burundi-cap.summary: Tanzania's state operator agreed with Burundi Backbone System to raise cross-border capacity from 4Gbps to 10Gbps through the National ICT Broadband Backbone, framed as a response to demand for cross-border digital services and enterprise connectivity.

2026-09-09-tza-moh-sekta-binafsi-interop.summary: Tanzania's health ministry permanent secretary, Dr Grace Magembe, said on 9 September 2026 that the government is cutting the number of separate digital health systems so the rest can exchange data, and linking private and public systems. Speaking at a primary health care conference in Arusha, she said a national Health Data Centre is being prepared to bring health information into one point of access.

2026-09-09-tza-mwananchi-zanzibar-mwongo.summary: Zanzibar's deputy minister for communications, Mohamed Sijamin Mohamed, told the House of Representatives on 9 September 2026 that the government is drafting a guideline on installing and sharing communications infrastructure. It responds to the spread of street poles erected by each internet provider for fibre-to-the-home. The guideline would promote a single fibre contractor or shared poles. No date for adoption is given.

2026-09-09-uga-independent-nira-staffing.summary: Uganda's National Identification and Registration Authority told Parliament on 8 September 2026 that about 5.4 million printed ID cards are uncollected, of roughly 15.4 million printed. Its executive director said 418 of 571 approved posts are filled, only 201 client-facing, and asked for 998 posts plus at least 2,700 temporary staff for 18 months. About 10.9 million Ugandans remain unregistered.

2026-09-09-undp-liberia-msc-ai-consultat.summary: The University of Liberia, with UNDP support, is running national stakeholder consultations on establishing Liberia's first MSc in Artificial Intelligence, bringing together government institutions, development partners, academia, private-sector actors and civil society.

2026-09-09-ustda-csquared-ghana-fibre-fe.summary: The US Trade and Development Agency signed an agreement on 9 September to fund a feasibility study for open-access fibre laid along Northern Electricity Distribution Company lines, which span more than 60 per cent of Ghana. The study is to assess commercial viability, quantify demand and develop a financing strategy; no grant value is stated.

2026-09-09-vanguard-first-bank-n6bn-annu.summary: First Bank of Nigeria spends more than N6 billion a year on cybersecurity, its chief executive Olusegun Alebiosu said at the Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria's annual conference. He said the bank monitors its systems around the clock, has set up a command centre and blocks millions of threats each month.

2026-09-09-vanguard-ncc-device-managemen.summary: The Nigerian Communications Commission said on 9 September 2026 that its new Device Management System will not give it access to users' personal data or communications. The system records IMEI numbers to check that SIM-enabled devices have type approval, and unregistered devices will be barred from networks. The first phase, with the customs service and importers, covers devices already in stock and new imports.

2026-09-09-von-eu-eib-boost-africa-impac.summary: The EU used the Boost Africa Impact Forum in Abuja to argue that access to finance realises African entrepreneurial potential only alongside technical expertise, networks and an enabling business environment. Its ambassador said the initiative, run with the European Investment Bank and the African Development Bank, has attracted more than EUR100 million; the figure is cumulative rather than a dated commitment.

2026-09-09-wearetech-injini-programme-12.summary: The South African edtech accelerator Injini has launched an eight-month programme for twelve teams across Southern Africa building affordable AI tools adapted to local classrooms. The five strongest projects will receive seed funding at the end of it to develop their tools and test their impact with pupils and teachers; no amount is stated.

2026-09-09-wearetech-jules-johanes-aho-b.summary: Jules Johanes Aho co-founded and runs Bénin Codeurs, a Cotonou firm founded in 2025 that designs and deploys custom software for organisations, from prototype to production with post-launch support, and offers team reinforcement so companies can add developers without direct hiring. The firm says it can mobilise a technical team within 48 hours. He co-founded a first company, Horygin Agence, in 2023, working on automation and digital marketing.

2026-09-09-wearetech-magalie-bemba-mines.summary: Magalie Bemba, a Congolese technology entrepreneur and public policy adviser, is among six African finalists in the Most Impactful Initiative category of the Women in Tech Global Awards 2026. She founded CODES Africa in Kinshasa in 2024, a platform running conferences and competitions on innovation and cybersecurity that has extended to Libreville and Kolwezi, and whose MiningTech Summit brings public decision-makers and industry together on digital sovereignty, traceability and local value creation; she also sits on the ICT committee of the DRC's National Assembly.

2026-09-09-wearetech-senegal-cloud-souve.summary: Senegal put a sovereign cloud for the state's sensitive data and an accelerated sectoral AI strategy at the centre of its digital priorities, in the prime minister's general policy statement of 8 September. The refocus sits within the New Deal technologique and narrows selection to initiatives that are feasible, financed and able to produce measurable results.

2026-09-09-xaf-dfc-board-notice-2026-09-.summary: The US International Development Finance Corporation put to its board meeting of 16 September 2026 an equity investment of up to US$155m in WIOCC Holding Company, the African digital infrastructure group. Its public summary puts total project costs at up to US$450m, including about 25MW of new data-centre capacity.

2026-09-09-yonhap-afdb-president-korea-a.summary: The African Development Bank's president said Korea and Africa hold complementary strengths in the AI era and set out an intention to put AI infrastructure, enabling regulation, capacity building and joint investment at the top of the Korea-Africa agenda. It is a statement of priority; no instrument or sum is attached.

2026-09-09-yonhap-korea-africa-k-ai-pack.summary: South Korea set out the K-AI Package at the 8th KOAFEC ministerial in Seoul, tying AI solutions, AI data centres and power supply facilities to infrastructure projects financed by its Economic Development Cooperation Fund. Delegations from 45 African countries adopted a joint declaration, approved 13 new trust-fund projects and signed a letter of intent for a Korea-Africa AI Hub at the African Development Bank. No commitment sum is stated.

2026-09-09-zaf-broadcastmediaafrica-icas.summary: South Africa's communications regulator ICASA launched two market inquiries, one into the effect of over-the-top services such as Netflix and WhatsApp on its telecoms, broadcasting and postal licensees, the other into telecoms affordability. Each runs in four phases, with 45 working days for written responses; findings will be published in the Government Gazette. No new charge on platforms has been announced.

2026-09-09-zaf-myza-parlimeter-custodian.summary: South Africa's Parliamentary Monitoring Group took over ParliMeter, a platform tracking MP attendance, bills, committee meetings and questions to ministers, as its EU co-funded phase closed on 9 September 2026. The platform was built by the Organisation Undoing Tax Abuse, the Parliamentary Monitoring Group and OpenUp; a Cape Town event marked the handover.

2026-09-09-zaf-sanews-mohai-oversight-pr.summary: South Africa's deputy minister for planning, monitoring and evaluation, Seiso Mohai, made an oversight visit on 9 September 2026 to the Presidential Hotline call centre run by the State Information Technology Agency (SITA) in Centurion. The visit reviewed the case-management technology, escalation and resolution tracking, and scope for automation. The hotline has operated since September 2009.

2026-09-09-zwe-applynow-potraz-digital-t.summary: Zimbabwe's Postal and Telecommunications Regulatory Authority, with the Research Council of Zimbabwe and the Scientific and Industrial Research and Development Centre, called for policy research proposals under a National Digital Technologies Policy Research Programme, closing on 3 October 2026. The five priority areas include AI governance, data governance and cybersecurity, platform regulation and connectivity policy. No funding amount is given.

2026-09-10-ago-opais-africell-afrimoney-.summary: Africell's Afrimoney wallet in Angola, licensed by the national bank as a payment service provider, has 3 million users among the operator's 8 million subscribers, its commercial manager Rodrigo Conceição said at the Benguela International Fair. The wallet now allows transfers to any bank account, and Africell presents agent cash-out as a way to cut ATM queues on civil-service paydays.

2026-09-10-amaco-ge-vernova-mombasa-ai-d.summary: A Greek energy group has partnered with a United States energy-equipment company to supply gas turbines for its proposed US$1.5 billion artificial-intelligence data centre at Mombasa. The turbines would sit in an unmotorised floating power barge feeding local or national grids, and the facility is intended to serve East African demand for computing infrastructure.

2026-09-10-angop-caianda-actualizacao-re.summary: Citizens over 18 in the municipality of Caianda, in Moxico Leste province, began updating their electoral data after a one-stop public service desk opened there. The municipal administrator was the first to update his own, and urged traditional authorities, religious leaders and youth organisations to bring communities in ahead of the 2027 general elections.

2026-09-10-ben-beninespoir-douane-demate.summary: Benin's customs directorate announced on 9 September 2026 that passes for foreign vehicles are now issued entirely online through the national platforms, replacing paper forms. No platform name, cost or usage figures are given.

2026-09-10-bfa-rtb-conseil-ministres-26.summary: Burkina Faso's Council of Ministers, meeting in Bobo-Dioulasso on 10 September 2026, adopted a decree on the civil-status powers of diplomatic and consular agents, replacing a 1963 decree. It adds deputy heads of mission as civil-status officers, allows delegation, including exceptionally to honorary consuls, and introduces mobile consular missions for citizens living far from a consulate.

2026-09-10-biometricupdate-african-digit.summary: The next constraint on African digital identity is physical infrastructure rather than biometrics, wallets or credentials, this account argues. It cites a US$300 million raise by a pan-African infrastructure group for data centres, terrestrial fibre and subsea capacity, and a US$75 million commitment to digital infrastructure in Cameroon including an AI-ready data centre at Douala with its own power plant.

2026-09-10-biometricupdate-nigeria-digit.summary: Nigeria's education ministry says academic certificate authentication is now fully digitalised, with the whole credential evaluation and authentication process completed online through a dedicated government portal. The minister described it as capping several months of coordinated work.

2026-09-10-biometricupdate-south-africa-.summary: South Africa's communications minister told parliament the government is not pursuing any blanket policy restricting under-16s from social media, saying platforms should instead strengthen their own protections against harmful content. The position separates the country from a growing number of states, several of them African, adopting age-assurance requirements.

2026-09-10-cadreco-cote-divoire-reforme-.summary: Cote d'Ivoire's banking reform folds digital finance into a wider legal architecture in which competition between banks, payment institutions, electronic money issuers, fintechs, Islamic finance and microfinance turns on licences, their obligations and their cost. The Council of Ministers adopted two bills in April as part of it.

2026-09-10-cenfri-open-finance-oversight.summary: A research organisation sets out what African regulators need to weigh in supervising open finance, on the argument that the evidence of financial reliability for millions of people sits scattered across mobile wallets, savings groups and informal ledgers. Connecting that data, it argues, is how providers could design products for the unbanked and underbanked.

2026-09-10-cipesa-mozambique-internet-sh.summary: Mozambique's Constitutional Council ruled in July that a government must first have lawful authority to order an internet shutdown before it can justify one. An advocacy organisation reads the ruling as requiring proof both that the power was lawfully created and that it was exercised by a legally authorised body, and sets it against a wider continental pattern of shutdowns.

2026-09-10-citizen-govtech-2026-digital-.summary: South Africa marks twenty years of its government technology conference when the 2026 edition opens in Durban, hosted by the state IT agency with the communications department. It brings together government, industry, academia, entrepreneurs and citizens, with digital sovereignty among its themes.

2026-09-10-civ-fratmat-comexmap-cartogra.summary: Cote d'Ivoire opened a two-day workshop in Abidjan to update the trade data behind its digital mapping of trade agreements and flows. The session updates the collection of agreements, the statistics and the flow data on a platform the government treats as strategic for its position in international trade.

2026-09-10-civ-fratmat-ia-afrique-batir-.summary: Without reliable energy, solid infrastructure and technical skills, artificial intelligence risks deepening the continent's technological dependence rather than accelerating its development, an Ivorian engineer argues here. The piece puts the foundations before the applications.

2026-09-10-civ-linfodrome-cgeci-data-day.summary: Cote d'Ivoire's employers' confederation held the second edition of its data day in Abidjan, with the edition's objectives around data and artificial intelligence set out at the opening.

2026-09-10-civ-linfodrome-impact-ia-2026.summary: The second edition of Cote d'Ivoire's national conference on artificial intelligence opened in Abidjan under the Prime Minister's patronage, on the initiative of the digital transition and technological innovation ministry. Accounts of the event differ on which day it opened.

2026-09-10-cmr-kamerandroid-max-it-orang.summary: Orange Cameroon has closed its Orange Money Afrique app and moved its mobile money services into Max it, an app that also handles line management, bill payments, a marketplace and entertainment. On 24 August the Max it team apologised to users for system errors that blocked some operations after an update. The app carries a 3.7 out of 5 rating on Google Play from about 47,800 reviews.

2026-09-10-cod-congoguardian-isys-regies.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo's tax directorate wrote to the finance minister on 3 September 2026 alleging that central bank staff siphoned tax revenue by manipulating the ISYS-REGIES revenue platform, and sought their suspension and a judicial inquiry. On 10 September the Banque Centrale du Congo denied it, saying every action on the platform is logged and cannot be altered after validation.

2026-09-10-cog-groupecongomedias-mobilit.summary: A workshop in Brazzaville from 8 September 2026, run by the association Avenir NEPAD Congo with funding from the Konrad Adenauer Foundation, examined movement and trade between the Republic of Congo and the DRC, which share a border of about 2,400km. It closed with a 'Brazzaville Declaration' proposing measures to ease crossings, secure the border and increase trade.

2026-09-10-cog-lesdepeches-technologies-.summary: Congo-Brazzaville presents space technologies as a strategic lever for development - forest observation, agriculture, telecommunications and scientific training - with a delegation led by the head of state at the international space summit in Paris. No agency, programme or budget is named.

2026-09-10-connectingafrica-kenya-standa.summary: Kenya's communications regulator opened a 30-day public consultation on a standalone licence for colocation data centres. It says the proposal would give greater regulatory clarity, improve visibility of data-centre operations and support investment, and it follows a broader overhaul of the telecommunications market framework begun in 2025.

2026-09-10-cote-divoire-ministre-ia-stra.summary: Cote d'Ivoire's digital transition minister called for a move from artificial intelligence strategy to execution at the opening of the second national AI conference in Abidjan. It now falls to the country to take a new step and deploy solutions concretely for people's benefit, he said.

2026-09-10-cpv-expressodasilhas-moderniz.summary: Cabo Verde's prime minister named state modernisation and digital transformation, alongside climate action, decentralisation and youth opportunity, as the government's priorities for the new phase of its United Nations partnership, at a high-level meeting with the country team in Praia.

2026-09-10-cpv-governo-onu-alinhamento-c.summary: At a high-level meeting between Cabo Verde's government and the United Nations in Praia on 10 September 2026, the UN country team reported that the Cadastro Social Único, the national social registry, covers 64 per cent of the population. UN Resident Coordinator Patrícia Portela de Sousa said the next cooperation framework, for 2028–2032, will follow the new National Development Plan.

2026-09-10-cpv-maa-fiti-fisheries-inform.summary: Cabo Verde presented its fisheries transparency work at a Fisheries Transparency Initiative (FiTI) session during the 37th meeting of the FAO Committee on Fisheries in Rome. The country joined the FiTI Standard in 2023 and has set up a public Fisheries Information System publishing data on licences, landings, catches, revenue, subsidies and the legal framework.

2026-09-10-dza-algerie54-hydraulique-tro.summary: Algeria's water ministry and the digitisation high commission launched three services on the national digital services portal on 9 September 2026: remote applications for drinking-water and sewerage connections, and Hydro-Qualif, a qualification certificate for contractors bidding for public works. The portal now offers 150 services, up from 21 at launch, and runs on state data centres and a sovereign cloud.

2026-09-10-dza-elwatan-dzair-digital-ser.summary: Algeria's High Commission for Digitisation added five tax services to the national Dzair Digital Services portal on 9 September 2026, launched with the tax directorate at Tipasa. They are the tax roll extract, the non-taxation certificate, the C20 certificate of existence and tax registration attestations for individuals and companies.

2026-09-10-dza-elwatan-tebboune-guichet-.summary: Algeria's President Abdelmadjid Tebboune ordered the investment single window to be operational by the end of September 2026 and a national census of industrial land to start immediately, at a meeting on 9 September. He required all investment procedures to be digitised in coordination with the tax, state property and customs administrations. Customs launched an electronic single window for foreign-trade authorisations in August.

2026-09-10-echorouk-algerie-baddari-ia-e.summary: The higher education minister has directed the five higher schools specialising in economics, finance and management to modernise their training and embed artificial intelligence, at a working meeting at the Kolea hub. He set the instruction out on his own social-media account, and no curriculum, timetable or funding accompanies it.

2026-09-10-egy-youm7-niyaba-amma-vothaiq.summary: Egypt's Public Prosecution said on 10 September 2026 that official copies of five kinds of personal-status record, including Muslim and non-Muslim marriage and divorce certificates, can now be obtained through its online portal, built with the communications ministry. Users must verify their identity with the Digital Egypt portal's digital ID.

2026-09-10-eth-techreviewafrica-ethswitc.summary: Ethiopia's national payment switch EthSwitch presented its interoperable payments work at the Global Fintech Fest in Mumbai on 8–11 September 2026, where its chief portfolio officer Abeneazer Lakew joined a digital public infrastructure panel. EthSwitch said in May that its EthioPay instant-payment service handled over one million transactions worth 5.1 billion birr in a single day.

2026-09-10-financialafrik-bceao-cybersec.summary: The West African central bank's monetary policy committee found the union's banking fundamentals sound - liquidity near FCFA 7,000 billion, credit growing and solvency above the regulatory norm - while calling on banks to stay vigilant against cyberattacks. No incident count or supervisory instrument accompanies the call.

2026-09-10-gab-gabonreview-afrinic-ipv6-.summary: The regional internet registry presented its mission and programmes to Gabon's technical community at a workshop in Libreville, held at the initiative of the national internet exchange point. The session focused on the transition to IPv6 as IPv4 addresses run out, and on the registry's role in a more accessible and secure African internet.

2026-09-10-gab-gabonreview-aninf-alertes.summary: Gabon's national agency pushed back against reading its 900,000 intrusion alerts as evidence of a vulnerable national digital system, saying the figure shows a system capable of seeing threats rather than one already submerged by them. In a dossier seen by the publication it addresses the confusions in the public reaction and the controversy over firewalls.

2026-09-10-gab-intelligence-artificielle.summary: Staff of Gabon's public accounts and treasury directorate (DGCPT) took a three-day, practice-led course on digital tools and artificial intelligence at the Centre Gabonais de l'Innovation in Libreville. They followed cohorts from the Communication ministry and the Budget directorate; the CGI presents the course as part of wider support to help the administration put AI to work in its tasks.

2026-09-10-gha-ghanamma-viamo-231-voice-.summary: Viamo, a Canadian digital non-profit, launched 231, a toll-free voice service in Ghana built with MTN. Callers on any basic phone can put spoken questions to its offline AI assistant in Twi, Ewe, Hausa, Dagbani, Ga or English without data or an app. Ghana is Viamo's fourth such MTN platform after Liberia, Zambia and Rwanda.

2026-09-10-gha-myjoyonline-bog-digital-f.summary: Ghana's central bank says digital fraud incidents rose 98 per cent between 2022 and 2025 as financial criminals exploited the growth in digital transactions. Its second deputy governor said fraudsters increasingly targeting digital platforms, as more people pay and transfer electronically, requires a significant change in how financial crime is tackled.

2026-09-10-gin-224-n-lambe-api-l-infrast.summary: A LinkedIn post presents 224 N'Lambé, a Guinean language-infrastructure venture offering APIs for translation between French or English and Pular, Malinké and Soussou. It pitches the language data for voice assistants, chatbots, fintech, education and digital public services, with a paid professional tier offering API keys and usage limits.

2026-09-10-gin-visionguinee-data-center-.summary: Guinea's prime minister, Bah Oury, visited the national data centre on 9 September 2026 and said it is still not fully operational a year after its inauguration in September 2025, despite nearly US$10 million invested. He said the work is about 90% complete with one payment outstanding, and that he will propose measures to the president to bring it into service.

2026-09-10-gsma-closing-digital-divide-r.summary: The GSMA published research on 10 September 2026 on refugee women's mobile use, drawing on fieldwork with Venezuelan refugees in Colombia and in Mauritania's Mbera camp. It reports that refugee women in Ethiopia are twice as likely to have SIMs registered in someone else's name, that in Uganda about a quarter use the internet against half of men, and that in Tanzania identity rules push women to register SIMs through intermediaries.

2026-09-10-hespress-morocco-ai-research-.summary: A scientific review available from 1 September records an expansion of Moroccan research applying artificial intelligence to drought, water scarcity and rising temperatures. It covers forecasting tools, resource monitoring, irrigation, and the management of energy and heat inside cities, across water, agriculture, energy, cities and natural hazards.

2026-09-10-ictworks-fcdo-digital-develop.summary: An ICTworks commentary argues that the UK Foreign Office's Digital Development Strategy 2024–2030 remains official policy but has little identifiable funding. The only digital line in published allocations is £70 million over three years for the Global Tech directorate, while the AI for Development programme alone is a £53 million commitment. The July 2026 development policy paper does not list digital as a priority.

2026-09-10-itweb-africa-liquid-targets-d.summary: A pan-African fibre operator's Kenyan chief executive says the continent's data-centre capacity is becoming a major concern for African telecom executives, as the business pushes deeper into artificial intelligence and cloud services. He puts Africa at 0.6 per cent of the world's data-centre capacity.

2026-09-10-itweb-africa-mozambique-telec.summary: Mozambique's communications regulator recorded 391,723 consumer complaints in 2025, up 44 per cent on 2024, with 372,846 of the telecommunications complaints resolved and an average satisfaction index of 82 per cent. It attributes much of the rise to better recording rather than worse service, one operator's logged complaints having gone from 213 to 24,036 on a new incident-tracking system.

2026-09-10-itweb-africa-mtn-nigeria-100-.summary: A second account of the same milestone puts the operator's July gain at more than two million active subscriptions, from 98.64 million in June to 100.86 million, its strongest monthly rise of the year. Its chief executive has previously linked subscriber gains to stronger customer additions and rising data consumption.

2026-09-10-itweb-co-za-aws-23bn-africa-c.summary: A large cloud provider says it has invested more than US$819 million in African infrastructure since 2018 and committed a further US$1.5 billion to 2029, with 154 services now available in its Cape Town region. Its general manager for Sub-Saharan Africa told a Johannesburg summit the Africa strategy is increasingly aimed at local developers building for regional markets, and claimed more than a million Africans trained in cloud and AI skills.

2026-09-10-itweb-co-za-lesaka-first-prof.summary: A South African payments group reported a net profit of R47.3 million for the year to June 2026 against a loss of R1.63 billion a year earlier. Its executive chairman called it full-year profitability for the first time since the group was created in 2022 out of a predecessor company; the results accompany a brand refresh.

2026-09-10-itweb-co-za-mtn-ai-gigabyte-t.summary: South Africa's largest mobile operator is using artificial intelligence for revenue assurance, identifying leakage where fraudsters tunnel traffic through zero-rated sites such as university websites. Its chief executive said adoption has accelerated as practical applications emerge across the business; zero-rating here dates from the pandemic response.

2026-09-10-itweb-co-za-sentech-trims-los.summary: South Africa's state signal distributor cut its net loss after tax to R60 million in 2025/26 from R246 million, an improvement of about 76 per cent, and reported a clean audit with no material findings. The previous year's loss was driven mainly by a provision for expected credit loss reflecting customers' economic difficulties.

2026-09-10-ken-lulu-coastal-submarine-ca.summary: A planned submarine cable would link Mombasa to Lamu through five landing points along Kenya's coastline, with a parallel terrestrial route to keep services running if the seabed link is disrupted. The developers say it will extend resilient connectivity along 500 kilometres of coast and support data centres, cloud services and technology businesses; the consortium is anchored on the Vipingo special economic zone.

2026-09-10-ken-techtrends-bcg-digital-go.summary: Boston Consulting Group's eighth biennial Digital Government Citizen Survey found 87% of Kenyan respondents use AI at least weekly, against a global average of 64%. Kenya's adoption of digital government services is 49%, net satisfaction fell five points since 2024 to 64%, and only 12% of users reported no problems, the lowest share of any market surveyed.

2026-09-10-ken-us-tech-giants-flag-inves.summary: Executives from four large United States technology and payments companies told a Nairobi business summit that unpredictable taxes, regulations and approvals could deter new capital from Kenya. They said investors need policy certainty to commit and expand, a warning aimed at the country's bid to be East Africa's digital investment hub.

2026-09-10-kenya-ai-democracy-human-agen.summary: Kenya's special envoy on technology met a foundation representative to discuss the changing relationship between technology, democracy and human agency. The engagement covered the country's digital and artificial intelligence agenda and open government, with participation, accountability and information integrity as the stated tests.

2026-09-10-kenyaengineer-itw-africa-powe.summary: At two Nairobi conferences the talk was more physical than usual, this account records: behind every model, cloud service and digital transaction, speakers returned to electricity, fibre, data centres, transmission networks, regulation, capital and the engineers needed to keep it running.

2026-09-10-kictanet-africa-seat-ai-safet.summary: A Nairobi university hosted the first African dissemination of the International AI Safety Report 2026, convened with a foreign mission. It drew policymakers, researchers, civil society groups and technology firms around the question of whether African institutions can keep pace with a technology moving faster than the evidence needed to govern it.

2026-09-10-koreaherald-eximbank-afdb-ai-.summary: Korea's export-import bank signed a pact with the African Development Bank in Seoul to expand financing for African projects in artificial intelligence, critical minerals and green infrastructure. It was signed during the eighth Korea-Africa economic cooperation ministerial, and the two institutions are to seek expanded joint financing including in digital infrastructure.

2026-09-10-ktpress-kagame-space-summit-t.summary: Rwanda's president warned at the first International Space Summit in Paris that African countries risk losing access to valuable orbital and radio-frequency resources as the global space industry expands, and urged the continent to coordinate its interests and take a stronger voice in rule-setting. He said Africa should be a full participant in the sector rather than only a consumer of satellite services, and sought the removal of technology export restrictions.

2026-09-10-lanation-djibouti-cloture-tec.summary: The first cohort of Djibouti's TechKid programme completed seven weeks of coding, robotics and artificial intelligence at the national technology and innovation centre. Ten children aged 9 to 16 presented their work to parents, mentors and trainers.

2026-09-10-lanation-djibouti-conquete-es.summary: State media traces Djibouti's space programme since its launch in 2020 as the head of state attends the first international space summit in Paris. It records the training of the country's first specialists and the design and orbiting of two nanosatellites among the steps taken.

2026-09-10-lanation-guelleh-sommet-inter.summary: Djibouti's president took part in the second day of the first International Space Summit in Paris, arguing for a national space ambition serving development. The summit gathered delegations from more than 120 countries, including heads of state and government, institutional leaders, scientists, commercial operators and civil society.

2026-09-10-lbr-transforming-taxpayer-ser.summary: The Liberia Revenue Authority said on 10 September 2026 that it is developing an AI-powered contact center for taxpayer information on tax and customs matters. Its Tax Knowledge Governance Committee recently held a working retreat in Margibi County on the contact center's knowledge base; the Taxpayer Services Division is leading the work with the Kwagei Group.
