2026-09-10-lby-cbl-revenue-expenditure-s.summary: The Central Bank of Libya's statement of revenue and expenditure for January to August 2026, released on 10 September, records spending of about 68.7 billion dinars and oil revenue of 80.8 billion. Telecommunications revenue was 31.1 million dinars, and the General Authority for Communications and its affiliates spent 25.2 million dinars, almost all on salaries and running costs.

2026-09-10-lby-green-industry-centre-ind.summary: Libya's industry ministry has published an engineering report of industrial and environmental indicators compiled from its own database of facilities. It records 305 registered industrial establishments, 301 of them private, and 26,034 workers, alongside data on industrial activity, resource and energy consumption and waste management.

2026-09-10-lby-libyaalahrar-3090-arqam-w.summary: Libya's Public Prosecutor halted 3,090 national identification numbers issued on forged civil-status data at the Majdul civil registry office, where investigators found failures in managing family records. The numbers had been used to obtain documents claiming citizenship rights. One suspect was remanded in custody and arrest orders were issued for others, within the jurisdiction of the Sebha Court of Appeal.

2026-09-10-lby-unified-economic-number-p.summary: Libya's national council for the Unified Economic Number has approved the start of pilot operations for issuing the number electronically. It opens the first phase of a project to give economic, commercial and investment entities a single identity, implementing a Cabinet decision of 2026.

2026-09-10-leadership-nitda-data-soverei.summary: Nigeria is seeking to convert its digital policies and data-sovereignty requirements into investable opportunities for private capital through a national cloud infrastructure strategy, the technology development agency's director-general said. He was speaking at a Nairobi conference session on turning policy into investable demand.

2026-09-10-lesahel-delegation-algerienne.summary: Niger's telecommunications and post college received an Algerian mission led by the adviser for partnership and development of that country's operator skills-centre network. The visit follows a partnership accord of July aimed at establishing a digital competence centre, and is presented as reflecting the two heads of state's intent.

2026-09-10-leseco-maroc-ia-2030-phase-op.summary: Morocco's digital transition minister, Amal El Fallah Seghrouchni, presented the operational phase of the Maroc IA 2030 roadmap in Rabat on 8 September 2026. It includes green data centres at Dakhla, a network of regional JAZARI institutes and language models in Darija and Amazigh. Targets for 2030 are MAD 100 billion added to GDP, 50,000 jobs and 200,000 trained people.

2026-09-10-liquid-kenya-ai-next-growth-f.summary: The same operator is repositioning from connectivity provider to a layered artificial intelligence, cloud and cybersecurity business on top of its fibre backbone, its vice-president and chief executive said at a Nairobi conference. Connectivity becomes the foundation of digital infrastructure rather than the product, he argued, naming data-centre capacity as the concern African telecom executives raise most.

2026-09-10-lso-africanewsroom-bnc-smart-.summary: Lesotho and South Africa concluded a mid-term review of their Bi-National Commission in Pretoria on 9 September 2026 after three days of talks. Outcomes included faster work on Smart One-Stop Border Posts at Maseru and Ficksburg, progress on a new migration model for labour mobility, and Phase II of the Lesotho Highlands Water Project. The next full session is set for South Africa in 2027.

2026-09-10-malawi24-nrb-nzika-digital-id.summary: Malawi's national registration bureau is to introduce a digital identity wallet, giving citizens a digital version of their national identity alongside the existing physical card. It is presented as an additional way of presenting and accessing identification as use of digital services grows.

2026-09-10-maliweb-afrique-intelligence-.summary: Will Africa be an actor in the artificial intelligence revolution or a market absorbing technologies designed, trained and controlled elsewhere? A researcher sets out the dependence risks the continent faces, against a technology usually presented as universal and available to anyone who connects.

2026-09-10-mar-journalducanada-oncf-vide.summary: Morocco's national rail operator, ONCF, issued a 1.08 million dirham tender for a study to design a national video-surveillance system with AI analytics and central supervision by 2030, reported on 10 September 2026. The study will size cameras, data storage, transmission networks and supervision centres for later procurement. No budget for the full system has been announced.

2026-09-10-mar-librentreprise-tamwilcom-.summary: Morocco's government authorised Tamwilcom, by decree 2.26.576 of 3 August 2026, to invest up to 347 million dirhams over three years in venture capital funds on behalf of the Fonds Catalytique Startups, under the Digital Morocco 2030 strategy. Nine fund managers were pre-selected, covering fintech, agritech, edtech, healthtech and climate tech. The funds are expected to raise close to 2.5 billion dirhams for startups.

2026-09-10-mdg-newsmada-registre-social-.summary: Madagascar's single social registry, which covers about 2.7 million households or close to 12 million people, is being extended to eight more districts beyond the 20 already covered, the population ministry's director general said on 9 September 2026. A new survey is updating the data and extending coverage to urban areas, under the national social protection strategy for 2024–2030.

2026-09-10-moz24h-macra-surveillance-con.summary: Malawi's communications regulator MACRA bought a $1.5 million social-media monitoring system from Ghana's Hashcom, and more than a year on no institution has said publicly what it collects or who can access it. Civil society letters to MACRA's board, Parliament and the President in early 2025 did not halt it. The human rights commission abandoned a planned inspection, citing a lack of technical expertise.

2026-09-10-mwananchi-tanzania-uchumi-kid.summary: Tanzania's digital economy needs more investment, the deputy communications minister said at a tower company's fifteenth anniversary event in Dar es Salaam. The operator is targeting 4,500 sites in the country by the end of 2026, against more than 4,000 now.

2026-09-10-namibiansun-5700-grant-benefi.summary: More than 5,700 Namibian pensioners and other social-grant beneficiaries remain locked out of the government payment system after their grants were suspended during an identity verification exercise earlier in 2026, the gender equality and child welfare minister told the National Assembly. She said 15,785 were affected in all, of whom 10,066 had verified their identities, been reinstated and paid, and defended the exercise as ensuring public money reaches only legitimate beneficiaries while acknowledging it had delayed vulnerable people.

2026-09-10-ncc-cbm-digital-access-pwds.summary: Nigeria's communications regulator and a disability organisation called for greater investment in accessible digital infrastructure, technologies and skills so that persons with disabilities have equal access to the digital economy. The call opened a two-day digital citizenship training in Lagos.

2026-09-10-ner-gouv-conseil-ministres-pr.summary: Niger's Council of Ministers adopted on 10 September 2026 a draft ordinance creating a legal regime for the electronic press and a draft decree on press correspondents and accreditation of foreign media. The government said online media had lacked a legal framework, preventing the communication observatory ONC from regulating them. The decree gives the ONC an opinion on foreign-correspondent accreditation.

2026-09-10-newsday-econet-3g-shutdown-20.summary: Zimbabwe's largest operator will shut down its 3G network by the end of December 2027, its chief executive said, retiring 3G before 2G because 2G remains widely used in rural areas by subscribers with basic feature phones. The operator is accelerating investment in 4G and 5G.

2026-09-10-newsday-global-south-ai-techn.summary: China's pursuit of technological self-reliance offers Africa a conceptual lesson, this piece argues: technological sovereignty is not isolation but the bargaining power to make independent choices in global technical cooperation, and to escape permanent dependency.

2026-09-10-nga-abuja-inquirer-tetfund-n6.summary: Nigeria's Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund) has approved N1bn for an ICT Experience Centre in each of the six geopolitical zones, N6bn in all, and the South-East centre at the Federal Polytechnic, Oko, was commissioned by the First Lady on 10 September 2026. The centres are to train students and lecturers in AI, cybersecurity, robotics and software. The approval date is not given.

2026-09-10-nga-businessday-1bn-space-inv.summary: Nigeria's Federal Executive Council has approved six new satellites, two for communications and four for Earth observation, and a space transport and propulsion centre, innovation minister Kingsley Tochukwu Udeh said at the International Space Summit in Paris. He said the sector could absorb more than US$1 billion and sought private and foreign partners. Approval dates are not stated.

2026-09-10-nga-newstimes-ncc-zero-rated-.summary: Nigeria's communications commission launched zero-rated data access to approved educational platforms in Abuja on 10 September 2026, starting on 1 October. Education minister Tunji Alausa said about five million students will get 100 MB of free data a day, worth about N180 billion a year; more than 240,000 schools are geomapped in the education management information system.

2026-09-10-nigeria-afcfta-certificate-of.summary: Nigeria has cut the processing time for continental free-trade certificates of origin to 24 hours from more than five days, the trade minister announced in Abuja. She disclosed it at the third-quarter meeting of the free trade area's central coordination committee, presenting it as easing business for exporters.

2026-09-10-nigeria-ai-economy-who-protec.summary: By the time Nigeria assembles the policies needed to regulate artificial intelligence, parts of the technology may already be in service, this piece argues. It takes as its example the open-access multilingual voice and text assistant the federal government unveiled in May with a private developer, a ministry and a research centre, and asks who answers when such systems get it wrong.

2026-09-10-nigeria-cameroon-mfum-ekok-bo.summary: Nigeria and Cameroon launched a border modernisation initiative for the Mfum-Ekok corridor during a joint assessment by their customs administrations. It covers border infrastructure, technology-driven solutions and the reduction of trade bottlenecks, and is presented as supporting the continental free trade area.

2026-09-10-nilepost-uganda-ai-sovereignt.summary: Uganda is developing an artificial intelligence strategy aimed at building national capacity to develop, govern and benefit from the technology rather than depend on foreign systems, its science and technology minister said. He named data, computing infrastructure, energy, models, applications and skills as the foundations that need investment.

2026-09-10-rwa-ktpress-bnr-cashless-camp.summary: The National Bank of Rwanda launched a national cashless campaign, #TwagiyeKashiresi, in Rubavu District on 7-9 September 2026. Its data show 85.3% of Rwandans hold a digital account but 92% still mainly use cash for everyday spending. The campaign promotes eKash, the national interoperable payment system, and moves to Huye and Rusizi later in September.

2026-09-10-safha1-egypt-lawyers-administ.summary: Lawyers filed an urgent suit at Egypt's Administrative Judiciary Court to suspend and annul the Ministry of Justice's prepaid fees for its remote criminal litigation platform, Al Safha Al Oula reported on 10 September 2026. The claim argues that court fees must be set by statute, not by ministerial decision; the Helwan lawyers' syndicate branch declared its support.

2026-09-10-sajim-emergent-data-governanc.summary: A peer-reviewed study of how Kenyan state agencies operationalise big data analytics, published in a South African information-management journal. It examines the data governance that emerges in practice as public-sector uptake grows.

2026-09-10-saps-bodycam-tender-facial-re.summary: South African Police Service body-worn cameras must be able to conduct facial recognition, according to state IT agency tender documents. The requirement sits in the bid specification for a three-year contract covering body-worn and vehicle dashboard cameras and related software, and says the solution must also integrate with various security platforms; bids close on 29 September.

2026-09-10-sdn-dabanga-bankak-outages-di.summary: Repeated outages on Bank of Khartoum's Bankak app and Faisal Islamic Bank's Fawry service disrupted transfers, payments and trade in Sudan between late August and early September 2026, pushing demand back to cash, Radio Dabanga reported on 10 September. A banking expert said some traders now accept only cash; an IT consultant called on the Central Bank of Sudan to lead a national interoperable payment system.

2026-09-10-sdn-fjajpress-police-forum-di.summary: Sudan's police leadership said at the fifth Police Forum in Khartoum that passports, national ID cards and driving licences will be obtainable online by phone or computer. Public service complexes have abolished cash through a partnership with seven banks, and completed transactions rose from 206,162 in 2025 to 522,225 in 2026; services are to extend to five more states.

2026-09-10-sen-aps-conseil-ministres-com.summary: Senegal's Council of Ministers on 10 September 2026 instructed the state digital company Sénégal Numérique SA, under the Prime Minister's office, to set up a national system for gathering and handling citizens' concerns, fed by ministries, local authorities and dialogue mechanisms. The meeting also set 15 September for the 2026 supplementary finance bill and 30 September for the 2027 finance bill.

2026-09-10-sen-seneweb-e-justice-jokko-a.summary: Senegal officially launched two judicial digital platforms at the Lat Dior courthouse in Dakar, in a ceremony chaired by the justice minister's chief of staff. The launch is presented as a turning point in the modernisation and citizen accessibility of the judicial system.

2026-09-10-sen-seneweb-plan-formation-nu.summary: Senegal's civil service ministry held a national workshop in Dakar to validate the digital training plan for state employees, which is now in validation. The one-day session was co-chaired by the civil service director-general and the telecommunications and digital minister's chief of staff.

2026-09-10-sierra-leone-child-data-prote.summary: Sierra Leone is strengthening safeguards for children's personal data as government institutions move toward more connected digital public infrastructure. The communication, technology and innovation ministry, with a United Nations children's agency and a digital public infrastructure centre, ran a three-day workshop on guardrails for children examining how government systems handle their data.

2026-09-10-som-dawan-somaliren-datacite-.summary: Somalia's research and education network, SomaliREN, joined DataCite and set up the country's first DataCite national consortium as its lead. Somali universities and research centres can now issue persistent identifiers (DOIs) for more than 30 types of research output, including theses, datasets and journal articles. No cost to members is given.

2026-09-10-ssd-mictps-rfb-eardip-fibre-r.summary: South Sudan's ICT ministry invited bids on 10 September 2026 to design, supply and operate a fibre backbone on Route A-B, financed under the World Bank-funded Eastern Africa Regional Digital Integration Project (grant E1780). Payments will be made directly by the World Bank.

2026-09-10-swz-positivenews-finscope-202.summary: Eswatini's Central Statistical Office has begun fieldwork for the FinScope 2026 Consumer Survey, covering 3,200 households in all four regions until the end of October 2026. It is the first such survey since 2018, when financial inclusion stood at 87%, and will look at use of banking, mobile money and digital financial services as well as access.

2026-09-10-tanui-amcham-american-tech-st.summary: Kenya's principal secretary for ICT and the digital economy gave the keynote at an American Chamber of Commerce roundtable in Nairobi on US technology partnership, with the US Commerce Department, the US Trade and Development Agency, Google, Microsoft and Oracle in the room. He named the energy backbone, data protection and data governance frameworks, and infrastructure for cloud and AI capacity as the government's investment priorities, and asked US firms for long-term partnerships. The post names no agreement or commitment.

2026-09-10-tcd-toumaiwebmedias-lac-citoy.summary: In an open letter to Chad's president, reported on 10 September 2026, Aboubakar Mahamat Tidjani says internet access in Lac province has been heavily restricted for nearly two years on security grounds, harming pupils, teachers and traders. He asks for phased, secured restoration where conditions allow, retention of essential services and better public information on the measure.

2026-09-10-techafricanews-airtel-unicef-.summary: An operator's foundation and a United Nations children's agency say they have connected more than 1,200 Nigerian schools to digital learning. The foundation said working with local governments helped it identify the schools that stand to gain most, and cites a Lagos primary school where pupils use the tools and connectivity provided.

2026-09-10-techafricanews-camtel-fibre-s.summary: Cameroon's state telecommunications operator is extending fibre connectivity to schools, covering communities from the northern to the southern and the eastern to the western regions. It presents the programme as digital inclusion in education, aimed at improving school internet access and pupils' reach to digital educational resources.

2026-09-10-techafricanews-kenya-armenia-.summary: Kenya and Armenia have opened discussions on cooperation in digital technologies, education, ICT, trade and investment, after a meeting between the ICT principal secretary and Armenia's ambassador. Artificial intelligence and cloud computing were identified as potential areas alongside youth skills; no instrument has been signed.

2026-09-10-techafricanews-kenya-digital-.summary: Kenya is extending its digital learning initiative to 10,384 public junior schools, distributing smartboards and laptops, digitising curriculum content and training teachers. It is run by the ICT ministry through its authority, with the education ministry, the curriculum development institute and the teachers' service commission.

2026-09-10-techafricanews-mtn-nigeria-10.summary: Nigeria's largest operator crossed 100 million active subscribers for the first time in July, ending the month at 100.86 million and 51.76 per cent of the market on regulator data. The national active base rose to 195.11 million from 192.23 million in June and teledensity reached 90 per cent, with the three other operators at 66.76 million, 23.63 million and 3.61 million.

2026-09-10-techafricanews-mtn-south-suda.summary: The operator's South Sudan chief executive restated its commitment to expanding connectivity and opportunities for young people through ICT hubs, at a youth dialogue at the University of Juba. The event was convened by a United Nations agency with the youth and sports ministry.

2026-09-10-techafricanews-new-last-mile-.summary: Tech Africa News reports that by May 2026, 40 operators in 37 African markets had launched commercial 5G fixed wireless access, using outdoor receivers mounted on homes instead of laying fibre. Safaricom reported 132,060 5G fixed wireless subscribers in the first half of its 2025/26 financial year, up 53%, and Airtel sells such services in Nigeria and Kenya.

2026-09-10-techafricanews-nigeria-regula.summary: Nigeria's technology development agency is shifting from a traditional regulatory posture to actively enabling market growth and private investment in digital infrastructure, its director-general said in a fireside chat at a Nairobi conference. The session formed part of a workshop on the country's digital infrastructure opportunity.

2026-09-10-techcabal-papss-regulatory-hu.summary: An account of what the pan-African payment system has built in four years and the regulatory obstacles still limiting it: 30 countries connected, about 200 financial institutions, and cross-border payments settling in an average of seven seconds against a 120-second design target. The system says it has cut the cost of cross-border transfers by up to 95 per cent and that volumes have grown more than tenfold over the past year.

2026-09-10-techcabal-south-africa-paymen.summary: South Africa is rebuilding both the rules of participation in its payments system and the infrastructure underneath, three payments executives said at a Johannesburg roundtable. A proposed activity-based regulatory model would let non-banks and fintechs offer payment services directly rather than through a sponsoring bank, alongside richer payment data and faster cross-border rails.

2026-09-10-techreviewafrica-atu-spectrum.summary: The African telecommunications union's secretary-general called for stronger alignment among African administrations on spectrum policy, at the 11th Africa spectrum management conference in Tunis. He singled out the mid-band ranges where mobile broadband demand will need capacity and coordination, and argued that policy must extend beyond identifying frequencies to how spectrum is priced and licensed.

2026-09-10-tgo-lomebougeinfo-portail-ser.summary: Togo launched a new version of its public-services portal at new.service-public.gouv.tg. Existing logins remain valid and users can see their earlier requests without re-filing; the portal handled more than 400,000 requests in 2024. No launch date or cost is given.

2026-09-10-thecitizen-tanzania-tighter-s.summary: Communications stakeholders in Rukwa have proposed tighter SIM card registration controls, including a 24-hour waiting period before a person may register another line, as the region records a high number of reported cyber-fraud cases. They also want the communications regulator to work more closely with other agencies on enforcement.

2026-09-10-thecitizen-tcra-mobile-fraud-.summary: Tanzania's communications regulator ran a three-day awareness campaign in Morogoro against mobile phone fraud and online scams. It put the national caseload at 7,334 reported cases, of which 2,495 or 34 per cent came from Rukwa and 2,079 or 28.4 per cent from Morogoro.

2026-09-10-thecitizen-zanzibar-integrate.summary: Zanzibar's government is introducing a monitoring framework to curb delays in development projects, its deputy minister for finance and planning told the House of Representatives at Chukwani. No system name, supplier, cost or timetable is given.

2026-09-10-thisday-airtel-africa-1-1bn-n.summary: A pan-African operator has earmarked US$1.1 billion for expanding and upgrading its network across its African operations, its chief executive said in a broadcast interview. He said spending has already risen from about US$120 million to US$390 million across 14 markets, with Nigeria its biggest.

2026-09-10-thisday-cbn-cyber-technology-.summary: Nigeria's central bank warned that cybersecurity can no longer be treated as each bank's internal responsibility, because a vulnerability in one institution or technology provider can cascade through an increasingly interconnected financial system. Banks' growing reliance on fintechs, payment service providers and cloud operators has widened the channels through which incidents spread, it said, calling for a collective defence.

2026-09-10-thisday-ispon-national-softwa.summary: Nigeria's institute of software practitioners says it will launch a national software industry registry within six months, announced at the inauguration of its new executive council in Lagos. Its president said the registry will document software achievements and developers to make the industry globally visible, criticising the loss of record of milestones already achieved.

2026-09-10-thisday-ncc-device-management.summary: Nigeria's communications regulator is strengthening enforcement of type approval for SIM-enabled devices through a technology-enabled framework, supported by a device management system that determines compliance electronically. The underlying obligation is in the communications statute, which requires approval before a device may be connected.

2026-09-10-thisday-ncc-q2-2026-ftth-isp-.summary: Nigeria's fibre-to-the-home subscriptions rose to 319,735 in the second quarter of 2026 from 214,750 in the first, across 99 licensed operators, on the communications regulator's statistics. Internet subscribers on core ISP networks reached 420,989 over the same period.

2026-09-10-times-eswatini-eptc-world-ban.summary: Eswatini's posts and telecommunications corporation is seeking a US$26 million World Bank loan to finance the Digital Eswatini Project, under a bill tabled in Parliament. The bill would authorise the finance minister to issue a government guarantee of up to that amount for the loan.

2026-09-10-times-eswatini-immigration-bi.summary: Eswatini's Immigration Bill would set up an information system to vet foreign nationals before entry and block those who fail requirements or are judged a risk. It was discussed at a consultation between Parliament and stakeholders in Ezulwini. The workshop heard that implementation would cost about E6 million.

2026-09-10-todaysecho-papss-china-india-.summary: The pan-African payment system plans to connect to China's largest payment system and to have India's live on its platform by the first quarter of 2027, its chief executive told a Lagos media session, with Brazil and others later in the year. He put transaction volumes up more than 1,000 per cent year on year and 30 countries connected against about 38 targeted by the end of 2026.

2026-09-10-togofirst-togo-ai-lab-public-.summary: Togo's AI laboratory is recruiting a technical lead for public-sector artificial intelligence projects, on a renewable one-year contract in Lome with applications open to 2 October. The lab is run by the public service efficiency and digital transformation ministry with a research centre at a United States university, and the role reaches agriculture, environment and local languages.

2026-09-10-tza-dailynews-integrate-prima.summary: Tanzania is integrating the digital systems used in primary healthcare, including digital payments to community health workers, the ICT director at the Prime Minister's Office for regional and local government, Erick Kitali, said in Arusha on 10 September 2026. He said the government has prepared a blueprint including a joint dashboard to track services and payments from community to national level.

2026-09-10-undp-tanzania-funguo-innovati.summary: More than 9,000 people attended the 12th Innovation Week Tanzania in Dar es Salaam, where the UN Development Programme's FUNGUO programme marked five years by giving TZS 1.3bn to a fifth cohort of 14 businesses, reported on 10 September 2026. The week also saw the launch of the Tanzania Innovation Nexus, a platform matching innovators with investors and mentors. FUNGUO says it has channelled over US$3m to innovators since 2021.

2026-09-10-vanguard-fg-scraps-data-charg.summary: Nigeria's federal government unveiled an initiative for zero-rated access to educational platforms and content, letting students reach approved platforms without paying for internet data. The education minister presented it as removing one of the largest barriers to technology-driven learning; the government also signalled moves to regulate internet access for under-16s.

2026-09-10-vanguard-inec-amupitan-ai-ele.summary: Nigeria's electoral commission chairman told a conference on responsible artificial intelligence and elections in Ottawa that successful deployment in electoral administration depends more on strong institutions, governance structures and safeguards than on the sophistication of the technology. He presented the country's experience of institutionalising responsible AI for that work.

2026-09-10-von-eu-eib-boost-africa-impac.summary: The EU and the European Investment Bank said at a forum in Abuja that their Boost Africa programme invested €108 million through venture capital funds over its first decade, attracting about €400 million more from other investors. EU ambassador Gautier Mignot named Nigeria a key beneficiary, and the EIB said it had launched new operations there.

2026-09-10-wearetech-burundi-ia-seoul-am.summary: Burundi presented the ambitions of its national artificial intelligence strategy at the Korea-Africa economic cooperation ministerial in Seoul, seeking the financing and partnerships to turn it into concrete projects. The strategy, validated in April, provides for strengthening connectivity, data infrastructure and local skills; the country's digital capacity remains limited.

2026-09-10-wearetech-creditchek-rachete-.summary: A Nigerian technology company has acquired a Ugandan banking-software firm, bringing every stage of credit - from verifying the borrower's identity to repayment - onto a single platform. The companies say the combination lets African financial institutions assess loan applications faster and lend more readily; no price is disclosed.

2026-09-10-wearetech-egypte-velents-impl.summary: An Egyptian enterprise artificial intelligence company has expanded into Bahrain with a local telecommunications operator. The partnership is to offer businesses there autonomous virtual assistants automating customer service, sales and recruitment, under local data-protection rules.

2026-09-10-wearetech-egypte-zeal-leve-10.summary: An Egyptian technology company has raised US$10 million for payment tools that add a layer to shop card terminals, identifying customers at the checkout so merchants can build loyalty. The money is to take the product into the Middle East, Europe and Africa; no investor is named.

2026-09-10-wearetech-guinee-equatoriale-.summary: Equatorial Guinea intends a mechanism letting the state capture part of the revenue large digital platforms generate in its market, a question sharpened where companies operate from abroad. The vice-president asked in Malabo for talks to be opened with one such platform and with comparable alternatives.

2026-09-10-wearetech-jacob-pinkus-bague-.summary: A South African founder profiled here is building contactless payment into a smart ring, detaching the act of paying from the bank card and the phone. His company, founded in 2021, sells the ring as a way to pay without a wallet, card or handset, on a prior synchronisation with the user's account.

2026-09-10-wearetech-kenya-kopo-kopo-sol.summary: A Kenyan technology company has launched an updated payment-integration tool letting businesses embed settlement options directly in their own software, merchant sites and mobile applications. It says more than 40,000 merchants can now automate refunds, send grouped payments and process transactions faster.

2026-09-10-wearetech-malloron-nair-ia-ge.summary: A South African economist and technology entrepreneur profiled here co-runs a consultancy, founded in 2019, that helps firms of every size modernise their information systems. It deploys targeted programmes to bring start-ups' technology up to date.

2026-09-10-xgl-elysee-declaration-space-.summary: Angola, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Madagascar, Mauritius, Rwanda and Tunisia are among the 49 states that signed, with the European Space Agency, a declaration on space-based scientific data published by France's presidency on 10 September 2026. It commits signatories to open access to satellite observation data, save for exceptions such as security and personal data, and to common exchange standards.

2026-09-10-zaf-worldbank-strategic-frame.summary: The World Bank published a strategic framework for offshore wind in South Africa, prepared by the Carbon Trust with the Department of Electricity and Energy and funded by ESMAP, posted on 10 September 2026. It estimates about 95 GW of technical potential along the 2,800 km coastline and notes that rules on site exclusivity and seabed leasing have not been enacted.

2026-09-10-zmb-cajnewsafrica-ict-centre-.summary: The Smart Zambia Institute, the government's e-government agency, endorsed President Hakainde Hichilema's Grow Zambia Agenda 2026–2031, which carries eight national targets on digital infrastructure, CAJ News reported on 10 September 2026. National coordinator Percy Chinyama said the institute is building a real-time dashboard reporting progress on all targets to Cabinet, and is digitising 2.5 million smallholder farmers under the National Farmer Registry.

2026-09-10-zwe-businesstimes-rbz-ghost-w.summary: The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe has closed ghost, fictitious and duplicate mobile money wallets after linking the Civil Registry's national database to mobile-money subscriber records, Business Times reported on 10 September 2026. The number of wallets closed, the operators affected and when the linkage began are not given.

2026-09-10-zwe-newziana-child-online-pro.summary: Zimbabwe's ICT minister, Tatenda Mavetera, told the National Assembly on 9 September 2026 that the National Child Online Protection Policy is moving to implementation. A committee with the education and social welfare ministries is installing content gateways on public free Wi-Fi and school networks so children reach only age-appropriate material; a social media ban would need further consultation.

2026-09-11-afreximbank-papss-network-exp.summary: PAPSS chief executive Mike Ogbalu III said in Lagos on 11 September 2026 that transaction volumes on the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System rose about 1,000% and values about 120% between comparable periods of 2025 and 2026. The network covers more than 30 countries, 24 central banks, over 200 banks and payment providers and 16 switches; about 10 countries joined in 2026.

2026-09-11-afriksoir-cote-divoire-pacte-.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's digital transition ministry, the employers' confederation CGECI and the national chamber of commerce signed a national pact on artificial intelligence on 11 September 2026, at the IMPACT IA conference in Abidjan. The pact is a voluntary framework and creates no legal, financial or investment obligations, with specific costed commitments left to later work. Signatory firms undertake to join a national AI alliance.

2026-09-11-ago-angop-imprensa-nacional-d.summary: Angola's state printing house, Imprensa Nacional, opened its own data centre in Luanda on 11 September 2026 to support official and security documents and document authentication systems. It has more than 170 terabytes of storage and over one terabyte of processing memory. The institution produces about 600 million fiscal stamps a year. The investment was not disclosed.

2026-09-11-ago-novojornal-exim-bank-usa-.summary: The Export-Import Bank of the United States announced a US$99.6m loan to the mobile operator Africell for network technology in Angola. Its statement says the loan will pay for American and European equipment and help Angola diversify its technology sources and keep national control of its infrastructure. No approval date or terms are given.

2026-09-11-anthropic-kenya-election-prop.summary: Anthropic said it removed an account that used Claude to produce Kenyan political posts in batches of 50 ahead of the 2027 election, TechCabal reported on 11 September 2026. The posts praised energy cabinet secretary Opiyo Wandayi and attacked opposition figures; Anthropic found no evidence of government involvement and no sign the content reached real people.

2026-09-11-ben-cadreco-tresor-penalites-.summary: Benin's Directorate-General of the Treasury and Public Accounting told road users in a communiqué dated 2 September 2026 to check for unpaid traffic penalties on the securoute.anatt.bj portal and pay them by 1 October 2026. After that date, unpaid penalties will be recovered by force during road journeys.

2026-09-11-ben-tribuneonline-seme-custom.summary: The Nigeria Customs Service offered Benin's customs a real-time exchange of declarations, manifests, transit data, risk profiles and enforcement alerts at the Sèmè–Kraké one-stop border post on 11 September 2026. Comptroller-General Adewale Adeniyi said the two services work under one roof but not on one system; Benin's customs chief endorsed the proposal. No timetable is given.

2026-09-11-bfa-lefaso-conseil-national-s.summary: Burkina Faso's National Statistics Council held its first 2026 session on 11 September, reviewing a draft 2027 statistical programme costed at CFA 10.6 billion, 52.7% funded by the state. The statistics institute INSD reported 67.8% execution of the 2025 programme. It plans an observatory using satellite, mobile-phone and web data and AI to produce indicators for all 351 communes.

2026-09-11-business-focus-nira-new-natio.summary: Uganda's new national identity cards cannot yet be used for SIM registration, banking or driving permits because partner institutions have not connected to the registration authority NIRA's data-exchange module, MPs heard on 9 September 2026. NIRA's director Rosemary Kisembo said the module began on 31 March 2026 and MTN was the first partner onboarded. The committee chair asked NIRA not to recall old IDs and to set activation timelines.

2026-09-11-businessincameroon-cameroon-e.summary: Cameroon's SME minister, Achille Bassilekin III, and the new EU ambassador agreed in Yaoundé on 11 September 2026 to focus cooperation on finance, digitalisation and value chains for small businesses. Financing agreements signed on 16 June 2026 total about CFAF37.16bn, including CFAF9.83bn each for Digital Business Boost for Africa and Digital Acceleration in Cameroon. The EU says MyBusiness.cm has helped formalise more than 25,000 businesses.

2026-09-11-bwa-businesstechafrica-nation.summary: The Bankers' Association of Botswana has launched a national electronic know-your-customer project letting banks check customer identities against the national citizen database instead of certified photocopies of identity cards. The report notes the association launched a similar eKYC system in 2021. No launch date is given.

2026-09-11-capitalfm-allafrica-plp-nethe.summary: About 1,700 young people from refugee and host communities in Kenya's Garissa and Turkana counties are to receive 25 weeks of training in AI, cloud computing and data analytics. Power Learn Project runs it with the ILO, Microsoft and Garissa County, funded by the Netherlands; over 700 have enrolled in Garissa and 16 of 37 hubs have begun. No funding sum is given.

2026-09-11-cioafrica-garissa-refugee-you.summary: Power Learn Project, the ILO, Microsoft and Garissa County Government marked the Garissa rollout of a 25-week digital skills and employment programme for refugee and host-community youth, funded by the Netherlands under the PROSPECTS Partnership. It targets 1,700 young people in Garissa and Turkana; over 700 have enrolled in Garissa, and Microsoft is providing up to 1,000 certification vouchers.

2026-09-11-cod-actualite-bcc-dement-isys.summary: The Central Bank of Congo denied on 10 September 2026 that state revenue had been deleted or altered in ISYS-RÉGIES, its revenue-collection platform built since 2021 with the French development agency AFD. It said gaps against its NAVISION accounting system mostly involve the savings bank CADECO, which is outside its clearing house, and are settled in a monthly reconciliation. AFD and the finance ministry signed a €12.5 million convention in 2021 to digitise and link the revenue agencies.

2026-09-11-cog-adiac-beb-child-protectio.summary: Congo's Minister of Social Affairs, Marie-France Lydie Hélène Pongault, met the US NGO Both Ends Believing in Brazzaville on 10 September 2026 about the Children First Software, a tool to monitor children in care institutions and help return them to their families. The NGO, a partner since 2023, said it would help build the platform, train ministry staff and supply equipment.

2026-09-11-dza-lejourdalgerie-foncier-re.summary: Algeria's prime minister, Sifi Ghrieb, ordered an immediate national census of industrial, agricultural and tourism land on 10 September 2026. Provincial governors are to collect the data on a unified template, and a map of available land is due at the investment promotion agency's one-stop window before the end of September, supported by the High Commission for Digitalisation.

2026-09-11-gab-lunion-cnamgs-120000-bene.summary: A Cour des comptes audit found about 120,000 people improperly registered among nearly one million on the file of Gabon's fund for the economically weak, managed by the health insurer CNAMGS, against some 900,000 actually covered. The court calls for the data to be cleaned and criticises poor traceability of spending on medical evacuations abroad.

2026-09-11-gha-gna-dbg-boa-mi-ai-agricul.summary: Development Bank Ghana, Opportunity International and the agricultural lending guarantor GIRSAL launched Boa Mi, a WhatsApp-based AI service giving farmers agronomic advice and loan officers portfolio data, in Accra on 11 September 2026. A pilot with rice farmers produced more than 8,500 queries in three months with 75% user satisfaction. It runs in English, with Twi, Dagbani, Ewe and Ga versions in development.

2026-09-11-gha-nca-5g-spectrum-licensing.summary: Ghana's National Communications Authority concluded the 700 MHz stage of its 5G spectrum award on 11 September 2026, giving two lots to MTN Ghana, the only qualified applicant, for US$100.9 million. The 2.3 GHz band, sought by Telecel Ghana and Goal Telecommunications, is under-subscribed, and the 3 GHz band is over-subscribed; both go to the next stage.

2026-09-11-gin-nimba224-rgph4-donnees-re.summary: Guinea's National Statistics Institute met officials of the Ministry of Women, Family and Solidarity on 10 September 2026 about using data from the fourth population census to identify people with disabilities, towards a planned disability card. The institute's director-general, Makan Doumbouya, asked staff to assess which data could be used. No timetable is given.

2026-09-11-gnb-ang-educacao-digitalizaca.summary: Guinea-Bissau's transitional prime minister, Ilídio Vieira Té, pledged on 11 September 2026 to raise education to 15 per cent of the state budget and to pay teachers where they work, through bank branches or Orange Money. The education ministry's plan also includes computerised teacher posting and digital audit.

2026-09-11-gnq-gqpress-tres-leyes-regist.summary: Equatorial Guinea's Chamber of Deputies unanimously approved three government bills on 11 September 2026: reforms of the Mining and Hydrocarbons laws and a new press freedom law. The mining reform creates a national geological service, a mining registry and cadastre, a national mining management platform and a digital geological registry, with licences awarded by international tender as the general rule. The press law replaces a 1997 law that does not cover digital journalism.

2026-09-11-iafrikan-africa-ai-data-centr.summary: An iAfrikan analysis sets two September 2026 announcements — Egypt's $1bn sovereign AI data-centre programme with about $200m committed to its first phase, and MTN's 150MW venture across Nigeria and South Africa — against power and water limits. It cites Africa Data Centres Association figures of 360MW active, 238MW under construction and 656MW planned, and McKinsey's estimate of 1.5–2.2GW of demand by 2030.

2026-09-11-itweb-anthropic-kenya-ai-infl.summary: Anthropic's September 2026 report on misuse of its AI models, covering December 2025 to August 2026, says a domestic Kenyan actor used Claude to mass-produce political posts made to look like grassroots opinion ahead of the 2027 election. Many praised energy secretary James Opiyo Wandayi. Anthropic found no evidence of government involvement and said the content did not reach genuine users.

2026-09-11-itweb-cape-town-cashless-driv.summary: The City of Cape Town will pilot cashless payments at three of its 18 driving licence testing centres, in Brackenfell, Fish Hoek and Strand, from 1 October 2026. Mayoral committee member JP Smith said the pilot will test feasibility across all centres. The city began cashless payments at its customer interaction centres and vehicle licensing offices in July.

2026-09-11-ken-kenyans-ntsa-licence-rene.summary: Kenya's National Transport and Safety Authority said on 11 September 2026 that a fault on its side was blocking online driving-licence renewals and first-time applications, which showed a blank page. It gave no date for a fix. The outage came a day after the authority began a nationwide document-compliance crackdown with the police.

2026-09-11-ken-kra-public-notice-approve.summary: The Kenya Revenue Authority has approved 15 vendors to provide electronic tracking of goods under customs control, moving the Regional Electronic Cargo Tracking System to a multi-vendor, user-owned model for dry-cargo and fuel seals. KRA-owned seals will be phased out by 26 October 2026. The notice does not list the vendors.

2026-09-11-ken-odpc-draft-additional-sen.summary: Kenya's Office of the Data Protection Commissioner published a draft notice on 11 September 2026 adding political affiliation and trade union membership to sensitive personal data under section 47 of the Data Protection Act 2019. It applies only to data transferred from countries whose law already treats them as sensitive. Public comment is invited; no deadline is stated.

2026-09-11-ken-peopledaily-korea-eximban.summary: Kenya's Treasury principal secretary, Chris Kiptoo, met Korea Eximbank in Seoul on 10 September 2026 to review the Ksh129.4 billion (US$1 billion) Economic Development Cooperation Fund framework. Projects discussed include the completed Ksh12.17 billion Kenya Advanced Institute of Science and Technology, the Intelligent Transport System and the recently approved Konza Digital Media City. No new amount or approval date is given.

2026-09-11-ken-techreviewafrica-undp-kon.summary: The UN Development Programme in Kenya and the Technopolis Development Authority signed a letter of agreement to put sovereign AI infrastructure into operation at the Konza Data Centre, TechReview Africa reported on 11 September 2026. The infrastructure is to support the AI Accelerator programme, green technology and applied research. No cost, capacity or timetable is given.

2026-09-11-ken-thestar-national-cybersec.summary: Kenya's National Cybersecurity Agency has a Director General in post but is not yet fully operational, according to a government implementation committee communiqué reported on 11 September 2026. Recruitment of technical and administrative staff and board appointments are still under way. Parliament received the memorandum for Legal Notice No. 89 of 2026, the order establishing the agency, in June.

2026-09-11-kenyans-wandayi-responds-anth.summary: Kenya's energy cabinet secretary, Opiyo Wandayi, said on 11 September 2026 that an Anthropic threat-intelligence report did not show that he or his ministry took part in an AI-generated social media campaign praising him over electricity tariffs. The report described one actor using Claude to produce Kenyan political posts in batches of 50 and found no evidence of government involvement.

2026-09-11-lbr-frontpageafrica-ayee-summ.summary: Liberia Telecommunications Authority chairman Clarence Massaquoi told the AYEE youth summit in Monrovia on 11 September 2026 that the regulator has an agreement with the youth and sports ministry to set up 15 digital hubs, one per county, backed by more than US$200,000. He also announced a partnership with the education ministry to connect 156 public high schools to high-speed internet.

2026-09-11-lbr-frontpageafrica-cybercrim.summary: A FrontPageAfrica commentary compares Liberia's Cybercrime Act of 2025, whose printed text is marked approved on 3 July 2026, with the 2019 Kamara Abdullah Kamara Act that decriminalised sedition and criminal libel of the President. It sets out the Act's speech-related offences, including cyberstalking and harmful data messages, and a judge-ordered interception power. It also notes a pending amendment, introduced in March 2026, to criminalise insulting language online.

2026-09-11-lbr-frontpageafrica-iaa-digit.summary: Liberia's Internal Audit Agency launched iSoft, a public-sector audit management system, in Monrovia on 10 September 2026 to replace paper-based audits. Director General David Kemah said auditors can plan audits, track findings and management responses, and produce real-time reports, with an audit trail for every government institution. No cost or supplier is given.

2026-09-11-lbr-liberianobserver-iaa-isof.summary: Liberia's Internal Audit Agency launched the iSoft Public Sector Internal Audit Management System in Monrovia, reported on 11 September 2026. Director General David Kermah said it replaces paper-based auditing and lets auditors plan audits, track findings and management responses, and produce reports from a central dashboard. No cost is given.

2026-09-11-lby-lana-abusalim-electronic-.summary: Abu Salim municipality in Tripoli, Libya, began using an electronic archiving system in its human resources department on 11 September 2026, storing staff data, records and documents electronically. The municipality says it will speed retrieval and reduce reliance on paper. No supplier or cost is given.

2026-09-11-le-meridien-cote-divoire-77-p.summary: Côte d'Ivoire selected 77 priority artificial intelligence use cases at the IMPACT IA 2026 conference in Abidjan, which closed on 11 September 2026, covering public administration, agriculture, health and education. Digital minister Djibril Ouattara said a national roadmap with financing is to be adopted at a further meeting in three weeks. The government plans to own specialised AI models adapted to local languages and conditions.

2026-09-11-malawi-nzika-digital-id-walle.summary: Malawi's National Registration Bureau announced the Nzika Digital ID Wallet, to launch on 16 September 2026, which will hold a digital copy of the national ID card with the same validity as the physical card. The bureau says 99% of citizens hold a national ID and more than 13.5 million people are enrolled; it expects the wallet to cut card-printing costs.

2026-09-11-mar-h24info-347-mdh-fonds-cat.summary: Morocco's startup catalytic fund, run by the digital transition ministry and managed by Tamwilcom, can invest 347 million dirhams over three years in venture capital funds backing digital startups, following decree 2.26.576 of 3 August 2026. Nine management companies have been shortlisted, and the funds are expected to raise about 2.5 billion dirhams.

2026-09-11-mar-ncsi-morocco.summary: The index version of 11 September 2026 gives Morocco full marks on critical information infrastructure (12 of 12). It also gives full marks on personal data protection (4 of 4). Cybersecurity policy scores 12 of 15. Cyber crisis management scores 2 of 9, and military cyber defence 2 of 6.

2026-09-11-mdg-moov-metfp-gip-pix-compet.summary: Madagascar's Ministry of Technical Education and Vocational Training and France's GIP Pix signed a partnership on 11 September 2026 to develop and certify young people's digital skills. Its eight areas include preparing learners for certification, setting up exam centres, training trainers and tracking candidates. The two will study adding Pix to the CAP, BEP and vocational and technological baccalaureate curricula.

2026-09-11-moz-techreviewafrica-intic-ce.summary: Mozambique's prime minister, Benvinda Levi, told the national ICT institute INTIC on 5 September 2026, at the Maputo International Fair (FACIM 2026), to speed up and extend its digital certification system to all state institutions. She was briefed on INTIC's work on cybersecurity, certification and licensing. No timetable or budget is given.

2026-09-11-mus-lexpress-mauritius-vision.summary: Mauritius's Cabinet approved the final report of Mauritius Vision 2050 on 11 September 2026, aiming for an economy of about USD 50 billion (about Rs 2,300 billion) by 2050. It rests on prosperity, sustainability and inclusivity, and names digital among seven strategic sectors alongside financial services, tourism, logistics, the ocean economy, high-value agriculture and life sciences.

2026-09-11-mwi-channelafrica-nzika-walle.summary: Malawi's National Registration Bureau is launching the Nzika wallet on 16 September, an app holding a digital national ID, birth certificate and marriage certificate, downloadable from Google Play and the App Store. Its spokesman, Norman Fulatira, said physical ID cards, held by more than 9 million registered citizens, stay valid because smartphone and internet access remain limited.

2026-09-11-ner-modernghana-aes-passeport.summary: Niger launched its own biometric passport, with President Abdourahamane Tiani enrolled first, making it the last of the three Alliance of Sahel States members to replace the ECOWAS passport. The system has five categories, including a hajj passport, and the Libyan firm Al Itissan Al-Jadeed is involved in production. Existing ECOWAS passports remain valid.

2026-09-11-nga-vanguard-ncc-type-approva.summary: The Nigerian Communications Commission has begun implementing a Device Management System that checks whether SIM-enabled devices meet its type-approval rules, using a central register of IMEI numbers, Vanguard reported on 11 September 2026. The first phase registers devices in stock and new imports with the Nigeria Customs Service; non-compliant and stolen devices can be blocked from networks. The commission says the system gives it no access to device contents.

2026-09-11-nga-von-nfiu-joint-financial-.summary: The Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit is working with banks, fintechs and insurers to design a Joint Financial Intelligence Collaboration platform for sharing intelligence on illicit financial flows, Voice of Nigeria reported on 11 September 2026. The Abuja meeting was backed by the British High Commission and the Convention for Business Integrity. No launch date or cost is given.

2026-09-11-sahara-reporters-nigeria-regu.summary: Nigeria's education minister, Tunji Alausa, said on 10 September 2026 that the government will regulate internet access for children under 16, with details to be announced by security officials within days or weeks. He also said zero-rated access should not extend to every platform calling itself educational. No rules have yet been published.

2026-09-11-sdn-sudanews-mof-pos-framewor.summary: Sudan's Federal Ministry of Finance signed a framework agreement with 11 companies to bid in restricted tenders to supply mobile point-of-sale devices for collecting public revenue in state institutions. IT director-general Lamia Mohamed Nour described the devices as a secure way to collect revenue. No contract value, signing date or delivery schedule is given.

2026-09-11-sen-le-senegal-adopte-son-pla.summary: Ministries and partners meeting in Dakar on 10 September validated Senegal's 2026-2029 national plan for state employees' digital skills, which aims to train all 183,502 state agents through a 25-module common core, ten sectoral programmes of 150 modules and an acculturation track for the 35,857 least digitally prepared, backed by 500 ambassadors. A survey of 1,878 agents found 57% at beginner level and 15% advanced; in a pilot with 583 agents early in 2026, 88 to 92% of those who sat the certification passed but 70% of those enrolled did not sit it. The FORCE-N programme, run by the Université numérique Cheikh Hamidou Kane with the Mastercard Foundation, designed the plan and supplies its online platform.

2026-09-11-senegal-public-sector-digital.summary: Senegal launched a digital skills programme for civil servants, led by the public service ministry with Cheikh Hamidou Kane Digital University through the Mastercard Foundation-backed Force-N programme. Training covers data, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and digital public services. Results will be tracked by completion rates, certifications and the inclusion of women. No cost, start date or number of trainees is given.

2026-09-11-sle-sierraloaded-childrens-va.summary: Sierra Leone's communications and technology ministry, with UNICEF and the Centre for Digital Public Infrastructure, held a three-day workshop on safeguards for children's data in connected government systems, reported on 11 September 2026. Officials from 16 ministries worked on birth registration, vaccination records, education data and social protection, including who may access vaccination records and where breaches could occur.

2026-09-11-sle-sierraloaded-ncra-2025-vi.summary: Sierra Leone's National Civil Registration Authority held a two-day meeting on 10 and 11 September 2026 to validate the draft 2025 Vital Statistics Report, focusing on fertility and mortality data. Director General Mohamed Mubashir Massaquoi called for greater national ownership of civil registration data and said figures from multiple external sources produce inconsistencies.

2026-09-11-sle-statehouse-bio-depac-data.summary: Sierra Leone's President Julius Maada Bio told the Presidential Development Partners Committee in Freetown on 10 September 2026 that the 2026 Population and Housing Census faces a US$37 million financing gap. Government has committed US$24 million, about US$15 million of it disbursed, and partners about US$1.5 million; Census Night is set for 1 December 2026.

2026-09-11-som-dawan-opinion-strategic-c.summary: An opinion piece on Somalia's Strategic and Communication Forum 2026 in Mogadishu, organised by the information ministry, notes that Deputy Prime Minister Jibril Abdi Rashid Haji Abdi proposed requiring NIRA national identification to open accounts, citing security and misinformation. The author calls for the proposal to be weighed against privacy and free expression, and for a mechanism to follow up the forum's recommendations.

2026-09-11-swz-positivenews-biometric-vo.summary: Eswatini's Elections and Boundaries Commission is rolling out continuous voter registration with computers and biometric capture ahead of the 2028 national elections, its deputy chairperson Sipho Tembe said. The system targets people newly turned 18 and those who have changed constituency, and is meant to prevent duplicate registration. No cost or supplier is given.

2026-09-11-swz-positivenews-matsapha-nat.summary: Matsapha became the first municipality in Eswatini to roll out the National Postcode and Addressing Project, with street signs due within eight weeks of 11 September 2026. The scheme, run by the regulator ESCCOM, gives every property a unique address linked to Google Maps. Phase one covers only properties inside the municipal boundary.

2026-09-11-tanzaniainvest-nldi-national-.summary: Tanzania's Ministry of Lands is building the National Land Data Infrastructure, a central store of official land records and geographic data, deputy minister Kaspar Mmuya said on a visit to the project offices in Dodoma. It will supply new aerial imagery and a platform for stakeholders to obtain data. On 8 September 2026 he told the valuers' and town planners' registration boards to speed up digital adoption.

2026-09-11-tcd-lendjampost-code-travail-.summary: Chad's Council of Ministers adopted on 3 September 2026 a draft Labour Code replacing the 1996 law. Platform workers are presumed to be employees where at least two criteria of subordination are met, platforms must be more open about the algorithms that direct work, and social security cover is extended. The draft also raises the end-of-contract payment on fixed-term contracts from 5% to 7%.

2026-09-11-techafricanews-gabon-national.summary: Gabon held workshops in Libreville on 9–10 September 2026 to review a draft public-private partnership between the state digital-infrastructure company SPIN and Gabon Fiber to run and extend the national fibre backbone. The project covers about 3,420km: 1,769km existing and 1,651km planned. Signature was scheduled for 14 September 2026.

2026-09-11-techafricanews-senegal-digita.summary: Senegal validated a national digital training plan for civil servants at a workshop on 10 September 2026, run by the public service ministry with the telecoms and digital ministry. Cheikh Hamidou Kane Digital University provides technical support through the FORCE-N programme, backed by the Mastercard Foundation; topics include data, AI, cybersecurity and digital public services.

2026-09-11-techmoran-plp-netherlands-ai-.summary: Power Learn Project is training 1,700 young people from refugee and host communities in Kenya's Garissa and Turkana counties in AI, cloud computing and data analytics over 25 weeks. Backed by the ILO, Microsoft and Garissa County and funded by the Netherlands, it has enrolled more than 700 learners in Garissa; women make up 35% of applicants. No funding amount is given.

2026-09-11-tgo-atop-certificat-nationali.summary: Togo's directorate for nationality and identity said on 11 September 2026 that its online nationality-certificate platform has received 241,617 applications and processed 179,690, or 74%, with average processing now about four months. The figures were given in Lomé as 300 final-year schoolgirls received free certificates under a programme for 4,200 girls nationwide.

2026-09-11-the-star-wandayi-distances-hi.summary: Kenya's Energy Cabinet Secretary Opiyo Wandayi said on 11 September 2026 that his ministry neither authorised nor took part in an AI-generated social media campaign praising its withdrawal of a Kenya Power tariff rise. A report found an unnamed actor used the Claude chatbot to produce batches of 50 posts under #PowerReliefKE, and found no evidence of government involvement.

2026-09-11-thepointng-reactions-fg-free-.summary: Nigeria's education minister, Tunji Alausa, said students in public senior secondary schools and tertiary institutions will receive 100MB of free daily data for approved educational platforms from 1 October 2026. The Nigerian Communications Commission runs the scheme with MTN, Airtel and Globacom; the ministry and the commission jointly approve platforms, which must meet data-protection and net-neutrality requirements.

2026-09-11-tnm-malawi-ocl-data-centre-cl.summary: Telekom Networks Malawi bought OpenConnect Limited's Tier 3 data centre at Kanengo, Lilongwe, for K12 billion, about US$6.9 million, unveiling it on 11 September 2026. TNM will link it with its Limbe data centre into one cloud platform to offer data centre as a service and host local AI platforms.

2026-09-11-tun-alchourouk-systeme-inform.summary: Tunisia's Ministry of Family, Women, Children and the Elderly brought into service a new information system for child protection delegates on 11 September 2026, built by national teams. It digitises and analyses case data on children at risk and children in conflict with the law. The ministry plans two training sessions for delegates in regional offices during September.

2026-09-11-uga-chimpreports-mobile-money.summary: Uganda's Ministry of Works and Transport said on 10 September 2026 that test runs of mobile money toll payment on the Kampala-Entebbe Expressway were complete, with dedicated lanes to follow. It did not say which platforms, what charges or when. Parliament's infrastructure committee is examining the reported UGX 122 billion five-year toll operation contract with Egis.

2026-09-11-uga-chimpreports-zombo-pdm-ta.summary: Thirty-one of the 61 Parish Development Model tablets issued in Uganda's Zombo District do not work, forcing parishes back to paper records, district officials said. The tablets handle data capture, disbursement tracking, biometric verification and the Wendi digital wallet, and ICT ministry rules bar local repair. Zombo has disbursed UGX 21.6bn to 22,263 beneficiaries since 2022.

2026-09-11-uga-mulengeranews-ura-etax2-d.summary: The Uganda Revenue Authority told manufacturers on 11 September 2026 that its eTax2 platform, in development since February 2026, will be web-only and will replace Tax Identification Numbers with National Identification Numbers and Business Registration Numbers. URA said the change is meant to fix duplicate and fragmented records in the taxpayer register.

2026-09-11-wearetech-cote-divoire-livrai.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's government took note on 9 September 2026 of a public-private partnership with Zipline to build and run a national drone network delivering medical supplies and blood products. A 27-month first phase covers Daloa, Biankouma, San Pedro and Kouto, with ten centres planned in all. The US government funds the infrastructure and the Ivorian state pays for operations; the contract value is not stated.

2026-09-11-wearetech-senegal-plan-nation.summary: Senegal validated a national digital training plan for civil servants on 10 September 2026, setting common training content graded by role and responsibility. It covers digital tools, data management, information systems, online public services, artificial intelligence and cybersecurity, and is to be assessed by skills acquired and certifications obtained. No budget or timetable is given.

2026-09-11-zaf-dailymaverick-iec-audit-t.summary: South Africa's Electoral Commission told the Electoral Court on 11 September 2026 that its audit trail shows no ANC activity on the online candidate nomination system in two of the six municipalities where the party blames glitches for missing the 28 August deadline. The commission says its servers had no downtime, and that 2,274 candidates from 45 parties were captured but never submitted.

2026-09-11-zaf-techcentral-digital-id-pl.summary: Zambia's ICT regulator ZICTA completed a key ceremony establishing a national root certification authority, eight days after Namibia's regulator CRAN launched its DigiNam public key infrastructure on 31 August 2026. South Africa has no state system deployed; three private providers are accredited, and Home Affairs plans infrastructure hosted at SARS by 31 March 2027 and roll-out in 2027/28.

2026-09-11-zmb-mwebantu-court-convicts-v.summary: A Lusaka magistrate convicted vlogger Joseph Chishimba on 11 September 2026 under section 54 of Zambia's Cyber Security and Cyber Crimes Act 2021 for forwarding to a WhatsApp group, in October 2024, a screenshot making allegations about presidential aide Chipokota Mwanawasa. The court found forensic evidence showed it was sent from his phone, though the post itself was not recovered. Sentencing was adjourned.

2026-09-11-zwe-openparly-unvalidated-tit.summary: Zimbabwe's justice minister Ziyambi Ziyambi told Parliament that the Digital Land Administrative Platform becomes the sole authoritative property register when the title-deed validation period ends in July 2027. Unvalidated paper deeds will then not be usable to sell or transfer land, though ownership is not lost. Validation costs US$215 including fees and VAT.

2026-09-12-ago-correiokianda-imprensa-na.summary: Angola's state printer, Imprensa Nacional, inaugurated its own data centre in Luanda on 11 September 2026. Board chair Lando Teta said it will let the printer produce and certify high-security state documents in-house rather than buying them abroad, and offer authentication and traceability services to private companies.

2026-09-12-alecso-charte-ethique-ia-vers.summary: The Arab League's education, culture and science organisation ALECSO has published an official English version of its Charter on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence, adopted earlier in 2026. The charter sets ethical rules for AI in education, culture and science across Arab states, including respect for privacy and human rights.

2026-09-12-ben-gouv-unicef-628-equipemen.summary: UNICEF handed Benin's Ministry of Secondary Education 628 items of computer equipment on 11 September 2026, including desktops, laptops, projectors and printers, for 43 secondary schools in nine departments and eight departmental education offices. The equipment will set up 12 new digital classrooms, adding to 55 already in place in UNICEF's areas. No value is given.

2026-09-12-brics-new-delhi-declaration-2.summary: The 140-paragraph New Delhi Declaration adopted at the 18th BRICS Summit on 12 September 2026 commits members to implement a separate Leaders' Statement on the Global Governance of AI, which was not published on the chairship's site as at 13 September. Its technology chapter also covers digital public infrastructure, cybersecurity and submarine cables.

2026-09-12-civ-fratmat-impact-ia-2026-77.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's second national AI conference, IMPACT IA 2026, closed in Abidjan on 11 September 2026 having identified 77 priority AI use cases. Digital minister Djibril Ouattara said a roadmap for the national AI strategy is due within three weeks.

2026-09-12-cmr-khalel-ekok-mfum-osbp-cus.summary: The Nigeria Customs Service and Cameroon's customs administration began a joint assessment of the Ekok-Mfum one-stop border post on 8 September 2026 and launched a border modernisation initiative to digitise customs workflows. Cameroon's customs director general Fongod Nuvaga called for real-time data sharing and joint risk management; a joint operational agreement is being drafted. No cost or completion date is given.

2026-09-12-cod-7sur7-mbadu-carte-okapi-i.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo's minister delegate for the diaspora, Crispin Mbadu Phanzu, said in a first-year review reported on 12 September 2026 that his ministry has introduced the OKAPI card for Congolese by origin who took another nationality, and is developing a digital identification system for the diaspora. No launch date, issuing body or enrolment figure is given.

2026-09-12-cod-acp-proposition-loi-viole.summary: Christelle Vuanga, a member of the Democratic Republic of Congo's National Assembly, announced she will table a bill this parliamentary session amending the penal code and the 2023 digital code to protect victims of non-consensual sharing of intimate images. She proposes prison terms of five to ten years with fines, and heavier penalties where blackmail or minors are involved.

2026-09-12-cod-acp-tshisekedi-ordonnance.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo's President Félix Tshisekedi signed an ordinance-law organising statistical activity, the 98th Council of Ministers reported on 11 September 2026. It governs the production, dissemination and archiving of official statistics and national censuses, names the Institut national de la statistique as principal statistical authority, and applies its confidentiality rules at once to operations under way.

2026-09-12-cod-opinioninfo-onip-identifi.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo plans to start national population identification in mid-December 2026, the 98th Council of Ministers heard from interior minister Jacquemain Shabani. The national population identification office, ONIP, will run the operation. The government said funding expected from partners and ONIP's own capacity could affect the timetable. No cost is given.

2026-09-12-cod-opinioninfo-ratification-.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo's Council of Ministers on 11 September 2026 adopted a bill to ratify the ordinance-law organising official statistics, submitted by the planning minister. The law sets principles of professional independence and statistical confidentiality, and bars use of data collected for statistics for control, prosecution or sanctions outside cases the law provides.

2026-09-12-cog-adiac-ccf-hoz-fablab-wome.summary: Congo-Brazzaville's Women's Advisory Council signed a partnership on 11 September 2026 with Hoz Fablab, a Brazzaville technology training centre, to train selected women students in digital skills for six months. The scholarship programme centres on designing, building and hosting websites.

2026-09-12-cog-adiac-congo-kazakhstan-fi.summary: Congo-Brazzaville and Kazakhstan are working to build and launch Congo's first Earth-observation satellite, Kazakh deputy prime minister Zhaslan Madiyev said after meeting President Denis Sassou N'Guesso in Paris, reported on 12 September 2026. The satellite is to monitor forests, farming, mining and flood-prone areas, and the talks also covered AI training for Congolese officials. No cost or launch date is given.

2026-09-12-cpv-expresso-mcc-elegivel-can.summary: Cabo Verde is among 42 countries listed as candidates for a new Millennium Challenge Corporation compact in the US agency's fiscal year 2027 report, published at the end of August 2026. The country has completed two compacts and had a third cancelled. Cabo Verde's ministry for special projects and fund access did not say whether it will apply.

2026-09-12-dza-algerian-darja-corpus-a-3.summary: Version 2 of the Algerian Darja Corpus, an open dataset on Zenodo mirrored on Hugging Face, holds 11,151 long-form conversational transcripts totalling about 34.3 million words (around 53 million subword tokens). This release adds 1,408 transcripts from media and tech channels and reruns a 15-stage cleaning pipeline including deduplication and dialect-purity filtering.

2026-09-12-egy-ahram-fra-real-time-credi.summary: Egypt's Financial Regulatory Authority has required consumer finance and small-business lenders to report to the credit bureau I-Score in real time, under board decisions 174 and 175 of 2026. Lenders must report approvals, disbursements, repayments, terminations and legal action on each loan.

2026-09-12-egy-egyptwindow-wuud-raqmana-.summary: An opinion column in Egypt Window, published as the school year opened on 12 September 2026, questions Egypt's education digitisation. It notes the education minister's 4 September pledge of free tablets for about 700,000 secondary pupils a year, over 1.2 million devices in total, and coding classes for 800,000 pupils, and argues that devices alone do not secure equal access given connection costs and teacher shortages.

2026-09-12-egy-newscentral-bread-subsidy.summary: Egypt's supply ministry has removed 850,000 people from the food subsidy system since June 2026, and targeting reforms are set to exclude millions more next year. The government says about 66 million people rely on subsidised bread.

2026-09-12-egy-youm7-madbouly-mujammaa-t.summary: Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly toured a technology-equipped government services complex in Green Island village, Kafr El Sheikh, on 12 September 2026, one of those built under the Hayah Karima rural initiative. He said such complexes should be judged on the service citizens receive, not on the building or the number of counters.

2026-09-12-egy-youm7-superhero-academy-a.summary: More than 6,000 children and young people from every governorate graduated from the third cohort of Egypt's Superhero Academy cybersecurity programme on 12 September 2026, with communications minister Raafat Hindi attending. The academy is run by the National Telecommunication Institute with the telecoms regulator's computer emergency team, EG-CERT, and industry partners.

2026-09-12-expertise-france-sila-appel-c.summary: A French-funded initiative for AI in the Mediterranean is taking applications from AI startups based in Algeria, Egypt, Lebanon, Morocco and Tunisia, with up to ten to be selected for grants of EUR 10,000 to 30,000 each. The call, implemented by Expertise France and financed by the French foreign ministry, closes on 14 September 2026; the page carries no date of its own.

2026-09-12-gha-graphic-nca-700mhz-spectr.summary: Ghana's National Communications Authority awarded two 700 MHz lots to MTN Ghana, the only qualified bidder, after opening best price offers on 11 September 2026. This account gives the fee as US$109.9 million; the regulator's release puts it at US$100.9 million.

2026-09-12-gha-yaw-opoku-mensah-criticis.summary: A former deputy spokesman for Ghana's education ministry, Yaw Opoku Mensah, said on Asaase Radio on 11 September 2026 that senior high school placement now runs on a third-party application, CloudSys, instead of the ministry's in-house system. He linked the 2026 placement problems, including students assigned to schools they did not choose, to the change.

2026-09-12-gin-mediaguinee-revue-mi-parc.summary: Guinea's Ministry of Modernisation of the Administration and the Public Service began a four-day mid-term review of its operational action plan at Forécariah on 12 September 2026, chaired by minister Faya François Bourouno. The review is to assess delivery, identify obstacles and set priorities for the rest of 2026.

2026-09-12-hiiraan-somalia-first-satelli.summary: Türkiye's ambassador to Somalia, Alper Aktaş, said in Mogadishu on 10 September 2026 that Somalia is expected to launch its first satellite in 2027, with a satellite operations and space research facility planned in Warsheekh district, Middle Shabelle. No Somali government agreement, budget or instrument is cited.

2026-09-12-iafrica-vodafone-egypt-cassav.summary: Vodafone Egypt and Cassava Technologies launched what they call Egypt's first AI factory, selling GPU capacity on NVIDIA hardware to government and business with data kept in the country. The piece places it within Vodafone Egypt's plan to invest more than EGP 20 billion this fiscal year and the minister's stated policy of courting several infrastructure partners at once.

2026-09-12-ken-css-cj-koome-make-new-app.summary: Kenya's interior cabinet secretary, Kipchumba Murkomen, appointed Lorna Ogolla Omondi and Jerop Joy Kibor to the board of the National Cybersecurity Agency for three-year terms, in a gazette notice dated 11 September 2026. The same round of notices named a chair and four members of the Kenya National Innovation Agency board.

2026-09-12-lbr-cdc-youth-league-accuses-.summary: Liberia's opposition CDC youth league demanded an investigation into Liberia Water and Sewer Corporation head Mohammed Ali and gender minister Gbeme Horace-Kollie. Its statement of 12 September 2026 alleges Ali posted on Facebook a spreadsheet of names, addresses, ages and schools of child abuse and neglect survivors, supplied by the minister. The allegations are the league's.

2026-09-12-moz-360mozambique-tmcel-parce.summary: Mozambique's finance ministry and communications ministry invited national and foreign bidders to express interest, within 15 days, in becoming strategic partner of the state telecoms operator Tmcel, possibly including a partial sale of the state's shares. The process was authorised by Government Resolution 67/2026 of 21 August; no amount is stated.

2026-09-12-mus-defimedia-national-crime-.summary: Mauritius published the National Crime Agency Bill 2026 on the National Assembly website, creating a lead agency to investigate financial crime, cybercrime and serious organised crime. It would repeal the Financial Crimes Commission Act 2023 and allow interception and real-time collection of communications data on a judge's order.
