The Assembly resumes on 20 October and the powers are not yet in force.

2026-09-12-mus-national-assembly-nationa.summary: Mauritius's National Assembly published the National Crime Agency Bill around 12 September 2026, setting up a lead agency to investigate financial crime, cybercrime and serious organised crime. The bill creates divisions including a Cybercrime Division and a Digital Forensic Laboratory, and repeals the Financial Crimes Commission Act 2023. The bill text carries no date or number.

2026-09-12-newswatch-nigeria-national-so.summary: Nigeria's IT development agency NITDA is driving a National Sovereign Cloud Initiative to keep sensitive data and essential digital services under Nigerian law and reduce reliance on infrastructure hosted abroad. The programme builds on the 2019 Cloud First Policy; no budget or timetable is given.

2026-09-12-nga-thisday-cac-ai-corporate-.summary: Nigeria's Corporate Affairs Commission is working with Google and other partners to bring AI into company registration, including service in English, Hausa, Yoruba, Igbo and Pidgin, registrar-general Hussaini Ishaq Magaji said at the commission's retreat in Bauchi. No launch date is given.

2026-09-12-nga-thisday-drli-independent-.summary: The Digital Rights Lawyers Initiative called for an independent audit of Nigeria's electoral technology and protection of voters' biometric data before the 2027 elections, at a PrivCon 2026 panel in Lagos on 1 September. It warned that weak oversight of the electoral commission's systems could damage public trust.

2026-09-12-primenews-ghana-nca-mtn-700mh.summary: Ghana's National Communications Authority assigned two 700 MHz lots, the most one applicant may win, to MTN Ghana for a licence fee of US$100.9 million. MTN was the only qualified bidder, which closes the 700 MHz stage of the 5G spectrum process; the 2.3 GHz and 3 GHz bands remain open.

2026-09-12-projectm-malawi-nzika-digital.summary: Malawi's National Registration Bureau is to launch the Nzika Digital ID Wallet at the Bingu International Convention Centre in Lilongwe, letting citizens carry a verified digital copy of their national ID on a phone. The homeland security minister will preside; no launch date is given.

2026-09-12-rfi-koafec-seoul-afdb-korea-a.summary: The Korea-Africa economic cooperation summit, KOAFEC, closed in Seoul on 11 September 2026 with agreements between the African Development Bank and South Korea towards an AI hub for Africa. One is a memorandum on co-financing and preparing government projects; no sums are reported.

2026-09-12-sanews-nzimande-global-south-.summary: South Africa's science and innovation minister Blade Nzimande told the Pujiang Innovation Forum in Shanghai on 12 September 2026 that the Global South must produce and own emerging technologies such as AI and quantum, not only consume them. He warned that science and technology are being used as weapons by some states.

2026-09-12-sen-ia-administration-publiqu.summary: Senegal's public service and telecommunications ministries, with the FORCE-N programme, validated a national training plan to give state employees digital and AI skills, with priority training for more than 35,000 agents. A first programme of five modules is ready to deploy, covering grades A, B and C plus modules for managers, and the plan targets at least 70% participation in exams and a 75% pass rate. A pilot early in 2026 trained 583 staff from the industry, digital and public service ministries and showed heavy drop-out at the exam stage.

2026-09-12-sen-seneweb-hackathon-cif-dig.summary: Team Mule Hunters won the first Senegalese edition of the CIF-DigiCoop-WA+ hackathon run by the West African financial institutions' confederation, taking 1.5 million FCFA for an anti-money-laundering compliance tool. Ten finalist teams, chosen from 65, spent 72 hours on compliance and automated microcredit scoring.

2026-09-12-sen-seneweb-nelvia-plateforme.summary: A school management platform called NELVIA was launched in Thiès on 12 September 2026 for Senegal's public and private schools, bringing pupil records, timetables, marks, finances and parent communication into one system. It issues QR-verifiable documents and a unique pupil identifier, the NELVIA ID.

2026-09-12-shuttlers-lagos-ride-share-te.summary: Lagos bus-sharing company Shuttlers is bringing back doorstep pickup through a service called Shuttlers Pod from 25 September, its chief executive told TechCabal. The firm says it runs more than 430 buses a day and has carried more than 10 million journeys.

2026-09-12-sle-sierraloaded-flot-digital.summary: Sierra Leone's First Lady Fatima Bio launched Flot, a fintech platform built with Zenith Bank Sierra Leone and Visa, in Freetown on 12 September 2026; it offers a Visa card for international payments. Communications Minister Salima Mormorna Bah said the government plans a Startup Act, expected in the first quarter of 2027, and an Innovation Investment Fund.

2026-09-12-som-wargeyska-dawan-somalilan.summary: The Bank of Somaliland met the country's banks and mobile money operators, including ZAAD, eDahab and KaashPlus, in Hargeisa on 11 September 2026 to plan a national credit information system. They discussed each party's role, the data required and how it will be shared, and agreed the central bank will lead the credit information bureau.

2026-09-12-swz-eswatinipositivenews-imba.summary: Eswatini's Elections and Boundaries Commission registered young women to vote at the Umhlanga reed dance at Mbangweni Royal Residence, reported on 12 September 2026. Registration requires a personal identification card and uses biometric capture, and the commission paired it with civic education ahead of the coming elections.

2026-09-12-the-hindu-brics-new-delhi-dec.summary: BRICS leaders adopted the New Delhi Declaration at their 18th summit on 12 September 2026, calling for wider access to AI resources and international cooperation on safe and inclusive AI. The Hindu reports its technology agenda spans AI, cybersecurity, digital public infrastructure, telecoms and submarine networks.

2026-09-12-tza-fullshangwe-e-ardhi-kigom.summary: Tanzania's e-Ardhi land information system has been extended to Kigoma region, where land officers from the Kasulu Town, Kigoma-Ujiji, Uvinza and Kibondo councils are being trained on it. Officials said residents will be able to start or follow some land services online instead of travelling to land offices. No date for full operation is given.

2026-09-12-tza-jamhurimedia-tanzania-kor.summary: Tanzania and South Korea agreed to speed up delivery of a US$2.5 billion Korean pledge for projects in transport, technology, culture, industry and health, Tanzania's finance minister Khamis Mussa Omar said in Seoul on the margins of the Korea-Africa economic cooperation meeting, reported on 12 September 2026. Korea Eximbank implements the funds. He cited years-long delays in some projects.

2026-09-12-us-h1b-visa-fee-african-tech-.summary: A TechCabal analysis argues that a proposed US$103,265 H-1B fee and a wage-weighted visa lottery, put forward by the US Department of Homeland Security, will make distributed teams in Lagos, Nairobi and Cape Town cheaper for American firms than hiring through the visa route. It is an opinion piece on a proposal, not a rule in force.

2026-09-12-von-ncc-8526-telecom-sites-ca.summary: Nigeria's mobile operators have built 8,526 of 12,179 committed coverage and capacity sites, about 70%, up from around 5,000 at the previous meeting, the Nigerian Communications Commission board said after its 110th meeting. The board also said its Device Management System is live, allowing stolen devices to be blocked across networks, and restated zero tolerance for call masking.

2026-09-12-youm7-egypt-telecom-egypt-we-.summary: Telecom Egypt's mobile brand WE launched an electronic know-your-customer service that lets customers verify their identity, sign electronically and buy and activate lines without paper documents. The first phase covers individual mobile lines and some other digital services. The company says the service meets regulatory and data-protection requirements, without naming the identity database used.

2026-09-12-zaf-sundaytimes-ncc-opt-out-r.summary: South Africa's National Consumer Commission issued a request for proposals for service providers to support its national opt-out registry for direct marketing, which it wants live in 2026, reported on 12 September 2026. Under amended consumer protection rules, marketers must register and check their lists against the registry, and face fines of up to R1 million or 10 per cent of turnover.

2026-09-12-zaf-sundaytimes-sumsub-deepfa.summary: Identity fraud in South Africa fell 31% year on year while deepfake incidents rose 269%, according to figures from verification firm Sumsub. Its chief executive credits tighter regulation and SIM-ID linkage for the fall and says the remaining attacks are fewer but more sophisticated.

2026-09-12-zmb-diggers-mansa-tailor-arre.summary: Police in Mansa arrested a 38-year-old man over a TikTok video allegedly insulting President Hakainde Hichilema, charging him under Zambia's Cyber Crimes Act with harassment using electronic gadgets. The police statement is dated 11 September 2026, after the Secretary to the Cabinet warned that insulting the President would be prosecuted.

2026-09-12-zmb-diggers-zamstats-15000-ta.summary: The Zambia Statistics Agency handed 15,000 tablets from the 2022 census to government ministries on 11 September 2026. Statistician General Sheila Mudenda said they will go to selected institutions in the national statistical system, which increasingly need to collect and exchange data electronically.

2026-09-13-africell-investors-page-four-.summary: The operator's investor page lists four markets — The Gambia, Sierra Leone, Angola and the Democratic Republic of Congo — with more than 14 million subscribers, more than 2,500 towers and revenue above US$400m. Its US$360m of 10.5% senior secured notes mature in October 2029.

2026-09-13-ago-angola24horas-mudei-fisca.summary: Chipilica Eduardo, a lawyer and member of Angola's civic movement MUDEI, told DW that political parties and civil society are not scrutinising the in-person electoral registration run by the Ministry of Territorial Administration. He questioned who checks the 'proof of life' step and the documents voters present, and how double registration could be detected without observers. The ministry's response is not reported.

2026-09-13-bfa-sidwaya-aneam-formation-i.summary: Burkina Faso's national association of blind and visually impaired students, ANEAM, trained 70 pupils and students in adapted computing in Ouagadougou from 7 to 11 September 2026, its fifth such course. Three levels ran from Word and Excel basics to internet search, email and artificial intelligence. The association's president said participants lack computers to practise on afterwards.

2026-09-13-cod-beto-onip-rgph2-deux-comp.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo's Council of Ministers, in a report read on 11 September 2026, set mass identification by the identity office ONIP to begin in December 2026 and the second general census to be enumerated in 2027. The two exercises fall under different ministries and budgets. The data protection authority has not yet been installed.

2026-09-13-cod-portbrief-banque-national.summary: DR Congo is building a national bank of geological data on critical minerals through its geological service SGNC, which signed a US$180 million mapping contract with Spain's Xcalibur in January 2026, its director Raoul Wazenga Vitima told Reuters. The bank is due to be fully operational by the end of 2026. Basic data will be free and more sensitive datasets charged for; the fee structure is not given.

2026-09-13-dza-mpt-arrete-calendrier-adj.summary: Algeria's post and telecommunications minister signed an order on 3 September 2026, published in the Official Journal on 13 September, setting the timetable for the tender to provide mobile coverage to sparsely populated localities under the universal service scheme. The tender was to be launched on 6 September and advertised on 7 September, with 45 days to bid and results due 30 days after bids are opened.

2026-09-13-eth-capital-ai-legal-framewor.summary: Capital Ethiopia reports expert warnings that AI systems trained on works without permission undermine copyright, patent and trademark protection, and that Ethiopia's data infrastructure leaves structural gaps. A York University law professor told the paper that copyright and patent laws are being dismantled by artificial intelligence.

2026-09-13-eth-capital-digital-logistics.summary: Ethiopian Shipping and Logistics launched a web and mobile self-service platform on 4 September 2026 for shipment orders, cargo tracking, freight payment and documents. The Ethio-Djibouti Railway has introduced its own customer portal for booking, tracking and payment.

2026-09-13-gab-agp-ged-electronic-docume.summary: Gabon's digital economy ministry announced the launch on 16 September 2026 of an electronic document management project for the administration, to modernise document handling and improve traceability. It falls under Ordonnance 0006/PR/2025 on digitalisation; no scope, supplier or cost is stated.

2026-09-13-gha-myjoyonline-sam-george-di.summary: Ghana's communications minister, Samuel Nartey George, said the government has signed agreements with 12 universities to put One Million Coders Programme courses into first-year programmes from this academic year, and that 141,954 learners had enrolled by August 2026. He spoke at the graduation of 26 trainees from a Plan International Ghana project backed by Nokia. The universities are not named.

2026-09-13-ifc-djibouti-country-private-.summary: The International Finance Corporation published a Country Private Sector Diagnostic for Djibouti in September 2026, prepared with the World Bank Group. It names off-grid solar energy, data centres and tourism as the three subsectors where private investment could grow, and identifies energy reform as a priority. It also notes state-owned enterprises' control of key sectors including telecommunications.

2026-09-13-ken-kachwanya-technopolis-dev.summary: Kenya's Technopolis Development Authority Board was fully constituted with three appointments, as the authority takes up a national mandate under the Technopolis Act 2026, commenced on 29 May 2026. The board moves the authority from developing Konza towards planning technopolises nationwide; no new locations, budgets or timelines were announced.

2026-09-13-lbr-moe-apo-standardize-schoo.summary: Liberia's Ministry of Education opened a five-day session in Kakata to develop and validate a Statutory School Record-Keeping Booklet, one nationwide system for school records on students, teachers, attendance and infrastructure. County teams are then to finalise education operational plans from the 2024/25 school census fact sheets.

2026-09-13-lby-spaceinafrica-starlink-li.summary: Talks between Starlink and Libya's General Authority for Communications and Informatics, open since 2024, had produced no agreement on licensing, spectrum or coverage as of 13 September 2026, according to regulator sources cited by Space in Africa. The regulator wants a local gateway in Libya, which Starlink has not accepted, though the company has agreed to set up a locally registered subsidiary.

2026-09-13-lso-finmark-gis-financial-acc.summary: FinMark Trust issued terms of reference for Phase 2 of Lesotho's GIS Financial Access Points Mapping Project, to update a 2018 baseline of 5,597 geo-referenced access points. The work covers every mobile-money agent, bank branch, ATM and post office across ten districts, with spatial analytics and a web map.

2026-09-13-mar-consonews-generation-aiot.summary: Morocco's Génération AIoT programme opened seven cohorts in Casablanca, Fès and Oujda, aiming at 1,200 trained people a year from February 2027. Launched in February 2026 by the digital transition ministry with a foundation and ABA Technology, it had drawn 2,118 applications and gathered 95 participants.

2026-09-13-mrt-enemray-toward-capable-la.summary: An arXiv technical report introduces Enemray, a language model for Hassaniya built by continual pretraining on Hassaniya and Mauritanian text, transferring that update into an instruction-tuned model and then supervised post-training on a largely new instruction corpus. The authors report the best English-to-Hassaniya translation among the open and proprietary models compared and the top score on Mauritanian translation error detection, while keeping most of the base model's general capabilities.

2026-09-13-mus-lexpress-damry-ai-city-go.summary: Mauritius' junior finance minister Dhaneshwar Damry told the 16th GOPIO international convention in Balaclava that the government will set up an "AI City" within the next two to three months. He presented Mauritius as an investment gateway and risk-reduction centre for Africa. No cost, location or operator is given.

2026-09-13-mus-mauriceinfo-conseil-minis.summary: Mauritius's Cabinet agreed on 11 September 2026 to introduce nine bills establishing a National Crime Agency as the lead investigator of financial crime, cybercrime and serious organised crime. The agency will gather and share intelligence and recover assets, and the Financial Crimes Commission Act will be repealed.

2026-09-13-nam-businessexpress-harmonise.summary: Namibia's ICT minister Emma Theofelus launched the Harmonised Government Communication Strategy 2026–2030 and the Government Corporate Brand Identity Manual at the public administration institute NIPAM on 9 September 2026. Cabinet approved both in March 2026; they set a single voice and brand for ministries, agencies, regional and local authorities and public enterprises.

2026-09-13-nam-namibian-universal-servic.summary: An opinion piece argues that cancelling and recycling inactive mobile numbers cuts people with irregular incomes off from employers, banks and government services, since a phone number now works as part of a person's digital identity. It calls for universal-service rules that weigh those consequences against efficient number management.

2026-09-13-nga-business-times-tinubu-bri.summary: At the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, Vice President Kashim Shettima, representing President Bola Tinubu, sought BRICS investment in Nigeria's artificial intelligence, digital infrastructure, telecommunications and critical minerals. He cited Project BRIDGE's broadband and fibre expansion; no agreement or amount was announced.

2026-09-13-nga-highstreet-digital-econom.summary: The Central Bank of Nigeria's quarterly bulletin records N1.053 quadrillion in electronic payments in the first quarter of 2026, up 2.85% on a year earlier and the highest quarter since its series began in 2019. Point-of-sale volume fell 19.9%. Nigerian Communications Commission data show 5,934 fibre-optic cable cuts in the first half of 2026, about 65 a day.

2026-09-13-nga-mytimeng-154-million-cons.summary: Nigeria had 319,735 fibre-to-the-home connections at the end of June 2026 against more than 192 million active telephone subscribers, according to Nigerian Communications Commission figures. Operators added 12.8 million SIM cards and Nigerians used 10.2 million terabytes of data in the first seven months of 2026.

2026-09-13-nga-punch-ncc-8526-network-si.summary: Nigeria's mobile operators have deployed 8,526 of the 12,179 coverage and capacity sites they committed to, about 70%, up from about 5,000 at the previous count, the Nigerian Communications Commission said after its board meeting of 9 September 2026. The regulator said fibre cuts caused a sharp rise in network disruptions in June.

2026-09-13-sdn-aswatnews-e-learning-regu.summary: The president of Sudan's National Council for Higher Education and Scientific Research approved the E-learning and Blended Learning Regulation 2026 by decision 138, signed and in force from 12 September 2026. An academic's commentary says it gives e-learning in higher-education institutions a formal legal basis rather than treating it as a wartime stopgap.

2026-09-13-sen-rts-cyberattaques-jamais-.summary: Colonel Aly Mime, Senegal's national cybersecurity chief at the DCSSI, said on RTS that the state has never paid a ransom after a cyberattack. He named the attacks on the DAF, the Treasury and the tax directorate and called attackers' claims about stolen data volumes largely bluff.

2026-09-13-techreviewafrica-world-bank-m.summary: A World Bank implementation-support mission reviewed the Uganda Digital Acceleration Project–GovNet with NITA-U and the ICT ministry. It visited the National Data Center, the national CERT, the Personal Data Protection Office and a skilling centre in Nakawa; the mission dates are not given.

2026-09-13-techtrends-edtech-out-of-scho.summary: A commentary argues that Nigeria's EdTech products were built to supplement schooling for enrolled students and do little for out-of-school children, whose exclusion is driven by poverty, insecurity and distance. It points to offline tools such as uLesson's preloaded devices and calls for donor and government partnership rather than venture funding.

2026-09-13-tun-lapresse-khadamet-50000-u.summary: Tunisia's Khadamet app for online public services registered 50,000 users in its first ten days, Ahmed Megdich of the Directorate-General for Information Technology said, reported on 13 September 2026. Social security, civil status, education, bill payment and road-traffic services were among the most used.

2026-09-13-uga-independent-kitgum-reside.summary: Residents of Lagoro sub-county in Kitgum District agreed to pay shs 500 each to transport NIRA officials delivering national ID cards locally, against shs 30,000–40,000 per trip to the municipal office. The district's chief administrative officer said it would seek approval for local structures to distribute IDs.

2026-09-13-uga-vividvoice-ura-foreign-in.summary: The Uganda Revenue Authority has begun sending notices to taxpayers whose names and tax numbers have been matched to foreign income or assets through international data exchange under the Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters. Affected residents have until mid-2027 to make voluntary disclosures and amend three years of returns before the data are used for audits and investigations.

2026-09-13-xgl-fmprc-xi-brics-summit-sta.summary: President Xi Jinping proposed five initiatives at the 18th BRICS Summit, among them a BRICS AI open-source community and a BRICS digital ecosystem cloud platform, and called for a consensus-based global AI governance framework. He restated China's zero-tariff treatment for the 53 African countries it has diplomatic relations with; no timeline or funding was attached.

2026-09-13-zaf-presidency-ramaphosa-bric.summary: President Cyril Ramaphosa proposed at the 18th BRICS Summit that BRICS set up an international mechanism for the independent scientific evaluation of artificial intelligence, resting on human-control principles and mandatory reporting of serious incidents. He also backed formal external checks and audits of AI companies; no draft terms or BRICS response are on record.

2026-09-13-zaf-sanews-tut-nsfas-qualific.summary: South Africa's student aid scheme NSFAS restored funding to 182 Tshwane University of Technology students after the university corrected wrong qualification codes that had triggered defunding under the N+ rule. The corrections followed more than 300 helpdesk cases raised by Deputy Minister Yusuf Cassim's office. A further 1,212 students placed in accredited housing after the NSFAS portal closed have not had accommodation costs paid.

2026-09-14-actuniger-presse-en-ligne-pro.summary: Fourteen Nigerien online editors welcomed the government's electronic-press text in a declaration dated 13 September and asked to be consulted on its implementing rules. They offered to work with the communication regulator and announced a representative body of their own.

2026-09-14-ago-angop-huambo-igca-janela-.summary: Angola's cadastral institute trained Huambo province's 17 municipalities on the land-concession single window created by Presidential Decree 84/25. Provincial officials said it will align municipalities with the government, raise revenue and tighten control of the cadastre.

2026-09-14-almasryalyoum-egypt-moj-defen.summary: The justice ministry added that SMS notification packages are paid to the contracted provider at the regulator's tariff rather than to the ministry. A full case file as a PDF is priced at the paper-copy rate of EGP 150 per 50 pages.

2026-09-14-babacar-mbengue-dechets-elect.summary: A profile of Senegalese engineer Babacar Mbengue, whose company RKovera, founded in January 2026, runs a traceability platform for e-waste collection, certified data erasure and recovery of metals.

2026-09-14-bamboo-cowrywise-dangote-ipo-.summary: Bamboo and Cowrywise apps failed on the opening day of the Dangote refinery IPO sold through approved fintechs. Cowrywise restored service in about an hour; Bamboo said it had opened more than 236,000 accounts the week before and that allocation is pro rata.

2026-09-14-bfa-lefaso-cn-mabg-transforma.summary: A second account of the same council session reports the permanent secretary's figures: hundreds of procedures dematerialised, more than 10,000 recruitments and over 200 organisation charts revised. The session set orientations for 2027.

2026-09-14-bfa-libreinfo-bclcc-cybercrim.summary: Burkina Faso recorded FCFA 906,123,245 in cybercrime losses in the first half of 2026, against FCFA 1.7 billion for the whole of 2025, Lieutenant Napougba Julien Legma of the central anti-cybercrime brigade said in an interview published on 14 September 2026. More than 1,000 complaints have been lodged so far this year.

2026-09-14-bfa-sidwaya-cn-mabg-modernisa.summary: Burkina Faso's National Council for the Modernisation of the Administration and Good Governance met under Prime Minister Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel OuÃ©draogo and rated the administration's 2025 performance at 85.38%. The Prime Minister named weak citizen uptake of digital service platforms among persistent shortcomings and called for national languages in public information systems.

2026-09-14-bosun-tijani-withdraws-itu-de.summary: Nigeria's communications minister Bosun Tijani withdrew his candidacy for ITU Deputy Secretary-General to stay on the domestic programme. He cited Project BRIDGE's 90,000 km of planned fibre, the tower programme, two planned satellites and a national postcode system.

2026-09-14-burkina-faso-administration-s.summary: Burkina Faso's digital transition ministry set the official launch of electronic signature in administrative procedures for 15 September in Ouagadougou, under the 2009 electronic-transactions law. More than 250 procedures were dematerialised in 2025, 95 of them on the Service Public BF portal.

2026-09-14-busha-mastercard-crypto-crede.summary: Nigerian crypto platform Busha made Mastercard Crypto Credential available, letting users send supported digital assets to verified email or phone aliases instead of wallet addresses.

2026-09-14-bwa-mmegi-fnbb-muscles-into-m.summary: First National Bank Botswana will let customers receiving money through its eWallet service transfer it directly to Orange Money, Mascom's MyZaka and BTC's Smega. The bank announced the plan with results for the year to June 2026, showing profit before tax up 12 per cent to P2.12 billion. No launch date is given.

2026-09-14-capitalfm-mutiso-ai-credit-sc.summary: In an opinion piece ahead of the National Credit Market Convention in Naivasha, Kevin Mutiso writes that Kenya's 256 licensed digital credit providers have disbursed 8.37 million loans worth over KES 150bn using scoring models. He proposes rules modelled on the EU AI Act, whose credit-scoring provisions took effect on 2 August 2026, but graded by how opaque and autonomous each system is.

2026-09-14-cell-c-easyequities-bidvest-t.summary: Cell C, EasyEquities and Bidvest Bank notified South African customers of a breach at an unnamed third-party provider, reported on 9 September. Cell C Fiber customers' names, emails, numbers and account numbers were exposed; Bidvest Bank's exposure awaits a forensic investigation.

2026-09-14-civ-techreviewafrica-national.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's digital transition minister Djibril Ouattara signed a National Alliance for Artificial Intelligence Pact with the heads of the employers' confederation CGECI and the Chamber of Commerce and Industry on 11 September 2026, at the close of IMPACT AI 2026 in Abidjan. The pact sets a framework for joint public-private AI programming. No funding is stated.

2026-09-14-cod-bankable-microfinance-swi.summary: Microfinance institutions in the Democratic Republic of Congo are seeking financial and technical support to move to digital payments before the central bank's ban on US dollar cash transactions takes effect on 9 April 2027. An August 2026 report by the microfinance and savings cooperative associations, ANIMF and APROCEC, with Innogence Consulting, names the deadline as a main constraint for smaller institutions.

2026-09-14-cod-digitalbusiness-rdc-pass-.summary: DR Congo's digital economy ministry said more than 9,000 candidates sat the recruitment test for RDC Pass agents and a first cohort of 50 was retained for the Kinshasa pilot. Training starts on 15 September, followed by extension to other Kinshasa zones and then nationwide.

2026-09-14-cod-ouragan-enquete-arptc-reg.summary: A joint press investigation calls DR Congo's telecoms regulator ARPTC unlawful and ineffective, noting that the successor authority created by a 2023 decree has never been installed. It details failings on service quality and equipment approval.

2026-09-14-cpv-expressodasilhas-vinti4-o.summary: The Banco de Cabo Verde reported on 14 September 2026 that residents made 4,992,880 operations worth 21,159.9 million escudos on the vinti4 card network in August, down 0.3% in number and 2.4% in value on July. Card purchases made up 3,768,595 operations. The interbank clearing system processed 131,456 operations worth 25,543.1 million escudos, down 19.1% in number.

2026-09-14-digwatch-botswana-national-da.summary: Botswana's Ministry of Communications and Innovation held a five-day data governance training and stakeholder workshop from 7 to 11 September 2026 to develop a National Data Strategy from its earlier National Data Policy. The work is backed by the African Union Commission and the European Union under the Data Governance in Africa Initiative, with AUDA-NEPAD and GIZ providing implementation support. No budget is given.

2026-09-14-djezzy-ugcaa-digital-transfor.summary: Djezzy signed a framework agreement with Algeria's traders' and artisans' union UGCAA to support their digital transformation. No date, terms or figures were published.

2026-09-14-dni-r2-1bn-digital-economy-in.summary: South African investment firm DNI announced more than R2.1 billion across Frogfoot, Vox and Hypa, Mission Mobile and KnowRoaming. Its consortium holds 34.8% of Frogfoot and Vox at an aggregate R14.4 billion valuation, with Frogfoot's capital aimed at 360,000 lower-income homes over 12 months.

2026-09-14-dza-algerie360-jeunesse-porta.summary: Algeria's High Commission for Digitalisation and the Ministry of Youth added seven youth services to the national government services portal, announced on 14 September 2026. They include Inkhirati for registering at youth centres, Charaka for youth associations to register and apply for project funding, and Moukhayami for holiday camp enrolment.

2026-09-14-egy-dailynews-unified-platfor.summary: Egypt's health minister, Khaled Abdel Ghaffar, discussed a proposed Egypt Smart Healthcare Platform with MTS and Inspur after reviewing China's digital health model. It would link health facilities through unified patient records, with telemedicine, a command centre and AI, and a pilot of the first phase was discussed. The ministry gave no cost, timetable or financing details.

2026-09-14-egy-enterpriseam-nafeza-overl.summary: Egypt's finance ministry has begun surveying road-freight firms at land ports in order to register them and link them to Nafeza, the national single window for foreign trade, according to three officials quoted on 14 September 2026. The plan adds consolidated bills of lading and pre-arrival cargo data for trucks, starting at the Red Sea ports of Nuweiba and Safaga.

2026-09-14-egy-maspero-fra-otp-sharikat-.summary: Egypt's Financial Regulatory Authority issued Decision 2735 of 2026, giving consumer finance and small-business finance companies two months to introduce one-time password verification of customers. A code must be sent to the customer's verified phone number when a finance contract is signed and when the finance is drawn, and the lender must keep a record of it.

2026-09-14-egy-menastartupdigest-yomo-di.summary: Yomo, a digital bank being developed by Commercial International Bank Egypt, has preliminary approval from the Central Bank of Egypt, reported on 14 September 2026. Chief executive Roshwan Hamady said up to US$300 million will be invested before a pilot launch, serving individuals, including Egyptians abroad, before small businesses. No approval or launch date is given.

2026-09-14-eswatinipositivenews-sadcopac.summary: SADCOPAC secretary-general Madala Mhlanga told public accounts committees across the region to act before scandals and losses. He urged digital forensics, data analytics and audits of the algorithms in government digital systems.

2026-09-14-eth-reporter-uneca-dhl-afcfta.summary: The UN Economic Commission for Africa and DHL Express Sub-Saharan Africa signed a three-year memorandum to help small businesses trade across African borders under the AfCFTA, through DHL's GoTrade programme. The first activity is a virtual training series on customs, logistics, e-commerce and digital trade tools. No value or signing date is given.

2026-09-14-fawry-dms-pos-medical-payment.summary: Fawry is linking its business POS terminals to DMS's medical and management software so hospital cashier amounts pass straight to the terminal and payment status updates in real time. No commercial terms or rollout figures were given.

2026-09-14-flutterwave-dangote-refinery-.summary: Flutterwave opened online subscriptions to the Dangote refinery IPO as a receiving agent, at NGN 525 a share with a ten-share minimum and a Bank Verification Number required. The offer closes on 13 October.

2026-09-14-flutterwave-stablecoin-paymen.summary: Flutterwave's stablecoin lead describes using stablecoins as settlement rails rather than a product, through its Circle partnership since April 2025 and several tokens on Polygon and Tempo. The company has applied to the central bank's second sandbox cohort.

2026-09-14-gab-agp-bad-cemac-sdmx-open-d.summary: Gabon's planning minister, Louise Pierrette Mvono, opened a CEMAC workshop in Libreville on 14 September 2026 on adopting the SDMX statistical data exchange standard and moving the six member states to version 2.0 of the Open Data Platform. The CEMAC Commission organised it with World Bank financing through the HISWACA statistics project.

2026-09-14-gab-agp-gabon-fiber-41-millia.summary: Gabon Fiber S.A., a private Gabonese company, said on 14 September 2026 that it will seek more than FCFA 41 billion on international financial markets to build 1,650 km of optical fibre to towns including Lambaréné, Makokou, Mouila and Tchibanga. Its director general spoke at the signing of concessions with the state infrastructure holding company SPIN.

2026-09-14-gab-agp-spin-gabon-fiber-part.summary: Gabon's state digital infrastructure holding SPIN signed a 20-year public-private partnership with Gabon Fiber S.A. in Libreville on 14 September 2026 to operate and extend the national fibre backbone to about 3,500km. Digital economy minister Mark-Alexandre Doumba said the concession is privately financed and returns the network, run by a foreign partner for over a decade, to Gabonese control.

2026-09-14-gha-myjoyonline-gaps-suicide-.summary: Ghana launched a national suicide situational report with media guidelines, which finds the country's data incomplete. Health records, the births and deaths registry and police data each miss age or method, and death certificates do not reliably reach the registry.

2026-09-14-gin-guineenews-data-center-na.summary: Guinea's prime minister, Bah Oury, pressed telecoms officials on a visit reported on 14 September 2026 to bring the national data centre into service. He was told the project, costing about US$10 million, is roughly 90% complete but not fully operational. He said he would demand detailed information from the digital economy ministry's agencies.

2026-09-14-gmb-thepoint-gala-condemns-fr.summary: The Gambia Action for Local Accountability condemned reports that citizens who had paid for national ID cards were told to reapply after a change of system operator. It asked the immigration department to explain and said it is documenting cases.

2026-09-14-gsma-refugee-women-digital-in.summary: GSMA research finds identity rules for SIM registration push refugee women in Ethiopia and Tanzania to register lines in others' names, limiting control of mobile money and communication. In Uganda about 25% of refugee women use the internet against 50% of men.

2026-09-14-intra-city-digital-divide-afr.summary: Okey Chigbu argues the digital divide runs inside cities as well as between city and village, contrasting dense fibre in Lagos's Ikoyi with thin coverage in Ajegunle and Makoko. He calls for broadband to be measured by ward rather than by state.

2026-09-14-itd-fintech-trust-developing-.summary: A journal article surveying 392 participants in emerging and developing economies treats fintech as a stand-in institution where capital markets fail, resting on trust in the platform.

2026-09-14-ken-kenya-appoints-two-member.summary: Kenya's interior minister Kipchumba Murkomen appointed Lorna Omondi Ogolla and Joy Kibor to the board of the new National Cybersecurity Agency for three years, effective 11 September 2026 under Gazette Notice 14420. Ogolla leads Google Research's machine-learning and AI partnerships in Africa; Kibor heads postgraduate ICT studies at Zetech University.

2026-09-14-ken-mps-find-gaps-in-the-rule.summary: Kenya's parliamentary finance committee, chaired by Kuria Kimani, recommended a near-total rewrite of the investment policy for the National Infrastructure Fund, reported on 14 September 2026. It found the policy silent on project risk, selection, borrowing and liquidity limits and exposure caps. The fund holds KES 340bn, mostly from the sale of the state's Safaricom stake, and ICT is one of its five sectors.

2026-09-14-ken-technopolis-development-a.summary: Kenya's Technopolis Development Authority board is now complete under the Technopolis Act 2026, in force since 29 May 2026, with the appointment of James Musee Nduna, Yvonne Teresia Ogwang and Yunis M. Omar. Ogwang is the Council of Governors' nominee.

2026-09-14-ken-techweez-airtel-telesonic.summary: Airtel Africa is winding up Airtel Kenya Telesonic, its wholesale fibre subsidiary, two years after launch, with a KES 16.1 million loss and no revenue in 2025. Its facilities licence was returned to the Communications Authority in February, with gazettement pending.

2026-09-14-ken-thestar-isaboke-national-.summary: Kenya's broadcasting and telecoms principal secretary, Stephen Isaboke, said a new National Communication Policy creates a National Communication Centre to validate and release state information, and ties ministries' communication plans to performance contracts. He called his department's KES 6.4 billion 2026 allocation inadequate and said digitised government services rose from 353 in 2022 to more than 21,500.

2026-09-14-ken-tukio-kdeap-smartboards-j.summary: Kenya's ICT principal secretary, John Tanui, and a World Bank delegation reviewed progress on the Kenya Digital Economy Acceleration Project, covering fibre, public Wi-Fi, digital government services and skills. Its Digital Smartboards Programme, run by the ICT Authority with the education ministry, has reached 10,384 public junior schools in all 47 counties and trained 62,364 teachers.

2026-09-14-ken-tukio-sha-provider-contra.summary: Kenya's Social Health Authority set out requirements for providers in its contracting cycle running from 1 October 2026 to 30 June 2029 across four funds, Tukio reported on 14 September 2026. Facilities must onboard through a Centralised Digital Platform, have a working electronic medical records or approved claims system, submit claims electronically and pass know-your-customer and financial checks.

2026-09-14-kenya-keiyo-south-public-wifi.summary: Kenya installed a free public Wi-Fi hotspot at Nyaru in Keiyo South, carrying fibre on Kenya Power poles. The ICT principal secretary also inspected the Chepkorio digital hub under construction.

2026-09-14-lbr-fpa-officials-post-vulner.summary: Liberian officials, among them the water utility's managing director, posted spreadsheets of children in a UNICEF-funded social protection programme to Facebook, with names, schools, home addresses and caregivers. A lawyer called it a breach of the Children's Law of 2011; no response from the ministry or UNICEF is reported.

2026-09-14-lby-bankawy-cbl-circular-9-20.summary: The Central Bank of Libya issued Circular 9/2026 on mobile payments and e-wallets, reported on 14 September 2026. It lets licensed payment companies issue wallets to legally resident foreigners with a valid passport or residence document. Daily limits for Libyan citizens are 100,000 dinars person to person, 500,000 person to company and 2 million company to company; foreigners' limits are lower.

2026-09-14-lebara-nigeria-mvno-launch-te.summary: Lebara Nigeria began commercial service as the second virtual network operator under the 2022 framework, after Vitel Wireless. It runs on Airtel's network under a 2023 licence and sells eSIMs with remote identity checks in its app.

2026-09-14-liberia-nid-crvs-link-osd-ppp.summary: Liberia's identification registry plans one system linking national ID with civil registration and vital statistics under its proposed US$54 million partnership with Austria's OSD. The signed agreement still needs parliamentary approval, and ID issuance has been suspended since June 2025.

2026-09-14-madica-adegboye-early-stage-f.summary: Emmanuel Adegboye, head of Flourish Ventures' Madica programme, says its US$200,000 cheques across ten markets including Algeria and Cameroon are not enough on their own, so the programme now co-invests. He is backing voice AI and calls for incentives to grow angel investment.

2026-09-14-mar-moroccopost-startup-catal.summary: Morocco's Startup Catalytic Fund, set up by the digital transition ministry and managed by Tamwilcom, will invest US$36m of public money over three years in venture capital funds expected to mobilise about US$258m for startups. Decree 2.26.576 of 3 August 2026 strengthened its framework, and nine fund managers were shortlisted from 47 applications.

2026-09-14-mar-nichan-niyaba-bahth-tajas.summary: Morocco's prosecutor general at the Casablanca Court of Appeal ordered a judicial investigation into a party leader's claim that his party's phones were being spied on. The national judicial police will verify the claim, which the prosecution tied to the proper conduct of the elections; the party is not named.

2026-09-14-mauritiustimes-ai-decision-ri.summary: Columnist Gleb Tsipursky argues Mauritius should map which AI tasks may execute, recommend, be verified or stay with humans before scaling adoption. He points to the AI Innovation Lab as the place to train for it.

2026-09-14-meta-ai-academy-kenya-itweb-a.summary: Meta and accelerator This Is Digital launched an AI Academy in Kenya on 11 September with free training and equity-free funding. A startup pitchathon closes applications on 30 September for a Nairobi final on 15 October, and an eight-week masterclass starts on 3 November.

2026-09-14-mli-maliweb-abdrahamane-keita.summary: Mali's cybercrime tribunal sentenced journalist Abdrahamane KeÃ¯ta, publication director of Le TÃ©moin, to two years in prison and 1 million CFA francs in damages over a television remark about Kidal. He has been detained since June, and his defence intends to appeal.

2026-09-14-moz-aim-mocambique-brasil-mod.summary: Mozambique's finance ministry and Brazil's Ministry of Management and Innovation in Public Services signed a memorandum of understanding in Maputo on 14 September 2026. It covers exchange of experience and staff training on public procurement, payroll management, digital transformation and administrative modernisation, with training starting immediately, finance minister Carla Loveira said.

2026-09-14-moz-clubofmozambique-correiog.summary: Mozambique's digital transformation agency said the government email service CorreioGOV was restored after maintenance, with some peripheral services still restricted. Neither the start of the outage nor its cause was given.

2026-09-14-moz-mznews-correiogov-restabe.summary: Mozambique's Digital Transformation and Innovation Agency said the government email service, CorreioGOV, had been fully restored after a technical intervention. Some services that had been unavailable remained partly restricted, with a return to normal expected during 14 September. No cause or duration of the outage is given.

2026-09-14-moz-profile-tmcel-novo-invest.summary: Mozambique's finance ministry has begun selecting a strategic investor to buy part of the state's shares in the state operator Tmcel, reported on 14 September 2026, with a technical team set up to run the negotiations. Tmcel's latest accounts show negative equity of about MZN 14.5 billion, and its auditor EY flagged material uncertainty over its ability to keep operating.

2026-09-14-msmeafrica-mastercard-cchub-g.summary: The Mastercard Foundation and Co-Creation Hub opened applications for their GATEWAY programme, which aims to train 400,000 young Nigerians over five years for gig-economy work. Participants choose digital marketing, graphic design, UI/UX design or video production, on a beginner or an advanced pathway, with mentoring and career support.

2026-09-14-mtn-nigeria-fibre-market-shar.summary: Regulator data for June put MTN at 176,468 of Nigeria's 319,735 fibre connections, a 55% share. Fibre remains about 0.2% of roughly 156.8 million internet subscriptions.

2026-09-14-mtn-south-sudan-network-cover.summary: MTN South Sudan says population broadband coverage rose from 76.6% to 85% and network availability to 99% over two years, after more than 500 sites were modernised with CREI's solar-hybrid power. Diesel use at supported sites fell by more than half; no investment figure is given.

2026-09-14-mus-mauritiustimes-national-c.summary: A Mauritius Times interview, published on 14 September 2026, examines the proposed National Crime Agency Bill. The commentator argues that constitutional status alone will not secure the agency's independence, and that appointment of its director-general by the President on the advice of a panel, after consulting the Prime Minister and opposition leader, leaves room for political influence.

2026-09-14-mus-newsmoris-legal-experts-c.summary: Mauritius's Director of Public Prosecutions, Rashid Ahmine, welcomed most of the National Crime Agency Bill but warned the agency could remain a dead letter without government resources. Under the bill, intrusive surveillance needs a judge's authorisation. The Bar Association president, Antoine Domingue, noted the bill sets no terms of office or removal procedures for appointees.

2026-09-14-mwi-247malawi-msukuma-schools.summary: Education expert Zizwa Msukuma told 247 Malawi News that digitalisation should be a pillar of Malawi's education reform. He cited a 2026 school connectivity analysis finding that 85.8% of secondary schools lack internet access, 47% have no electricity, one computer serves 356 students on average, and 43% of school computers are in five urban districts.

2026-09-14-nam-namibian-6th-grain-n13m-c.summary: US firm 6th Grain Corporation is demanding N$13 million from Namibia's government after Cabinet ordered its crop-monitoring contract cancelled for failing legal and procedural requirements. A demand letter dated 9 September 2026 claims payment for completed work, commercial loss and reputational damage.

2026-09-14-nga-africaintelligence-meta-2.summary: Meta is negotiating a settlement with Nigeria's consumer protection commission over its US$220 million fine after a first appeal was rejected, Africa Intelligence reports. No terms or timetable are given.

2026-09-14-nga-businessday-200-telecom-t.summary: Nigeria's communications ministry said at least 200 towers for unconnected communities will be live by December, out of about 3,700 planned, with a new satellite for places neither towers nor fibre reach. The remarks came at the opening of the data protection commission's new Abuja headquarters, which reported 356 licensed compliance organisations.

2026-09-14-nga-cyberera-ndpc-arcon-data-.summary: Nigeria Data Protection Commission head Vincent Olatunji told an advertising regulator's webinar that only 12.3% of advertising agencies comply with the data protection law. He called for the two regulators to work together on data processing in marketing.

2026-09-14-nga-thales-alenia-space-nigco.summary: Thales Alenia Space signed a contract with Nigeria's NIGCOMSAT to build the NigComSat-2A geostationary satellite on a Spacebus B2 platform, with a service life above 15 years and coverage from West to Southern Africa. No contract value, financing or launch date is stated.

2026-09-14-nga-vanguard-okoye-2023-cyber.summary: Former INEC commissioner Festus Okoye said the commission's platforms faced many cyberattacks during the 2023 presidential election but he could not say they caused the IReV portal failure, which he attributed to a technical malfunction.

2026-09-14-nga-von-ict-contribution-gdp-.summary: Nigeria's communications and digital economy minister Bosun Tijani said on 14 September 2026 that the ICT sector's share of GDP has risen from about 16 to 21 per cent in three years. He spoke at the opening of the Nigeria Data Protection Commission's Abuja headquarters, in a property recovered by the EFCC. The commission said it has licensed 356 compliance organisations and earned more than N12 billion in three years.

2026-09-14-nigeria-ai-defences-elections.summary: An INEC delegation led by chairman Joash Ojo Amupitan met Google, Microsoft and IFES in Ottawa on AI, cybersecurity and electoral resilience ahead of Nigeria's 2027 polls. No agreement or programme was announced.

2026-09-14-nitda-unveils-cloud-policy-pa.summary: Nigeria's IT development agency NITDA released four cloud policy instruments, reported on 14 September 2026, under a Cloud First mandate for government: a cloud computing guideline, a technical guideline, a single national certification for data centres and cloud services, and an investment strategy with the government as anchor customer. It puts Nigeria's cloud market at US$1.03bn in 2025, rising to a projected US$3.28bn in 2030.

2026-09-14-optasia-h1-revenue-itweb.summary: Optasia's revenue rose 58% to US$185.3 million in the six months to June, with mobile financial services 72% of the total and Ghana about 31.5%. In Nigeria all operator partners were live again by 24 June after a suspension of airtime-credit services, and FirstRand raised its stake to 26.1%.

2026-09-14-rwa-techreviewafrica-irembo-s.summary: Rwanda's Irembo hosted a Guinean water utility delegation, the Congolese ambassador and a Smart Africa workshop on cross-border digital public infrastructure to share its experience of digital public services.

2026-09-14-sajim-online-admission-system.summary: A scoping review of 18 studies on online admission systems in education frames South Africa's systems as e-government and finds gaps in usability and equity of access.

2026-09-14-sdn-sudanhorizon-national-eco.summary: Sudan's National Economic Management Committee, chaired by Prime Minister Kamil Idris, met in Khartoum on 13 September 2026 and called for electronic connectivity and coordination among ministries and training in digital transformation. It backed the Tax Chamber to widen the tax base and directed that imports be regulated through the Baladna platform.

2026-09-14-sdn-sudantimes-cash-crisis-hu.summary: Families receiving humanitarian aid in Sudan's East Darfur are losing 40% to 45% of payments to fees for converting Bankak app transfers into cash, amid a banknote shortage and traders' refusal of electronic payment. A displaced mother in El Daein received 780,000 Sudanese pounds and collected 468,000.

2026-09-14-seevcash-dawuda-iddrisu-trans.summary: A profile of Ghanaian engineer Dawuda Iddrisu, co-founder of SeevCash, a cross-border transfer fintech set up in 2022 in the United States with a Ghana base. It handles dollars, sterling, euros, cedis, naira and USDC and offers a business suite.

2026-09-14-sen-lesoleil-cybastion-300m-t.summary: US company Cybastion announced a US$300 million investment in Senegal's digital infrastructure, data security and sovereignty, in Washington. No date, instrument, projects or timetable are given.

2026-09-14-sen-lesoleil-nouveau-directeu.summary: Cheikh Tidiane Sarr, a former SONATEL and Orange Finances Mobiles SÃ©nÃ©gal executive, was appointed director-general of the regulator ARTP by a decree of 10 September after an open call for applications. He inherits a market of 21.7 million internet lines, with rural access gaps, high tariffs and weak fibre competition.

2026-09-14-sle-apexnews-land-title-certi.summary: Sierra Leone's lands minister, Turad Senesi, announced that Cabinet has approved a nationwide land title certificate system, which still needs parliamentary approval before it is implemented. The opinion piece asks how costs for registration and surveying will affect low-income and rural landholders and how customary land will be handled. No costs, procedures or timetable are given.

2026-09-14-smartnewsliberia-mgcsp-benefi.summary: Liberia's Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection confirmed on 13 September 2026 that beneficiary records from its Save the Future Project circulating on social media are authentic and were never authorised for release, and opened an internal investigation. The records concern children removed from street situations; the ministry rejected claims they list survivors of gender-based violence and said it had shared collated data with funding partners.

2026-09-14-som-hiiraan-eac-trade-digital.summary: An opinion piece notes intra-EAC trade reached US$14.33 billion in 2024 while its share of total trade fell to 11.8%. It argues for sharing cross-border trade data once rather than repeatedly at each border.

2026-09-14-south-sudans-fibre-push-is-mo.summary: South Sudan's ICT ministry has invited international bids for about 397km of terrestrial fibre on the Juba–Nadapal route towards the Kenyan border, financed by World Bank grant E1780 under the Eastern Africa Regional Digital Integration Project. Bids close on 26 October 2026. The backbone is to have at least 17 points of presence; no contract value is stated.

2026-09-14-techish-safaricom-ethiopia-15.summary: Safaricom Ethiopia announced on 3 September 2026 that it has passed 15 million 90-day active subscribers, five years after receiving its licence in July 2021. It had 14.7 million on 30 June 2026. The company reports more than 3,500 network sites covering about 60% of the population; no exact subscriber figure was given.

2026-09-14-tgo-republiquetogolaise-certi.summary: Togo began issuing free nationality certificates to 4,200 schoolgirls, 600 in each of seven education regions, with the first 300 final-year pupils served in Grand Lomé. The online nationality certificate platform launched in 2024 has received 241,617 applications and processed 179,690, or 74%; officials blame delays on documents from prefectures and intermediaries withholding SMS notices.

2026-09-14-tgo-republiquetogolaise-factu.summary: About 50 businesses were briefed in Lomé by Togo's employers' council and the revenue authority, OTR, on certified electronic invoicing, introduced by the 2026 finance law. Each invoice must carry a QR code, a unique number and a digital fingerprint, and be kept electronically for ten years. Firms may use the tax authority's platform or connect their own systems to it. No start date is given.

2026-09-14-tgo-sahellibertynews-social-p.summary: Togo's National Social Protection Programme, launched on 18 December 2025, pays unconditional cash transfers to more than 700,000 vulnerable people, with XOF 25,000 per household sent by mobile money. Initial funding of XOF 3.5 billion came with support from the World Bank, AFD and the African Development Bank. The September 2026 article reports no new development.

2026-09-14-thisday-dele-oye-uber-exit-re.summary: Dele Oye of the Alliance for Economic Research and Ethics says Uber's exit from Nigeria exposes gaps in transport regulation. He calls for transparent airport e-hailing rules and equal treatment of ride-hailing firms and car-hire operators.

2026-09-14-thisday-fg-n10-5bn-digital-tr.summary: Nigeria launched a Digital Training Academy in Abuja with more than N10.5 billion to train over 32,000 young people in six-month online courses. The National Open University and Yaba College of Technology host study centres, and the academy certifies the 3 Million Technical Talent programme.

2026-09-14-thisday-mtn-ihs-deal-antitrus.summary: A lawyer reads MTN's acquisition of IHS Towers against Nigeria's competition law, setting out the regulators' conditions: a Nigerian sell-down of up to 30%, no exclusivity and existing contracts left unchanged.

2026-09-14-togo-otr-employers-certified-.summary: About 50 businesses met Togo's revenue office on 10 September on the certified electronic invoicing introduced by the 2026 budget law. Each invoice will carry a unique number, QR code and digital fingerprint; firms may use the office's solution or connected software, and paper invoices stay valid until a gradual launch.

2026-09-14-top-ict-tenders-sita-activity.summary: South Africa's State IT Agency placed four of the week's top ten ICT tenders, including a 36-month incident management system for the police, whose tender says it has no single integrated system for logging reported incidents. The Electoral Commission is tendering for identity governance, and the consumer commission for opt-out registry partners.

2026-09-14-tun-assabah-tunis-taamir-buil.summary: The Municipality of Tunis began adopting the Taamir platform for filing and tracking building-permit applications, keeping the paper route open for now. Taamir was launched in 16 municipalities in June under an interior ministry agreement with German cooperation and USAID funding.

2026-09-14-tun-tunisiatv-plateforme-nume.summary: Tunisia's social affairs minister, Issam Lahmar, told the Arab Labour Conference in Cairo on 13 September 2026 that his ministry has prepared a digital labour-administration platform to launch during September. He said it will support labour inspectors and provide up-to-date data on the social situation.

2026-09-14-tun-webmanagercenter-platefor.summary: The municipality of Tunis launched Taamir, a digital platform for filing and tracking building-permit applications, announced on 14 September 2026. The municipality said the existing paper procedure stays in force for now. The national platform was announced on 24 June for 16 municipalities.

2026-09-14-twiga-foods-administration-ke.summary: GT Flow, formerly Twiga Foods One, entered administration on 17 August, according to a gazette notice of 11 September. Twiga raised about US$185 million; the notice does not say what sits in the company or whether its distributors are affected.

2026-09-14-tza-jamhurimedia-digital-tanz.summary: Tanzania's Digital Tanzania Project, funded since 2021 by a US$150 million World Bank loan, is due to close on 31 October 2026, an ICT director in the President's Office said on 14 September 2026. Officials said it has built 758 new towers, upgraded 304 to 3G and 4G, added 60 Gbps of government internet capacity, and opened 32 one-stop service centres in post office buildings.

2026-09-14-uga-eagle-ura-data-driven-tax.summary: The Uganda Revenue Authority began implementing its taxpayer compliance risk management strategy and compliance improvement plan for 2026/27. It will use taxpayer records, transaction data and sector trends to target evasion, inaccurate declarations, non-registration and late filing, and prioritises compliance with the EFRIS e-invoicing system and digital tax stamps.

2026-09-14-uga-observer-free-internet-ac.summary: A rural community broadband network built by the Women of Uganda Network with netLabs!UG and the Internet Society Foundation is in technical testing at 12 sites in Uganda's Oyam district. Market traders already use it instead of buying mobile data; one vendor put her former spend at about Shs5,000 a day. More than 60 people have received digital literacy training.

2026-09-14-uga-ugstandard-tvet-diplomas-.summary: Uganda's TVET Council approved new national technician diploma curricula including cyber security, digital forensics and governance, and data science and analytics, alongside engineering and construction courses, its executive director Moses Kasakya said. Colleges may teach them only once accredited, and institutions have been asked to apply.

2026-09-14-uma-maghrebarabe-appel-offres.summary: The Arab Maghreb Union invited bids from audit firms to audit payments made from January to June 2026 to a migration statistics consultant hired under its 2023–2026 cooperation project with Statistics Sweden. The audit is to take 15 working days, and bids close on 23 September 2026. No contract value is given.

2026-09-14-undp-malawi-youth-leadership-.summary: Malawi's Zomba, Likoma and Mangochi district councils won US$20,000 under the Youth in Leadership Innovation Challenge, announced by the youth ministry and UNDP in Lilongwe on 11 September 2026. The councils will develop and test youth-led digital solutions to local service-delivery problems within their existing systems.

2026-09-14-worldbank-djibouti-country-pr.summary: The World Bank Group's private sector diagnostic for Djibouti, released on 13 September 2026, identifies reforms that could unlock at least $600 million of private investment and about 12,000 jobs over five years in off-grid solar, data centres and tourism. Data centres could draw $160 million to $240 million; existing capacity, served by eight submarine cables, is nearly full.

2026-09-14-xaf-aip-apm26-4-abidjan-posit.summary: CÃ´te d'Ivoire hosts the fourth and final African preparatory meeting for the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference in Abidjan from 15 to 17 September, under the African Telecommunications Union. Delegations will settle common proposals and candidacies before Doha in November.

2026-09-14-xaf-steyn-au-ai-strategy-impl.summary: Johan Steyn contrasts the African Union's 2024 endorsement of a continental AI strategy with the thirteen national strategies adopted since 2018. He cites South Africa's withdrawn draft policy as an example of the implementation gap.

2026-09-14-xaf-techzim-open-letter-afric.summary: Engineer Jacob Mutisi, a former Zimbabwe ICT association chair, wrote to African leaders urging an AU threat-monitoring centre, joint cyber defence and AI safety standards.

2026-09-14-xaf-thisisafrica-algorithm-di.summary: Blessing Vava argues that platform algorithms shape what African voters see, drawing on Zambia's 2026 election, including fake GEN-20 forms and a disputed video. He calls for rules on algorithmic governance before the next elections.

2026-09-14-xaf-uneca-eca-dhl-mou-msmes-i.summary: The UN Economic Commission for Africa and DHL Express Sub-Saharan Africa signed a non-exclusive three-year memorandum of understanding in Addis Ababa on 14 September 2026 to help small businesses trade across African borders under the AfCFTA. The first activity is a virtual training series on customs, logistics, e-commerce and digital trade through DHL's GoTrade programme. No financial value is attached.

2026-09-14-xna-aljazeera-shamal-afriqia-.summary: An Al Jazeera analysis asks whether North Africa will become an AI compute hub or merely host foreign capacity, weighing cables, renewable power and land against water limits on cooling. It puts the cost of each AI ecosystem at US$10-20 billion and argues the terms of value capture decide the answer.

2026-09-14-youm7-egypt-moj-remote-litiga.summary: Egypt's justice ministry defended the charges on its remote criminal litigation platform ahead of the new Criminal Procedure Law taking effect on 1 October, citing Article 531 as the basis for remote sessions. Technical office head Wadie Hanna Nashed said lawyers' use is optional and was requested by the bar, at EGP 500 a year for felony hearings and EGP 100 for detention renewals.

2026-09-14-youm7-egypt-ntra-mobile-walle.summary: Egypt's telecom regulator counted 57.01 million operator mobile wallets in the first half of 2026, up 23% in a year, with EGP 2.96 trillion transacted and penetration at 45%. Vodafone Cash held 77% of transaction value, and 67% of wallets were registered to men.

2026-09-14-zaf-groundup-activists-appeal.summary: The Housing Assembly and Foxglove, represented by the Legal Resources Centre, appealed the City of Cape Town's 14 July rezoning approval for an Equinix hyperscale data centre at King Air Industria, GroundUp reported on 14 September 2026. They say nearby communities were not consulted and that the application lacked information on water, electricity, emissions and noise for the proposed 174 MVA facility. Equinix has not yet submitted a site plan.

2026-09-14-zaf-sars-modernisation-3-0-ta.summary: South African Revenue Service Commissioner Johnstone Makhubu set out the agency's strategy at the 13th Tax Indaba in Sandton on 14 September 2026, putting trust, institutional capability, modernisation and partnership at its centre. He said consultations with taxpayers, practitioners and staff had produced four expectations: fairness, professionalism, responsiveness and partnership. No budget or timetable is given.

2026-09-14-zmb-solwezitoday-egp-tenders-.summary: Zambia published 103,326 tenders on its electronic government procurement system in 2025, up from 45,724 in 2024, according to the Zambia Public Procurement Authority's annual report. The system has recorded 173,428 tenders since 2016. An economist attributes much of the rise to electronic procurement becoming mandatory from April 2025.

2026-09-14-zoyk-zoykpay-autorisation-rdc.summary: Zambian fintech Zoyk received DR Congo central bank approval to deploy Zoykpay, which brings banks and mobile-money operators into one collection system for businesses. The approval date is not given.

2026-09-14-zwe-herald-rbz-mobile-money-c.summary: The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe says all mobile money providers are now linked to the national Civil Registry, allowing identity checks at sign-up and in ongoing KYC reviews. Governor John Mushayavanhu said operators completed a customer verification exercise by the 30 June 2026 deadline set in his February monetary policy statement, and all wallets were rescreened against the registry.

2026-09-14-zwe-ungm-laboratory-informati.summary: The UN Development Programme posted tender GP4382002 on the UN Global Marketplace for a company to implement a laboratory information management system in Zimbabwe. A pre-bid conference was held online on 10 September 2026. No budget, scope or closing date is given in the notice.

2026-09-15-ago-angop-ministro-destaca-pr.summary: Angola's telecoms minister, Mário Oliveira, said on 15 September 2026, at the launch of a podcast by Rádio Nacional de Angola, that the station's modernisation will improve signal and extend coverage in phases. He put Angola's mobile subscribers at about 29 million and mobile internet users at 18.7 to 19 million, and said Angola Online has about 183 free access points.

2026-09-15-ago-angop-rna-ganha-centro-de.summary: Angola's telecommunications minister, Mário Oliveira, inaugurated a centre in Luanda on 15 September 2026 that monitors Rádio Nacional de Angola's national transmitter network in real time, and the station switched from analogue to digital at the same event. He said this completes the Luanda phase of the station's modernisation project, with Namibe and Huíla next.

2026-09-15-ago-lusa-unita-registo-eleito.summary: The main opposition leader accused the government of using state means to register the governing party's own members early in the electoral roll update for the 2027 elections, speaking after completing his own proof-of-life step.

2026-09-15-ago-pti-mario-oliveira-lancam.summary: Angola's telecommunications minister, Mário Oliveira, was due in Benguela province on 16 September 2026 to launch Angola Telecom's TudoNossoFibra internet service at Baía Farta and the first Angola Telecom and MSTelcom broadband link in Restinga, Lobito. He was also to hand over a primary school rehabilitated under the Ngola Digital project.

2026-09-15-ben-techreviewafrica-apdp-17-.summary: Seventeen officers of the data protection authority were sworn in before the Cotonou court of first instance on 14 September under the digital code, formally binding them to the obligations of their duties.

2026-09-15-bfa-lefaso-administration-pub.summary: Burkina Faso's digital transition ministry launched Faso Sign, a national electronic signature platform for the public administration, in Ouagadougou on 15 September 2026. It is built into three existing platforms: CIMEXT for mission orders, SIGEG for administrative mail and SYCAD for land and property records. The prime minister told ministries to set a timetable for adopting it, calling its use an obligation.

2026-09-15-bfa-sidwaya-uemoa-journaliste.summary: The West African Economic and Monetary Union Commission held its annual briefing session for economic journalists from its eight member states in Ouagadougou from 14 September 2026, with its media platform PDM-UEMOA. Topics included the regional artificial intelligence strategy, the IMPACT 2030 strategic plan, competition policy and infrastructure projects.

2026-09-15-biometricupdate-e-gova-camero.summary: A digital government summit in Yaounde from 14 to 17 October will address how to build connected, interoperable, secure and accessible public service delivery systems across the continent.

2026-09-15-biometricupdate-south-africa-.summary: The state IT agency is seeking a supplier to equip the police with facial recognition integrated into body-worn and dashboard cameras, the software also to include automatic number plate recognition.

2026-09-15-caf-agenceecofin-cardip-banqu.summary: The country's component of the Central Africa digital integration programme is to launch in April 2027, after a week of work in Bangui by a financier mission covering connectivity, public services, data and cybersecurity.

2026-09-15-cipesa-beyond-ai-safety-afric.summary: A policy organisation argues that safety is not the whole question for African countries in global artificial intelligence governance: without infrastructure, skills, resources and representation, safety without sovereignty and agency is not enough.

2026-09-15-citinewsroom-ghana-200m-digit.summary: The communications minister said government has begun implementing measures against gaps a UNESCO readiness assessment identified in digital infrastructure, artificial intelligence capacity and cybersecurity, putting US$250m against an AI computing centre and US$200m against digitalisation.

2026-09-15-civ-afriqueeconomie-pnd-2026-.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's digital transition minister, Djibril Ouattara, presented 541.3 billion FCFA of digital investment opportunities to the private sector in Abidjan on 15 September 2026, drawn from the 2026–2030 National Development Plan. The ministry puts the digital economy at close to 6% of GDP and targets 15% by 2030. The private sector is expected to provide 70.2% of the plan's financing.

2026-09-15-civ-aip-position-africaine-un.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's digital transition minister Djibril Ouattara opened the last African preparatory meeting for the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference in Abidjan on 15 September 2026, calling for a common African position before the Doha conference in November. He announced Côte d'Ivoire's candidacy for the ITU Council for 2027-2030. The African Telecommunications Union said about 18 African countries are contesting 13 Council seats.

2026-09-15-civ-aip-snt-38000-producteurs.summary: About 38,000 cocoa farmers in Côte d'Ivoire sold beans using their producer cards between 1 and 13 September 2026, the first two weeks of the mandatory national traceability system, with transactions sent in real time to the Coffee-Cocoa Council. Reuters figures put purchases over the period at more than 26,000 tonnes, and 450 waybills covering over 18,000 tonnes were validated in the council's stock-reporting system.

2026-09-15-cmr-journalducameroun-4e-rgph.summary: Counting closed on 15 September for the fourth population and housing census, coupled with the agriculture and livestock census, after a start on 24 April and extensions in May and July. Coverage remained below expectation.

2026-09-15-cmr-journalducameroun-minjec-.summary: The youth ministry signed a three-year renewable partnership with a company on 14 September to digitise, unify and speed access to employment and training for 15- to 35-year-olds, across six areas including socio-economic integration.

2026-09-15-cog-adiac-central-africa-tele.summary: A regional workshop in Brazzaville on 15 and 16 September worked towards a common framework for national emergency telecommunications plans across central Africa, convened by the international telecommunications union with the regional regulators' assembly and the economic community.

2026-09-15-cog-labreveonline-artac-eccas.summary: Experts from eight Central African countries met in Brazzaville on 15–17 September 2026 to review a model national emergency telecommunications plan for keeping communications running in disasters. Figures presented there credit Congo's universal service fund FASUCE with connecting more than 380,000 people in isolated areas and over 250 localities.

2026-09-15-com-lagazette-udc-pnud-unipod.summary: The national university and the United Nations development programme signed a memorandum on training, research and innovation, at its centre a shared innovation space intended to bring students, researchers, entrepreneurs and institutions together on local problems.

2026-09-15-connectingafrica-dni-129m-sou.summary: A privately owned South African investment company announced investments above R2.1bn, about US$129.2m, across a fibre network operator, two internet service providers, an eSIM company and a mobile technology and fintech company.

2026-09-15-connectingafrica-gates-founda.summary: A foundation committed US$1bn over two years to artificial intelligence tools for health workers, farmers and teachers in the world's poorest regions, published alongside its tenth annual progress report on whether AI narrows or widens global disparities.

2026-09-15-crvs-laws-morocco-coordinatio.summary: A legal analysis of Morocco's civil registration law finds that Decree 2.22.04 permits, but does not require, the interior ministry to share civil-status data with the statistics authority. Law 36.21 establishes a digital registration system, and no national coordinating committee for civil registration, statistics and identity exists.

2026-09-15-cssps-over-6-000-of-8-000-com.summary: Ghana's education ministry said on 15 September 2026 that it had resolved more than 6,000 of about 8,000 complaints about the Computerised School Selection and Placement System, most concerning residential status. Resolution centres were extended by a week and the 18 September school reopening date stands; the minister announced a technical committee to review the system.

2026-09-15-dailynews-world-bank-digital-.summary: With the US$150m Digital Tanzania Project due to complete on 31 October, its financier signalled support for a second phase in which artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies would take a central place. Nothing about a second phase is committed or costed.

2026-09-15-dza-elmawkie-avancees-paiemen.summary: The national economic, social and environmental council held a conference in Algiers on making electronic payment general, setting out the progress made against wider economic change.

2026-09-15-dza-radioalgerie-zerrouki-ai-.summary: The posts and telecommunications minister called for closing the global gap in artificial intelligence capability and for an international AI governance agency, speaking at a ministerial meeting on the margins of a global forum on AI ethics.

2026-09-15-egy-enterprise-digital-egp-ve.summary: A market explainer sets out how a digital pound would differ from existing instant payments and wallets: central bank money held directly rather than a claim on a bank or telco. The central bank is laying ground for a wholesale rollout before any retail use.

2026-09-15-egy-maspero-toya-technology-i.summary: A military production ministry subsidiary signed a memorandum with a global chip maker at the ministry's training complex in Cairo, framed as part of a push to localise technology and deepen domestic manufacturing. No value or deliverable is stated.

2026-09-15-egy-truthng-africa-data-centr.summary: Partnerships between a telecoms group, a pan-African operator and a domestic engineering contractor could draw as much as US$1bn into data-centre infrastructure, pairing large-scale development with locally hosted artificial intelligence computing.

2026-09-15-egy-youm7-fra-qarar-2863-tahl.summary: Egypt's Financial Regulatory Authority issued Decision No. 2863 of 2026 requiring licensed consumer-finance companies to verify applicants digitally and to check behavioural credit scores based on alternative data from the credit bureau I-Score before granting or refusing loans. The scoring requirement applies from 1 April 2027, once I-Score's system is ready, chairman Islam Azzam said.

2026-09-15-eth-norvan-eep-cuts-power-bit.summary: The state power utility cut supply to bitcoin mining and data-mining operations as a hydropower shortfall deepened, giving up the revenue that load was earning.

2026-09-15-fasoamazone-oni-cib-aes-enrol.summary: Burkina Faso's national identification office opened nine extra enrolment sites across Ouagadougou for the Sahel alliance biometric identity card after heavy demand at its main centre. Cards are promised within 48 hours during the special operation, which runs to International Identity Day on 16 September; no enrolment figures are given.

2026-09-15-gab-agp-cgi-pnud-techspace-ma.summary: The Gabonese Innovation Centre and the UN Development Programme signed an agreement in Libreville on 15 September 2026 to launch TechSpace Masuku, a technology and AI incubator at the Université des sciences et techniques de Masuku.
