It aims to train more than 300 young people, with emphasis on women; UNDP funds and supervises the project as part of UniPod Gabon. No budget is given.

2026-09-15-gab-agp-snedai-digitalisation.summary: Gabon's housing minister Mays Mouissi, with the planning and digital economy ministers, met SNEDAI Groupe on 14 September 2026 about digitising land records and civil registration under the Gabon Digital programme. SNEDAI's chief executive Adama Bictogo offered to help start the project, including through prefinancing. Costs were discussed but not disclosed.

2026-09-15-gab-gabonreview-backbone-nati.summary: Gabon's digital infrastructure holding company, SPIN, signed a 20-year concession with Gabon Fiber in Libreville on 14 September 2026 to run and extend the national fibre backbone, taking over from Axione, whose contract expires in November. More than 41 billion CFA francs is to add 1,651km of fibre to the existing 1,782km, in three phases.

2026-09-15-gab-gabonreview-gabon-fiber-c.summary: Gabon's digital infrastructure holding SPIN signed a 20-year public-private partnership with Gabon Fiber SA on 14 September 2026 to run, upgrade and extend the national fibre backbone from 16 November, when the Bouygues–Axione contract expires. SPIN keeps the existing 1,769 km, and Gabon Fiber will finance 1,651 km more, under an open-access obligation.

2026-09-15-gha-graphic-local-government-.summary: Ghana's local government minister, Mahama Ayariga, announced on 15 September 2026 that the Ghana Broadcasting Corporation will carry live coverage of general assembly and town hall meetings of metropolitan, municipal and district assemblies, with the civic education commission. The ministry is to procure 51 pickup vehicles for the work. No start date for the broadcasts was given.

2026-09-15-gha-graphic-one-million-coder.summary: Ghana's One Million Coders Programme had enrolled 141,954 accounts by August 2026, communications minister Samuel Nartey George said on 15 September. He said demand is highest for cybersecurity, data analytics and AI, and that 12 universities have signed agreements making its courses compulsory for first-year students from this academic year.

2026-09-15-gha-graphic-police-automated-.summary: The Ghana Police Service will begin full enforcement of traffic offences through its automated TRAFFITECH-GH programme on 1 October 2026, using cameras and handheld devices. Offenders will receive electronic notices by SMS and pay fines through Ghana.gov within 14 days. The pilot issued about 120,000 caution notices in 2024 and 2025.

2026-09-15-gha-myjoyonline-knust-epa-nat.summary: Researchers at Ghana's Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology took Environmental Protection Authority staff through tests of a national Air Quality Data Hub, reported on 15 September 2026. The platform, supported by the Clean Air Fund, brings sensor data held by different bodies into one store with a map dashboard, and the authority is to take ownership once a sustainability plan is agreed.

2026-09-15-gha-myjoyonline-traffitech-gh.summary: The Ghana Police Service published guidelines for TRAFFITECH-GH, its automated traffic enforcement system, which takes full effect on 1 October 2026. Cameras and sensors detect offences such as speeding, and notices are sent by SMS from the sender ID GPS-MTTD. Motorists have 14 days to pay through ghana.gov.gh, mobile money or *222#, or contest online, after which a 1% daily penalty applies.

2026-09-15-gha-neoreportgh-smart-africa-.summary: The Smart Africa Secretariat held a validation and roadmap workshop for Ghana under its AEDIB 2.0 programme in Accra on 9 and 10 September 2026, co-hosted by Ghana's science and communications ministries. Participants examined overlaps between a policy in development, a proposed Science and Technology Development Agency Bill and an advisory council not yet operating, and produced a workplan canvas.

2026-09-15-gha-onuaonline-african-approa.summary: The same minister called for a distinctly African approach to artificial intelligence, arguing African values, data, computing infrastructure and human capacity should be reflected in how AI is built and governed globally.

2026-09-15-gha-police-traffitech-gh-moto.summary: The Ghana Police Service's question-and-answer brochure for Traffitech-GH sets out how its automated traffic enforcement works. Cameras and sensors record offences such as speeding and red-light running, and the police send an electronic notice of violation by SMS to the vehicle owner. Fines are payable, or contestable online, within 14 days; after that a penalty of 1% of the fine is added for each day of default.

2026-09-15-gha-u-s-commerce-department-e.summary: A United States commerce delegation met the communications regulator in Accra on artificial intelligence regulation, emerging technologies and closer cooperation between the two institutions.

2026-09-15-gmb-mansabanko-competition-co.summary: The Gambia's National Assembly took the Competition and Consumer Protection Commission Bill 2026 through second reading on 15 September and sent it to committee. Tabled by trade minister Mod K. Ceesay, it replaces the 2007 competition and 2014 consumer protection Acts, creates an independent commission with powers to investigate and impose penalties, and extends consumer protection to distance selling and digital content.

2026-09-15-gnq-el-ministerio-de-transpor.summary: The transport, telecommunications and civil aviation ministry handed out certificates in Malabo after a two-month executive programme in artificial intelligence, machine learning and cybersecurity for its own staff.

2026-09-15-gnq-equatorial-guinea-starlin.summary: All satellite internet sales are to run through the telecommunications regulator, under the supervision of the artificial intelligence state secretariat, and contracts citizens obtained outside official channels are to be cancelled, decided at a working session on 9 September.

2026-09-15-gsma-somic-2026-global-ai-div.summary: The GSMA released its State of Mobile Internet Connectivity Report 2026 in New York on 15 September 2026, saying more than 3.4 billion people still do not use mobile internet. By end-2025 an entry-level smartphone cost the poorest fifth in Sub-Saharan Africa 76% of average monthly income, and memory prices more than doubled between late 2025 and early 2026, driven by demand for AI data centres.

2026-09-15-gsma-state-of-mobile-internet.summary: The GSMA's State of Mobile Internet Connectivity 2026 finds 4.8 billion people, 59% of the world, use mobile internet on their own device. Sub-Saharan Africa has the lowest rate at 25%, with a 66% usage gap and a 9% coverage gap. Its survey puts mobile internet use in Senegal at 87% of urban and 75% of rural adults.

2026-09-15-guinee-amadou-oury-bah-exige-.summary: Guinea's prime minister, Amadou Oury Bah, visited the national data centre at Koloma on 15 September 2026, found it about 90% complete but not operational, and ordered it brought into service. The investment is put at close to $10 million. He asked the digital economy ministry to identify blockages and wants concrete results within two to three weeks.

2026-09-15-horonyafinance-uemoa-strategi.summary: The West African Economic and Monetary Union (UEMOA) Commission presented a draft regional artificial intelligence strategy to journalists on 14 September 2026. It has four pillars: governance and regulation; infrastructure including regional compute centres and a sovereign cloud; skills; and innovation finance, with a regional AI academy and innovation fund proposed. No adoption date or budget is given.

2026-09-15-itweb-acsa-metaverse-patrol-r.summary: Airports Company South Africa's annual report sets a plan to 2031 to bring AI, connected sensors, blockchain and robotics into airport operations, from check-in and baggage handling to patrol robots and a metaverse proof of concept. The plan sits within a R21.7bn five-year capital pipeline that also covers wider modernisation.

2026-09-15-itweb-africa-sadc-bloc-rethin.summary: The Communications Regulators' Association of Southern Africa opened its 46th executive committee meeting in Mangochi, Malawi, chaired by the Malawian regulator, with AI, satellite services, cross-border platforms and cybersecurity on the agenda. The three-day meeting is also reviewing regional consumer-protection and universal-service frameworks.

2026-09-15-itweb-bma-digital-port-health.summary: South Africa's Border Management Authority launched a Port Health Management System at Durban Harbour, replacing shipping agents' e-mailed requests with online inspections, free pratique applications, endorsements, invoicing and payment. Durban is the pilot; no date is set for other ports.

2026-09-15-itweb-dbsa-backs-48000km-fibr.summary: The Development Bank of Southern Africa said businesses it financed through fund management contributed to 47,545km of fibre deployed in South Africa in the year to March 2026. It reported R20.7bn in disbursements and net profit up 47% to R7.8bn, but gave no fibre-specific investment figure.

2026-09-15-itweb-integrity360-cape-town-.summary: A 40-desk security operations centre opened in Cape Town on 14 September under a R55m investment, providing monitoring and incident response for customers across Africa and internationally, and stated to create about 100 jobs over three years.

2026-09-15-itweb-woan-comeback-kzn-uk-fu.summary: A R7m UK-funded programme in KwaZulu-Natal, run with South Africa's communications department, will support 25 local community network operators to deploy 250 public Wi-Fi hotspots, connect 150 schools, libraries and clinics and reach 1,500 homes. It applies the shared wireless open-access model locally after the national version was put on hold; no term or completion date is given.

2026-09-15-ken-businessdaily-somaliland-.summary: Berbera is being positioned as an alternative digital gateway for landlocked Ethiopia and South Sudan, offering providers, businesses and governments another route to global data connections beside the established Mombasa gateway.

2026-09-15-ken-digital-health-agency-pus.summary: The digital health agency, established under the Digital Health Act to coordinate health systems, is working to link facilities so patient records can be shared and patients need not carry physical files to treatment or referral.

2026-09-15-ken-ecofinagency-kdeap-review.summary: Kenya and the World Bank reviewed the $390 million Kenya Digital Economy Acceleration Project on 14 September 2026; more than 62,000 teachers have been trained and over 5,000 smart boards distributed. A 2025 World Bank aide-memoire found only eight of 25 results indicators on target and $10.6 million disbursed, 3.1% of the appraised amount. The project closes on 31 October 2028.

2026-09-15-ken-icta-rfb-538567-national-.summary: Kenya's ICT Authority issued bidding documents on 15 September 2026 for three-year framework agreements to extend the national fibre backbone (Lot 1) and cross-border and metro links (Lot 2). The procurement falls under the Kenya Digital Economy Acceleration Project, financed by credits 7289-KE and 7290-KE, and bids are due on 29 October 2026. No contract value is given.

2026-09-15-ken-kenya-in-talks-with-china.summary: The treasury's principal secretary met a Chinese development bank executive in Beijing to review projects the lender already supports and seek more funding for roads, water and connectivity.

2026-09-15-ken-kenya-takes-13-mega-proje.summary: The public-private partnership directorate took thirteen priority infrastructure projects to international investors in Seoul, covering transport, energy, water, irrigation and technology development for the current financial year.

2026-09-15-ken-sh320bn-raised-for-nation.summary: The president said about Sh320bn has been raised for the National Infrastructure Fund, which is now established in law with its top management appointed and its investment policy framework complete. The money is to finance roads, energy and water.

2026-09-15-ken-standard-kra-electronic-s.summary: The Kenya Revenue Authority is replacing its government-owned electronic cargo seal system with a multi-vendor framework from 26 October 2026, under the Regional Electronic Cargo Monitoring System. Importers, exporters, agents and transporters will choose among 15 approved private vendors for dry cargo and fuel seals; the authority says this brings GPS tracking and geofencing.

2026-09-15-lby-economy-ministry-makes-el.summary: The requirement bites in stages: a transitional period runs to the end of 2026, then from January 2027 for businesses whose annual transactions or shipments are worth US$1m or more.

2026-09-15-lby-gia-unified-directory-nat.summary: Libya's General Authority for Information met information centres from the Prime Minister's Office and the ministries of oil and gas, marine wealth, economy and trade, and vocational education in Tripoli on 14 September 2026 to work on a Unified Directory for National Indicators. Each body is to send its draft to the authority, which will prepare a final version for approval by the High Technical Committee for the National Information System.

2026-09-15-lby-mandatory-registration-of.summary: Decree 465 of 2026 makes registration on the unified digital trade system compulsory for importers, exporters and foreign companies supplying the market through Libyan companies, issuing a registration certificate and an electronic identification number.

2026-09-15-lby-stability-of-dinar-needs-.summary: The central bank governor, reviewing two years in office, named a unified budget, instant salary payment, electronic payments and point-of-sale terminals among his tenure's highlights, and said currency stability depends on fiscal discipline and unified spending channels rather than on the bank alone.

2026-09-15-lby-tripoli-chamber-of-commer.summary: The capital's chamber of commerce met on the economy minister's decision 449 of 2026, which from 30 September requires importers and foreign exporters to register on the unified digital trade system. Members questioned whether the date can be met and what the decision will cost them.

2026-09-15-levisionnaire-togo-ipdcp-mise.summary: The data protection authority convened ministry chiefs of staff and secretaries-general in Lome on their obligations under the 2019 personal data law and the measures needed to bring public-sector processing into conformity.

2026-09-15-liberianobserver-mafalleh-dat.summary: An opinion piece on the newly enacted Data Protection Act argues the law is the easy part: it sets the country's first standalone framework for collecting, processing, storing and using personal data, and implementation is what will decide whether it means anything.

2026-09-15-liberianobserver-wilkins-glob.summary: An opinion piece argues for a global body on artificial intelligence modelled on the climate conferences, framed as ensuring that AI never controls the world rather than controlling AI itself.

2026-09-15-lso-lesotho-s-biggest-foreign.summary: The country signed a US$6.2bn agreement, its largest recorded foreign investment, for a hydropower plant and artificial intelligence data centre. A feasibility study runs over the next year, then implementation agreements including water-use plans, and a potential conflict of interest has surfaced.

2026-09-15-lso-minister-may-benefit-from.summary: The public works minister holds shares in a firm the energy minister named among potential local partners for the country's US$6.2bn artificial intelligence and hydropower project. He has previously been accused of conflict of interest.

2026-09-15-mar-moroccoworldnews-ebrd-25m.summary: A development bank approved a EUR 25m loan to a Moroccan bank for small and medium businesses financing climate-related investments, part of a wider EUR 65m package.

2026-09-15-mar-panorapost-mou-vertiv-inf.summary: The digital transition ministry and a critical digital-infrastructure supplier signed a memorandum in Rabat on developing digital infrastructure, cloud computing and artificial intelligence.

2026-09-15-mar-panorapost-seghrouchni-ia.summary: The digital transition minister said the country aims to make artificial intelligence a lever of digital sovereignty, territorial equity and inclusive development, speaking at an event on AI in public services.

2026-09-15-mdg-2424-task-force-reclamati.summary: The finance ministry announced a task force on mobile money complaints, bringing the banking supervision commission and the communications regulator together to speed up resolution. Users report lost money, failed transactions and long waits.

2026-09-15-mdg-demainafrique-refondation.summary: A public-life observatory president assesses ten months of the transition, conceding measurable social gains but pointing to an energy crisis, rising debt and instability, and proposing six work programmes over eighteen months.

2026-09-15-mdg-fid-location-serveurs-clo.summary: A development fund opened a tender, closing 29 September, to rent two cloud servers under a World Bank-financed girls' empowerment and resilience project.

2026-09-15-moz-clubofmozambique-electron.summary: Electronic money accounts reached 130.9 per 100 adults in the second quarter of 2026, against 33.8 per 100 for traditional bank accounts, on central bank figures covering three operators.

2026-09-15-moz-igc-ispc-compliance-mobil.summary: A study of small-taxpayer compliance in Maputo province finds the payment process itself costly: among those who had difficulty paying, 27 per cent cited service unavailability, 22 per cent lack of money and 19 per cent long queues. Mobile wallet payment could cut those costs, though fraud concerns reduce willingness to adopt it.

2026-09-15-moz-mznews-atdi-plano-operaci.summary: The digital transformation agency met in Maputo to set the basis of an operational plan for 2026 to 2029, its stated aim to replace isolated systems with a common architecture. A sovereign cloud and data centre and a national interoperability platform are among the priorities.

2026-09-15-moz-sapo-moeda-eletronica-con.summary: The same central bank figures show the accounts skewed male: 144.7 per 100 adult men against 118.5 per 100 adult women.

2026-09-15-mrt-maurinews-starlink-maurit.summary: Mauritania appears on a satellite operator's list of sixteen African markets targeted for launch during 2026, after roughly two years seeking a licence. The authorities' conditions concern security guarantees and control over data, and an application lodged with a local partner is still pending.

2026-09-15-mwi-ednews-givedirectly-canva.summary: A cash-transfer organisation working in Malawi since 2019 expanded after a US$150m donation, paying unconditional lump sums of about US$550 directly to the poorest adults by mobile money.

2026-09-15-mwi-malawi24-90-percent-scams.summary: Malawi's communications regulator, MACRA, said prisoners are behind up to 90% of reported mobile money scams, with Zomba Maximum Security Prison a major source. Methods include SIM swaps, fake promotions, calls demanding border clearance fees for non-existent parcels, and WhatsApp account takeovers. No measures by the prison service or network operators are reported.

2026-09-15-mwi-mwnation-digital-rights-c.summary: Three district councils each won US$20,000 under a youth innovation challenge to develop and test youth-led digital solutions to service delivery problems inside existing council systems.

2026-09-15-nam-namibian-beyond-certifica.summary: A commentary sets vocational training against an unemployment rate of 36.9 per cent and youth unemployment of 44.4 per cent, alongside reported shortages in more than seventy occupations, arguing the country produces qualifications faster than capability.

2026-09-15-ner-journalduniger-cnib-aes-a.summary: Enrolment for the regional bloc's biometric national identity card opened in Agadez at the regional police headquarters, fingerprints and biometric parameters collected locally and processed centrally.

2026-09-15-ner-modernghana-media-adjustm.summary: The council of ministers approved an overhaul of the media regulatory framework on 10 September, tightening accreditation for foreign correspondents and carrying a draft ordinance requiring online press publishers to be identified, with legal responsibility on digital newsrooms for what they carry.

2026-09-15-nga-ngcert-advisory-escalatin.summary: The national computer emergency response team issued an advisory recording a significant rise in high-impact incidents across multiple sectors, driven by phishing, ransomware, business email compromise and data breaches, enabled by cybercrime-as-a-service models and AI-driven techniques.

2026-09-15-nga-nitda-naccima-partnership.summary: Nigeria's IT development agency, NITDA, and the national chambers of commerce body, NACCIMA, signed a memorandum of understanding at GITEX Nigeria in Lagos on 3 September 2026, published by NITDA on 15 September. It covers a shared digital platform, digital transformation for small businesses, technology adoption and training. No sum, term or funding source is stated.

2026-09-15-nga-nitda-nahcon-digitise-haj.summary: The information technology development agency and the Hajj commission renewed a commitment to digitise pilgrimage administration, after the commission's chairman led a delegation to the agency's Abuja headquarters.

2026-09-15-nga-thecabal-inec-nin-integra.summary: Nigeria's electoral commission (INEC) said on 15 September 2026 that it has used National Identification Numbers to audit and clean the voter register ahead of the 2027 elections, working with the identity commission. Acting chairman Rhoda Gumus told an African Union mission that close to 100 million voters will be served across 176,846 polling units.

2026-09-15-nga-von-cac-unified-beneficia.summary: The corporate registry's registrar-general called for the country's three separate beneficial ownership registers, held under different institutional frameworks, to be harmonised and centralised.

2026-09-15-nist-ir-8587-protecting-token.summary: A United States standards body published final implementation recommendations for agencies and cloud providers on protecting authentication tokens and assertions from forgery, theft and misuse.

2026-09-15-pamfp-mobilization-of-non-oil.summary: An undated page from Equatorial Guinea's public-finance modernisation programme sets out plans for a unique taxpayer identification number and an integrated revenue system linking the tax, customs and treasury administrations. It also lists extending the SYDONIA customs system to seven sites outside Malabo; no timetable or delivery status is given.

2026-09-15-programme-de-modernisation-de.summary: An undated Moroccan interior ministry page describes the 2011-2015 programme to computerise civil registration across 2,176 civil-status offices staffed by more than 12,000 municipal officials, including digitising historical registers. It records a steering committee created by ministerial order in November 2010; no completion figures are given.

2026-09-15-punch-hotspot-world-bank-500-.summary: Nigerian rural infrastructure firm Hotspot Network secured a World Bank-backed results-based facility to bring 2G, 4G, broadband and community Wi-Fi to 500 unserved communities. The work sits under the US$750m DARES renewable-energy access programme run with the Rural Electrification Agency; the facility's amount and signing date are not reported.

2026-09-15-rwa-newtimes-online-vat-regim.summary: A New Times commentary on Rwanda's ministerial order on VAT for online services, in force since 29 April 2026, notes that the revenue authority's registration portal was due by 29 July but is not yet running. Under the order, banks must withhold VAT on payments to unregistered suppliers, and the author says the order sets no turnover threshold for non-residents and no reverse charge for business customers.

2026-09-15-rwa-taarifa-university-forum-.summary: A university faculty head called on educators, researchers and policymakers to rethink education as artificial intelligence changes how people learn and work, speaking at the fifth conference of a lifelong-learning project bringing together universities from Rwanda, Uganda, Ethiopia and Norway.

2026-09-15-sanews-dpsa-batho-pele-ai-cha.summary: The public service department's chatbot, launched in late August, gives public servants access to policy updates, circulars and legislation in nine official languages.

2026-09-15-sdn-alradar-white-nile-electr.summary: The standards and metrology body's White Nile branch began collecting fees electronically, issuing a receipt at the moment of payment, presented as enforcement of a state-wide electronic collection decision.

2026-09-15-sdn-sudantimes-dagalo-unified.summary: Rapid Support Forces commander Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo ordered traders in RSF-held areas of Sudan to charge one price whether customers pay in cash or through the Bankak app, a Future Bank manager in East Darfur said. The gap between cash and electronic prices had reached about 40% in some markets. Government bodies in those areas were told to stop collecting payments through Bankak and use Future Bank instead.

2026-09-15-sen-seneweb-preparation-ia-se.summary: The West African Economic and Monetary Union Commission presented a draft regional artificial intelligence strategy at a press session in Ouagadougou, with Oxford Insights' 2025 government AI readiness figures placing Senegal first of the union's eight states on a score of 46.10. The draft covers a common regulatory framework, data governance, skills, computing infrastructure and phased adoption in health, education and agriculture. The rankings as reported are internally inconsistent.

2026-09-15-sle-techreviewafrica-open-sou.summary: The communications ministry will take its open-source software agenda to a side event at the United Nations General Assembly on 24 September, with a UN partner, arguing open source supports affordable, secure and locally owned digital systems.

2026-09-15-sle-thisday-free-nationwide-l.summary: The lands minister said the government plans free nationwide land registration and title certification, with systematic registration of parcels across the country.

2026-09-15-smartafrica-kitsoft-mou-publi.summary: The Smart Africa Secretariat signed a memorandum of understanding with Kitsoft, a GovTech company of Ukrainian origin, on public-sector digital transformation, announced on 15 September 2026. It covers digital public infrastructure, e-governance and AI, including building public services on Kitsoft's low-code Liquio platform. The release gives no signing date, value or duration.

2026-09-15-som-dawan-opinion-vanishing-s.summary: A university dean argues the shilling's disappearance from daily commerce reflects institutional collapse, dollarisation, technological change and eroded trust, and that restoring it is a credibility exercise rather than a printing one.

2026-09-15-ssd-radiotamazuj-oped-china-a.summary: An opinion piece argues South Sudan should learn from China's route into artificial intelligence, reading the global realignment as driven by computing capability rather than by arms or raw materials.

2026-09-15-ssd-techreviewafrica-data-gov.summary: The communications authority joined a three-day workshop on domesticating the continental data policy framework, hosted by the African Union Commission, its development agency and two partners with the ICT ministry, to set a roadmap for implementation.

2026-09-15-swz-eswatinipositivenews-illi.summary: Delegates at a regional public accounts committees conference found the institutions fighting illicit financial flows fragmented across the southern African region, leaving gaps through which funds move faster than authorities can detect or recover them.

2026-09-15-swz-eswatinipositivenews-sadc.summary: A commission of the SADC public accounts committees' 18th annual conference in Eswatini reported that governments may see spending data almost in real time while parliamentary oversight can come 12 to 24 months later. It considered using data analytics and AI to screen transactions for auditors, with secure oversight access to financial systems, and warned against treating technology as a substitute for human judgement.

2026-09-15-swz-technology-devices-school.summary: Eswatini's education minister, Owen Nxumalo, said on 15 September 2026 that Taiwan has donated more than 1,140 computers and 60 printers to 49 schools, and that the cabinet has bought 40 interactive screens, installed in five schools per region, with 106 more schools to follow. He said the ministry has secured a US$4.75m Global Partnership for Education grant for technology in education, without giving its timing.

2026-09-15-swz-times-businessmen-switch-.summary: The revenue service says some businessmen change the order or variation of their names to avoid detection, making taxpayers hard to identify, and that digital identification would establish when different names belong to the same person.

2026-09-15-syc-statehouse-hydrographic-o.summary: Cabinet approved a hydrographic office inside the maritime safety authority, to bring hydrographic information together from across government and international partners for navigation, search and rescue, marine planning and the blue economy.

2026-09-15-tcd-alwihdainfo-abeche-adetic.summary: Abeche's town hall, the provincial telecommunications delegation and the ICT development agency met on 15 September to strengthen a partnership digitising municipal services and training staff in digital tools.

2026-09-15-tcd-lendjampost-commerce-nume.summary: With a world trade forum in Geneva debating the digital transformation of services trade, expected to grow 4.8 per cent in 2026, a commentary asks what a landlocked country can take from a shift that moves trade onto screens rather than through ports.

2026-09-15-techafricanews-axian-telecom-.summary: AXIAN Telecom is renaming itself Yas Group, extending to corporate level the brand its operators in Madagascar, Comoros, Senegal, Togo and Tanzania adopted in November 2024. Tower, infrastructure and fintech units such as TowerCo of Africa and Mixx keep their own names.

2026-09-15-techafricanews-gsma-ai-divide.summary: An industry association's 2026 connectivity report warns of a divide between artificial intelligence haves and have-nots: more than 3.4 billion people do not use mobile internet although over 90 per cent of them live inside mobile broadband coverage, with smartphone affordability the obstacle.

2026-09-15-techafricanews-helios-towers-.summary: Helios Towers Malawi said it had built 233 tower sites in 2026, 40% in remote rural areas, with 55 more due by early October. The company gave the figures at a meeting with regulator MACRA, which pressed for lower-cost infrastructure in underserved areas.

2026-09-15-techafricanews-kenya-ca-consu.summary: The communications regulator opened a consultation on a licensing framework for GSM-based alarm response systems, which use SIM-enabled devices on public mobile networks to transmit alarm signals, to define their regulatory scope and licensing requirements.

2026-09-15-techafricanews-kenya-digiken-.summary: A multi-stakeholder digital programme carrying about US$4.26m in funding and co-financing supports fifteen innovation hubs in media and information literacy, digital skills, platform entrepreneurship and sustainable agriculture. Its steering committee reviewed progress.

2026-09-15-techafricanews-orange-egypt-c.summary: An operator and a pharmacy management company signed a partnership to combine pharmacy management technology with connectivity, covering sales, dispensing, inventory and customer management in one connected system.

2026-09-15-techafricanews-senegal-wave-d.summary: Senegal's government held talks with mobile-money company Wave on 10 September 2026 about digitising transport, health and Treasury services, with data management and the Telecommunications Code also discussed. No agreement was announced; further workshops are planned.

2026-09-15-techafricanews-tanzania-ict-m.summary: The ICT minister visited the state telecom's fibre experience centre in Dar es Salaam and was briefed on the services delivered over its fibre-to-the-home and fibre-to-the-x connections.

2026-09-15-techcabal-buupass-safaribucks.summary: A travel-booking startup is adding cross-border payments through a partnership with a Nairobi digital wallet, letting travellers pay for buses, flights and transfers with transactions settled through local payment rails.

2026-09-15-techcabal-kenya-high-court-vo.summary: A three-judge High Court bench voided the government's sale of a 15 per cent Safaricom stake, a KES 204.3bn transaction that closed less than three months earlier, ruling it unconstitutional because key information was withheld from the public, the cabinet and parliament.

2026-09-15-techcabal-madica-five-startup.summary: Pre-seed programme Madica invested $200,000 each in five startups, its first in Algeria (HR software firm Talenteo) and Cameroon (neobank Paysika), alongside ChipMango in Nigeria and Delta Oil and Bekia in Egypt. Its portfolio now stands at 18 companies in 10 markets, with $1.6m deployed in 2026.

2026-09-15-techcabal-terrahex-bitcoin-mi.summary: A Nigerian founder plans bitcoin mining sites built around stranded power, treating oil fields as mines: cheap electricity that has no other buyer.

2026-09-15-techtrends-africa-shape-ai-ec.summary: A commentary argues the continent supplies labour, data and increasingly the market for artificial intelligence but rarely the ownership, and that on present course it will spend the next decade paying rent in a house it helped build.

2026-09-15-tgo-digital-bus-ticketing-wid.summary: Togo's public bus operator SOTRAL plans to extend digital ticketing across its network by the end of 2026, after a pilot on routes serving University of Lomé students. The transport ministry is finalising the project with operator Yas Togo, including USSD ticket purchase by phone, while SOTRAL standardises fares. SOTRAL carries nearly 26,000 passengers a day.

2026-09-15-tgo-levisionnaire-matglac-eta.summary: The territorial administration ministry ran a three-day technical workshop from 8 September for the cell supporting the review of the 2009 civil status law, a review formally opened on 21 August.

2026-09-15-tgo-savoirnews-lome-surveilla.summary: About forty biologists, technicians, researchers and bioinformaticians from west and central Africa are in Lome from 9 to 22 September for a workshop under a thirteen-country genomic surveillance programme built after the Covid-19 period, strengthening sequencing capacity and outbreak response.

2026-09-15-tun-realites-ai-forward-summi.summary: A second artificial intelligence summit opened on 9 September in Yasmine Hammamet, organised by the Arab ICT organisation with the communications ministry, bringing more than 450 participants to questions of sovereignty and governance.

2026-09-15-tun-tunisienumerique-tradenet.summary: The trade network opened a web portal for electronic invoicing from 15 September, aimed at businesses and professionals with low invoicing volumes, letting them configure their environment and prepare and track invoices.

2026-09-15-tza-dailynews-data-governance.summary: A commentary argues the country is generating more data than ever while its capacity to govern, integrate, protect and use that data has not kept pace, and that the gap threatens the growth digital transformation is meant to deliver.

2026-09-15-tza-habarileo-helios-camara-m.summary: A tower company opened an ICT laboratory worth 30m shillings at a secondary school in Iringa, with 26 desktop computers and a projector, for 873 students and 43 teachers.

2026-09-15-tza-thecitizen-digital-transf.summary: A commentary argues digital transformation amounts to more than connectivity, and that treating network reach as the measure mistakes the means for the end.

2026-09-15-tza-timesmajira-kairuki-ttcl-.summary: The ICT minister, after visiting the state telecom's fibre centre, said smartphone use has reached 47 per cent and that the ten-year digital transformation plan continues, including wider access to modern devices.

2026-09-15-tza-timesmajira-omdtz-ramani-.summary: A mapping organisation working with government began handing ward flood preparedness plans to communities in five Dar es Salaam wards, over five days from 14 September, under an externally funded project using mapping and geographic information to reduce disaster risk.

2026-09-15-uga-businessoftech-sandi-ai-g.summary: A Ugandan startup using artificial intelligence and agricultural data to help rural farmers reach finance without conventional collateral won a US$50,000 prize at a continental agrifood forum.

2026-09-15-uga-cajnews-stricter-measures.summary: The communications regulator said it is working with parliament on a framework allowing targeted denial of service to repeat abusers of cyberspace, its director likening the measure to withdrawing a driving licence. No bill, offence definition or appeal route is published.

2026-09-15-uga-kikubolane-central-bank-p.summary: Bank of Uganda governor Michael Atingi-Ego told a parliamentary committee on 14 September 2026 that the bank will investigate claims that mobile money operators it supervises, MTN and Airtel, helped digital lenders recover unpaid loans from the wallets of people listed as guarantors without consent. Standalone digital lenders fall under the finance ministry, not the central bank.

2026-09-15-uga-newvision-ai-training-tve.summary: Uganda has added artificial intelligence modules to 17 new specialised technician diploma curricula in its revised technical and vocational training system. A trainer orientation ran from 14 to 18 September 2026 at Nakawa Vocational College. Trainers said instructors need to understand the technology first and that institutions lack the laboratories and computers to teach the modules.

2026-09-15-uga-nilepost-ura-lauds-manufa.summary: The Uganda Revenue Authority told the Uganda Manufacturers Association in Kampala that more than 1,680 manufacturers and importers are registered on its Digital Tax Stamps portal, run by SICPA Uganda since 2018, Nile Post reported on 15 September 2026. The authority said the stamps and its EFRIS e-invoicing system supported nearly 40% growth in domestic revenue in 2024/25, and that stamp costs are tax-deductible.

2026-09-15-ustda-afridata-nigeria-data-c.summary: The US Trade and Development Agency has granted US$1,870,000 to Infragora Global Capital for a feasibility study of two data centres in Nigeria's Lagos and Delta states, with 60–70 MW of combined capacity expandable to 100 MW. US firms are invited to bid by 13 October 2026. The centres would be owned by AFRIDATA Datacenter Nigeria Ltd, a company formed for the project.

2026-09-15-wearetech-benin-nigeria-douan.summary: The two countries' customs administrations launched a pilot interconnection of their systems at the Seme-Krake border post on 11 September, to exchange data in real time and cut repeated formalities.

2026-09-15-wearetech-tesfa-ai-natnael-ke.summary: A profile of an Addis Ababa company founded in 2025 to embed artificial intelligence in organisations' operations, building virtual assistants that carry out complex tasks rather than answer questions.

2026-09-15-wearetech-vula-mobile-3-milli.summary: South African referral app Vula Mobile, which connects rural health workers with specialist doctors, has passed three million patients referred. It operates in five southern African countries, which the report does not name.

2026-09-15-xaf-afdb-africa-korea-partner.summary: The African Development Bank and South Korea's finance ministry signed a letter of intent in Seoul on 9 September 2026 to strengthen the Korea-Africa Economic Cooperation (KOAFEC) Trust Fund and cooperate through Korea's Economic Development Cooperation Fund, naming AI and digital technologies as priorities. Korean contributions to the trust fund total US$132.82m; no new sum is attached to the letter.

2026-09-15-xaf-african-court-unesco-ai-j.summary: The African Court on Human and Peoples' Rights and UNESCO opened a four-day seminar on AI and the rule of law in Arusha on 15 September 2026 for more than 50 judges and staff, based on UNESCO's justice-sector toolkit. UNESCO cited its survey finding that 44% of judicial operators worldwide use AI tools but only 9% have had formal guidance or training.

2026-09-15-xaf-afriksoir-apm26-4-ouvertu.summary: Côte d'Ivoire opened the fourth and final African preparatory meeting for the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference in Abidjan on 15 September 2026, under the African Telecommunications Union. The meeting, closing on 17 September, is to settle common African proposals and candidatures for the Doha conference. The union also launched the fifth edition of its Innovation Challenge, with US$60,000 in prizes.

2026-09-15-xaf-star-internet-users-gende.summary: Figures from the UN Economic Commission for Africa's Economic Report on Africa 2026 show 43% of African men and 31% of African women used the internet in 2024, a 12-point gap. Worldwide the rates were 70% and 65%. Women's use in Africa peaked at 34% in 2022.

2026-09-15-xca-7joursinfo-cemac-sdmx-odp.summary: The Central African Economic and Monetary Community (CEMAC) held a workshop in Libreville from 14 to 18 September 2026, backed by the African Development Bank and UNFPA, to train experts from its six member states in the SDMX data-exchange standard. It is preparing national statistics sites to move to Open Data Platform 2.0 and a regional platform, CEMAC-Data.

2026-09-15-xca-depechesbrazzaville-eccas.summary: About 50 officials from eight Central African states met in Brazzaville on 15–16 September 2026 to draft a model national emergency telecommunications plan for floods, storms and other disasters. The workshop was organised by the ITU, the region's telecoms regulators' assembly and Congo's regulator, ARPCE.

2026-09-15-xca-lepaystchad-beac-reforme-.summary: The Bank of Central African States governor, Yvon Sana Bangui, met the IMF's Africa director on 14 September 2026 to define a new banking model for the CEMAC zone. Priorities include a central bank digital currency, stronger powers for the regional banking commission COBAC, mobile money and secure cross-border payments. The IMF has warned about the effect of the bank's special refinancing window on foreign exchange reserves.

2026-09-15-xea-igad-communique-74th-extr.summary: The IGAD Council of Ministers, meeting in Djibouti on 15 September 2026, endorsed in principle an IGAD Artificial Intelligence Centre of Excellence and invited member states to bid to host it. The council also recorded that five of seven members — Djibouti, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia and South Sudan — have ratified the 2023 IGAD Treaty, meeting the threshold for its entry into force.

2026-09-15-xwa-adomonline-ecowas-commiss.summary: ECOWAS has appointed Ghanaian engineer and former roads minister Amin Amidu Sulemani as Commissioner for Infrastructure, Energy and Digitalisation for 2026–2030, under new Commission President Birame Diop. The appointment was approved at the ECOWAS Assembly in Abuja. The portfolio covers digital economy and post, energy and mines, and transport.

2026-09-15-xwa-gouvernement-burkina-aes-.summary: A regional bloc meeting in Ouagadougou called for closer coordination between the administrative authorities of member states' border regions, framed around borders serving peace and development.

2026-09-15-zaf-sowetan-gumede-cybersecur.summary: An opinion piece argues the redrafted national artificial intelligence policy must carry sovereignty — independent control over technology, data security, privacy and infrastructure — against the dominance of a small number of foreign AI companies.

2026-09-15-zaf-techcentral-vodacom-safar.summary: Kenya's High Court on 15 September 2026 declared the government's sale of a 15 per cent Safaricom stake to Vodacom's Vodafone Kenya unconstitutional and ordered the shares returned to the state. The three-judge bench found public participation inadequate and the buyer's identity concealed. The June sale raised KSh204.3 billion; Vodacom said it will appeal and seek a stay.

2026-09-15-zaf-thesouthafrican-sassa-gra.summary: A grant recipient describes being asked for bank statements, school enrolment letters and the full first-application paperwork to keep her children's social grants through the agency's review process.

2026-09-15-zmb-diggers-vlogger-9-months-.summary: A Lusaka magistrate sentenced vlogger Joseph Chishimba to nine months on 15 September 2026, four days after convicting him under section 54 of Zambia's Cyber Security and Cyber Crimes Act 2021. He had posted to a WhatsApp group in October 2024 a screenshot of a Facebook post making claims about Chipo Mwanawasa.

2026-09-15-zmb-lusakatimes-government-la.summary: Zambia's government and Ignite Access launched a three-year programme on 15 September 2026 to connect 70 schools to Starlink satellite internet and fit solar power where schools are off the grid. Ignite Access will provide equipment and data free in the first year. Government targets 66% electricity access and 80% internet access by 2031.

2026-09-15-zmb-zambiamonitor-zicta-revok.summary: The communications regulator revoked an operator's network and service licences with effect from 14 September, citing persistent failures to meet regulatory, operational and financial obligations after considering the operator's representations.

2026-09-16-ago-angop-angola-digital-180-.summary: Angola's telecoms minister, Mário Oliveira, said in Benguela on 16 September 2026 that the Angola Digital project, promoted by the communications development fund FADCOM, now has about 180 free public internet access points in 18 of the country's 21 provinces. He said the satellite-based Conecta project is also present in 18 provinces.

2026-09-16-ago-angop-manutencao-preventi.summary: Angola's interbank payments operator EMIS warned that maintenance from 17 to 19 September 2026, between 01:00 and 04:00, may briefly disrupt the Multicaixa card network.

2026-09-16-ago-angop-ministro-mario-oliv.summary: Angola Telecom switched on its Tudonosso fibre-to-the-home service at the 1,000-dwelling Baía Farta housing centre in Benguela on 16 September 2026, the first site of a project the telecoms minister placed within the national broadband network.

2026-09-16-ago-angop-rede-de-banda-larga.summary: Angola inaugurated the first link of its national fibre broadband network at Lobito on 16 September 2026, on a route from Luanda through Bengo and Cuanza Sul. Angola Telecom named Huambo, Namibe and Cabinda for the next phase, with all 21 provinces as the aim.

2026-09-16-ago-pocnoticias-mercury-angol.summary: Mercury and Angola Telecom brought into service a new broadband backbone link at Restinga, Lobito, in Benguela province on 16 September 2026, under Angola's National Broadband Programme. The first phase provides 100 Gbps of capacity, and the operators describe it as the first of several provincial backbone links. No cost is given.

2026-09-16-ago-poligrafo-despacho-361-26.summary: Angola's President João Lourenço authorised spending of 90.5 billion kwanzas, about $98 million, on goods and services for a customs supervision project, by Presidential Order 361/26 of 14 September 2026, Polígrafo África reported. The purchase, in two lots, is a direct award on grounds of technical aptitude, covering centralised supervision, automated inspection and data analysis; Finance Minister Vera Daves was delegated to sign the contract. No supplier is named.

2026-09-16-bceao-communique-homologation.summary: The BCEAO certified the business APIs of a first group of participants on the regional instant payment platform on 16 September 2026, letting firms send and receive payments, submit bulk settlements and track transactions across the monetary union whatever the other party's provider.

2026-09-16-bceao-liste-api-business-pi-s.summary: The BCEAO's list of September 2026 names 23 participants whose business APIs are certified on the regional instant payment platform: nine in Senegal, seven in Côte d'Ivoire, two in Niger and one each in Benin, Burkina Faso, Guinea-Bissau, Mali and Togo.

2026-09-16-ben-lanation-economie-la-cryp.summary: La Nation explains that no law in Benin bars individuals from holding cryptocurrency, but it is not legal tender in the West African monetary union and no merchant must accept it. Taxes cannot be paid in it directly, and the union's own framework for crypto-assets is still being built.

2026-09-16-ben-lanation-recensements-gen.summary: ECOWAS member states began validating a practical guide for population and housing censuses in Cotonou on 15 September 2026, meant to make West African census data more reliable and comparable across countries.

2026-09-16-bfa-libreinfo-fasosign-lancem.summary: Burkina Faso launched FasoSign, a national electronic signature platform for the public administration, on 15 September 2026. It is already built into the mission-order, mail and cadastre systems, and the government says its keys and certificates are held under state responsibility.

2026-09-16-bfa-sidwaya-journee-internati.summary: Burkina Faso's Ministry of Security and the National Identification Office marked International Identity Day in Ouagadougou on 16 September 2026, on the use of biometrics and basic identification to secure academic and professional diplomas. Security Minister Mahamoudou Sana said the aim is a national framework for verifying qualifications, and that more than 70 police and gendarmerie files are being examined for sanction over roadblock harassment.

2026-09-16-biometricupdate-international.summary: International Identity Day 2026 turned the emphasis from population coverage to trust, with ID4Africa's executive chairman arguing that identity systems should be judged on whether they are useful, secure and under people's control throughout their lives.

2026-09-16-broadcastmediaafrica-crasa-46.summary: Southern African communications regulators meeting in Mangochi, Malawi, for the 46th executive committee of their association, CRASA, called for more agile and collaborative regulation as AI, satellite services and cross-border platforms reshape the sector. Host regulator MACRA's director-general urged more knowledge sharing and harmonised approaches.

2026-09-16-caf-arcep-observatoire-marche.summary: The Central African Republic's telecoms regulator, ARCEP, reported 1.56 million internet clients at the end of June 2026, up 22.9% in a year, and 3.9 million mobile clients. Starlink, licensed in March 2026, held over 70% of fixed-wireless internet clients and carried 22.89 million of the 36.11 million GB of traffic in the half. Operator revenue exceeded 41.68 billion CFA francs.

2026-09-16-carte-numerique-dagriculteur-.summary: Guinea's agriculture minister Félix Lamah received a delegation from the firm Pula, which presented a portal for mapping farms and registering producers to build the first national farmers' database, ahead of the handover of the first digital farmer cards. The ministry says the work is a deliverable of the World Bank-backed commercial agriculture project PDACG. No figures or timetable are given.

2026-09-16-civ-aip-pnd-2026-2030-sept-pi.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's digital minister presented seven pillars and 40 projects for the digital part of the 2026-2030 development plan, from universal connectivity and interoperable administration to AI, cybersecurity and skills. The target is to raise the digital economy from an estimated 6 to 8% of GDP to 15% by 2030.

2026-09-16-cmr-ecomatin-bunec-52-milliar.summary: The director-general of Cameroon's national civil registration office, BUNEC, said on 14 September 2026 that completing the digitisation of civil-status records will cost 52 billion FCFA, against 27 billion estimated in 2018. Since the 2020 pilot, 60 of the country's 432 civil registration centres have been digitised, 13.9%. Completion is targeted for 2029–2030 if the money is found.

2026-09-16-cod-7sur7-rdc-pass-formation-.summary: DR Congo began training the first 50 enrolment agents for its RDC-Pass digital identity platform on 15 September 2026, three months after its launch. The digital economy minister said RDC-Pass is an authentication tool, not a national identity card, and does not replace civil registration.

2026-09-16-com-alwatwan-gouvernance-nume.summary: The Comoros government's secretary-general, Nour El Fath Azali, has begun answering citizens' questions on public policy through his social media accounts to counter online rumours, his office said, reported on 16 September 2026. In one reply he gave 2020-2025 job figures and described a one-stop shop that lets diaspora and foreign investors register companies remotely.

2026-09-16-connectingafrica-vodacom-keny.summary: Vodacom and Kenya's Treasury both said on 16 September 2026 that they will appeal the High Court ruling that voided the sale of a 15% government stake in Safaricom. The court found the deal lacked meaningful public participation and hid material information, and ordered the stake returned to the state.

2026-09-16-cpv-expressodasilhas-ministro.summary: Cabo Verde's health minister said on 16 September 2026 that sharing clinical records and test results across health facilities would stop patients repeating examinations as they move between islands. He set digitalisation beside new financing sources as Global Fund support declines.

2026-09-16-cpv-inforpress-maio-transform.summary: Cabo Verde's economy and digital transition ministry presented 'Maio Transforma' on the island of Maio on 16 September 2026, a programme within the national 'Cabo Verde Transforma' pilot to develop farming, fishing, enterprise and the digital economy. Minister António Baptista said projects on internet access and training would start within days. No budget is given.

2026-09-16-crasa-46th-exco-malawi.summary: The Communications Regulators' Association of Southern Africa held the 46th ordinary meeting of its Executive Committee on 14–16 September 2026 at Makokola Club, Mangochi, hosted by the Malawi Communications Regulatory Authority. The meeting had been rescheduled because of venue availability. The listing gives no outcomes.

2026-09-16-dfc-wiocc-155m-equity-african.summary: The US International Development Finance Corporation's board approved more than $8 billion of new investments on 16 September 2026, including an equity investment in WIOCC Group, a wholesale connectivity and data-centre provider in Africa. DFC described WIOCC as the preferred partner for US technology companies expanding in Africa. No amount was published for the WIOCC investment.

2026-09-16-dgi-mauritanie-teleservices.summary: Mauritania's tax directorate runs an online filing and payment system for businesses and a set of teleservices for all registered taxpayers, covering online returns, the taxpayer's file, payment schedules and a secure channel to the administration.

2026-09-16-dji-adi-ministre-telecommunic.summary: Djibouti's telecoms minister received a Huawei vice-president to discuss cooperation on new-generation infrastructure and services, calling the company a leading partner in the country's ambition to be a regional connectivity hub. No agreement was announced.

2026-09-16-dji-lanation-previsions-meteo.summary: Djibouti's meteorological agency and its disaster risk secretariat held regional workshops in Ali-Sabieh and Tadjourah under the WISER programme, working with local officials, farmers and herders on turning forecasts into early action.

2026-09-16-dpi-map-mali-country-profile.summary: The DPI Map profile for Mali records the NINA identity number but no identity or civil registry act, no regulation for digital ID, no biometric use and no digital authentication function, while noting a national data protection law is in place.

2026-09-16-egy-ahram-mcit-intel-mou-ai-t.summary: Egypt's communications ministry signed a three-year memorandum with Intel on 16 September 2026 to train one million citizens a year in AI online and certify 500 trainers a year, in support of the national AI strategy for 2025-2030.

2026-09-16-egy-fintechgate-mcit-sommet-i.summary: Egypt's Ministry of Communications and Information Technology took part in the second AI summit organised by the Arab ICT Organization and the Arab League in Hammamet, Tunisia, from 7 to 10 September 2026. The ministry joined sessions on AI governance, trust and digital sovereignty, and on women in AI, where an alliance of Arab and African women in AI leadership was launched.

2026-09-16-egy-youm7-civil-registry-digi.summary: A Youm7 feature describes Egypt's interior ministry moving civil-registry services onto self-service machines that issue civil status documents at any hour, placed beyond registry offices in busy public locations. The piece gives no count of machines or transactions.

2026-09-16-egy-youm7-fintech-app-oversig.summary: Egypt's Supreme Council for Media Regulation and the Financial Regulatory Authority signed a protocol on 16 September 2026 on oversight of apps and platforms in the non-bank financial markets. Before licensing any app that uses the names of FRA-supervised firms or carries on such activity, the council must obtain the authority's technical opinion, due within 15 days.

2026-09-16-eth-birrmetrics-cbe-fayda-id-.summary: The Commercial Bank of Ethiopia has given customers outside Addis Ababa, Dire Dawa, Harari and 24 other cities until 9 November 2026 to link their accounts to the Fayda national digital ID, under a National Bank of Ethiopia directive. Unlinked accounts in areas already covered face debit restrictions blocking withdrawals and transfers. Linking can be done at branches or online.

2026-09-16-gab-gabonreview-data-center-i.summary: A Chinese government delegation inspected La Poste and Gabon Telecom sites in Libreville on 15 September 2026 as a possible home for an AI data centre serving the public administration. The postal site can host more than 300 servers; the project depends on the Gabon-China partnership being finalised.

2026-09-16-gabonreview-ged-basculement-a.summary: Gabon's digital economy ministry launched a pilot electronic document management system in Libreville on 16 September 2026 at the government's general secretariat and the examinations directorate. The system is developed by the national digital infrastructure agency ANINF with support from partners including the World Bank, and sits alongside an ordinance on electronic archiving (0003/PR/2026). No cost or rollout date is given.

2026-09-16-gha-myjoyonline-bog-digital-a.summary: The Bank of Ghana told a digital assets summit on 16 September 2026 that firms should build compliance, transparency and customer asset protection into their operations from the start. The organiser named the virtual assets law passed in December 2025 as the main change since the previous edition.

2026-09-16-gha-myjoyonline-customs-reven.summary: Ghana's revenue authority says customs collections have risen from about US$350 million to as much as US$450 million a month since an AI valuation system was installed at the ports in April 2026. It attributes the rise to more accurate valuation and classification rather than new taxes.

2026-09-16-gha-myjoyonline-household-reg.summary: Ghana's National Household Registry now covers 11.24 million people in 2,906,288 households across all 16 regions, 508,870 of them classed extremely poor. It is the targeting base for the LEAP cash grant, whose ceiling has risen to 450,000 households.

2026-09-16-gimtel-missions.summary: GIMTEL, the Mauritanian interbank card group set up under the central bank, groups ten banks and the postal service to develop card payments, including acceptance of international card networks and a domestic interbank network for payments and withdrawals.

2026-09-16-gnq-seneweb-coupure-facebook-.summary: Facebook and TikTok have been unreachable in Equatorial Guinea without a VPN since 2 September 2026, with internet speeds throttled, AFP reports. The restrictions followed a viral video accusing Vice-President Teodoro Nguema Obiang of corruption; its author was arrested.

2026-09-16-gov-t-to-tackle-misinformatio.summary: Kenya's broadcasting principal secretary Stephen Isaboke directed all ministries, departments and agencies to build communication into their programmes under the National Communication Policy 2026, at a forum opened on 15 September 2026. The National Communication Centre is being strengthened as the government's information repository, using AI tools for public sentiment analysis.

2026-09-16-graphic-telecel-ghana-nca-5g-.summary: Ghana's National Communications Authority awarded Telecel Ghana three lots in the 2.3 GHz band to support its 5G rollout, all the lots it applied for out of five on offer. The award is part of a competitive process covering the 700 MHz, 2.3 GHz and 3 GHz bands. Neither the assignment date nor the licence fee is stated.

2026-09-16-ipr-digital-sovereignty-empty.summary: An Internet Policy Review essay argues that digital sovereignty has come to mean so many conflicting things, from rights protection in the EU to content control in China, that it is empty as a concept, though not without limits.

2026-09-16-itweb-africa-kenya-ica-nation.summary: Kenya's ICT Authority tendered two framework agreements, national backbone links and cross-border and metro links, each for three years extendable by two. Treasury puts the public-sector fibre network at 30,454km against a 100,000km target before the 2027 election.

2026-09-16-itweb-africa-nigeria-governme.summary: An assessment presented to Nigeria's IT development agency found only 47% of about 30 government digital platforms met an accessibility threshold, with failures also on banking and payment platforms. The agency said it has written accessibility into revised website guidelines and is considering national standards.

2026-09-16-itweb-hollard-rejects-hacking.summary: An extortion attack on insurance technology provider MIP Holdings, detected on 14 June 2026, exposed personal data linked to customers of about 45 South African insurers. Hollard said a ransomware group's claim against it traced to that incident, not to its own systems.

2026-09-16-itweb-sa-banks-ai-value-micro.summary: PwC's review of South Africa's six largest banks for the first half of 2026 finds them moving from counting AI use cases to measuring returns, judged on fraud prevention, credit decisions, service speed and cost. Combined headline earnings rose 9.3% to R82.3 billion.

2026-09-16-ken-nation-editorial-safarico.summary: The Daily Nation's editorial welcomes the Kenyan High Court ruling that annulled the government's Sh204.3 billion sale of its 15% Safaricom stake to Vodacom Group as unconstitutional. The court found inadequate public participation, concealment of material information and bypassed regulatory review, and ordered the 6 billion shares returned to state ownership.

2026-09-16-ken-nation-opposition-irreduc.summary: A Kenyan opposition and civil-society coalition led by former Chief Justice David Maraga set five electoral demands for 2027, including an independent international audit of the voter register and biometrics and mandatory biometric voter identification. It also wants the electoral commission's technology policy, source code and procurement specifications published by 30 September 2026.

2026-09-16-ken-standard-ai-outpaces-regu.summary: The 2026 International AI Safety Report, presented at Daystar University in Kenya, warns that general-purpose AI is advancing faster than regulation. It notes at least 700 million weekly users of leading systems, with adoption below 10% across much of Africa, Asia and Latin America.

2026-09-16-ken-techtrendske-icta-kdeap-n.summary: Kenya's backbone tender will be scored 80% on technical factors and 20% on cost, with winning bidders required to disclose beneficial ownership. Public-sector fibre stood at 30,454km in 2026, up from 22,486km in 2022.

2026-09-16-lbr-apo-boakai-national-ident.summary: Liberia's President Joseph Nyuma Boakai declared 16 September 2026 National Identification Day, a working holiday, by proclamation. The proclamation states that about 720,000 people are enrolled in the National Biometric Identification System, run by the National Identification Registry set up by law in 2011, and that every person in Liberia is required to enrol.

2026-09-16-lbr-fpa-cbl-financial-inclusi.summary: Liberia's draft national financial inclusion and education strategy went through a two-day validation and will be revised. Participants said its success depends on the identity registry, business registration and credit reference systems, and parts will need legislation and budget.

2026-09-16-lbr-fpa-prime-credit-sues-cbl.summary: Prime Credit Reference Bureau is suing the Central Bank of Liberia for US$1,180,953, alleging the bank never supplied or ordered lenders to supply the loan data its November 2025 licence depended on. It says the bank later wrote that it lacked clear authority to license private bureaux; the claims are untested.

2026-09-16-lby-libyaherald-customs-autom.summary: Libya's Customs Authority met foreign contractors on 15 September 2026 to revive automated inspection, container scanning and coastal monitoring contracts signed in earlier years but never completed. The meeting reviewed what had been delivered and what had blocked the rest; no contract values or dates were given.

2026-09-16-lso-govls-data-value-creation.summary: Lesotho's Ministry of Information, Communications, Science, Technology and Innovation presented a draft National Data Value Creation Blueprint for validation at a workshop in Maseru, reported on 16 September 2026. Participants reviewed its strategic framework, priority use cases and required infrastructure, with three to five flagship use cases to be selected. The Smart Africa Digital Academy is guiding the work; the draft itself is not published.

2026-09-16-lubombo-mps-join-dpm-to-make-.summary: Eswatini's deputy prime minister, Thulisile Dladla, asked Lubombo MPs on 16 September 2026 to build community trust in Imbeleko, the national social registry, before household data collection runs from 12 October to 27 November 2026. 216 data collectors and 22 supervisors have been recruited from the region. The exercise follows enumeration in Shiselweni in 2025.

2026-09-16-mar-assabah-rni-poursuites-im.summary: Morocco's National Rally of Independents said on 16 September 2026 that it will take to court anyone who made or spread doctored images and false content about two of its figures, Fatima Khair and Benaissa Al-Jarrari, during the election campaign.

2026-09-16-mar-hespress-ai-campagne-elec.summary: A New Democrats candidate in Tangier-Assilah for Morocco's 23 September 2026 legislative election has put QR codes on his posters linking to a site where an AI system answers voters' questions from the party programme.

2026-09-16-mdg-lexpressmg-etat-civil-20-.summary: About 20% of Madagascar's population remains outside the civil register, L'Express reports from the National Identity Day launch in Antananarivo. Officials named biometric registration in the communes and simpler procedures at communal offices as priorities.

2026-09-16-mdg-midimadagasikara-cooperat.summary: Madagascar's industrialisation ministry handed biometric cards to the first 124 registered cooperatives in Analamanga on 15 September 2026, under a UNDP-funded census building a verified national database of cooperatives. The census has also begun in Atsinanana and Analanjirofo.

2026-09-16-mdg-midimadagasikara-etat-civ.summary: Madagascar opened a second phase of its Izaho Tokana 2.0 birth-registration drive on National Identity Day, 15 September 2026, with support from the Francophonie organisation's civil status project. The 2025 multiple indicator survey found close to 20% of children under five without a birth certificate, 21% in rural areas against about 12% in towns.

2026-09-16-mesrs-etablissements-enseigne.summary: Mauritania's higher education ministry lists 17 public and 10 private higher education institutions on its site, with 33,049 students and 500 teaching staff.

2026-09-16-moz-mznews-cooperacao-brasil-.summary: Mozambique's ICT institute INTIC, led by board chairman Lourino Chemane, met Cilair Rodrigues de Abreu of Brazil's public management ministry in Maputo to discuss cooperation on data governance and protection, digital certification, interoperability and staff training. Brazil's Pix payments system, its QR-code biometric identity card and facial recognition against fraud were cited as references.

2026-09-16-moz-mznews-regulamento-segura.summary: Mozambique's Council of Ministers approved a Postal Security Regulation on 15 September 2026, setting controls against theft, fraud and cyber threats to the postal network as e-commerce parcels increase.

2026-09-16-mrt-ami-conseil-ministres-pro.summary: Mauritania's Council of Ministers took a statement on 16 September 2026 proposing a national framework on minors' use of social media, with an access threshold at 16. It would switch off recommendation algorithms, infinite scroll and autoplay for minors by default, ban advertising aimed at them and add a reporting route for children harmed online; no draft text has been published.

2026-09-16-mrt-ami-hmayt-qasrin-mnsat-ta.summary: Mauritania's youth minister said the government is preparing legal and technical measures to protect minors on social media. The Council of Ministers approved an interministerial committee, including the population registry agency and the data protection authority, to propose a framework law with technical mechanisms to limit children's access to harmful platforms. A draft law banning online gambling is also being prepared.

2026-09-16-mrt-ami-rqmnt-tahil-tasnif-mu.summary: Mauritania's housing minister, Naha mint Hamdi ould Mouknass, said on 16 September 2026 that qualification and classification of construction firms now runs only through a government platform linked to tax, transport, procurement, social security and company registry databases, to reduce fraud. She was presenting a draft decree that would replace Decree 172-2022 and cut the classification commission from 22 members to 15.

2026-09-16-mrt-instant-payment-system-in.summary: Mauritania sought providers for an instant payment system to make financial services interoperable, under the World Bank-financed regional digital integration programme. The call closed on 3 June 2025.

2026-09-16-mrt-internet-society-pulse-co.summary: The Internet Society rates Mauritania's internet resilience at 43%, with 3% of the 1,000 most-visited websites served from local servers or caches against a 50% target. About 46% of the population uses the internet.

2026-09-16-mus-ttp-first-electronic-bill.summary: Mauritius Commercial Bank completed the first electronic bill of exchange under Mauritian law with Export Trading Group, which created five bills in under 30 minutes and transferred them to the bank in under an hour. It is the first live use of the electronic transferable records framework Mauritius adopted through the Finance Act 2025.

2026-09-16-mwi-information-requests-ati-.summary: A Malawi24 investigation published on 16 September 2026 found that 65 per cent of 30 surveyed requesters received no reply within the 15 days set by Malawi's Access to Information Act. The outlet filed requests with ten public bodies, including the Anti-Corruption Bureau, the health ministry and the revenue authority, and none supplied the information. The Human Rights Commission said it can only make recommendations, as the Act carries no penalties.

2026-09-16-mwi-malawi24-drops-expiry-dat.summary: Malawi's homeland security minister ordered on 16 September 2026 that national identity cards be issued without expiry dates from that day. He gave the order at the launch of the Nzika digital ID wallet, which lets citizens show government credentials on a phone by QR code.

2026-09-16-mwi-undp-nzika-digital-id-wal.summary: Malawi launched the Nzika Digital ID Wallet in Lilongwe on 16 September 2026 and from the same day removed the expiry date from national identity cards. The wallet, built by the National Registration Bureau with UNDP and funded by the EU, Ireland and Norway, holds national IDs and birth, marriage and death certificates. Homeland Security minister Peter Mukhito said it complements the physical card.

2026-09-16-nam-namibiansun-itransfer-tea.summary: iTransfer, a self-funded Namibian platform launched in January 2026, matches public servants who want to swap postings and has registered 970 teachers across the 14 regions. It does not approve transfers and charges N$200 for three months.

2026-09-16-ner-actuniger-lancement-passe.summary: Niger opened mass enrolment for the Sahel confederation's biometric passport in Niamey on 15 September 2026, with enrolment kits to go to every region and the diaspora. An ordinary passport costs 45,000 FCFA and runs five years, with online pre-enrolment through mobile money services.

2026-09-16-nga-authorityngr-au-pre-elect.summary: An African Union pre-election mission, in Nigeria from 13 to 19 September 2026, asked the electoral commission for details of its readiness for the 2027 elections on voter registration, technology, logistics and funding. The mission described its role as supportive, not supervisory.

2026-09-16-nga-digitalbusiness-etat-repr.summary: Nigeria's Data Protection Commission moved into a new Abuja headquarters in a building recovered by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, opened by communications minister Bosun Tijani on 14 September 2026. National commissioner Vincent Olatunji said the commission has generated more than N12bn (about $9m) in revenue over three years despite funding constraints.

2026-09-16-nga-health-ministry-nhtdao-di.summary: Nigeria's Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare inaugurated the steering committee of a new National Health Technology and Data Analytics Office in Abuja on 16 September 2026. The office, approved by President Bola Tinubu, is to coordinate the national digital health architecture. The minister of state named fragmented, unconnected electronic medical record systems as the problem it must address, through enforced minimum standards.

2026-09-16-nga-hughes-nigcomsat-2a-2b-ju.summary: Nigeria's state satellite operator NIGCOMSAT has chosen Hughes Network Systems' JUPITER gateway for the ground segment of its NIGCOMSAT-2A and 2B satellites, Hughes announced on 16 September 2026. Preparation begins in 2026 ahead of launches targeted for 2028 and 2029, and Hughes expects to advise on local assembly of satellite terminals. No contract value is given.

2026-09-16-nga-nan-nhrc-accountability-l.summary: Nigeria's National Human Rights Commission and Accountability Lab called on 16 September 2026, at a stakeholders' meeting in Abuja, for a coordinated framework to handle complaints of rights violations online. The commission's executive secretary, Tony Ojukwu, said referral routes are unclear and there are no standard procedures for preserving digital evidence. No framework or timetable was adopted.

2026-09-16-nga-premiumtimes-cbn-nfis-4-f.summary: The Central Bank of Nigeria said on 16 September 2026 it has completed its review of the third National Financial Inclusion Strategy and begun a fourth, focused on usage, affordability and safety. It put Bank Verification Number enrolment at 67.8 million at end-2025 and its shared agent network above 2 million, and plans a geospatial register of financial access points.

2026-09-16-nga-prestigenews-ndpc-nidcom-.summary: Nigeria's Data Protection Commission and the Nigerians in Diaspora Commission agreed to work together on data-protection awareness for Nigerians at home and abroad, during a visit by national commissioner Vincent Olatunji to the diaspora commission's chair, Abike Dabiri-Erewa. No instrument, budget or timetable is named.

2026-09-16-nga-thisday-fg-december-deadl.summary: Nigeria's government set December 2026 as the deadline for 95% national identity number coverage, announced on National Identity Day. Officials put the database at close to 140 million and said physical e-ID cards will be issued before the end of the year.

2026-09-16-nga-thisday-nhrc-accountabili.summary: Nigeria's human rights commission and AccountabilityLab called for coordinated mechanisms so victims of digital rights violations can get justice quickly, at a meeting of agencies, regulators, lawyers, media and technology firms in Abuja.

2026-09-16-nga-thisday-sanusi-telcos-ent.summary: Former central bank governor Sanusi Lamido Sanusi said at the launch of Nigeria's 2026 Access to Financial Services survey that he was wrong to delay telecoms operators' entry into financial services during his tenure. He said concern for depositors after the banking crisis drove the decision and that it slowed financial inclusion.

2026-09-16-rwa-taarifa-hec-higher-educat.summary: Rwanda's Higher Education Council is developing a national framework to measure the performance of universities and other higher learning institutions. Director general Kadozi Edward said data on students, lecturers, research and graduate outcomes will be collected, digitised and published, and shared with bodies such as UNESCO and the World Bank. No adoption date is given.

2026-09-16-rwa-umunota-nida-digital-id-1.summary: Rwanda's National Identification Agency said on 16 September 2026 that it has captured photographs and biometrics, including fingerprints and iris scans, for more than 10 million people in 27 of the country's 30 districts, as registration opened in Rusizi District. The digital ID, launched in 2023 with the World Bank at a cost of about Rwf200 billion, offers a physical card, a QR-code version and a separate token.

2026-09-16-sdn-sudanindependent-cash-swa.summary: The commission for exchanging bank-app balances such as Bankak for cash has risen to as much as 10% in Sudan's Khartoum State amid a cash shortage and restrictions on several banking apps, Sudan Independent reported on 16 September 2026, citing Darfur24. Most dealers charge 5%. Locals said the dollar rose from about 6,150 Sudanese pounds in early September to about 8,000.

2026-09-16-sdn-suna-itzan-budget-system-.summary: Sudan's minister of state for finance, Mohamed Nour Abdeldaim, announced on 16 September 2026 that the ministry has begun launching Itzan, a national budget system covering estimates, execution and analysis. It is in its final stages and is planned for use in the 2027 budget and in full from 2028, with support from UNDP, the IMF and the World Bank.

2026-09-16-sen-pressafrik-atelier-region.summary: Senegal's National Assembly hosted a regional workshop on regulating artificial intelligence in Dakar from 16 to 18 September 2026, with members of parliament from Senegal, Benin, Burkina Faso and Côte d'Ivoire. The chair of the assembly's digital committee, Aliou Sène, called for an African approach to AI regulation based on regional cooperation and protection of citizens.
