2026-09-18-bwa-yourbotswana-openevidence.summary: OpenEvidence and Penn Medicine announced on 15 September 2026 a partnership to deploy OpenEvidence's AI clinical decision-support platform to Penn's clinicians and to extend it to Botswana through the Botswana-UPenn Partnership. A customised set of tools is to be built with the partnership's clinicians. No timetable, site count or cost for Botswana is given.

2026-09-18-cemac-sdmx-odp-workshop-agp.summary: A workshop of the African Development Bank, CEMAC and UNFPA in Libreville on SDMX and the Open Data Platform closed on 18 September 2026 with 14 recommendations for moving Central African statistical systems to ODP 2.0. National statistics institutes are asked for costed migration roadmaps; the World Bank is asked to issue no-objection notices faster, and HISWACA project units to cut disbursement delays.

2026-09-18-civ-aip-3000-enseignants-form.summary: Côte d'Ivoire launched a project on 17 September 2026 to train about 3,000 teachers, supervisors and heads of technical and vocational schools in the teaching use of AI by 2027, with UNESCO support. The pilot starts in Abidjan before national extension and includes modules on AI ethics and data security. It planned 1,000 participants but had 1,907 enrolled at launch.

2026-09-18-civ-techafricanews-signature-.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's civil service ministry enrolled the mayor and secretary-general of Marcory in the administration's electronic signature system on 15 September, extending it to local government. No count of enrolled officials is published.

2026-09-18-cmr-businessincameroon-camtel.summary: Cameroon's state operator plans 245 new mobile sites, taking its declared network from 473 to 718, with decongestion of 122 existing sites and a new billing system; a second shipment of equipment from China arrived on 17 September. No cost or completion date is stated.

2026-09-18-cod-rdcmonde-wameso-ia-banque.summary: The governor of DR Congo's central bank, André Wameso, told the Central Bank of Kenya's AI conference in Nairobi on 16 September 2026 that the bank plans to use AI in macroeconomic forecasting, banking supervision, payment-system oversight and decision support. He said an internal audit of the national financial system and a consultation of local experts will come before any major deployment.

2026-09-18-cod-transforme-copa-digital-p.summary: DR Congo's World Bank-financed Digital Transformation Project (PTN) and the TRANSFORME project signed an agreement in Kinshasa on 18 September 2026 to run COPA Digital, a grant competition for digital startups, small firms and incubators, using TRANSFORME's competition platform and procedures. The first cycle is a pilot of about 16 months. Eligibility rules, grant amounts and the opening date have not been published.

2026-09-18-dcdt-upbeat-after-entities-sh.summary: South Africa's communications department reported clean audits for three of its entities and an unqualified opinion for the Post Office, its first in six years. The department presents it as a governance recovery.

2026-09-18-dji-techreviewafrica-dco-ai-c.summary: Digital Cooperation Organization secretary-general Deemah AlYahya and Djibouti's digital economy minister Safia Mohamed Ali Gadileh discussed cooperation on AI, digital skills, innovation and capacity building. Djibouti recently unveiled a National AI Strategy for 2026–2030. No agreement, funding or timetable is reported.

2026-09-18-drc-using-anonymized-mobile-o.summary: Anonymised call, text and internet records from a mobile operator are being used with a Swedish nonprofit to map population movements in the DR Congo's Ebola outbreak, flagging Kisangani and Kinshasa as relatively high risk. The outbreak had reached 7,200 confirmed cases and 3,475 deaths by 12 September; the same method was used during COVID-19.

2026-09-18-egy-elmydan-biometric-verific.summary: Egypt's communications and interior ministries launched a platform for remote biometric identity verification and electronic signature, which licensed telecom operators can offer inside their own smartphone applications so users need not visit a branch. It was built by the telecom regulator with the IT industry development agency, a local developer and licensed signature providers; no user count or list of relying services is given.

2026-09-18-egy-fintechgate-ntra-platform.summary: Egypt's National Telecom Regulatory Authority said social media platforms that fail to comply with new child-protection rules could be suspended and blocked in Egypt, whatever their size. Its vice-chairman, Mohamed Ibrahim, said platforms have three months to comply, the rules cover existing accounts of under-15s, and age checks must collect only necessary data.

2026-09-18-eri-martinplaut-new-cash-rest.summary: An Eritrean human-rights group reports that a central bank legal notice of 9 September caps the cash an individual may keep beyond 15 days at 25,000 nakfa, with higher limits for businesses, following a June order to deposit cash holdings. It notes that the country has no generally available cash machines or cards and thin branch access outside the main towns.

2026-09-18-eth-fana-knowledge-digital-se.summary: Ethiopia told an Africa-Europe gathering that services trade, digital services and local capacity should be at the centre of new partnerships. The statement sets positions, not agreements.

2026-09-18-eth-fana-mesob-citizen-center.summary: Ethiopia's MESOB one-stop public service presented its digital government model at a Chinese technology vendor's conference in Shanghai. The account is promotional and gives no new usage figures.

2026-09-18-eu-urges-businesses-to-turn-t.summary: At the launch of Eswatini's new trade and investment dashboards, the European Union urged businesses and investors to use them for better-informed decisions.

2026-09-18-fg-sets-up-technical-committe.summary: Nigeria set up a technical sub-committee to review the 2025 tax laws within six weeks, tasked with a Finance Bill 2027, revised withholding tax regulations and an amended significant economic presence order, the rule that reaches foreign digital businesses. The drafts themselves are not yet published.

2026-09-18-gab-sgcm-communique-final-con.summary: Gabon's Council of Ministers, meeting in Port-Gentil on 18 September 2026, adopted a decree on issuing qualified electronic-signature certificates and other trust services, including e-seals, e-invoices and the e-visa, and three decrees reorganising the national statistics institute, council and fund. It also approved hosting an African preparatory meeting for the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference in Libreville.

2026-09-18-gha-currentissues-access-bank.summary: Access Bank Ghana and Visa launched Visa Accept on 18 September 2026, a feature in the bank's mobile app that lets small merchants take contactless card payments on their own smartphones without a point-of-sale terminal. Ghana is the first market for the service in Visa's Central and Eastern Europe, Middle East and Africa region; the bank plans a door-to-door merchant campaign. No fees are given.

2026-09-18-gha-modernghana-access-bank-v.summary: Access Bank Ghana and Visa launched Visa Accept in Accra on 18 September 2026, a virtual point-of-sale tool in the bank's mobile app that lets small merchants take card taps, QR codes or payment links on a smartphone, with funds credited instantly. The bank's retail director Eugene Ocansey said the transaction records could help informal businesses qualify for credit.

2026-09-18-ghana-must-turn-research-into.summary: Ghana's chief of staff called for closer collaboration between universities, research institutions, industry and policymakers so that research becomes practical solutions. The speech carries no programme or funding.

2026-09-18-ghanaian-times-volta-chiefs-c.summary: A delegation of Ghana's Volta Regional House of Chiefs signed three memoranda with Chinese companies during a business visit to China, the first with a technology firm on digital transformation and technology transfer in the region. The others cover construction and investment; no values or project list are stated.

2026-09-18-gin-guinee114-atelier-extensi.summary: Guinea's territorial administration minister, Djenabou Touré, opened a workshop on 18 September 2026 on extending the national register of natural persons (RNPP), run jointly by the civil registration and identification office ONECI and the elections directorate. She asked that the first phase of an identity verification and validation platform be completed before the end of 2026.

2026-09-18-gin-mediaguinee-conakry-termi.summary: Conakry Terminal, a subsidiary of Africa Global Logistics in Guinea, launched online payment for port services on 18 September 2026 with the fintechs TouchPoint and Akiba, letting clients invoice, pay and obtain delivery orders without visiting a counter. Director-general Édouard Léno said more than 300 clients had made over 10,000 transactions worth more than 60 billion Guinean francs, and set a goal of raising the digital share of payments from 20% to 50%.

2026-09-18-gmb-alkambatimes-moherst-sdai.summary: The Gambia's higher education minister secured Saudi backing, at UNESCO's AI ethics forum in Riyadh, for putting artificial intelligence into universities, technical colleges and madrassa reform. He set out plans to teach AI ethics, data protection and algorithmic accountability in tertiary programmes; no agreement text or funding is stated.

2026-09-18-gmb-voicegambia-gra-wataf-tax.summary: The Gambia's revenue commissioner called at a West African tax forum in Ghana for closer regional cooperation among tax administrations to protect tax bases, including as economic activity moves online.

2026-09-18-gov-t-is-committed-to-moving-.summary: A Ghanaian minister of state told a digital assets summit that the government means to move from digital policy to jobs and investment. The keynote announced no instrument.

2026-09-18-government-plans-unified-syst.summary: Kenya's head of public service convened the public service commission, the examinations council and the education ministry to build a single mechanism linking academic credential databases to hiring agencies, to cut verification delays and fake certificates. No design or date is set.

2026-09-18-govt-eyes-e3bn-in-new-loans.summary: Eswatini's finance minister said the government will table a World Bank loan package for ICT, including support for the state posts and telecommunications corporation and lower data costs, within a wider borrowing programme. He gave no amount or date for the ICT package.

2026-09-18-heads-must-roll-there-is-noth.summary: Ghana's acting rent control commissioner called for an investigation into a digitisation programme on which US$1.7 million was reportedly spent under the previous government, saying he found only four computers at the facility. No audit finding is yet on record.

2026-09-18-hollard-data-hits-dark-web-af.summary: Data allegedly stolen from a South African insurer appeared on the dark web, a researcher confirming it is public, after the June attack on its software supplier. The criminal group had demanded a ransom from the insurer to keep it private.

2026-09-18-ifc-complete-farmer-to-transf.summary: The World Bank's private-sector arm partnered with a Ghanaian agricultural technology company to extend data, farm technology and financing to smallholders. No amount or farmer target is stated in this account.

2026-09-18-inside-the-fake-aarto-fine-sc.summary: South Africa's road traffic infringement agency is considering an investigation into whether the national vehicle database was accessed, after fake traffic-fine messages began quoting motorists' correct number plates. The fines platform being impersonated says its own system was not breached.

2026-09-18-internet-society-pulse-sao-to.summary: The Internet Society's resilience index scores São Tomé and Príncipe at 33 out of 100, below the Middle Africa average of 38 and the Africa average of 44, across infrastructure, market readiness, performance and security.

2026-09-18-ken-kbc-mwea-huduma-centre.summary: Kenya's Deputy President, Kithure Kindiki, commissioned the Mwea Huduma Centre at Ngurubani on 18 September 2026; it has operated since July. It is Kenya's 61st Huduma Centre and offers identity documents, birth and death certificates and Kenya Revenue Authority services under one roof, with a Jitume ICT hub for youth digital skills.

2026-09-18-ken-kehc-matey-v-safaricom-ru.summary: Kenya's High Court ruled on 18 September 2026 in Matey v Safaricom that Safaricom must, within 21 days, give a subscriber her subscriber details and records of every request for access to her communications, M-Pesa and transaction data, plus access logs, for March 2024 to January 2025. The court relied on the constitutional right of access to information, subject to the Data Protection Act.

2026-09-18-ken-peopledaily-sha-e-contrac.summary: Kenya's Social Health Authority put its E-Contracting Portal live at 3pm on 17 September 2026 for health providers seeking contracts under four health funds. Chief executive Mercy Mwangangi said earlier applications were tests and would be archived, so every provider must apply again.

2026-09-18-kenya-mobile-money-accounts-h.summary: Kenya's regulator put mobile money subscriptions at 54,005,800 at the end of June 2026, up 1.2 per cent in the quarter and 13.2 per cent on the year, while more than 34,000 registered agents left the market in the same three months. Subscriptions count accounts, not people.

2026-09-18-kenya-plans-to-expand-bpo-and.summary: Kenya's ICT principal secretary set out plans to extend outsourcing and global business services jobs beyond Nairobi and Mombasa for young people, noting that one international operator runs more than 2,500 seats in the two cities.

2026-09-18-kenya-takes-ai-and-technology.summary: Kenya's technology envoy said the country will press AI governance, digital resilience, investment and technology capacity at the 81st UN General Assembly. The briefing set out positions, not commitments.

2026-09-18-kenya-to-spread-bpo-jobs-beyo.summary: Kenya's ICT principal secretary said the government wants business process outsourcing and global services jobs to spread beyond Nairobi and Mombasa to smaller towns, after touring a French outsourcing firm's Nairobi operation. No incentive or site plan is named.

2026-09-18-kenyan-fintech-payd-to-resume.summary: A Kenyan cross-border payments startup serving about 30,000 freelancers and businesses paused payouts around May after foreign-exchange losses left it short of customer balances, and says it will resume after overhauling its treasury system. The case shows how currency exposure can strand customer funds at small payment firms.

2026-09-18-l-algerien-nacer-abdelli-lie-.summary: A profile of an Algerian entrepreneur whose platform, founded in 2020, combines vocational training courses and tests with recruitment, so employers can choose and train future staff in one tool. No user figures are given.

2026-09-18-lby-libyaupdate-cbl-governor-.summary: Libya's central bank governor presented the bank's payments modernisation, including instant transfers and a salary-payment project, to Arab and international banks in London. The meeting discussed widening correspondent banking; no agreements are reported.

2026-09-18-malawi-drops-id-card-expiry-d.summary: Malawi launched the Nzika digital ID wallet on International Identity Day, holding national ID, birth, marriage and death credentials on a phone as an optional complement to the physical card. The homeland security minister also ended expiry dates on the biometric ID card with immediate effect.

2026-09-18-mar-assahafa-idarati-portail-.summary: Morocco's digital transition ministry launched a new version of the Idarati portal, giving access to 874 online services organised around user journeys and 2,533 published administrative acts, with a feedback function, an accessibility redesign and a marketplace of AI solutions. The ministry presents it as groundwork for Idarati X.0.

2026-09-18-mar-mmsp-inauguration-btechno.summary: A French telecom group's Moroccan engineering subsidiary opened in Rabat with more than 1,000 staff, close to 850 of them engineers, working on fibre, 5G, AI, cybersecurity and network supervision. The digital transition minister placed it under the Digital Morocco 2030 strategy and its talent and digital-export aims.

2026-09-18-mar-mtnra-communique-idarati-.summary: The Moroccan digital transition ministry's own communiqué on the relaunched Idarati portal presents it as a proactive, user-centred single access point to administrations' digital services.

2026-09-18-mar-telquel-paiement-digital-.summary: A Moroccan analysis finds that cash in circulation has doubled since 2019 despite payment accounts, cards, wallets and instant transfers, and that less than fourteen of every hundred dirhams passing through a bank card are spent as payments. It notes that direct social aid lands in payment accounts and is withdrawn within hours.

2026-09-18-mdg-moov-frontieres-plus-inte.summary: The International Organization for Migration's Japan-funded Smarter Borders project closed in Madagascar on 18 September 2026 after two years. It installed mobile MIDAS migration-data kits at the port of Mahajanga, trained national instructors and ran a maritime simulation with 13 institutions; Madagascar was one of four beneficiaries of the US$3 million regional programme.

2026-09-18-moz-360mozambique-incm-intern.summary: Mozambique's telecoms regulator says a tariff management system due in November 2026 will compare operators' packages, identify the effective price including validity, and stop data bundles running out before their stated expiry, after consumer complaints. It is also restructuring packages.

2026-09-18-mwi-malawi24-macra-warns-misu.summary: Malawi's communications regulator warned publicly that using AI or other digital tools to create or spread false or manipulated information could bring civil and criminal liability, citing the Penal Code's section on false statements likely to cause fear and alarm. It says it and other authorities are acting to identify and trace those responsible.

2026-09-18-mwi-techreviewafrica-giz-data.summary: GIZ ran a three-day training-of-trainers programme for Malawi's data protection authority in Lilongwe, to build capacity to implement the country's data protection framework.

2026-09-18-nam-economist-namfisa-fintech.summary: The Namibia Financial Supervisory Authority announced its FinTech Square 2026 event for 14 October in Windhoek, with the Bank of Namibia and other partners. The event will launch the second cohort of NAMFISA's regulatory sandbox, covering crowdfunding and peer-to-peer lending, after a first cohort on microlending. Twelve exhibitors from the non-banking financial sector are to be selected.

2026-09-18-nam-neweralive-cyber-threats-.summary: Namibia's communications regulator reports cyber threat events up 57 per cent and vulnerabilities up 40 per cent in the April-June quarter, alongside 2 per cent growth in mobile subscriptions to about 2.79 million and about N$243m invested in networks.

2026-09-18-ner-anp-plateforme-regulateur.summary: Media and communication regulators of the Alliance of Sahel States founded a joint platform, PAREMEC, at a constitutive assembly in Niamey that closed on 18 September 2026, with its seat in Niamey and Mali's communication authority head Coulibaly Gaoussou as first president. Recommendations to governments included laws regulating traditional and digital media, tools to monitor digital content, and a common approach to digital platforms.

2026-09-18-new-trade-dashboards-open-glo.summary: Eswatini launched two public dashboards, one on investment attractiveness and one on export-market intelligence, built by the trade ministry and the investment promotion authority with the International Trade Centre under EU support. No data licence or update schedule is stated.

2026-09-18-nga-arusha-mandate-ai-examina.summary: The registrar of Nigeria's National Examinations Council was elected vice-president of the Association for Educational Assessment in Africa at its 42nd conference in Arusha, and Abuja will host the 2027 meeting. The piece argues that this puts Nigeria in a position to shape how African examinations are run as AI enters assessment.

2026-09-18-nga-blueprint-digital-id-akum.summary: The Secretary to the Government of the Federation told the National Day of Identity that Nigeria's digital identity infrastructure is now a trusted foundation for banking, telecommunications, social protection and cross-border trade. He credited the National Identity Management Commission Act 2026 with giving it a stronger legal footing and making the commission the country's root certification authority for identity, citing no enrolment figure.

2026-09-18-nga-ecowas-biometric-card-enb.summary: At a Lagos media workshop the migration organisation, Nigeria's immigration service and the ECOWAS Commission set out the case for the regional biometric identity card, presenting it as the instrument of the free movement protocol and as conferring the right to live and trade in any member state. The card is put at N35,000 to acquire, a figure another account of the same workshop gives as N35,500.

2026-09-18-nga-ndifs-digital-invoices-fi.summary: Nigeria inaugurated the steering committee of a National Digital Invoicing and Financial Optimisation Strategy, meant to let businesses raise working capital against verified digital invoices. The trade minister framed it as moving e-invoicing beyond tax compliance into a national receivables-finance corridor; no rules or launch date are set.

2026-09-18-nga-thisday-smedan-koica-undp.summary: Nigeria's small-business agency broke ground in Abuja on a US$12 million entrepreneurship centre funded by Korea through KOICA and developed with UNDP. It is to support 500 young entrepreneurs and 400 start-ups in fintech, edtech, healthtech and agritech; no completion date is stated.

2026-09-18-nga-tinubu-digital-free-zones.summary: The president declared Nigeria's Digital Free Zones initiative moved to its implementation stage, with one zone licensed. The stated aim is that Nigerian technology and service companies raise global capital and serve international markets without incorporating or holding intellectual property abroad; the declaration came through an adviser's release and carries no zone count, investment figure or timetable.

2026-09-18-nigcomsat-picks-hughes-for-ne.summary: Nigeria's satellite operator says part of the ground equipment for its two next communications satellites, due to launch in 2028 and 2029, will be assembled locally with engineering support from the US firm supplying the ground system. The satellites themselves are being built by European and Israeli manufacturers.

2026-09-18-niger-begins-operational-roll.summary: Niger opened public enrolment for the Alliance of Sahel States biometric passport in Niamey on 15 September, with regional and diaspora centres and online pre-enrolment through mobile money to follow. An ordinary passport costs FCFA 45,000; Niger is the last of the three states to issue it.

2026-09-18-nigeria-warns-pos-agents-agai.summary: Nigeria's anti-corruption agency warned point-of-sale agents against facilitating money laundering, terrorist financing, ransom payments and fraud, saying investigations show such funds are often routed through their machines. It asked the agents' association to keep full records of operators and transactions.

2026-09-18-rdc-transco-et-firstbank-s-al.summary: Kinshasa's public transport company signed a partnership with a commercial bank on 17 September to digitise several of its systems, starting with revenue management, and to prepare a prepaid fare card. No timetable or cost is stated.

2026-09-18-rgph-2-le-gouvernement-impliq.summary: The DR Congo's planning minister met telecom operators to enlist them in spreading information about the second general population and housing census. The meeting concerned publicity for the census rather than any use of operator data.

2026-09-18-sakaja-gives-nairobi-traders-.summary: Nairobi's governor told traders to apply for county permits directly through official online channels rather than intermediaries, and announced ways to verify county enforcement officers against impersonators. No figures on permits or fraud cases are given.

2026-09-18-sashin-sookroo-fnb-connect-vi.summary: FNB Connect, the connectivity business of South Africa's First National Bank, recorded R28.6 billion in customer value and sales in its latest financial year, up 18%, and gross revenue of more than R3 billion, its chief executive Sashin Sookroo told TechCabal. Its mobile network data use reached about 50 petabytes, and it has about 1.02 million active SIMs.

2026-09-18-sle-calabash-ncra-identity-da.summary: Sierra Leone's National Civil Registration Authority registered 100 inmates from three Freetown correctional centres for National Identification Numbers on 17 September 2026, International Identity Day. The inmates will receive ID cards free, with the government meeting the cost. The Correctional Service said the exercise builds on inmate biometric registration pilots in 2018 and 2020.

2026-09-18-sle-sierraloaded-stats-sl-cen.summary: Statistics Sierra Leone completed nationwide mapping for the December 2026 census, the country's first digital census, and the census technical committee received the mapping completion report on 15 September. The committee also reviewed an August mock census; Census Night is set for 1 December.

2026-09-18-som-wardheernews-digital-iron.summary: Somali journalists and political figures had Facebook accounts suspended, removed, or falsely marked as belonging to the dead, including the pages of two regional presidents and a journalist with more than a million followers. The account disruptions are documented; responsibility for them is not, and the piece states plainly that no evidence establishes who ordered or carried them out, calling for an independent investigation.

2026-09-18-south-africa-harmful-online-c.summary: Research ICT Africa, the Centre for Analytics and Behavioural Change and Moxii Africa launched a study in Johannesburg on 17 September 2026 finding that South Africa's laws on harmful online content are adequate but enforcement is fragmented. It found platform moderation in English alone leaves out 10 of 11 official languages, and that cases of harassment, doxxing and deepfakes can take up to seven years to resolve. The study was EU-funded.

2026-09-18-south-africa-sme-funding-gap-.summary: An African Bank executive argues that South Africa's estimated R350 billion small-business financing gap persists despite funders doubling since 2018 because lenders lack usable data on small firms. It is a commentary, and the remedies it proposes are a lender's view rather than policy.

2026-09-18-tcd-lendjampost-digitalisatio.summary: A Chadian analysis finds the state's push to go paperless and cashless under the 2026 finance law, with 3,000 payment terminals in revenue offices and compulsory electronic invoicing, held back by power cuts, thin connectivity in the provinces and some officials' limited digital skills. It also names the integrated public-finance system and a June 2026 awareness campaign; no transaction figures are given.

2026-09-18-tcd-tchadinfos-anie-moov-mone.summary: Chad's investment and export agency ANIE signed an agreement with Moov Money Tchad on 18 September 2026 so that fees at its one-stop shop for company creation can be paid electronically. No fee levels, start date or transaction charges are given.

2026-09-18-techcabal-mafab-5g-spectrum-n.summary: A Nigerian licensee is seeking to transfer its 2x20 MHz at 2.1 GHz and its 100 MHz block at 3.5 GHz to the largest operator, subject to regulatory approval. It paid US$273.6 million for the 3.5 GHz lot at the December 2021 auction against a US$197.4 million reserve, took a unified access licence in July 2022 and never reached commercial service; a wider review of underused spectrum is attributed to people familiar with the matter rather than to the regulator.

2026-09-18-terra-industries-leads-1m-rou.summary: Aeon, a Nigerian cybersecurity startup built inside a cloud infrastructure platform, raised US$1 million in a pre-seed round led by a defence-technology firm, with several African venture funds participating. It sells risk detection, vulnerability management and in-network monitoring to banks, energy and mobility operators.

2026-09-18-tgo-togofirst-sme-financing-p.summary: Togo's credit information bureau presented a portal on which small businesses will submit financing requests that banks and microfinance institutions review directly, guiding applicants through the documents a complete loan file needs. It is to launch by the end of 2026 with development-finance support, and Togo was chosen as the pilot country because of existing public programmes to strengthen small-business financing.

2026-09-18-transformation-numerique-les-.summary: The Comoros' digital development agency and UNDP signed a memorandum on 16 September to run a national digital readiness assessment covering skills, connectivity, public services, regulation and the digital economy across the three islands. It is presented as a way to target the next investments under the Comores Numérique 2028 strategy; no timetable is given.

2026-09-18-tun-directinfo-ministere-agri.summary: Tunisia's agriculture ministry says it is integrating the E-Houwiya digital identity into its online services to unify access and secure transactions, setting 15 November 2026 as the deadline for the bodies under it.

2026-09-18-tun-leconomistemaghrebin-paie.summary: A Tunisian central bank and GIZ mission studied Brazil's PIX instant payment system, its architecture, governance, regulation and economic model. The outlet stresses that nothing indicates Tunisia is building its own version: no adoption or launch calendar has been announced.

2026-09-18-tun-radiosfax-formation-profe.summary: Tunisia's new online registration platform for vocational training received about 112,000 applications by 17 September 2026, the start of the training year, against 70,000 in 2025, the Tunisian Vocational Training Agency said. A second platform handles hostel and canteen applications and fee payments.

2026-09-18-tun-tunisietribune-ministere-.summary: Tunisia's agriculture ministry issued a circular requiring every body under it to integrate the E-Houwiya digital identity into its platforms by 15 November 2026. It makes the E-Houwiya identifier the sole reference for any new digital service and requires strong multi-factor authentication where extra checks apply.

2026-09-18-tun-webdo-kef-laboratoire-ia-.summary: Tunisia's employment and vocational training minister, Riadh Chaoued, announced on 17 September 2026 the creation of an artificial intelligence laboratory at the vocational training centre in Le Kef, in partnership with Tunisie Telecom. It is the first of 12 AI labs the ministry announced on 7 September for vocational training centres in 2026-2027. No cost is given.

2026-09-18-tza-citizen-jkt-digital-patri.summary: Tanzania's National Service (JKT) has added digital patriotism, covering responsible use of social media, to its training curriculum, its commander Major General Rajabu Mabele said on 18 September 2026 at Kanembwa camp in Kigoma Region. This year's training, which began on 8 September across all camps, for the first time combined compulsory national-service recruits and volunteers.

2026-09-18-tza-thecitizen-kcb-zed360-sch.summary: KCB Bank Tanzania began a nationwide rollout of Zed360, a school-fees platform acquired with its purchase of fintech RiverBank, with 18 schools using it, The Citizen reported on 18 September 2026. Each student gets an invoice or control number linked to school records, and Mixx by Yas agents also collect payments. Managing director Cosmas Kimario said Zanzibar is included in the plan.

2026-09-18-uga-ceoeastafrica-centenary-b.summary: Uganda's Centenary Bank launched GonzaPay, a wallet running as an app and over USSD for customers without smartphones, and says it will add savings, lending, insurance and investment with AI-based credit assessment. The account is the bank's own, given in an interview, with no user figures.

2026-09-18-uga-kampalareport-parish-deve.summary: An inter-ministerial meeting put Uganda's Parish Development Model at 3,571,108 beneficiaries against UGX 4.317 trillion capitalised through 10,589 parish SACCOs, lending up to UGX 1 million at 6 per cent a year. It says 183,430 of 222,389 enterprise groups are profiled on the programme's information system; the figures are the government's own.

2026-09-18-vodafone-warns-network-shutdo.summary: A Vodafone report argues that deliberate network shutdowns are growing in frequency, length and cost while often failing to achieve their stated aims, citing at least 313 shutdowns across 52 countries in 2025, the worst year on record, and an economic cost approaching US$20 billion. It is an operator's own study drawing on civil-society counts, not a regulatory finding.

2026-09-18-xaf-latribune-wiocc-dfc-data-.summary: The US International Development Finance Corporation approved an equity investment of up to about US$155m in WIOCC, part of which is to add about 25MW of data centre capacity in Africa. The DFC puts the whole programme at up to US$450m, including submarine and terrestrial networks. Days earlier WIOCC signed a US$300m subscription with Africa Finance Corporation and Vision Invest.

2026-09-18-zaf-africaninsider-octotel-me.summary: South African fibre operators Octotel and MetroFibre confirmed they are assessing a possible merger, reported on 18 September 2026. Old Mutual's African Infrastructure Investment Managers owns all of Octotel and 37% of MetroFibre; a combined network would rank third behind Vumatel and Telkom's Openserve. No deal has been finalised.

2026-09-18-zaf-citizen-opinion-social-me.summary: An opinion piece argues South Africa should consider an under-16 social-media age restriction rather than a ban, with the obligation resting on platforms as it does in Australia, and as part of a wider child-development and online-safety strategy rather than as a solution on its own.

2026-09-18-zaf-citizen-sassa-digital-gra.summary: South Africa's social security agency set out a modernisation programme taking grant services online: applications and payment-detail changes, electronic life certification, messaging support, self-service kiosks and free Wi-Fi at its offices. Its systems are being integrated with other government institutions, which the agency says will help detect fraud and speed processing; no uptake figure is published for any of it.

2026-09-18-zaf-ewn-black-sash-social-gra.summary: A South African rights group reports a spike in calls from grant beneficiaries facing the social security agency's review, citing transport costs, queues, poor network coverage and offices that are offline. It urges beneficiaries to respond to review notices despite the system problems.

2026-09-18-zaf-mip-breach-hackers-extort.summary: The group behind the June breach at an insurance software supplier is now extorting South African insurers directly, after the supplier paid a ransom for an undertaking to destroy the data. Material on a leak site includes policyholders' names, their children's names, identity numbers and email addresses; about 45 insurers' customers were exposed.

2026-09-18-zambia-turns-to-ai-to-hit-tou.summary: Zambia's tourism ministry says it will use artificial intelligence and other technologies toward its target of doubling international arrivals to 5 million a year, opening with a first Tourism and Technology Symposium in Lusaka on responsible AI and smart tourism. No specific system, budget or timetable is named.

2026-09-18-zmb-efficacynews-70-schools-s.summary: Zambia launched a three-year programme to connect an initial 70 public schools by satellite, with solar power for schools off the grid, run by the presidential delivery unit with private partners. No cost or school list is stated.

2026-09-18-zmb-lusakatimes-govt-tech-par.summary: Zambia's Ministry of Technology and Science told a visiting Hikvision delegation that technology partnerships must include skills transfer, local value retention and compliance with Zambian law. It said internet subscriptions rose from 10.4 million to 14.68 million between 2021 and 2025, fibre coverage grew from about 15,000 to over 42,000 km, and mobile money transactions rose from K169 billion in 2021 to K486 billion in 2024.

2026-09-18-zwe-businesstimes-mavetera-te.summary: Zimbabwe's ICT and postal minister told the first annual postal and courier conference that the sector must reinvent itself as an engine of e-commerce and trade. The speech sets out an expectation, not a programme or funding.

2026-09-18-zwe-herald-30-new-vehicles-bo.summary: Zimbabwe's home affairs minister commissioned 30 vehicles for the civil registry department to improve mobility and service delivery nationwide.

2026-09-19-aacb-papss-board-egyptian-par.summary: The Central Bank of Egypt told the board of governors of the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System that Egyptian banks can now execute and fund cross-border payments with African counterparts directly, without intermediary clearing agents or the US dollar, reported on 19 September 2026. Egypt joined PAPSS in November 2024 and is assessing the PAPSS Card scheme.

2026-09-19-ben-lanouvelletribune-acte-na.summary: Benin's national identification agency (ANIP), with UNICEF, is issuing birth certificates free to children under 14 until 30 September 2026, for births registered without a certificate being collected. Parents can retrieve the identification number and certificate through the ANIP BJ app or online portal, or by USSD code *151# without internet access.

2026-09-19-cpv-inforpress-bendi-max-incl.summary: Bendi Max, a pilot to train 250 women traders in Cabo Verde to use digital tools in their businesses, starts on Maio island in October 2026 with 30 participants, Inforpress reported on 19 September. It then extends to Fogo, Santiago and São Vicente, with the economy ministry, Pró-Empresa, Cabo Verde Digital and the United Nations as partners.

2026-09-19-dza-elmoudjahid-hcn-verificat.summary: Algeria's High Commission for Digitisation trained information system managers from several sectors to use a mechanism it built for verifying electronic documents issued through the Dzair Digital Services portal. Administrative bodies can then accept these documents without asking citizens to obtain them again from the issuing office. The training follows presidential instructions of 12 July 2026 to widen the portal's use.

2026-09-19-eabc-eac-investment-forum-ai-.summary: The first East Africa CEO and Investment Forum closed in Nairobi on 18 September 2026 with 95 pre-screened investment opportunities valued at nearly US$3.95bn, including digital infrastructure. The East African Business Council, the EAC Secretariat and the East African Development Bank launched a regional AI and productivity study, and EASTECO's cooperation with Hessen under the EAC AI Alliance was presented.

2026-09-19-egy-egypttoday-sisi-5g-data-c.summary: The presidency directed the expansion of fifth-generation mobile networks, hyperscale data centres and a unified government services card. The instruction is tied to a target of eight billion dollars in digital exports by 2028.

2026-09-19-expense-ai-day-1-1000.summary: A Lagos expense-tracking startup abandoned open banking after the account-data calls it depended on came to about 200 naira each, and rebuilt the product around reading receipts instead. It now reports 10,000 users across 100 countries.

2026-09-19-gha-myjoyonline-jollof-case-r.summary: Ghana is prosecuting a senior nursing officer, Salomey Awiti Bafoh, under the false-news provisions of the Criminal Offences Act over videos from the UK-based "Ghana Jollof" TikTok account. Arrested on 13 September 2026, she was denied bail and remanded to 30 September. Lawyer Oliver Barker-Vormawor said on 19 September that the use of mobile-money records and device access needs close judicial oversight.

2026-09-19-gha-myjoyonline-jollof-case-s.summary: Ghanaian opposition MP John Ntim Fordjour asked on JoyNews on 19 September 2026 whether section 208 of the Criminal Offences Act, on false publications, is applied only to NPP supporters and government critics. He criticised the police CID over the arrest of a nursing officer linked to the TikTok user known as Ghana Jollof, and said pro-government content goes unpunished.

2026-09-19-gin-africaguinee-decret-recen.summary: Guinea's president, Mamadi Doumbouya, instituted the country's first general census of businesses (RGE1) by decree on 18 September 2026, under the planning ministry, with a national council chaired by the prime minister and a technical bureau run by the national statistics institute. It is to count and geolocate formal and informal businesses, build a statistical business register and help rebase the national accounts. No budget is given.

2026-09-19-ken-techtrendske-fixed-broadb.summary: Kenya had 2.84 million fixed internet subscriptions at 30 June 2026, up 32.4% in a year, according to Communications Authority statistics. Fibre rose 29.7% to 1.57 million, Starlink held 27,616 subscriptions, about 1% of the market, DSL fell to 23, and international bandwidth reached 28,950 Gbps.

2026-09-19-lbr-smartnewsliberia-cybercri.summary: Liberia's Cybercrime Act of 2025 has been published as approved law, and its first public test is a warning by the Executive Protection Service director, Sam Gaye, that makers of manipulated material meant to insult or harass could be prosecuted. It followed an arrest over a doctored video of Vice-President Jeremiah Kpan Koung. The article weighs this against the constitution's free-expression guarantee.

2026-09-19-mtn-foundation-ict-business-s.summary: The eighth phase of an operator foundation's skills programme narrowed its intake to young women running micro businesses in six states. Its grant pool is 100 million naira for 100 participants, against 300 million for 600 in the previous phase.

2026-09-19-nga-businessday-data-boom-tel.summary: Nigeria's communications commission recorded mobile data use of 1.66 million terabytes in July 2026, the highest in its published series, and about 10.18 million terabytes from January to July, up roughly 43.6% on 2025. The commission logged more than 5,000 fibre cable cuts in the first half of 2026. MTN Nigeria has committed over $240 million to a Lagos data centre.

2026-09-19-nga-dnl-truecaller-lagos-cour.summary: The High Court of Lagos State ruled on 14 September 2026, in Data Privacy Lawyers Association v Truecaller International LLP, that a Truecaller user's consent to upload contacts does not amount to consent from the non-users whose numbers are uploaded, declining to follow a 2023 Federal High Court decision. The court nonetheless refused the reliefs sought because damages were not established, applicants' counsel Olumide Babalola wrote.

2026-09-19-nga-thenicheng-katsina-ncc-mt.summary: The governor of Katsina State constituted a four-member joint implementation committee with the communications regulator and the dominant mobile operator, to turn a courtesy visit into a costed connectivity plan.

2026-09-19-papss-14th-governing-council-.summary: Central Bank of Egypt Governor Hassan Abdalla attended the 14th Governing Council meeting of the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System in Nairobi, which discussed adding participating banks and reducing cross-border payment risk. Egypt joined the system in November 2024 and its council in January 2025, and is assessing the PAPSS Card and Marketplace services.

The Central Bank of Egypt's governor, Hassan Abdalla, attended the 14th meeting of the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System's governing council in Nairobi on 19 September 2026. The council discussed increasing participation by central and commercial banks and tighter risk controls. Egypt's central bank has been studying the system's technical and legal features so that Egyptian banks can join.

2026-09-19-rwa-aenews-cabinet-18-septemb.summary: Rwanda's Cabinet, chaired by President Paul Kagame on 18 September 2026, approved a bill to ratify an International Development Association loan of additional financing for a project to accelerate digital adoption, signed in Kigali on 11 July 2026. It also approved the Rwanda Development Cooperation Policy 2026–2050. No loan amount is stated.

2026-09-19-sen-socialnetlink-css-prestat.summary: Senegal's Social Security Fund, CSS, began paying several benefits through the Wave mobile money service, including family allowances, prenatal and postnatal allowances, and maternity and pension payments below 100,000 FCFA. Beneficiaries must enrol using a form available at agencies or online. The fund also opened a customer contact centre with a free number, 800 222 222.

2026-09-19-sle-sierraloaded-nmsa-health-.summary: Sierra Leone held a two-day workshop on 17 and 18 September 2026 on a shared digital public infrastructure for health, attended by the National Medical Supplies Agency among others. It mapped existing digital health systems, gaps and duplication, and discussed costing and funding. Participants planned a technical working group to validate the implementation plan. No decision is reported.

2026-09-19-som-somalistream-somalia-paki.summary: A 15-member Somali delegation completed a ten-day peer-learning programme on digital identity and public infrastructure in Islamabad and Lahore, designed by UNDP and the two countries' identity authorities. A Somali official said the national identity authority registers only about 2,000 people a day, far below capacity, and that Somalia has no national data exchange layer.

2026-09-19-som-sonna-national-identifica.summary: Somalia's National Identification Week closed in Mogadishu, reported on 19 September 2026. The National Identification and Registration Authority said it has registered 1.5 million citizens through 59 registration centres, 17 mobile teams and 31 centres at embassies.

2026-09-19-techtrends-african-developers.summary: A survey of open-source work across Africa counts 9.3 million developer accounts in the first quarter of 2026 and committers up 18 per cent over 2025. It notes that some governments now build public infrastructure on open code, citing a Rwandan payment service running on an open-source switch.

2026-09-19-tunisie-cni-hosting-services-.summary: Tunisia's national computing centre describes the state data centre that carries the government's major applications: about fifty servers serving some 4,500 workstations across ministries, regional offices, public bodies and municipalities, with a replicated backup site.

2026-09-19-xaf-timeslive-afcfta-mene-dat.summary: The head of the continental free trade area told a conference that Africa should aim for more than 700 data centres within ten years to carry a digital economy he put at 700 billion dollars. About 260 are counted now, and he named South Africa, Nigeria and Kenya as the builds to replicate.

2026-09-19-zmb-diggers-tiktoker-arrested.summary: Police in Ndola, Zambia, arrested a 24-year-old TikToker, Natasha Nambeya, for allegedly harassing truck drivers, after a trustee of the Truck Drivers Association of Zambia complained about videos accusing drivers of stealing fuel and poor hygiene.

2026-09-19-zmb-lusakatimes-njapau-id-inv.summary: Former Zambian deputy home affairs minister Grace Njapau defended the government's invalidation of national identity documents held by people she accused of an online campaign against President Hakainde Hichilema, naming Emmanuel Mwamba, JJ Banda, Sishuwa Sishuwa and Lillian Mutambo. The number affected, who among them is included and the legal process used are not stated; no government statement is cited.

2026-09-19-zwe-spikedmedia-mavetera-2030.summary: Zimbabwe's ICT, Postal and Courier Services ministry set 2030 as the deadline to turn the country's more than 250 post offices into Smart Post Offices, announced at a postal conference in Harare on 18 September 2026. The plan includes a ring-fenced fund for Zimpost's universal service obligation, AI parcel tracking and drone delivery. A postal policy and an e-commerce bill are being drafted.

2026-09-20-aacb-48th-meetings-bureau-dai.summary: The Association of African Central Banks approved a second edition of the African Financial Stability Report and constituted the board of the African Monetary Institute, closing its 48th annual meetings in Nairobi with the governors of 34 of its 41 member central banks present. Egypt joined the Bureau of Governors as deputy chair for North Africa and chairs the taskforce preparing the report, which is to be published through the stability committee's portal.

2026-09-20-businessdaily-eac-insurance-r.summary: Insurance regulators from six East African states adopted a harmonised assessment template built on about 25 insurance core principles, and agreed to run assessments against it and compare them in December. The same meeting approved regional guidelines on complaints handling and on comparable market data, and progressed a shared supervisory software for information exchange between the regulators.

2026-09-20-cemac-data-governance-roadmap.summary: A five-day African Development Bank, CEMAC and UNFPA workshop closed at Libreville with a 2026-2029 calendar for migrating the six member states to SDMX and version 2.0 of the Open Data Platform. The stated aim is not to make the national statistical systems uniform but to define common structures that let them interoperate; 14 recommendations were addressed to the institutes, the Commission, the Bank and the World Bank.

2026-09-20-civ-fratmat-caidp-referentiel.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's access-to-information commission CAIDP has begun building a national register of public documents, a finding tool to show what documents public bodies hold, who holds them and how to obtain them. It is being developed with the network of about 200 public information officers and will point to existing archives and inventories, not hold the documents. It will be discussed in Abidjan on 24, 25 and 28 September 2026.

2026-09-20-dza-echaab-rakmana-shafafiya-.summary: A dossier in Algeria's Echaab newspaper on 20 September 2026 reviews the High Commission for Digitalisation's work since April 2024: a national digital transformation strategy published in May 2025, a national cloud and certified data centres, the IRIES secure network linking ministries, cybersecurity and network operations centres, and the national digital services centre opened in July 2026. It says a digitalisation law is in the final stages of study.

2026-09-20-egy-ahram-digilians-digital-s.summary: Egypt pays training costs of EGP 500,000 to EGP 1 million per participant in its presidential Digilians digital-skills initiative, ICT ministry adviser Hesham Farouk said on 19 September 2026. Tracks cover AI, data science, software, digital arts and cybersecurity; about 40,000 applied for the first cohort and 1,674 were accepted. More than 50 companies are expected at an October jobs event.

2026-09-20-egy-alnahar-ai-data-centre-ra.summary: Egypt's communications minister, Raafat Hindy, signed a memorandum with China on cloud computing, data centres, semiconductors and cybersecurity during President Xi Jinping's visit, and then received a US data-centre consortium. Huawei had earlier offered to build AI data centres using 1,408 Ascend 950 chips within 12 months; Nvidia, AMD and Microsoft have formed a rival US bid.

2026-09-20-egy-arabfinance-efinance-tamw.summary: Shareholders of Egypt's e-finance for Digital and Financial Investments approved the acquisition of a 99.32% stake in Tamweely Financial Services, for EGP 956.37 million in cash plus 146.08 million new e-finance shares issued to Tamweely's main shareholder, Turin Egypt. An independent study valued Tamweely at EGP 6.426 billion. The Financial Regulatory Authority approved the deal in August.

2026-09-20-egy-youm7-madbouly-infrastruc.summary: Egypt's communications minister told a cabinet meeting on digital projects that the ministry is drawing up an integrated national data-centre strategy with other ministries, to expand capacity inside the country. He set out the incumbent's programme to replace copper with fibre nationally, including in the villages of the rural development initiative, and the finance minister said state spending is being steered towards digital infrastructure and artificial intelligence. No text, timetable or cost was given.

2026-09-20-gha-worldports-icolms-courier.summary: Ghana's communications minister Samuel Nartey George launched the Integrated Courier and Logistics Management System (iCOLMS-GH), a paperless licensing platform for courier companies and delivery riders linked to Ghana.GOV and the National Identification Authority. A compliance grace period ran from 12 to 31 March 2026, with police and regulator enforcement from 1 April; the report appeared on 20 September 2026 and gives no launch date.

2026-09-20-icasees-sdmx-odp2-cemac-deleg.summary: A Central African Republic delegation from the statistics institute ICASEES and the CEMAC Commission took part in a workshop in Libreville, 14–18 September 2026, run by the African Development Bank, CEMAC and UNFPA on the SDMX data standard and Open Data Platform 2.0. ICASEES presented its national plan for moving from ODP 1.0 to 2.0 and demonstrated a locally installed ODP 2.0 system.

2026-09-20-ken-healthcaremea-moh-hakika-.summary: Kenya's health cabinet secretary, Aden Duale, launched the Social Health Authority's 2026-2029 contracting cycle, HAKIKA, and an e-contracting platform at KICC in Nairobi. Providers will submit applications, upload compliance documents, verify licences and sign contracts online; the contracts set claims-processing timelines and downtime safeguards. Providers were urged to transfer before 1 October 2026.

2026-09-20-ken-standard-iebc-voter-regis.summary: Kenyan political parties and election observers are to be given access to the source code and audit logs of the electoral commission's continuous voter registration system, following a court directive. The account is a free lede behind a paywall and names neither the court, the case nor the date of the directive.

2026-09-20-lby-lana-ar-national-cybersec.summary: Libya's minister of state Mohammed bin Ghalboun chaired a meeting in Tripoli on 20 September 2026 on drawing up an integrated national cybersecurity plan, with the heads of the cybersecurity authority, the General Information Authority and the national information security authority. It covered cyber emergency plans, early warning, incident response and a joint mechanism to monitor compliance. No plan text or deadline was published.

2026-09-20-mrt-trustmag-bcm-fintech-monn.summary: The Central Bank of Mauritania's newsletter for August 2026 reports a week of sandbox tests for its central bank digital currency proof of concept. It also reports a data platform holding over 78 million records since January 2024, two GIZ-backed fintech hackathons set for 19–22 October 2026, and a draft monetary and financial code due by mid-2027.

2026-09-20-nam-namibian-ransomhouse-ndf-.summary: A ransomware group listed the Namibian Defence Force among its victims and published an evidence pack it says shows access to the force's systems, with a message accusing its IT department of concealing the incident. No confirmation or response from the force is on record, and the defence minister said he had not heard of it.

2026-09-20-nam-technews-defence-ministry.summary: Namibia's national cyber incident response team, NAM-CSIRT, confirmed unauthorised activity on the Ministry of Defence and Veterans Affairs network and attributed it to the RansomHouse ransomware group, reported on 20 September 2026. It is coordinating investigation and recovery. It did not say what data was accessed, stolen or encrypted.

2026-09-20-ner-anp-cfaic-reglementation-.summary: Niger's collective of community internet access providers (CFAIC-Niger) called on 20 September 2026 for Wi-Fi Zone rules that operators can realistically meet. It welcomed the order placing Wi-Fi Zones under a declaration regime but contested provisions on equipment, file-review fees, annual royalties and technical limits, and asked for six months to comply.

2026-09-20-papss-im-bank-kenya-go-live-t.summary: The Pan-African Payment and Settlement System went live for customers of I&M Bank Kenya, the second Kenyan bank on the network. Customers can send to participating African markets in Kenyan shillings through the bank's branches rather than converting into an international currency; no volume, fee or corridor detail was published.

2026-09-20-papss-meeza-card-integration-.summary: Afreximbank is connecting the continental card scheme to Egypt's Meeza national card network so cards issued on either side work across more African markets. The first phase joins the two infrastructures and establishes a settlement layer; payment would be in the currency of the country being visited, and no availability date was given.

2026-09-20-sle-techreview-civil-servant-.summary: Sierra Leone's Ministry of Communication, Technology and Innovation is training civil servants in digital skills with the public administration ministry, the Human Resource Management Office and the Public Service Academy. In its second week, reported on 20 September 2026, the first cohort of administrative staff learned to draft letters and reports with AI tools and keep registers in Google Workspace; the cohort ends on 25 September.

2026-09-20-som-hiiraan-national-id-1-5-m.summary: Somalia's identity authority has registered more than 1.5 million citizens since 2023, against a target of 15 million citizens and residents by 2029. The interior minister said issuance would extend to embassies abroad, with priority for persons with disabilities and displaced communities.

2026-09-20-tcd-lendjampost-house-of-afri.summary: A campaign on digital citizenship and the risks of internet use was launched at Abeche by a non-governmental organisation with Chad's national youth council, backed by an external democracy initiative. No participant target, duration or further location was given.

2026-09-20-techtrends-digital-skills-gap.summary: An account of the cybersecurity staffing gap in African governments, putting 63 per cent of sub-Saharan organisations short of cyber staff and Nigeria's shortfall at 90.6 per cent against 25,760 people in post. It runs through recent attacks on the core of the state, among them three on Senegalese public institutions in under six months.

2026-09-20-the-next-wave-the-expensive-l.summary: An account of the Kenyan business-to-business commerce company Twiga Foods, which raised about US$185.4 million over twelve years without reaching profitability. It traces the premise that software could displace the brokers between smallholder farmers and neighbourhood kiosks, and what the company's farming arm, its Tatu City lease and a creditor's petition have cost that premise.

2026-09-20-timeslive-joburg-wifi-plan-fa.summary: Johannesburg's city-owned Metropolitan Tech Company says in its 2026/27 business plan that it is under-capacitated, with 26 network staff maintaining 1,200km of fibre. The plan budgets about R570m for operations but R20.7m for capital spending, and says more than 60% of its city subsidy services a shareholder loan. Its free Wi-Fi target for 2026/27 is 200,000 connections, against 1,574,979 recorded in 2024/25.

2026-09-20-tun-allafrica-anis-ben-said-f.summary: Tunisian tax adviser Anis Ben Saïd told Diwan FM on 19 September 2026 that electronic invoicing is now mandatory for about 380,000 liberal-profession providers, including doctors, lawyers, engineers and accountants, with registration on the platform open since 15 September. Invoices are validated through the mobile digital identity and cannot be changed once signed; errors require a credit note.

2026-09-20-tza-tanzaniainvest-e-ardhi-si.summary: Tanzania's e-Ardhi land system now lets people sign title deeds from any region instead of travelling to where the service started, a Ruvuma lands official said in a Ministry of Lands broadcast reported on 20 September 2026. The system covers planning, surveying, allocation, registration and valuation, and is in use in Dodoma, Arusha, Tanga, Mbeya and Mwanza.

2026-09-20-uga-nilepost-mtn-internet-bus.summary: 305 people graduated in Kampala from the sixth phase of a mobile-classroom digital and financial literacy programme run by the largest mobile operator's foundation, taking the number trained to more than 6,700. The training covers safe internet use, digital productivity and the use of digital financial services.

2026-09-20-xgl-reuters-bessent-he-ai-tra.summary: The US Treasury Secretary and China's Vice Premier were to meet to prepare possible agreements on artificial intelligence, tariffs and critical minerals ahead of a Washington summit, with the trade truce between the two set to expire on 10 November. The report is held only as far as its paywall.

2026-09-20-zwe-newzimbabwe-mnangagwa-ai-.summary: Zimbabwe's president named the digital divide, online safety and fair artificial intelligence as the country's priorities for the UN General Assembly, saying the world must rebuild trust to manage a transformation moving faster than ever. The statement was made in a post on his own account on arriving in New York.

2026-09-20-zwe-techreviewafrica-postal-c.summary: Zimbabwe's ICT minister Tatenda Mavetera set out a three-phase plan for the postal and courier sector at its annual conference: ring-fencing the Universal Service Fund, then Smart Post Offices by 2030 with AI, drones and e-commerce, then strategic equity partnerships. A Postal and Telecommunications Amendment Bill is before Parliament and an E-Commerce and E-Transactions Bill is being drafted.

2026-09-21-ago-angop-abanc-campanha-cont.summary: The Angolan Bankers Association launched a 60-day public campaign against banking fraud in Luanda on 21 September 2026, working with the interbank processor EMIS. Its president linked the campaign to the risks of banking by phone and to customers' low financial literacy. The campaign will appear in traditional and digital media, on billboards and ATMs, and through banks' own channels.

2026-09-21-ago-expansao-kwik-carteiras-d.summary: Transfers between digital wallets were only 0.6% (Kz 3.1 billion) of the Kz 557.4 billion that passed through Angola's Kwik instant-payment system in the first half of 2026, according to EMIS data. Wallets sent about 38% of the value, nearly all of it to bank accounts, while banks sent about 62%, and only Kz 2.8 billion of that went to non-bank providers. Only the free opening of the article is held.

2026-09-21-bfa-burkina24-orange-max-it-n.summary: Orange Burkina Faso relaunched its Max It app on 18 September 2026 with a promotional caravan through four cities. The new version adds messaging and TV to mobile money, calls and SMS, and is open to customers of other networks. It links to almost all the country's banks for transfers to wallets, and takes water and electricity bills and public charges such as the vehicle tax.

2026-09-21-bfa-csc-paremec-plateforme-re.summary: The media regulators of Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger adopted the founding texts of a joint platform, PAREMEC, at a meeting in Niamey on 17–18 September 2026, according to Burkina Faso's Conseil supérieur de la communication. The platform is to pool the three bodies' skills and resources to harmonise media and communication regulation across the Confederation of Sahel States.

2026-09-21-biometricupdate-kenyas-digita.summary: Kenya's electronic birth notification system, launched in June 2026, registered more than 270,000 newborns and gave them unique personal identifiers within two months. It sends birth details from hospitals to civil registration offices. Principal Secretary Belio Kipsang said 2.4 million national IDs were issued from January to September 2026, and an e-notification system for deaths is planned.

2026-09-21-bwa-weekendpost-absa-google-p.summary: Absa Bank Botswana has made Google Pay available on Android for its Visa debit, credit and multi-currency virtual cards, with no extra fees. The launch date was not given. The service only works where merchants have NFC terminals, and the report says these are patchy outside Gaborone and Francistown.

2026-09-21-civ-aip-pagds-realisations-di.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's World Bank-funded PAGDS project, approved in April 2019, reported its digitalisation results on 21 September 2026, and its coordinator said a second phase has started. The results include digital allocation and tracking of pupils in private schools, patient tracking under universal health coverage, electronic payment of state transfers and online company registration. World Bank figures cited put average growth in non-oil tax revenue at 12.4% against a 5% target, and customs revenue at 19.2% against 6%.

2026-09-21-cod-7sur7-igf-afd-transformat.summary: DR Congo's Inspection Générale des Finances asked the French development agency AFD, at its Paris headquarters on 18 September 2026, to support its digital transformation. The plan centres on a national store of state financial data for auditing. The head of the DRC's digital transformation project said AFD could help through that project, but the talks were exploratory and no amount was named.

2026-09-21-cod-actualite-dibandi-protect.summary: Alfred Dibandi Nzondomyo, a national deputy in the Democratic Republic of Congo, filed a private member's bill on protecting minors in the digital environment on 21 September 2026. He said it complements the Digital Code and child-protection law, with rules by age band for under-6s, under-11s and under-15s. The bill's text has not been published.

2026-09-21-cod-actualitecd-bcc-adhesion-.summary: DR Congo joined the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System on 18 September 2026, when the central bank governor, André Wameso, signed the accession agreement in Nairobi. The same day he signed the East African Community central banks' memorandum on currency convertibility and repatriation, which Burundi, Uganda, Tanzania, Kenya and South Sudan had already joined.

2026-09-21-cog-adiac-sicom-bilan-23-reso.summary: Congo's first information, communication and media fair closed at Kintélé on 19 September 2026 with 23 resolutions from participants. They call for rewriting the three core media laws to take account of digital broadcasting, online platforms and AI, and cover digital content, advertising and tax. These are recommendations from the profession, not government decisions.

2026-09-21-com-pfss-tms-55000-menages-mo.summary: Comoros began a new phase of its World Bank-funded social cash transfers on 20 September 2026, reaching 55,000 households, 15,000 of them new, with USD 11 million in additional financing. Payments go through the mobile-banking operators Mvula and Huri Money, and households are selected from the unified social registry.

2026-09-21-cpv-ccip-afdb-reoi-sgit-nomad.summary: Cabo Verde's integrated project coordination centre, CCIP, invited expressions of interest on 21 September 2026 from firms to build a statistics and data module for the National Digital Nomads Programme within the SGIT system, interoperable with other state platforms. The 12-month contract is financed from an African Development Bank credit to the Morabeza Innovation Project. No contract value is given.

2026-09-21-dza-interfil-conseil-ministre.summary: Algeria's Council of Ministers, meeting under President Tebboune on 20 September 2026, called for a presidential decree setting up a secure plan for data exchange between state bodies, overseen by the High Commissioner for Digitalisation. The president asked for the plan to reach the wilayas too, with strong protection of citizens' data. He also ordered that payments to farmers at the state cereals office be digitised immediately.

2026-09-21-egy-dailynewsegypt-fra-movabl.summary: Egypt's Financial Regulatory Authority surveyed creditors on the services and electronic system of the Egyptian Movable Collateral Registry and met them with the registry's operator, E-Finance, to review the findings, Daily News Egypt reported on 21 September 2026. The proposals will undergo technical and legal review before priorities are set. No timetable is given.

2026-09-21-egy-mubadala-paymob-35m-pre-s.summary: Egyptian payments company Paymob raised $35 million in a pre-Series C round co-led by Abu Dhabi's Mubadala and the EBRD, with BII, Global Ventures and DPI Ventures also taking part (21 September 2026). The money will fund expansion across the Middle East and North Africa. Paymob says revenue from the Gulf grew sevenfold in 18 months and now makes up close to half the total.

2026-09-21-egy-newkerala-india-egypt-ict.summary: India's ambassador to Egypt, Suresh Reddy, met communications minister Raafat Hindy to discuss closer cooperation on ICT. According to the Indian embassy, the talks covered India's digital public infrastructure and how it could be used elsewhere, cooperation between institutions, and links between the two countries' tech companies. No outcome was announced.

2026-09-21-egy-zawya-orange-egypt-marake.summary: Orange Egypt will design, install and operate telecoms networks at four Marakez developments: Ramla, District 5, Aeon Towers and Mall of Arabia. The deal covers fibre to the home, bundled broadband, TV and voice, public Wi-Fi and a smart CCTV system for the mall's first phase. No value was disclosed.

2026-09-21-gab-gabonmediatime-dgdinc-ani.summary: Gabon's Council of Ministers appointed Anicet Claude Andjouat on 18 September 2026 to head a new Directorate-General for digital infrastructure and cybersecurity, created in December 2025. Gabon Media Time reports that the directorate's remit over spectrum, digital infrastructure and cybersecurity overlaps with that of the existing agency ANINF, and that no public division of responsibilities has been set out.

2026-09-21-gab-gabonreview-cemac-systeme.summary: Experts from six CEMAC member states met in Libreville on 21 September 2026 to prepare national energy information systems and a common regional system, with support from the African Energy Commission. They examined a draft community regulation on collecting, validating and disseminating energy data ahead of a ministerial meeting on 25 September.

2026-09-21-gab-gabonreview-permis-condui.summary: Gabon's transport minister Ulrich Manfoumbi Manfoumbi suspended enrolment for the digitalised driving licence on 21 September 2026, six months after launch, to review the scheme; no resumption date was given. 6,993 printed licences await collection in Libreville, and unnamed sources linked the pause to production problems under heavy demand and power cuts.

2026-09-21-gamtel-company-profile-ace-25.summary: The Gambian state operator's undated company profile. It says Gamtel has four international gateways on the ACE submarine cable giving 25 Gbps, and a 28 Gbps backup link through Senegal's Free that traffic switches to if ACE fails.

2026-09-21-gin-agenceecofin-donnees-agri.summary: Guinea's agriculture ministry presented on 16 September 2026 the pilot results of its national agricultural data services programme, run with the Kenyan start-up Pula: 20,463 producers registered and 23,507 farms mapped in Kindia, Kankan and Mamou. Each producer receives a card with a QR code and NFC chip giving authorised users access to verified data on a secure portal.

2026-09-21-gin-mediaguinee-hac-interdit-.summary: Guinea's media regulator, the Haute Autorité de la Communication, on 21 September 2026 banned ten web TV channels and two news sites nationwide and on all digital platforms for broadcasting online without authorisation. Those named include Dabola TV, Coyah TV and Siguiri 24 Star TV. The regulator said earlier warnings to regularise had been ignored.

2026-09-21-gmb-gnnliberia-lra-gra-revenu.summary: The Liberia Revenue Authority signed a memorandum of engagement to help the Gambia Revenue Authority build a dashboard that tracks revenue collection; it was announced from Accra on 20 September 2026 and signed during meetings of the West African Tax Administration Forum. The help covers a review of GRA's data sources, choice of indicators, design, a prototype, integration and staff training. The LRA will send the developer of its own dashboard to Banjul for an initial three weeks.

2026-09-21-gmb-thepoint-gra-lra-digital-.summary: The Gambian account of the Liberia–Gambia revenue dashboard agreement, summarised under the GNN Liberia report. It adds that the LRA pays the expert's airfare while the GRA covers lodging and local transport.

2026-09-21-gsma-pdaa-advancing-digital-c.summary: The report behind the GSMA and PDAA roadmap, summarised under the launch. It counts 550 million internet users in Africa in 2025 (36% of the population) and projects about 700 million by 2030 on current trends. Halving the coverage and usage gaps could add some 514 million people and take the total past 1 billion.

2026-09-21-gsma-pdaa-roadmap-1-billion-c.summary: The GSMA and the Partnership for Digital Access in Africa launched a roadmap in New York on 21 September 2026 on how to reach 1 billion connected Africans by 2030. Based on 11 markets, it finds about 906 million people living within mobile broadband coverage but not using the mobile internet, against 122 million with no coverage at all. Its three priorities are moving over 600 million 2G and 3G connections to 4G or 5G, investing in energy and connectivity together, and reaching rural areas more cheaply.

2026-09-21-itweb-africa-kenya-hoover-ins.summary: Kenya's foreign ministry signed a five-year memorandum of understanding with the Emerging Markets Working Group at Stanford's Hoover Institution during the UN General Assembly in New York. The signing date was not given. The first project is an El Niño monitoring and response system that brings climate, geospatial, water, farming and infrastructure data together by county. Later work is to include a digital trade readiness index and a tracker for public-private partnerships.

2026-09-21-itweb-africa-malawi-india-tec.summary: India's High Commission and the mHub innovation hub held a workshop in Lilongwe on AI, digital skills and technology investment, attended by more than 70 companies. India's high commissioner pointed to openings in agriculture, digital public infrastructure and financial inclusion. No agreement or commitment came out of it.

2026-09-21-itweb-fpb-ai-oversight-stream.summary: South Africa's Film and Publication Board has approved a strategy on digitisation and AI and plans to try generative AI for monitoring, classifying content and managing cases over the next three to five years. None of it is yet in use. Its enforcement committee fined 21 content distributors a total of R16.175 million in September 2026.

2026-09-21-ken-cbk-draft-nps-policy-and-.summary: Kenya's National Treasury and central bank published a draft National Payment System Policy and a draft National Payment System Bill, 2026 for public comment on 21 September 2026. The bill would replace the current Act and license payment providers and system operators by category, with minimum capital of Ksh5 million to Ksh250 million. It also requires interoperability, allows open-finance data sharing with consent and brings virtual asset providers that offer payments under the law, while the policy commits the government to a national instant payment switch.

2026-09-21-ken-diaspora-go-ke-kenya-dias.summary: Kenya's government, the United Nations in Kenya and Equity Group Holdings signed a joint declaration of intent in New York on 20 September 2026 to work on the Kenya Diaspora Impact Platform, a digital gateway linking diaspora investors to verified investment and development projects in Kenya. No budget, operator or launch date is given.

2026-09-21-ken-kenyans-ardhisasa-outage-.summary: Kenya's ArdhiSasa land platform announced an outage on 21 September 2026 affecting searches, transfers, title and lease registration, and stamp duty and land-rent payments, with no time given for restoring service. The Law Society of Kenya had already complained that the platform was unavailable from 1 September.

2026-09-21-ken-treasury-draft-national-p.summary: Kenya's draft National Payment System Policy, dated August 2026, which identifies ten gaps in the current system. It commits to a national instant payment switch, requires open APIs and gives non-banks access to settlement. The consultation is summarised under the Treasury and central bank's joint release.

2026-09-21-ken-treasury-national-payment.summary: The full draft text of Kenya's National Payment System Bill, 2026, which runs to 79 clauses. It sets licence capital of Ksh5 million to Ksh250 million, requires interoperability, provides for open finance, brings virtual asset providers into scope and sets fines of up to Ksh20 million. The consultation is summarised under the Treasury and central bank's joint release.

2026-09-21-lbr-frontpageafrica-cybercrim.summary: A second account of the Wrotto arrest, summarised under the New Dawn report. It adds a justice ministry prosecutor's view that the state, not the vice-president, decides whether a prosecution goes ahead, and notes that the Act does not mention AI or deepfakes.

2026-09-21-lbr-newdawn-koung-seeks-relea.summary: Liberia's vice-president Jeremiah Koung asked for the release of Jerry Nyantee Wrotto, whom police detained under the Cybercrime Act over AI-made images and videos of Koung, and said he would not press charges. It is one of the first high-profile uses of the Act, signed on 19 August 2026 with the Data Protection Act. The head of the Executive Protection Service defended the arrest, while critics including former finance minister Samuel Tweah said the Act's cyberbullying clauses cover protected speech.

2026-09-21-lby-alwasat-cbl-unified-datab.summary: Libya's central bank governor, Naji Issa, put forward an electronic system and a single national database for recording and following up international grants, projects and support. He made the proposal on 21 September 2026 at the second meeting of the committee set up under prime-ministerial decision 422 of 2026. The idea is still under discussion and has not been adopted.

2026-09-21-mdg-newsmada-gasy-money-bgfib.summary: BGFIBank Madagascar launched Gasy Money, a mobile banking app open to people without an account at the bank, including those with no bank account at all, on any mobile network. The launch date was not given. It handles deposits and withdrawals through agents, branches and ATMs, merchant and bill payments, top-ups of prepaid Visa cards, and transfers to bank accounts and Airtel Money.

2026-09-21-mli-burkina24-centre-ia-robot.summary: Transition president Assimi Goïta opened Mali's artificial intelligence and robotics centre, CIAR-Mali, at Kati on 21 September 2026. He had laid its foundation stone on 7 June 2023.
