2026-09-23-zaf-parliament-paia-court-rul.summary: South Africa's parliamentary justice committee agreed on 23 September 2026 that the Department of Justice may publish proposed amended court rules for applications under the Promotion of Access to Information Act. The draft rules standardise section 78 applications across all courts, require sworn section 80 representations five days before hearings, and repeal the previous PAIA rules. They are not yet in force.

2026-09-23-zaf-sovereignty-govt-digital-.summary: At GovTech 2026 in Durban, SITA board chair Stella Bvuma framed digital sovereignty as control over where public data sits, who can reach it and how services survive a supplier or network failure. She reported that SITA spent R183 million with SMEs in the first four months of 2026/27, 49% of available procurement spend against a 45% target.

2026-09-23-zaf-uct-r101m-ai-microscopy-a.summary: The University of Cape Town launched openScopes AIDDiA, a four-year, Wellcome Trust-funded programme worth GBP 4.4 million (about R101 million) pairing open-source microscopy with machine-learning image analysis for research on TB, malaria and other infectious diseases. Partners are KEMRI, Uganda's Mbarara University, Côte d'Ivoire's CSRS and Imperial College London.

2026-09-23-zmb-rmb-payment-system-china-.summary: Stanbic Bank Zambia launched direct renminbi settlement for Zambia–China trade through China's Cross-Border Interbank Payment System in Lusaka on 23 September 2026. Zambia's commerce permanent secretary Lillian Bwalya said it would cut currency-conversion and intermediary costs and support Chinese investment in mining, manufacturing and infrastructure.

2026-09-23-zwe-sirdc-africa-data-protect.summary: Zimbabwe's telecoms regulator POTRAZ held a national workshop on guidelines under the Cyber and Data Protection Act and on amendments to Statutory Instrument 155 of 2024 on administrative fines, marking the first Africa Data Protection Day on 21 September 2026, according to the research centre SIRDC. The text and status of the amendments are not given.

2026-09-23-zwe-sirdc-budget-automation-p.summary: Zimbabwe held the second pilot workshop of its National Budget Automation System, known as the Blue Book System, in Kwekwe from 21 to 25 September 2026. The research centre SIRDC, which took part, presents it as automating public finance management for more accurate and transparent budgets.

2026-09-24-afdb-unga81-ai-training-publi.summary: The African Development Bank Group, the UNDP-led AI Hub for Sustainable Development, Google and Apolitical launched free, self-paced AI courses for African public officials at the UN General Assembly in New York, announced on 24 September 2026. The courses, by Stanford University Online and SDA Bocconi, cover AI fundamentals, leadership and procurement, and are open to officials in the Bank's regional member countries.

2026-09-24-africa-ai-disability-data-hai.summary: A Hub for AI and Disability Inclusion (HAIDI), hosted by KNUST's Responsible AI Lab, and an African Disability Data Network were launched at the Global Data Festival in Nairobi with backing from IDRC, the UK FCDO and AI4D. They plan to map disability-related datasets, build three new datasets, assess how national AI strategies treat disability and fund three startups with grants of up to KES 5 million.

2026-09-24-angolanewswire-17-million-ide.summary: Angola has issued 17,166,000 national identity cards at home and abroad, the national director of registries, Aristides Marques, said in Luanda on 24 September 2026. Daily production capacity has risen from 12,000 to 60,000 cards, cards are now printed in all 21 provinces, and the target is a card for every registered adult by December 2026. A draft law would make the card the only valid identity document.

2026-09-24-bfa-sidwaya-ia-secretaires-ge.summary: Burkina Faso's digital transition ministry trained the secretaries general of ministries and institutions in the use of artificial intelligence in Ouagadougou on 24–25 September 2026. The course covered generative AI tools and which administrative data can be entered into them without disclosing confidential information.

2026-09-24-civ-emerging-technologies-dig.summary: Launching Ivoire Tech Forum 2026, to be held in Abidjan on 11-13 November, digital minister Djibril Ouattara announced a startup labelling platform that will give labelled startups access to the country's fiscal incentives. He also named connectivity, administrative digitalisation and digital skills as priorities.

2026-09-24-cog-aci-data-center-82-pource.summary: The Republic of Congo's vice-prime minister, Jean-Jacques Bouya, said on 22 September 2026 that the African Development Bank-funded national data centre at Bacongo, Brazzaville, will be operational by the end of 2026, with works at 82%. He inspected it with digital minister Frédéric Nzé alongside the 12 MW Kintélé solar farm meant to back its power supply.

2026-09-24-cog-vox-vpm-inspecte-data-cen.summary: The Republic of Congo's deputy prime minister, Jean-Jacques Bouya, and the telecoms and digital economy minister, Frédéric Nzé, inspected the national data centre at Bacongo, Brazzaville, and the Kintélé solar farm on 22 September 2026. Bouya said the data centre, built with the African Development Bank, should be operational by the end of 2026 or early 2027, after energy tests and then two to three months of data-centre tests.

2026-09-24-cpv-ugpe-review-meeting-digit.summary: A World Bank mission reviewed the Digital Cabo Verde project between 22 and 26 September, reporting about 80% disbursement of the original US$20 million financing (2020-2025) and about 40% of the US$20 million additional financing (2025-2028). School connectivity was named the priority for the additional financing, with stronger coordination across ministries and a clearer role for the DGTED.

2026-09-24-digitalbusiness-africa-camero.summary: Cameroon's Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications launched train.patnucelearning.cm in Yaoundé on 21 September 2026, an online platform to train 15,000 civil servants and public-enterprise staff over 50 days in AI and blockchain, digital project management and electronic records. It runs under PATNUC, the digital transformation project financed by a 42 billion CFA franc World Bank loan.

2026-09-24-dza-algerie-eco-cnr-assistant.summary: Algeria's national pension fund, the Caisse nationale des retraites, launched a virtual assistant chatbot on its website cnr.dz, announced on 24 September 2026. It answers questions about the pension system around the clock from a database of pre-set replies, to reduce visits to local offices.

2026-09-24-dza-ecotimesdz-djezzy-payment.summary: The Bank of Algeria's Monetary and Banking Council authorised Djezzy Payment Services, a subsidiary of the mobile operator, to form a payment service provider, announced on 23 September 2026. It has twelve months to apply for the licence it needs to operate. Payment accounts under the rules are capped at 100,000, 500,000 or 1,000,000 dinars depending on the level of identity verification.

2026-09-24-dza-leprovincial-djezzy-payme.summary: Algeria's Monetary and Banking Council authorised Djezzy Payment Services, a subsidiary of Optimum Telecom Algérie, to be set up as a payment services provider under monetary law 23-09, the Bank of Algeria announced on 23 September 2026. The firm must apply for a full licence within 12 months.

2026-09-24-dza-observalgerie-cnr-assista.summary: Algeria's National Pensions Fund, CNR, launched a 24-hour online virtual assistant on its website on 24 September 2026 to answer pensioners' routine questions. In July 2026 the labour ministry set a target of cutting visits to CNR offices by at least 50% by the end of 2026. Some pensioners can already confirm they are alive through the R-FACE facial recognition system in the RetraiteDz app.

2026-09-24-ecowas-startup-awards-5m-deal.summary: The Economic Community of West African States opened the second edition of its Startup Awards in Abuja on 21 September 2026, with 60 startups chosen from more than 6,000 applicants across six sectors including fintech and health tech. ECOWAS aims to broker US$5 million in investment and deals, with regional finals on 30 September.

2026-09-24-egy-fra-decision-2684-consume.summary: Egypt's Financial Regulatory Authority issued Decision No. 2684 of 2026, in force from 24 September, requiring consumer-finance companies to build links from their databases to the authority's. Customer records, real-time purchases, repayment standing and solvency data are to flow under controls the authority will issue within six months. No terms on consent or retention are stated.

2026-09-24-egy-moneyhash-geidea-payment-.summary: Payment orchestration platform MoneyHash partnered with payments provider Geidea, giving businesses already integrated with MoneyHash access to Geidea's online gateway and payment methods in Egypt, the UAE and Saudi Arabia without a separate connection.

2026-09-24-eth-ena-unga81-digital-financ.summary: Ethiopia and UNCDF held a side event at UNGA81 presenting digital payments, the Fayda national ID and digital public infrastructure as tools for financial inclusion and the SDGs. Planning minister Fitsum Assefa cited Digital Ethiopia 2030, the National Financial Inclusion Strategy, interoperable payments and BRIDGE 2030.

2026-09-24-eth-her-cybertracks-women-cyb.summary: Nearly 50 women cybersecurity professionals from across Africa met in Addis Ababa for the Her CyberTracks Regional Training Africa 2026. The programme is funded by Germany, the European Commission and Italy and delivered by the ITU and GIZ with UNODC's Global Programme on Cybercrime.

2026-09-24-gab-gabonreview-cybercriminal.summary: Gabon's foreign minister, Marie-Édith Tassyla-Ye-Doumbeneny, signed the UN Convention against Cybercrime on 23 September 2026 during the UN General Assembly's high-level week, alongside the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons. Gabon presents the convention as a framework for mutual legal assistance and exchange of electronic evidence. It has signed, not ratified.

2026-09-24-gab-la-connectivite-universel.summary: Gabon's digital agency ANINF told an ITU workshop on universal meaningful connectivity in Dakar, 22-24 September 2026, that the country had 2.41 million internet subscriptions in the first quarter of 2026, 94% of them mobile, on ARCEP data. It proposed moving from counting subscriptions to measuring meaningful connectivity, and setting up a national dashboard to track it.

2026-09-24-gha-gmb-nca-pura-benchmarking.summary: Ghana's National Communications Authority is hosting a delegation from The Gambia's Public Utilities Regulatory Authority for a benchmarking visit from 22 to 25 September, PURA's second this year. The visit covers regulatory governance, consumer protection, dispute resolution, quality-of-service indicators and broadcasting.

2026-09-24-gha-myjoyonline-intel-ai-for-.summary: Ghana signed an agreement with Intel on the sidelines of UNGA81 to expand the AI for Youth programme into K-12 schools, with Coral Reef and the Ministry of Education as partners. The gender minister signed on behalf of the First Lady; no value or timeline was given.

2026-09-24-gha-myjoyonline-mobile-money-.summary: Bank of Ghana data show monthly mobile money transaction values rose from GH¢446.2 billion in January 2026 to GH¢518.8 billion in August 2026, about GH¢3.8 trillion for the year to date. There were 26.4 million active accounts against 85.8 million registered in August 2026. Transactions totalled GH¢4.54 trillion in 2025.

2026-09-24-ifc-airtel-money-2026-90m-sta.summary: Airtel Money, Airtel Africa's mobile money arm in 13 markets, filed for a London Stock Exchange listing in which existing shareholders sell shares, aiming to raise about US$800 million at a valuation of US$8-9 billion. The IFC agreed to buy up to GBP 67.2 million (about US$90 million) of shares at the offer price.

2026-09-24-journaldebangui-caf-ane-data-.summary: A fire damaged part of the data-processing centre of the Central African Republic's National Elections Authority in the week before 24 September 2026, and the government opened an investigation. Territorial administration minister Bruno Yapandé said the residual elections scheduled for October 2026 will go ahead. No cause or estimate of damage is given.

2026-09-24-ken-biznakenya-coop-bank-uncd.summary: Co-operative Bank of Kenya and UNCDF launched a US$900,000 loan portfolio guarantee under the DigiKen programme, backing up to US$1.8 million of lending to fintechs, digital credit providers, e-commerce and digitally enabled small firms, and innovation hubs. UNCDF covers 50% of outstanding principal, rising to 70% for borrowers in the Arid and Semi-Arid Lands.

2026-09-24-ken-childrens-rights-ai-roadm.summary: President Ruto co-hosted the launch of a 2026-2027 Roadmap for Children's Rights and Protection in the Age of AI at the UN General Assembly, alongside the leaders of France, Spain and Australia. Kenya's technology envoy Philip Thigo said Kenya would take the work forward at home, across Africa and globally.

2026-09-24-ken-cipesa-kenya-ai-emerging-.summary: CIPESA submitted comments on draft guidance notes on AI and on emerging technologies issued for consultation by Kenya's Office of the Data Protection Commissioner. It warns that requiring adequacy assessments for cross-border transfers could lead to blanket data localisation. It also asks for impact assessments on biometric processing, audits of feed algorithms and oversight of state use.

2026-09-24-ken-cross-border-digital-publ.summary: ICT Cabinet Secretary William Kabogo proposed that willing African Union member states jointly pilot one cross-border public service and report back by February 2027. He made the proposal at an AUC-Google ministerial roundtable in New York, pointing to eCitizen's more than 22,500 services and Kenya's Government Interoperability Framework.

2026-09-24-ken-mcaai-dholuo-speech-data-.summary: The Maseno Centre for Applied Artificial Intelligence ran a preparatory visit to Suba ahead of collecting Dholuo speech data to improve the language's representation in AI systems, onboarding participants to its SmartVoice app. The work involves the ACTS-AI4D team.

2026-09-24-ken-pulse-co-ke-anthropic-ai-.summary: Kenya and Anthropic signed a Joint Declaration in New York on 22 September covering AI skills, research, responsible public-sector use, AI safety and evaluation, and applications in education and health. Pilots, research and training with Kenyan institutions are to follow, governed by Kenyan law including on data protection and cybersecurity.

2026-09-24-kenya-kenswitch-domestic-card.summary: Kenswitch, Kenya's largest independent payments switch, launched a domestic card scheme on 22 September that lets banks and other institutions issue physical and virtual cards on its network of more than 2,200 ATMs, 50,000 point-of-sale terminals and 80,000 agent outlets. It named no issuers, launch dates or pricing against Visa and Mastercard.

2026-09-24-lbr-liberianobserver-dara-dig.summary: Ten Liberian civil society organisations signed a memorandum founding the Digital Advocacy and Rights Alliance. It commits them to press for an independent data protection authority, amendments narrowing the Cybercrime Act of 2025 and tighter oversight of state interception, and court authorisation for internet shutdowns. A founding assembly is due within 90 days; the signing date is not given.

2026-09-24-lbr-real-world-validation-of-.summary: A prospective study at John F. Kennedy Medical Center in Monrovia tested an offline AI system on a smartphone fundus camera for referable diabetic retinopathy in general outpatients. Among 1,198 participants with a gradable eye it caught 10 of 11 referable cases (sensitivity 90.9%) and cleared 1,183 of 1,187 negatives (specificity 99.7%), though the small number of positives leaves a wide confidence interval on sensitivity.

2026-09-24-lbr-thenewdawn-justice-minist.summary: Nimba County Senator Nya Twayen asked Liberia's Justice Ministry to publish enforcement guidelines for the Cybercrime Act of 2025, including clear charging thresholds, to protect free expression and due process. His call follows the arrest and four charges under the Act against Jerry Nyantee Wrato over allegedly manipulated content about the Vice President; Wrato was later freed after court intervention.

2026-09-24-lusakatimes-zmb-funeral-schem.summary: Zambia's Public Service Management Division said its funeral scheme for public servants, run with Madison Life Insurance, will move to a digital platform in the first week of October 2026, reported on 24 September. Members will be able to update details, register family members and track claims by phone or computer, with Chinsali among the first districts for awareness meetings. No cost is given.

2026-09-24-lusakatimes-zmb-kgs-digital-c.summary: Zambia's education ministry has trained 25 guidance teachers in Lavushimanda District to verify Keeping Girls in School beneficiaries on a tablet app instead of paper forms, under the GEWEL project. The girls are captured and sign on the tablet themselves; the training is run three times a year.

2026-09-24-mdg-2424mg-bpo-training-asana.summary: Madagascar's Asanai programme certified 99 of the 111 trainees in its second seven-week cohort in business process outsourcing skills on 24 September 2026. The programme is run by the digital development ministry with World Bank support through the Integrated Growth Poles (PIC) project and delivered with ArkeUp Academy.

2026-09-24-moz-estado-centraliza-compras.summary: Mozambique has created a central purchasing body, the Central de Aquisições do Estado, by Decree 22/2026 of 8 June, to run certain purchases of works, goods and services for the State, subject to annual external audit. Decree 46/2026 adds framework agreements, dynamic purchasing systems and joint purchasing, with electronic contracting meant to improve traceability.

2026-09-24-moz-jornalnoticias-registo-ci.summary: Mozambique's justice ministry is installing 100 civil registration posts in health units with maternity wards so that newborns are registered before leaving hospital, with partners supplying computer equipment. About 250 birth registration posts already operate in health units, covering roughly 25% of the country's approximately 1,000 health units. No completion date is given.

2026-09-24-ner-actuniger-new-minister-co.summary: Hamani Kargné took office as Niger's Minister of Communication and New Information Technologies at a handover ceremony on 22 September 2026, succeeding Adji Ali Salatou. His stated priorities include digitising public services through a secure government intranet, narrowing the digital divide between rural areas and towns, supporting start-ups and cybersecurity.

2026-09-24-nga-apc-cccis-national-strate.summary: The Association for Progressive Communications reported on 24 September 2026 that Nigeria's National Strategy for Community-Centred Connectivity Initiatives, running to March 2027, is moving into implementation. Regulators estimate more than 100,000 communities may be eligible for support, and an aggregator licensing model is under study. A first community connectivity bootcamp was held in Abuja from 28 September to 2 October.

2026-09-24-nga-data-protection-digital-i.summary: At UNGA81, Nigeria Data Protection Commission head Vincent Olatunji said personal data used in social protection programmes and social registers must follow the safeguards of the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, and called for African datasets built with proper rights protections. Communications minister Bosun Tijani cited the BRIDGE broadband project, which he said is expected to reach more than 20 million Nigerians.

2026-09-24-nga-ngcert-whatsapp-vulnerabi.summary: Nigeria's national CERT issued a critical advisory on two WhatsApp flaws (CVE-2026-23866 and CVE-2026-23863) on iOS, Android and Windows that allow malicious links to run from crafted Instagram Reels messages and attachments to be spoofed. It advised updating the app, including forced updates through mobile device management.

2026-09-24-nga-nuran-wireless-starlink-b.summary: NuRAN Wireless will pilot Starlink low-Earth-orbit satellite backhaul at a rural site in Nigeria with its partner Infratel, its first LEO integration, to test capacity, 4G migration and site costs. The satellite service is bought through third-party providers; NuRAN has no direct contract with Starlink or SpaceX.

2026-09-24-nga-von-ndpc-olatunji-africa-.summary: In a keynote at a Vivacity Development event on the sidelines of UNGA81, Nigeria Data Protection Commission head Vincent Olatunji named regulatory alignment, data sovereignty and trust as the three foundations of Africa's digital economy. He argued for compatible data-protection rules across African jurisdictions and described data governance as economic infrastructure.

2026-09-24-nigeria-ufarmx-agri-credit-da.summary: A TechCabal feature profiles UfarmX, founded by Alexander Zanders in Oyo State, which turns farm data into credit ratings used by commercial banks and retailers rather than lending itself. The company says it has facilitated more than US$6.8 million in trade across over 10,000 farmers in Nigeria, Senegal and Liberia.

2026-09-24-rwa-newtimes-jordan-digital-t.summary: Rwanda's ICT minister, Paula Ingabire, and Jordan's digital economy minister, Sami Smeirat, signed a memorandum of understanding on digital transformation on 23 September 2026 at the UN General Assembly in New York. It covers sharing experience on digital public services, including Jordan's government Super App, and reciprocal visits. No sum or timetable is given.

2026-09-24-sen-beninwebtv-daf-cyberattac.summary: The director of Senegal's file-automation department (DAF), Ibrahima Dieng, confirmed that the February 2026 incident which halted national identity-card production was a cyberattack, but said the identity-card and electoral files were intact and no personal data was compromised. The Interior Ministry had earlier called it only an incident; a group's claim to have taken 139 terabytes of biometric and immigration data remains unverified.

2026-09-24-sen-digital-ministry-sonatel-.summary: After a week-long workshop, Senegal's digital ministry and Sonatel set out a package of initiatives for Sonatel's contribution to the New Deal Technologique, covering infrastructure, e-government, the digital economy and services for citizens and businesses. Minister Samba Diouf asked other operators, banks, fintechs and startups to bring forward contributions of their own, with timelines and monitoring.

2026-09-24-sen-etat-civil-77-de-centres-.summary: Senegal's civil registration agency, ANEC, has digitised 483 of the 629 civil registry centres it targets outside Dakar, 77 per cent, its director general Matar Ndao said, and aims for all of them by 31 December 2026 with its management software and the SAMA État civil platform. He said a complete national civil register and common tools across communes, some of which run other software, were still needed.

2026-09-24-sen-guindima-pins-interoperab.summary: Senegal's Ministry of Telecommunications and Digital Economy invited firms on 24 September 2026 to bid for a study of infrastructure needs for the national interoperability platform PINS, based on X-Road, under the World Bank-financed PAENS project. The consultant is to design an architecture that starts small and grows across national and sectoral data centres, integrated with the national PKI. Bids closed on 7 October.

2026-09-24-sen-seneweb-biometric-id-card.summary: Senegal's Interior Ministry has begun a legislative process to extend the validity of the first ECOWAS biometric identity cards, issued in 2016 and nearing expiry, the head of the file automation directorate, Ibrahima Dieng, said on 24 September 2026. The text has been in committee at the National Assembly. The length of the extension and the cards covered are not yet set, and normal renewal remains open.

2026-09-24-swz-independentnews-ers-e-inv.summary: The Eswatini Revenue Service said at the opening of the 2026 filing season, reported on 24 September, that three technology providers, one a young local entrepreneur, are being integrated into its TaxCore e-invoicing system. Businesses' accounting and point-of-sale systems will have to connect to TaxCore to strengthen VAT collection. No start date is given.

2026-09-24-swz-positivenews-change-readi.summary: About 40 change agents from five ministries and parastatals held a change-readiness workshop in Mbabane on 24 September, assessing their own directorates ahead of implementation of the World Bank-financed Digital Eswatini Project (US$65 million, about E1.06 billion). They are to help public servants adjust to the new digital systems.

2026-09-24-swz-times-national-data-centr.summary: Eswatini's Royal Science and Technology Park confirmed that an incident at the National Data Centre disrupted at least 12 government digital services, including e-Visa, company registration, the government website and the financial management system. It did not confirm social-media claims of a hack or ransom demand, and said outside experts were helping restore services.

2026-09-24-tcd-wearetech-ndjamena-civil-.summary: English-language report of the same N'Djamena civil-registry digitisation launch and ANATS memorandum of 23 September. It adds that an earlier OIF-backed project regularised the civil status of 53,000 children in Tandjile and Ennedi Est in 2024 and 2025.

2026-09-24-tchad-ndjamena-numerisation-e.summary: N'Djamena's municipality launched a project on 23 September, backed by the Organisation internationale de la Francophonie, to digitise and secure its civil registers, and signed a memorandum with the secure-documents agency ANATS to link municipal records to the national identification system. ANATS counted more than 623,000 school-age children without a birth certificate in 2023.

2026-09-24-uga-airtel-starlink-satellite.summary: Airtel Uganda launched Starlink satellite-to-mobile service, giving compatible smartphones SMS and light data such as WhatsApp outside terrestrial coverage, free for a 30-day trial and then through data bundles. Uganda is Airtel Africa's second commercial market for the service after the DRC in August.

2026-09-24-uga-sunbird-ai-launches-sunfl.summary: Ugandan non-profit Sunbird AI released Sunflower v2 on 24 September 2026, widening its open models from 31 Ugandan languages to 67 African languages. The suite has five models: 27B and 9B language models built on Qwen, a compact Gemma-based model for phones, speech recognition covering 51 languages and text-to-speech covering 20. All models and their datasets are published openly on Hugging Face, with Sunbird claiming its speech recognition beats leading closed systems on most languages tested.

2026-09-24-undp-africa-ai-crossroads-blo.summary: A UNDP Africa blog argues that AI adoption is a set of development choices about institutions, markets and rights, drawing on 26 AI Landscape Assessments completed between 2024 and 2026. It finds that readiness does not end when implementation starts, and links the work to the African Union's Continental AI Strategy.

2026-09-24-xaf-gmb-cioafrica-africa-plac.summary: At the African AI Governance Summit convened by Lawyers Hub in New York on 22 September, Gambian ambassador Muhammadou Kah urged Africa to co-design its technology and own its data rather than import both. He set out five markers: negotiate as one bloc, finance its own digital rails, co-author global AI rules, write rules with entrepreneurs and turn presence into influence.

2026-09-24-xaf-rockefeller-mission-300-e.summary: The Rockefeller Foundation's Mission 300 Accelerator announced the Emergent Grid Project on 24 September 2026, testing whether AI computing placed at African mini-grids can act as an anchor customer and improve their finances. The first sites are five in Kenya, a solar plant in DR Congo and three in Sierra Leone, serving about 85,000 people, with local electricity demand given priority over computing. No amount is stated.

2026-09-24-xea-maegovbi-eac-payment-syst.summary: A ten-member East African Legislative Assembly delegation led by Saïd Kibeya held an oversight session in Bujumbura on 22 September 2026 on integrating East African Community payment and settlement systems. Burundi's EAC programme director general backed the regional Payment and Settlement Systems Initiative and named harmonised laws, supervision, cybersecurity and technical capacity as conditions for success.

2026-09-24-xgl-mofcom-china-us-first-ai-.summary: China's commerce ministry said the eighth round of China-US trade consultations in New York included the first dialogue on artificial intelligence under the consultation mechanism, between Vice Premier He Lifeng and US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. No outcome on AI was stated beyond continued communication.

2026-09-24-zaf-microsoft-digital-soverei.summary: At a GovTech breakfast for senior officials, Microsoft South Africa set out six dimensions of digital sovereignty: data, control, operational, AI, resilience and assurance. It presented sovereignty as a range of controls set by workload and regulatory risk rather than a yes-or-no choice, and pointed to its two Azure regions in South Africa.

2026-09-24-zwe-google-ai-digital-economy.summary: ICT minister Tatenda Mavetera said President Mnangagwa met Google senior vice president James Manyika on the sidelines of UNGA81 to deepen engagement on AI, digital skills, research and home-grown innovation. No agreement, funding or programme was announced.

2026-09-24-zwe-zse-invoicex-invoice-disc.summary: The Zimbabwe Stock Exchange opened InvoiceX, a regulated invoice-discounting market run under the Zimbabwe Entrepreneurship Exchange, for invoices of US$1,000 to US$1.5 million. Once a buyer authenticates an invoice, licensed banks and microfinance lenders bid on the discount rate, with supplier payment targeted within 48 hours and platform fees of 0.65% of the transaction.

2026-09-25-africa-web3-funding-lisk-exit.summary: Lisk, the Swiss Web3 company, is to shut its blockchain on 31 October and move its remaining products and developers to Celo, removing one of the few ecosystems still funding early-stage African Web3 founders, often with grants of about $4,000 in its own token. African blockchain companies raised $90.1 million across 28 deals in 2025, down 26.6% on the year before, according to Crypto Valley VC.

2026-09-25-ago-uae-space-cooperation-loi.summary: Angola's space programme office GGPEN and the UAE Space Agency signed a letter of intent on cooperation in the peaceful uses of outer space, covering space sciences, technologies and applications. It was signed in Abidjan on 25 September at the Africa Space Expo, where Angola is guest country of honour.

2026-09-25-ap-zwe-us-health-funding-ends.summary: The US Embassy in Harare said on 25 September 2026 that US funding for Zimbabwe's health programmes ends at the end of September, after Zimbabwe declined a bilateral health memorandum. Zimbabwe objected in part to a requirement to share sensitive health data, including virus samples. Ambassador Pamela Tremont said relations would shift to trade and investment.

2026-09-25-bct-tun-circulaire-2026-10-et.summary: Tunisia's central bank issued Circular 2026-10 on payment institutions on 25 September 2026, replacing Circular 2018-16 with effect three months after publication. It sets three tiers of client payment accounts, allows remote account opening with reliable identity checks, caps cash transfers at 3,000 dinars per operation and requires an annual IT security audit by a firm certified by the national cybersecurity agency.

2026-09-25-ben-gouv-semo2-digitalisation.summary: Benin's finance ministry made electronic payment of official mission expenses mandatory across public administrations by a circular of 25 September 2026. This is the second phase, SEMO 2, of the mission-management platform run by the national control directorate, whose first phase was used to detect overlapping missions and fictitious staff. Geolocated proof of mission is to follow.

2026-09-25-burkina-faso-safa-airport-dig.summary: Burkina Faso's state airports company SAFA signed a memorandum with ACI Africa and Germany's Barthauer Software to pilot the SACOS airport certification and operations platform. The pilot covers runway inspections, certification, document management and safety tracking, before any wider roll-out.

2026-09-25-china-eximbank-cmr-2026-enhen.summary: Cameroon's higher education minister, Jacques Fame Ndongo, and a China Exim Bank delegation led by Wang Chunying reviewed the E-National Higher Education Network project in Yaoundé on 24 September 2026. The ministry listed its outputs as 500,000 computers for students, ten university digital centres, campus interconnection and e-learning and administrative applications. No usage figures or new financing were given.

2026-09-25-civ-space-digital-transformat.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's digital minister Djibril Ouattara told the Africa Space Expo in Abidjan on 24 September that satellite infrastructure should complement terrestrial networks to extend coverage, which he put at 95% nationally, towards a 100% target. A radiocommunications forum alongside the expo is addressing the integration of terrestrial and satellite networks.

2026-09-25-cmr-nigerian-fintech-grey-ope.summary: Nigerian fintech Grey opened a corridor sending CFA francs from dollar, euro or sterling balances straight to MTN Mobile Money and Orange Money wallets in Cameroon, at $1.80 a transfer. BEAC figures put Cameroon at 30.99 million of CEMAC's 51.28 million mobile money accounts in 2024.

2026-09-25-dfc-wiocc-signing-ceremony-un.summary: The US International Development Finance Corporation held a signing ceremony in New York during the UN General Assembly for its board-approved equity investment in WIOCC, the African digital infrastructure group. Executives from WIOCC, Vision and the Africa Finance Corporation attended. The release gives no amount.

2026-09-25-egy-ai-council-national-ai-st.summary: Egypt's National Council for AI adopted the first-half 2026 progress report on the National AI Strategy 2025-2030 and reviewed the outline of a National Quantum Computing Strategy 2027-2030. It also discussed guidelines on government AI procurement, generative AI in government and the safe use of AI applications by children.

2026-09-25-egy-techafrica-fra-consumer-f.summary: Egypt's Financial Regulatory Authority ordered licensed consumer-finance companies to link their databases to its own and report each customer's data on approval and their purchases of goods and services in real time. Decision No. 2684 of 2026 was announced on 24 September by FRA chairman Islam Azzam; detailed controls are due within six months.

2026-09-25-gab-agp-cemac-sie-reglement-v.summary: Energy ministers of the Central African Economic and Monetary Community (CEMAC), meeting in Libreville on 25 September 2026, validated a regulation creating a community energy information system, SIE-CEMAC, and adopted a roadmap for it. The regulation sets rules for collecting, processing, sharing and archiving energy data. Both texts go to the UEAC Council of Ministers for adoption.

2026-09-25-gab-agp-mouila-seminaire-digi.summary: Gabon's education ministry, with UNICEF and Airtel Gabon, opened a two-day training in Mouila on 25 September 2026 for primary teachers and head teachers in Ngounié province on the Learning Passport platform. Programme coordinator Fabrice Mabika said the pilot has grown from nine schools to 69 and is entering a scale-up phase, and that more than 120 schools are connected by satellite through Airtel Gabon.

2026-09-25-gab-gabonreview-archives-parl.summary: Gabon's National Assembly closed a two-day seminar on 24 September on managing, preserving and digitising parliamentary archives, held with the French Parliament under a parliamentary cooperation programme. It trained archive, IT and records staff and aimed to lay the basis of a document policy suited to digital transformation.

2026-09-25-gab-gabonreview-donnees-energ.summary: CEMAC energy ministers met in Libreville on a draft regulation creating a community energy information system (SIE-CEMAC), setting rules for collecting, processing, keeping and sharing energy data. Gabon's energy minister asked the African Energy Commission for technical and financial support and said the sharing of some energy data must be limited because it falls under national sovereignty.

2026-09-25-gab-sonapresse-drones-satelli.summary: At the first Gabon Drone Expo, Drone Hub's director-general Nicolas Adias said Gabon loses about €15 million a year to illegal logging and that near-permanent cloud cover limits optical satellite monitoring of forests and coastal waters. He presented drones, already used by the space observation agency AGEOS, as a way to fly under the clouds and give near real-time information.

2026-09-25-gha-myjoyonline-gcif-ai-phish.summary: The Ghana Cybersecurity Industry Forum, the industry body provided for under the Cybersecurity Act, 2020, warned at an Accra news conference that criminals are using AI to make phishing messages convincing. It named a skills shortage as its main challenge and set out student engagement, a virtual assets workshop and community roadshows for October to December 2026.

2026-09-25-gha-myjoyonline-prempeh-ai-el.summary: Opening the Third Electoral Integrity Summit in Accra, CDD-Ghana's executive director Henry Kwasi Prempeh called on African states to strengthen safeguards against AI-driven disinformation, deepfakes and coordinated manipulation of elections. He said the question is not whether to use these technologies but under what safeguards and who is accountable when they cause harm.

2026-09-25-gmb-information-commission-cs.summary: The Gambia's Information Commission and the UN system opened a three-day workshop on 23 September training civil society organisations on the Access to Information Act and the Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act, both of which the Commission implements.

2026-09-25-gnq-ahoraeg-inege-anuario-est.summary: Equatorial Guinea's statistics institute INEGE presented the ninth edition of the national Statistical Yearbook in Malabo, covering the last five years. It named stronger administrative registers, digitised processes and interoperable information systems as outstanding challenges, and announced a fifth population and housing census and a first agricultural census, with no dates.

2026-09-25-ken-citizendigital-ai-confere.summary: At the Africa AI Stakeholder Meeting in Nairobi, Kenya's deputy data commissioner John Walubengo said an agreement with the Central Bank of Kenya requires digital lenders to hold a data-protection compliance certificate before being licensed. A Schneider Electric speaker said Kenya has 0.6% of global data-centre capacity, with local facilities about 37% utilised.

2026-09-25-ken-kictanet-herspace-tfgbv-i.summary: The Kenya ICT Action Network launched HerSpace Kenya, a two-year programme backed by Co-Impact against technology-facilitated gender-based violence. It will train police, prosecutors and judges to handle digital evidence, train women on reporting, and engage platforms on content moderation. A 2023 KICTANet study found 54% of women respondents had experienced such violence.

2026-09-25-lbr-fpa-dara-digital-advocacy.summary: Ten Liberian civil society organisations, including CENTAL and the Liberia Equality Network, signed a memorandum establishing the Digital Advocacy and Rights Alliance (DARA). The coalition is to work on digital rights, privacy, online safety and digital freedoms.

2026-09-25-lbr-fpa-dopoh-cybercrime-enfo.summary: Senator Francis Dopoh, who chairs the Senate telecoms committee, defended the Cybercrime Act approved by President Boakai on 3 July 2026 as aimed at fraud, harassment and child exploitation rather than free speech. He called on the executive to designate critical national information infrastructure, set up a national cybersecurity centre and a 24/7 emergency response team, publish the Act's regulations within its six-to-twelve-month timeline and fund its implementation.

2026-09-25-lbr-fpa-wrato-detention-heari.summary: A Monrovia criminal court gave the police a last opportunity to justify holding Jerry Nyantee Wrato, a suspect under the Cybercrime Act, after no officer appeared for the second time. The judge found the state had not shown the case was lawfully before the court and postponed the habeas corpus hearing to 25 September.

2026-09-25-nam-nampa-labour-market-info-.summary: The Namibia Statistics Agency and the Ministry of Justice and Labour Relations launched the country's first National Labour Market Information System on 24 September 2026, to bring labour data from government institutions and the private sector onto one platform.

2026-09-25-nam-neweralive-ncrst-ai-insti.summary: Namibia's National Commission on Research, Science and Technology launched the National Artificial Intelligence Institute in Windhoek, with centres for research, software, datasets and AI innovation. The commission said 2,000 students have received AI training and it has funded two GPU-enabled high-performance computing centres at the Namibia University of Science and Technology and the University of Namibia. No cost is given.

2026-09-25-nam-neweralive-theofelus-ai-d.summary: Namibia's ICT minister, Emma Theofelus, said at the launch of the National AI Institute in Windhoek on 23 September 2026 that 4G covers about 89% of the country and internet use is about 62%. She said construction of the National Data Centre at Kenya House has begun. No measurement date for the coverage figures is given.

2026-09-25-nga-punchng-fg-fibre-1-2bn-pr.summary: Nigeria's federal government is seeking about US$1.2bn in private capital for its planned 90,000km national fibre network, with physical rollout due from October 2026. Of the estimated US$2bn cost, US$800m is covered by World Bank, African Development Bank and EBRD loans, and a newly incorporated company is to carry out the project.

2026-09-25-nga-thisdaylive-inec-ai-elect.summary: Nigeria's electoral commission INEC said it has begun using AI tools in its results-management process to flag discrepancies and errors in result records before final validation, with every automated check subject to human audit. Chairman Joash Amupitan said INEC has set up an AI Division and adopted an AI roadmap and governance framework ahead of the January and February 2027 elections.

2026-09-25-nga-thisdaylive-ondo-ai-civil.summary: Ondo State launched Ondo AI, a platform built by SmartApps IT Limited that automates civil-service personnel records, payroll, retirement processing and pension migration. It flags workers nearing retirement and gives staff self-service payslips.

2026-09-25-nga-thisdaylive-stakeholders-.summary: Bank and fintech executives at a Lagos forum on 24 September called on the Central Bank of Nigeria to extend and phase its 1 January 2027 deadline for hosting all payment data in Nigeria, calling it virtually impossible to meet. FCMB's technology chief said bank CIOs had been unable for three months to get clarity from the CBN on which data must be kept on-premise.

2026-09-25-nga-vanguard-ai-deepfakes-cyb.summary: The RACE Centre opened a two-day training in Abuja for the Feminist Digital Watch Collective on responding to technology-facilitated gender-based violence, including AI-generated deepfakes and cyberstalking. Its AI-enabled tracker, launched two months earlier, has documented about 24,000 human-verified cases across five social media platforms.

2026-09-25-nga-vanguard-hcpan-connect-he.summary: The Health Care Providers Association of Nigeria launched HCPAN Connect, a platform linking private providers, health maintenance organisations, regulators, government and patients and pooling their data in a central repository, reported on 25 September 2026. Its president, Dr Austin Aipoh, said it will issue health-insurance authorisation codes and support telemedicine, starting in Lagos. The launch date is not stated.

2026-09-25-nigeria-moniepoint-pos-invest.summary: Moniepoint is selling shares in the Dangote Petroleum Refinery's ₦2.15 trillion IPO through its agent point-of-sale terminals across all 774 local government areas. Buyers are identified by their Bank Verification Number and capped at ₦100,000 each, a test of the agent network as a channel for investment products.

2026-09-25-nigeria-remita-banking-app.summary: Remita launched a mobile app at Nigeria Fintech Week on 23 September that brings several bank accounts into one interface. Users can make payments, invest and send money to other African countries.

2026-09-25-rwa-ktpress-nsengiyumva-ai-go.summary: Prime Minister Justin Nsengiyumva told an AI governance discussion at UNGA81 that Rwanda's National AI Agency could host shared testing of advanced AI systems for the region, so African countries can evaluate frontier models themselves. No timetable, funding or partner countries were stated.

2026-09-25-rwa-newtimes-ai-scaling-healt.summary: Rwanda's ICT ministry hosted a session at UNGA81 on deploying AI at scale in health, agriculture, education and public services, presenting the country as a proof of concept for Africa, with partners including the Gates Foundation, Google, Zipline, Anthropic and UNICEF. The discussion covered the national AI agency, the national data hub and Kinyarwanda-language AI; no new commitment was reported.

2026-09-25-rwanda-jordan-digital-coopera.summary: Rwanda and Jordan signed a memorandum of understanding on ICT cooperation on the sidelines of UNGA81 on 24 September, between Rwanda's ICT minister Paula Ingabire and Jordan's digital economy minister Sami Smeirat. It covers sharing experience in digital public services, digital identity and AI and identifying joint projects.

2026-09-25-sajim-ai-delivery-acceptance-.summary: A systematic review of 42 studies on consumer acceptance of AI-driven delivery systems in sub-Saharan Africa, with implications for South Africa, finds perceived usefulness and ease of use studied together most often, in 57% of studies. Infrastructure access and digital literacy were examined together in a third of them, and institutional and policy support least often.

2026-09-25-sdn-soudan-un-assistant-autom.summary: Sudan's Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research launched a chatbot on its online admissions portal, reported on 25 September 2026. It answers general admission questions in Arabic and refers complex or personal-data requests to a human support centre reachable on the number 2511, as part of the 2026-2027 registration campaign.

2026-09-25-sen-lesoleil-kaolack-digital-.summary: The Forum Civil held a two-day regional workshop in Kaolack for civil society and community leaders on digital issues, under an EU-funded project, Recentrer le civisme numérique. It aims to equip young people and community leaders to understand and use digital tools.

2026-09-25-sle-dpg-registry-four-teams.summary: Four Sierra Leonean teams met all nine Digital Public Goods criteria and submitted their products to the global registry, it was announced at a UNICEF event at UNGA81, with three more teams meeting six or seven criteria. The Christex Foundation, which prepared them over six to seven months, used its own AI-assisted assessment tool, Pipeline.

2026-09-25-sle-dpi-country-ownership-ung.summary: Communications minister Salima Monorma Bah told an AU-UNDP ministerial panel at UNGA81 that Sierra Leone's foundational digital identity covers more than 90% of the population, a national payment switch is scaling rapidly and a data exchange layer is being piloted in the financial sector. She presented the ECOWAS Data Embassy Framework as a way to pool digital infrastructure regionally rather than every country building the full stack alone.

2026-09-25-sle-open-source-policy-unveil.summary: Sierra Leone's communications ministry presented a new open source policy at a UNICEF event on the sidelines of UNGA81, as its answer to duplicated government systems, rising proprietary costs, systems that cannot interoperate and vendor lock-in. The policy's text, adoption date and instrument were not given.

2026-09-25-som-sokodirectory-hormuud-get.summary: Hormuud Telecom and GetPhone said their smartphone financing programme in Somalia has sold more than 2,500 phones since its launch in May 2026 and is expanding through 15 more branches in Jubaland, South West, Hirshabelle and Galmudug. In nearly 1,700 contracts signed in August, borrowers with credit scores under 500 had repaid 89.7% of amounts due, against 90.5% for those scoring 650 or above.

2026-09-25-tcd-ministere-femme-whatsapp-.summary: Chad's Ministry of Women and Early Childhood banned the sending of official documents over WhatsApp, Messenger and other mobile apps, in a circular signed by Minister of State Kitoko Gata Ngoulol and reported on 25 September 2026. It found that officials, including senior staff, routinely shared correspondence and decisions this way; breaches are now disciplinary faults. The circular's date is not given.

2026-09-25-techreviewafrica-smart-africa.summary: Smart Africa's chief executive Lacina Koné told a GSMA and Partnership for Digital Access in Africa summit on the sidelines of UNGA81 that affordability should be treated as an economic and fiscal policy priority, not only a telecoms matter. The roundtable addressed the goal of bringing one billion Africans into meaningful digital participation by 2030.

2026-09-25-tgo-arcep-aaoo-004-2026-carto.summary: The regulator opened a tender on 25 September 2026 for a map of fibre-to-the-home networks, as a single lot estimated at FCFA 250 million. Delivery is due within 240 days of notification, the bid bond is FCFA 7.5 million and bids open on 30 October 2026. The 141-page dossier relaunches an earlier call.

2026-09-25-tgo-togofirst-togo-mali-data-.summary: Togo's personal data protection authority (IPDCP) and Mali's APDP signed a cooperation agreement on 23 September covering information exchange, joint handling of complaints and compliance checks, and staff training. Their talks also touched on cross-border data transfers, cybersecurity and AI.

2026-09-25-thecitizen-tza-tcra-communica.summary: Tanzania's regulator TCRA reported that mobile-network fraud reports fell 69% between September 2023 and June 2026, from 23,328 to 7,334 cases. Mobile money accounts rose from 32.7 million in March 2021 to 87.0 million in June 2026, and only 15.4% of the country's 17,690 Gbps of international capacity was in use.

2026-09-25-tun-chatel-digital-transforma.summary: A 2026 study of Tunisia's digital transformation and AI sets recent infrastructure gains, including the Medusa submarine cable landing at Bizerte in November 2025, the first national supercomputer entering trials in July 2026 and a national AI strategy for 2026-2030 presented in August, against continuing emigration of engineers. It cites more than 7,000 engineers leaving in 2025 and an expected 8,000 in 2026, and asks how the country can turn that talent into value created at home.

2026-09-25-tun-chourouk-tabelette-inspec.summary: Tunisia's labour-inspection director-general Noureddine Triki said the inspection platform is to exchange data with the national social security fund and the national business register by the end of 2026, and with other ministries' systems from January 2027. Inspectors are to move to tablets that record findings and geolocate establishments, with three regional workshops to train most of them.

2026-09-25-tun-telehealth-connect-2026-p.summary: Tunisia is hosting Telehealth Connect 2026 in Tunis from 29 September to 1 October, with more than 500 participants from 30 countries expected. The health ministry reports teleradiology in 30 facilities, 99 facilities implementing electronic medical records and 800,000 active registrations for the national health identifier. It is preparing Sahetna, a platform for patients to view appointments and health records.

2026-09-25-tza-cash-still-king-public-tr.summary: Of 62.18 million passengers recorded through online ticketing in Tanzania's public transport over four years, 95.3 per cent paid cash and 4.7 per cent paid digitally, the Land Transport Regulatory Authority's director general Habibu Suluo said. Electronic payments made up TSh144.28 billion of TSh2.13 trillion collected, or 6.8 per cent, although the law requires electronic payment for several services.

2026-09-25-tza-nest-digital-procurement-.summary: Tanzania's National e-Procurement System (NeST), launched by the Public Procurement Regulatory Authority in 2023, has cut procurement processing time from 234 to 79 days and links 21 government systems, according to World Bank figures reported on 25 September 2026. Savings on printing and transport are put at US$12.5m over two years. The World Bank is providing US$15m over four years for the wider reform.

2026-09-25-tza-samia-scholarship-ds-ai-n.summary: Tanzania's deputy education minister Wanu Hafidh Ameir met the 50 beneficiaries of the Samia Scholarship Extended DS/AI+ programme on 23 September 2026 at the Nelson Mandela African Institution of Science and Technology in Arusha. They are in a 10-month training camp in data science and artificial intelligence.

2026-09-25-tza-tix-100g-core-upgrade.summary: The Tanzania Internet eXchange in Dar es Salaam upgraded its core switching to 100G, the ISP association TISPA said on 23 September. On the exchange's own statistics its 66 connected networks averaged about 205 Gbps in late September 2026, up from about 110 Gbps a year earlier.

2026-09-25-uemoa-fapbef-ai-forum-dakarac.summary: The federation of UEMOA banking associations (FAPBEF) held a sub-regional forum in Dakar on AI for financial inclusion and banking, with the BCEAO's national director for Senegal present. Its president, Guy Awona, called for a federated and controlled approach to AI across the Union's banks rather than treating it as a purely technological matter.

2026-09-25-uga-mtn-mobile-money-toll-pay.summary: MTN Uganda and the Ministry of Works and Transport launched Mobile Money toll payment on the Kampala-Entebbe Expressway, at the Busega, Kajjansi and Mpala plazas on designated lanes. The motorist gives a phone number to the attendant and approves a PIN prompt; no fee was named.

2026-09-25-uga-ucc-ai-content-moderation.summary: Uganda's ICT minister, Justine Kasule Lumumba, said the Uganda Communications Commission is procuring an AI system to identify and filter sexually explicit and other harmful content before it is distributed online, and that it must understand local languages. The system, its cost, supplier and deployment date are not given.

2026-09-25-who-afro-gates-foundation-xaf.summary: The WHO Regional Office for Africa launched DIGIT-HCM, a three-year initiative to digitise the planning, delivery and monitoring of health campaigns such as vaccination drives, built with the eGov Foundation and supported by the Gates Foundation. The first phase covers seven pilot countries; a pilot ran in a district of N'Djamena Province during Chad's June 2026 polio campaign. No funding figure is given.

2026-09-25-world-bank-nga-2026-project-b.summary: Nigeria's communications minister Bosun Tijani said in New York on 22 September 2026 that Project BRIDGE, a 90,000 km national fibre build, will be delivered in three years rather than five, with cable laying from the fourth quarter of 2026 and completion by 2028 or early 2029. Development lenders have committed $845 million, including $500 million from the World Bank; the government will hold at most 49% of the project company.

2026-09-25-zaf-ai-distillation-employee-.summary: An opinion piece asks whether a South African employer that has an employee train an internal AI agent on her work thereby acquires her professional capability. It argues that South African case law, including Automotive Tooling Systems v Wilkens and Nuvest Chemicals v Meyer (January 2026), treats skills and know-how as the employee's own rather than the employer's property.

2026-09-25-zaf-fnb-ai-governance-measura.summary: FNB's AI executive for retail and business banking, Dané Liebenberg, said the bank judges its AI deployments on four measures: sales revenue, process efficiency and cost to serve, fraud losses, and the effect on employees' workload. Its AI tools include the FNB banking app and NAVi, which supports advisers with customer insights.

2026-09-25-zaf-mybroadband-gauteng-e-pan.summary: Gauteng's Department of e-Government said in replies to DA questions, reported on 25 September 2026, that its e-Panic Button contract with Evolve Value Added Services is worth R269 million in total and runs to 10 March 2027. It has paid R131.3 million over three years, and the app gained only 15,000 new downloads between October 2025 and August 2026, out of more than 180,000 overall.

2026-09-25-zaf-paystack-shopify-onsite-c.summary: Paystack introduced an onsite card checkout for Shopify merchants in South Africa, letting shoppers pay by card without leaving the merchant's checkout. It also added a Shopify integration for its in-store Paystack Terminal.

2026-09-25-zmb-integrated-media-reportin.summary: Zambia's Ministry of Information and Media launched an Integrated Media Reporting System, built in-house, to bring its institutions' reporting onto one platform, reported on 25 September 2026. It will track the eight presidential priorities for the Presidential Delivery Unit and El Niño-related matters. No cost or rollout date is given.

2026-09-26-afcfta-digital-trade-rules-70.summary: AfCFTA Secretary-General Wamkele Mene said in New York that Africa's digital economy could exceed US$700 billion by 2035 if common rules on payments, data transfers and digital identity remove barriers between national markets. He pointed to the Protocol on Digital Trade and the eight annexes the African Union adopted in February 2025.

2026-09-26-africa-ai-dependency-opinion-.summary: An opinion piece argues that African governments should adopt a pragmatic sovereign stance on artificial intelligence, using it for development while building their own compute, data governance, procurement and research capacity rather than importing foreign technology stacks and regulatory templates wholesale.

2026-09-26-bfa-lefaso-aes-telecom-regula.summary: The telecoms regulators of Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger signed a convention creating the Conseil des régulateurs du Sahel, reported on 26 September 2026. Its priorities include harmonised regulation, consumer protection, coordinated infrastructure and tariffs, with work on border frequency coordination, free roaming across the three states and coordinated 5G. Statutes are still to be adopted; no signing date is given.

2026-09-26-bmz-egy-2026-itida-giz-ict-in.summary: Egypt's Information Technology Industry Development Agency and GIZ Egypt launched an initiative in which 14 ICT companies, including IBM, Microsoft, DXC and Orange Business, will co-develop a playbook for recruiting and including persons with disabilities. The consultancy Fit For Life will run 15 workshops and sessions. No funding figure is given.

2026-09-26-civ-afriksoir-aspex-satellite.summary: At the Africa Space Expo in Abidjan on 25 September 2026, Côte d'Ivoire's telecoms regulator said three operators already sell satellite internet, two on geostationary satellites and one on a low-orbit constellation. It said it regulates them through a sandbox, periodic market analyses and the same consumer rights as terrestrial service.

2026-09-26-cod-theppppost-fibre-concessi.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo plans to extend its fibre-optic backbone by 11,600 km through four 20-year concessions tendered internationally, with gap financing for routes whose revenues cannot cover the cost, reported on 26 September 2026. Expressions of interest for the supervision consultancy close on 14 October 2026, for work from June 2027.

2026-09-26-com-komor-ia-lance-annotation.summary: Komor-IA launched Annotation Studio, which it describes as the first platform for named-entity and part-of-speech annotation of Shikomori, letting any speaker tag sentences without technical skills. The platform follows the Universal Dependencies standard so the data can be compared with other Bantu languages such as Swahili, and the results will be released under CC BY-NC 4.0 for research and non-commercial use.

2026-09-26-dza-jeune-independant-guessou.summary: An Algerian business-federation head welcomed the presidential decree being drafted on a secure digital interoperability plan, arguing that administrations should verify information directly with each other rather than ask citizens and firms to resupply it. The decree was ordered by the Council of Ministers on 20 September 2026 and has not been published.

2026-09-26-egy-afronews-imc-corporate-st.summary: Egypt's Industrial Modernization Center agreed with a local software firm to move small and medium-sized factories onto locally built ERP and other applications on a monthly subscription, with the centre adding incentives and technical support. No price, number of factories or timetable was given.

2026-09-26-eth-wardheernews-tigray-commu.summary: Internet and phone services were severely disrupted across Ethiopia's Tigray region as fighting resumed between Tigrayan forces and the federal army, reported on 26 September 2026. Ethio Telecom services were fully down and Safaricom partly working, and NetBlocks confirmed the disruption. Residents already short of cash lost access to mobile money. Responsibility for the shutdown is disputed.

2026-09-26-gab-agp-itu-pp26-reunion-prep.summary: Gabon's digital economy minister joined an African Union ministerial consultation in New York on ITU governance, preparing a high-level AU meeting in Libreville on 29 and 30 October 2026 on content regulation, satellite internet providers and infrastructure. Gabon is standing for a seat on the ITU Council, to be elected at the Plenipotentiary Conference in Doha from 9 November.

2026-09-26-gin-hac-onc-niger-digital-reg.summary: Guinea's media regulator, the Haute Autorité de la Communication, and Niger's Observatoire national de la communication met in Conakry on 26 September 2026 under the regional audiovisual regulators' platform PRA-UEMOA-Guinée. In a joint communiqué they agreed to press digital platforms for protocols on algorithm transparency, promote media and digital literacy, and pursue the platform's 2026–2028 roadmap.

2026-09-26-gin-mediaguinee-hac-bans-baro.summary: Guinea's media regulator, the Haute Autorité de la Communication, banned Baro TV, a web television service in Kouroussa prefecture, at an extraordinary session on 24 September 2026. It ruled that the service was broadcasting audiovisual information online illegally and that its promoter, Lamine Camara, does not hold professional journalist status.

2026-09-26-gin-mediaguinee-hac-bans-four.summary: Guinea's media regulator, the Haute Autorité de la Communication, banned four web TV outlets — Fewndaare TV, Global TV, Kimanbourou TV and BTV — with immediate effect at an extraordinary session on 26 September 2026. It said they broadcast audiovisual content online without any legal authorisation, and that web TV on digital platforms requires one.

2026-09-26-ken-capitalfm-unga-kdip-diasp.summary: Kenya signed a 2026-2030 country partnership programme with UNIDO at the UN General Assembly, linked to about US$750 million in investment opportunities in industry, technology transfer and manufacturing. President Ruto also discussed an East African refinery and a regional office of the Africa Finance Corporation in Nairobi.

2026-09-26-lbr-finance-minister-washingt.summary: Liberia's Finance Minister Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan told a diaspora conference in Washington that the Inclusive Instant Payment System, launched by the Central Bank of Liberia in December 2025, processed more than 1.5 million transactions worth over L$1.4 billion and US$9 million in its first three months. It first linked the Lonestar MTN and Orange mobile-money platforms. A national electronic payment switch is the longer-term aim.

2026-09-26-lumiernews-rdc-national-id-ca.summary: A Congolese civic group asked the government and the identification office on 24 September 2026 to account for the funds spent on the national identity card and to publish a delivery timetable, three years after the first card was handed to President Tshisekedi. It says he remains the only Congolese publicly issued one, and asks why mass enrolment has not reached provinces such as Tshopo.

2026-09-26-mwi-nzika-wallet-laxton-biome.summary: A Malawi24 investigation reports that a Hong Kong-registered company won a US$5.09 million World Bank-financed contract in March 2026 to supply 2,400 biometric registration kits to the National Registration Bureau, with remote software support. The procurement authority says remote access reaches the kits only; the bureau, the communications regulator and the supplier did not say who else can reach the identity system.

2026-09-26-sdn-suna-omdurman-bank-sudapa.summary: Omdurman National Bank became the first bank in Sudan to link to the national digital identity SudaPass on 26 September 2026, letting customers inside and outside the country update their data through its digital channels without visiting a branch. The digital transformation ministry and the Central Bank of Sudan are connecting other banks as each becomes technically ready.

2026-09-26-sen-lesoleil-6888-ecoles-inte.summary: Senegal's government plans to connect 6,888 schools to broadband internet, with satellite links for more than 2,000 others, it said at an interministerial council on the 2026–27 school year on 25 September 2026. Under the 2025–2029 education digital strategy, 6,547 tablets have been distributed and 12,385 teachers certified in digital skills and AI. No cost or timetable for the connections is given.

2026-09-26-techtrends-africa-startup-eco.summary: A feature argues that African venture capital is spreading beyond Lagos and Nairobi, citing Startup Genome's 2026 ranking of eleven Sub-Saharan ecosystems from Lagos to Dar es Salaam. It puts first-quarter 2026 startup funding at US$705 million across 59 deals in 14 countries, while Egypt, Nigeria, Kenya and South Africa still take the majority.

2026-09-26-thecitizen-tza-finland-startu.summary: A Tanzanian delegation from the ICT Commission, with officials and startups, spent a week studying Finland's innovation system under the EU-funded Digital for Tanzania twinning project. Its leaders said Tanzania needs reliable data on innovation and AI adoption and more domestic investment in startups.

2026-09-26-tun-rne-rejoint-ebra.summary: Tunisia's national business register, the RNE, became a full member of the European Business Registry Association on 21 September 2026, the first African registry to join. Membership lets it take part in the association's work on digitalisation, information-system interoperability and identifying beneficial owners. The association has 42 members.

2026-09-26-zwe-iecms-gweru-justice-digit.summary: Zimbabwe's Judicial Service Commission is extending its Integrated Electronic Case Management System to magistrates' courts in Midlands and Mashonaland West on 1 October 2026, ahead of Harare and Bulawayo by year-end. The system, begun in 2022, already covers the Constitutional, Supreme and Labour Courts and the High Court; a public awareness event was held in Gweru.

2026-09-27-abagore-barenga-600-000-batan.summary: The National Bank of Rwanda's governor, Soraya Hakuziyaremye, said 615,000 women had been brought into mobile financial services under the Gendana Konti campaign, against a target of 150,000, as the campaign closed. More than 200,000 of them opened mobile money accounts for the first time. Begun in 2023 in Nyaruguru and Nyamasheke districts, the campaign later expanded to other districts.

2026-09-27-africa-cdc-igihe-africa-healt.summary: The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention and Smart Africa are co-hosting the fifth Africa HealthTech Summit in Kigali from 30 September to 2 October 2026, IGIHE reported on 27 September. Africa CDC and Transform Health will hold a consultation on the draft African Continental Health Data Governance Framework on 30 September.

2026-09-27-african-development-bank-lbr-.summary: The African Development Bank published on 27 September 2026 the completion report for DIGIGOV Liberia, part of its project to digitise government payments in the Mano River Union. The project aimed to set up an e-payment system hosted by the Liberia Revenue Authority for customs tax collection, build local digital finance capacity and run consumer-protection work. The summary page gives no results or figures.

2026-09-27-bdi-la-transformation-numeriq.summary: Bienvenu Irakoze, coordinator of Burundi's World Bank-backed PAFEN digital programme, wrote that the project will soon start a basic digital skills programme to train 5,000 civil servants and 10,000 young people within 12 months. He said the project also works with innovation hubs and startups, and set the training alongside its spending on infrastructure and platforms.

2026-09-27-cpv-anacao-helio-varela-ia-so.summary: In an interview, Cabo Verdean specialist Hélio Varela rejects alarm about losing control of artificial intelligence and argues that the real risk is its concentration in a handful of countries and companies. He proposes a pragmatic technological sovereignty for the islands rather than protectionism.

2026-09-27-egy-egyptke-finance-minister-.summary: The head of Egypt's Real Estate Tax Authority, Rami Youssef, acknowledged faults in the property tax registration app and said he had asked the finance minister to extend the registration deadline, which the minister said was under study. About one million citizens had registered with two days left. The authority is working with the app's contractor to fix outages.

2026-09-27-egy-sisi-orange-group-ceo-mee.summary: After Orange Group's chief executive met President El-Sisi, the operator announced training grants for about 200,000 people in artificial intelligence and cybersecurity, EUR 25 million for AI and advanced-technology startups, and technology laboratories for Egyptian universities. The President also sought its help with the second phase of the national digital health project.

2026-09-27-forumlibre-cobac-cemac-esg-ai.summary: The Central African banking supervisor met the region's bank and microfinance chiefs in Malabo on 25 September 2026 to set priorities on climate-related risk, stress testing, cybersecurity and the use of artificial intelligence. A single banking law and a green taxonomy for the CEMAC zone were among the reforms discussed.

2026-09-27-gab-gabonreview-ai-national-s.summary: Gabon's digital economy ministry and the UN Development Programme opened consultations toward a national artificial intelligence strategy, held in Libreville from 28 to 30 September 2026. The announcement sets out the themes but gives no budget, adoption date or priority uses.

2026-09-27-gab-gabonreview-oyem-digital-.summary: Gabon's First Lady visited the former governorate building in Oyem, which is being converted into a centre for coding, robotics, fabrication and entrepreneurship for children, young people and adults. It grows out of a local youth coding programme, and no cost or opening date is given.

2026-09-27-gha-real-time-vat-cross-borde.summary: An explainer by an adviser to the Ghana Revenue Authority describes its Real-Time VAT framework under the VAT Act, 2025, run on the Sentinel system: VAT is taken at the point of payment when a Ghana-issued card, mobile money account or wallet pays a foreign supplier of digital services. Banks and payment providers must integrate; about 167 non-resident e-commerce firms are registered, paying an estimated GH¢515 million a year.

2026-09-27-ken-access-to-information-day.summary: Kenya's Broadcasting and Telecommunications Principal Secretary, Steve Isaboke, said on 24 September 2026 that the government will publish information before citizens have to request it, and that with a newly approved Access to Information Policy the focus now shifts to implementing the 2016 Act. He spoke at a forum hosted by the Finnish embassy with UNESCO and the Commission on Administrative Justice.

2026-09-27-lby-alwasat-national-number-f.summary: Libya's public prosecutor announced another case of civil-status records falsified for money, reviving concern over forged national identity numbers, which the last official tally put above 89,000. The report traces the problem to 2022, when forged numbers were found to have drawn salaries and family grants, and asks how the civil registry's gaps can be closed.

2026-09-27-lso-ppd-forum-lnsw-reforms-st.summary: Lesotho's prime minister, Sam Matekane, told a public-private dialogue forum in May 2026 that nine agreed reforms had not started or were awaiting Cabinet, according to a World Bank-funded project newsletter reported on 27 September. The same newsletter says the National Single Window operates without its own law and the central bank is still building a government e-payment gateway.

2026-09-27-mar-canal212-afdb-insurtech-a.summary: Morocco's insurance supervisor (ACAPS) launched an InsurTech programme with the African Development Bank, a US$680,000 technical assistance package of which the bank gives US$510,000 as a grant and ACAPS US$170,000. Running to early 2027, it begins with a tendered study of regulatory barriers to digital insurance.

2026-09-27-mwi-nzika-digital-id-public-t.summary: An opinion piece asks how Malawi's new Nzika digital identity wallet, launched on 16 September 2026, will protect the biometric data of more than 13.5 million registered people. It notes that reports on a World Bank-financed contract for 2,400 biometric registration kits do not show any data was compromised, and calls for clear rules on access and storage.

2026-09-27-nam-namibian-national-ai-inst.summary: Namibia's ICT minister launched a National Artificial Intelligence Institute in Windhoek, made up of software development, datasets, innovation and research centres. It is to work on skills, local datasets and uses in health, education, food security, energy and public services.

2026-09-27-nga-nigeriaupdates-uk-customs.summary: The Nigeria Customs Service and the UK's HM Revenue and Customs met in Abuja to finalise a Customs Mutual Administrative Assistance Agreement on information sharing and compliance, after about six months of virtual talks, reported on 27 September 2026. Nigerian customs said it hopes the agreement will be signed in the first week of December at the World Customs Organization Policy Commission.

2026-09-27-nga-uk-fcdo-amuvi-community-c.summary: A community connectivity hub sponsored by the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office and run by the Initiative for Digital Inclusion was commissioned at Amuvi, Arochukwu, in Nigeria's Abia State. It offers free internet access and free eight-week training for 100 people in digital marketing, online management and personal digital security. No cost or commissioning date is given.

2026-09-27-rwa-newtimes-bk-cips-trader-r.summary: Rwandan importers who buy from China, the country's largest source of imports, expect Bank of Kigali's direct membership of China's yuan payment system to cut the cost of converting francs into dollars and then into yuan. An economist cautions that the gain depends on the bank's rates and fees, and that trade with China will not stop using the dollar.

2026-09-27-sdn-sudanhorizon-mof-mtn-suda.summary: Sudan's Ministry of Finance signed an agreement with MTN Sudan to provide SMS services for Eesaly, the state electronic collection and payment system, the ministry said on 27 September 2026. Citizens with MTN SIM cards will be able to use Eesaly services and track their transactions by text message. No cost or start date is given.

2026-09-27-sen-seneweb-ia-souverainete-c.summary: A Senegalese professor argues that Africa's future in artificial intelligence depends on turning its young population into producers rather than consumers of technology. He calls for investment in science and mathematics education, research and computing capacity as the basis of what he terms cognitive and algorithmic sovereignty.

2026-09-27-sen-seneweb-pi-spi-gratuite-p.summary: The West African central bank's instant payment platform, live since September 2025, makes transfers between people and payments to merchants free to the customer across banks and wallets. The report looks at how that undercuts mobile money operators' fee income and network advantage as the deadline for institutions to connect approaches.

2026-09-27-techcabal-kenya-payments-revo.summary: A commentary argues that Kenya's success with mobile money has left the rest of its payments system neglected, citing central bank figures of 94.35 million registered accounts and KES 728.7 billion moved in July 2026. It calls for attention to bank rails, cards and cross-border payments beyond the dominant wallet.

2026-09-27-tgo-togofirst-arcep-mobile-qu.summary: Togo's telecoms regulator found neither mobile operator meeting its quality-of-service standards in a national campaign across 86 locations from July to August 2026, with YAS at about 75% compliance and Moov Africa Togo at about 54%. It is drafting rules that would require 95% compliance nationwide, backed by penalties.

2026-09-27-uga-dailystar-whistleblowers-.summary: Whistleblowers asked President Museveni, the Inspectorate of Government, the Auditor General and the procurement regulator to halt a proposed Shs158 billion Ministry of Works and Transport purchase of vehicle registration components from Global Security, the contractor for Uganda's digital number plates. They say it pays twice for functions already covered and gives one foreign vendor the registry and its data. The paper says the claims were not independently established.

2026-09-27-xaf-cipesa-fifafrica26-agenda.summary: The 2026 Forum on Internet Freedom in Africa, hosted in Mauritius by CIPESA with a local partner, has published its agenda: 18 pre-events and 41 sessions across eight themes, chosen from more than 450 proposals. The themes run from data governance and AI to platform accountability and digital security.

2026-09-27-zaf-smart-id-bank-partnership.summary: South Africa's Home Affairs smart ID service is available at more than 500 bank branches: Capitec 247, Standard Bank 144, FNB 96 and Absa 15. Minister Leon Schreiber has said it will reach 750 branches, add first-time ID and passport applications and offer home delivery by the end of 2026. A deputy director-general said the green ID book will be phased out within two years; no invalidation date is set.

2026-09-27-zwe-ai-traffic-camera-enforce.summary: Harare's AI-powered traffic cameras had recorded more than four million violations by the end of September 2026, up from 2.3 million in mid-August, and Zimbabwe's police have begun calling offenders in to pay fines after verification, reported on 27 September.
