2026-10-08-gmb-thepoint-gppa-procurement.summary: The Gambia Public Procurement Authority held training from 8 to 10 October 2026 for procurement officers on the Public Procurement Act 2022, the 2024 Regulations, new standard documents and the rollout of the electronic government procurement system. Officials said use of the new instruments becomes mandatory from January 2027.

2026-10-08-gnq-ahoraeg-getesa-huawei-red.summary: Equatorial Guinea's Vice-President Teodoro Nguema Obiang Mangue told the finance ministry on 7 October 2026 to investigate and urgently release financing for state operator GETESA's network expansion agreement with Huawei, which Treasury payment arrears have slowed. GETESA will cancel non-essential maintenance contracts until December, saving over 262 million CFA francs a month for reinvestment in the network.

2026-10-08-gnq-ahoraeg-ley-libertad-de-p.summary: An Equatorial Guinea Senate committee approved by consensus its report on a new Press Freedom and Journalism Bill and sent it to the full Senate. The bill gives digital and audiovisual journalists the same protections and duties, sets a right of access to public information with deadlines and appeals, separates editorial oversight from spectrum management by ORTEL and creates a college of journalists.

2026-10-08-ken-gpsdd-idc-action-plan-202.summary: Kenya drafted its second Inclusive Data Charter action plan, for 2026 to 2030, at a workshop on 5 to 7 October. It widens the first plan's focus on disability to gender, children and older persons.

2026-10-08-ken-nation-iebc-id-data-voter.summary: Kenya's electoral commission IEBC is moving its voter registration targets from census estimates of the voting-age population to National Registration Bureau and immigration data on issued ID cards and passports, according to a parliamentary committee report adopted by the National Assembly. Its target of 6.3 million new voters for 2027 was set under the old census model.

2026-10-08-ken-the-star-spacex-fcc-15000.summary: US regulatory approval for up to 15,000 SpaceX direct-to-device satellites could expose Kenyan mobile operators to competition from space, this analysis argues. Safaricom's mobile data revenue passed voice for the first time in the year to March 2026.

2026-10-08-latimes-u-s-zambia-sign-2-49-.summary: Zambia and the United States signed their five-year health financing memorandum in Lusaka after clauses on specimen sharing and patient data were removed. The State Department put it at US$2.49 billion, US$1.52 billion from the United States and US$975 million from Zambia, and Zambia said minerals were not part of it.

2026-10-08-lbr-police-online-clearance-u.summary: Liberia's online police clearance system has generated more than US$200,000 since May 2026, the deputy information minister said. No figure for the manual system it replaced was given.

2026-10-08-lby-2026-companion.summary: The Central Bank of Libya's statement of state revenue and spending for January to September 2026, issued on 8 October, puts revenue at LYD 114.5bn, mostly from oil, and spending at LYD 88.6bn, of which LYD 1.6bn was development spending. Telecommunications brought in LYD 31.1m, and the General Authority for Communications spent about LYD 31.7m. It also lists electronic payment indicators.

2026-10-08-lby-lana-audit-bureau-athar-p.summary: Libya's Audit Bureau presented its Athar platform for managing and following up audit tasks to more than 140 audited bodies at a seminar in Tripoli on 7 October 2026. Bureau head Khaled Shakshak said it is the digital channel for communication and information exchange between the Bureau and the bodies it audits.

2026-10-08-lby-lana-us-strategic-coopera.summary: Libya's communications authority and the US State Department signed a cooperation framework in Washington covering digital infrastructure, AI, data centres, cybersecurity and satellite communications. No programme or amount was published.

2026-10-08-lexpress-mg-transparence-budg.summary: Madagascar's economy and finance ministry plans to publish more budget information and widen citizen participation after an International Budget Partnership assessment of 2024-2025 scored the country below 61 out of 100. The Court of Audit says it will resume publishing the budget settlement law document in 2027, interrupted since 2020. The exact score is not given.

2026-10-08-m-kopa-reaches-10-million-cus.summary: M-KOPA reported revenue of US$600 million for its 2025 financial year, up 45%, and ten million customers since 2011 across Kenya, Nigeria, Ghana, Uganda and South Africa.

2026-10-08-mar-maroc24-ausim-ia-2030-sou.summary: Morocco's digital transition minister set out five priorities for the 'Maroc IA 2030' roadmap, among them bringing sovereign compute into service and completing the legal framework for AI. The roadmap aims to add MAD 100 billion to GDP by 2030.

2026-10-08-mdg-allafrica-tana-digitalisa.summary: Antananarivo's urban commune began digitalising its markets: traders are registered on tablet and issued chip and QR cards debited by collectors' payment terminals in place of paper tickets. Markets bring the commune MGA 7 to 9 billion a year.

2026-10-08-mdg-sputnik-ministre-souverai.summary: Madagascar's digital development minister said sovereignty means controlling infrastructure and data while staying open to foreign expertise. AI is at an early stage but already used by customs for risk analysis.

2026-10-08-moz-aim-cybersecurity-measure.summary: Mozambique's communications and digital transformation minister, Américo Muchanga, said on 7 October 2026 that the Cybersecurity Law (Law 13/2026) and Cybercrimes Law (Law 14/2026) of 1 July are in force. A national network of incident response teams now covers government, the regulator INCM, the telecoms sector and four provinces, and the national cybersecurity strategy is being updated for 2026-2030.

2026-10-08-moz-bcl-estrategia-internet-p.summary: Mozambique's regulator is validating a proposed national 'Internet para Todos' strategy with operators, academia and civil society, with targets to 2030. Figures presented put internet access at about 20% of the population.

2026-10-08-moz-mznews-certificacao-digit.summary: A Mozambican government team is training in Brasília until 16 October on public key infrastructure and digital certification, ahead of a national certification system. A digital signature pilot at home involves about 40 entities.

2026-10-08-moz-pav-pawapay-licensed-psp.summary: The Bank of Mozambique licensed payments aggregator PawaPay as a payment service provider through its local subsidiary, among the first such licences. It can now onboard merchants directly across the country's three mobile money operators.

2026-10-08-mus-lexpress-atelier-maurice-.summary: Mauritius's ICT ministry and Meta held a workshop at Ebene on 7 October 2026 on online abuse, disinformation and deepfakes. Figures presented show reported security incidents rising from 5,221 in 2024 to 6,073 in 2025 and cyberbullying cases from 491 to 702; the government is preparing bills and amendments to the ICT Act on cybersecurity and cybercrime, and wants faster takedown channels with Meta.

2026-10-08-mus-lexpress-portabilite-mobi.summary: Mauritius' ICT Authority opened a call for applications for a new mobile number portability licence, announced at a three-day ICTA workshop in Balaclava reported on 8 October 2026. Chairman Tassarajen Pillay Chedumbrum said subscribers will be able to keep their number and SIM when changing operator. No launch date is given.

2026-10-08-mus-mitci-meta-online-abuse.summary: Mauritius's ICT ministry met Meta on faster removal of fake accounts, impersonation and illegal content, moderation in Kreol and a local presence for the company. Amendments to the 2021 cybercrime law and age assurance for children were also discussed.

2026-10-08-nam-biometricupdate-mps-digit.summary: Namibian MPs questioned the planned digital ID on rural reach, cost, data ownership and cybersecurity at a briefing by two ministries. The rollout planned for September was delayed because the legal framework had not been finalised.

2026-10-08-nam-nampa-cabinet-mict-online.summary: Namibia's Cabinet directed the ICT ministry to develop a standard template for reporting which government services are available online.

2026-10-08-nam-techafricanews-paratus-eu.summary: Paratus Namibia launched Eutelsat's OneWeb low earth orbit satellite service across Namibia, with capped and uncapped packages for homes and businesses.

2026-10-08-nga-cbn-insists-on-january-1-.summary: The Central Bank of Nigeria said its 1 January 2027 deadline for storing payment transaction data in Nigeria has not changed. Industry executives warned that a rushed migration carries operational and security risk.

2026-10-08-nga-nan-orodata-csos-frontier.summary: Nigerian research group Orodata published a brief urging civil society to take part in governing frontier AI. It warns that voluntary commitments by technology companies are no substitute for enforceable rules.

2026-10-08-openzambia-zambia-and-us-sign.summary: Zambia and the United States signed a five-year health memorandum and a data sharing agreement. On this account the agreement exchanges only aggregated, de-identified programme data, with Zambia keeping ownership under its own laws; the health minister said the money will fund 40,000 health workers.

2026-10-08-opt-out-registry-arrives-as-m.summary: South Africa's opt-out registry is to be enforced from April 2027, sixteen years after it was first proposed. The direct marketing industry is meanwhile moving from contact databases to targeted digital advertising.

2026-10-08-pesalink-s-new-id-makes-bank-.summary: Kenya's bank-owned instant payment switch says a portable identifier is ready, so a sender need not know the recipient's bank, and institutions must now map customers to it. A fintech association asks who will own the rail as the alias takes hold.

2026-10-08-rwa-igihe-inside-a-new-infras.summary: Signalytic, a health technology company, has installed solar-powered units supplying Wi-Fi and electricity at 65 health posts in 21 Rwandan districts, working with the Ministry of Health and Gavi. Another 85 facilities are planned, for a target of 150. The units support digital immunisation records, insurance checks and vaccine refrigerators.

2026-10-08-rwa-igihe-rwanda-cyber-fraud-.summary: The National Bank of Rwanda said on 8 October 2026 that financial-sector fraud cases fell to 2,879 in the second quarter of 2026 from 4,128 a year earlier, and the sums involved to Rwf471 million, but only 3.6% had been recovered. Governor Soraya Hakuziyaremye said electronic payments reached 341% of GDP in the first half of 2026.

2026-10-08-rwa-ktpress-bnr-digital-agri-.summary: Rwanda's central bank is piloting a digital agricultural lending platform meant to cut farmers' wait for a loan from five to seven weeks to under 48 hours. The six-month pilot began in September 2026 with two microfinance institutions and two banks; a national rollout is planned for 2027.

2026-10-08-rwa-newtimes-rdb-mulls-new-pl.summary: The Rwanda Development Board said on 8 October 2026 it is preparing a Business Obstacles Alert platform for businesses to report and track obstacles in accessing public services after registration. It said 95% of more than 250,000 services processed since January 2026 met their standard timelines. No launch date is given.

2026-10-08-rwa-nida-temporarily-suspends.summary: Rwanda's identification agency suspended the photography exercise for the digital identity card and gave no date for resuming it. Pre-enrolment through Irembo continues, and residents are asked to correct civil-registration details first.

2026-10-08-sdn-alsudantoday-mof-sudani-e.summary: Sudan's Ministry of Finance signed a contract with Sudani Telecom on 8 October 2026 for SMS services supporting Eesaly, the government's electronic collection and payment system, according to the Sudan News Agency. No value or duration is given.

2026-10-08-sdn-globalsurvivorsfund-rfp-d.summary: The Global Survivors Fund opened a tender for a secure, offline-capable digital registry of survivors of conflict-related sexual violence in Sudan, to be run with the AWAFY Sudanese Organization in Darfur, Kordofan, Khartoum, Northern State and Blue Nile. The 18-month project starts on 1 November 2026; bids close on 27 October. No budget is disclosed.

2026-10-08-sen-camou-communication-un-et.summary: Senegal's parliamentary commission of inquiry into the One Student, One Computer laptop programme opened hearings on 5 October 2026. A former higher-education funding director testified that she found a recorded order for 25,000 computers from two suppliers without the contracts and referred it to the procurement regulator, ARCOP, in September 2025; ARCOP presented its review of two contracts signed in April 2025.

2026-10-08-sle-blacknews-iprp-dismisses-.summary: Sierra Leone's procurement review panel dismissed a bidder's complaint over the evaluation of the World Bank-funded government network contract. It directed the ministry to open financial proposals and proceed to award.

2026-10-08-ssd-caretaker-finance-ministe.summary: South Sudan's caretaker finance minister called for digital payment systems that reach rural areas, to ease the demand for physical cash, at a workshop on the liquidity crisis.

2026-10-08-ssd-radioyei-juba-city-counci.summary: South Sudan's Juba City Council, at its first executive meeting under caretaker Mayor Christopher Sarafino Wani, made the move from manual to digital revenue collection a priority to reduce leakage and fund services. Central Equatoria State had launched a digital revenue collection system and e-services for the council in September 2026. No meeting date, cost or timetable is given.

2026-10-08-ssd-radioyei-mtn-government-d.summary: South Sudan's caretaker trade minister Labanya Margaret Mathya held a virtual meeting with MTN's senior management on reopening Mobile Money transactions, connectivity problems and digital banking, and said the government would urgently address the company's difficulties. The report does not say when or why Mobile Money transactions were halted.

2026-10-08-starlink-rival-maps-out-sa-st.summary: Amazon Leo said it has applied for licences to bring a direct-to-device satellite service to South Africa with mobile operators, probably from around 2028. Its fixed satellite broadband is to be distributed by Herotel from 2027.

2026-10-08-swz-escom-national-cyber-dril.summary: Eswatini held its first national cyber drill on 5 October: a multi-sector ransomware simulation for energy, telecoms, government, aviation, health and finance, facilitated by Lesotho's regulator. The communications commission showed a prototype incident-sharing platform.

2026-10-08-tcd-uneca-chad-national-ai-st.summary: Chad pre-validated its draft National Artificial Intelligence Strategy at a workshop in N'Djamena on 8 October 2026. The UN Economic Commission for Africa led the drafting with the digital economy ministry. The draft sets AI priorities for 2027–2035 in agriculture, public administration, security and defence, education and health, and is to go to government by the end of 2026.

2026-10-08-tgo-atop-kozah-dialogue-gouve.summary: Community groups in Togo's Kara region were briefed on the risks and uses of AI at a regional dialogue run by two associations with outside funding, part of a citizen dialogue project on AI governance.

2026-10-08-tun-alchourouk-remote-work-bi.summary: Tunisia's social affairs minister Issam Lahmar said on 8 October 2026 that the remote-work bill is ready and completing its final administrative stages. He said the ministry has also studied the platform economy and prepared a legal text on it, and is working on core labour-law principles and mediation in labour disputes. No date for submission to parliament is given.

2026-10-08-tza-mwigulunchemba-pm-meets-s.summary: Tanzania's prime minister met SpaceX and Starlink representatives in London on 7 October about investment in the communications sector, with three ministers present. No outcome was stated.

2026-10-08-uga-itweb-child-online-protec.summary: Uganda launched a nationwide child online protection campaign at a Kampala secondary school. A regulator survey of students there found 88.5% had met digital harm and 74.2% of those exposed had told no one.

2026-10-08-uga-techtrendske-mam-telecom-.summary: Ugandan startup MAM Telecom received a US$250,000 grant from an unnamed South African businessman to license and build a settlement platform that lets mobile-money agents obtain digital float. It has not launched.

2026-10-08-uga-ucc-child-online-protecti.summary: A second account of the Uganda Communications Commission's child online protection campaign, launched during cybersecurity awareness month and aimed at children, parents and teachers.

2026-10-08-xaf-achpr-draft-guidelines-pu.summary: The African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights invited comments by 8 January 2027 on draft Guidelines on Public Interest Content in the Digital Era, in a call dated 8 October 2026. The draft, prepared by its special rapporteur on freedom of expression under a 2025 resolution, sets out state obligations and responsibilities for technology companies and digital infrastructure services.

2026-10-08-xaf-techafricanews-single-who.summary: Ghana, Rwanda and South Africa have each moved away from the single wholesale network model for mobile broadband. Commercial sharing of towers, fibre and spectrum between operators is replacing it.

2026-10-08-xea-apo-eac-health-ministers-.summary: East African Community health ministers, ending their 26th meeting in Arusha on 6 October 2026, advanced a regional platform for sharing pandemic and epidemic intelligence. They noted that all eight Partner States are onboarded and trained on the digital platform of the EAC pooled procurement mechanism, and called for a dashboard to track regional health decisions.

2026-10-08-xwa-bceao-communique-connexio.summary: The Central Bank of West African States announced on 8 October 2026 that WAEMU public treasuries are being connected to its PI-SPI instant payment platform, to send and receive salaries, grants, subsidies and taxes whatever the counterpart's account. Côte d'Ivoire's treasury already makes regular bulk payments through it; the others are being integrated progressively.

2026-10-08-xwa-bceao-instruction-020-mon.summary: The Central Bank of West African States (BCEAO) issued Instruction No. 020 on 8 October 2026, in force from 2 November, capping the e-money one identified client may hold with one issuer at FCFA 4 million and monthly reloads at FCFA 15 million, unless the BCEAO authorises more. Issuers must keep at least 65% of the e-money float in demand deposits.

2026-10-08-za-icasa-regulate-when-not-to.summary: ICASA's chairperson said the regulator has developed a draft satellite licensing framework and will use sandboxes and lighter-touch approaches beside licensing. He named data centres and cloud computing as infrastructure it must now address.

2026-10-08-za-spam-calls-opt-out-registr.summary: South Africa's consumer commission launched a national opt-out registry against a count of 17.5 billion spam calls in the first half of 2026. Marketers must register and clean their lists monthly before any campaign.

2026-10-08-zaf-citizen-weaknesses-in-sas.summary: South Africa's Department of Social Development received a qualified audit opinion for 2025/26 because of weaknesses in the South African Social Security Agency's payment system, including grants paid to deceased people and government employees, Parliament's social development committee heard from the Auditor-General on 6 October 2026. Committee chair Bridget Masango called for tighter verification and controls.

2026-10-08-zaf-nyakaza-accountability-ov.summary: Gauteng legislature committees said after a joint meeting on 5 October 2026 that the provincial Department of e-Government notified the Information Regulator of the e-Panic Button data exposure only that morning, about two weeks after being alerted on 21 September. The department could not say how many records were exposed, and the committees demanded an investigation independent of the app's service provider.

2026-10-08-zwe-herald-papss-5-8-million-.summary: Afreximbank said Zimbabwe is processing US$5.8 million a month through the pan-African payment and settlement system. Yuan clearing is being brought onto the platform through its link to China's interbank system.

2026-10-08-zwe-herald-zrp-hit-crime-mana.summary: Zimbabwe's home affairs minister told the National Assembly that a crime management system built by the Harare Institute of Technology is running as a proof of concept at Warren Park and a few other police stations. Reporting crime by mobile phone is to follow, and wider deployment depends on the test.

2026-10-09-ago-pti-angolaid-testes.summary: Angolan company Tech By Tech released a test version of AngolaID, a private digital identity wallet and verification service, on Google Play and the App Store, announced on 7 October 2026. Users create a credential by video liveness check and facial recognition, and institutions can integrate it by API and SDK. The company says it does not issue or replace the state identity card.

2026-10-09-assabah-bank-al-maghrib-cbdc-.summary: Morocco's central bank published two research working papers on a central bank digital currency, one on the stakes and lessons for Morocco and one a modelling exercise. It presents them as its researchers' work, shared for debate.

2026-10-09-au-stc-cict-6th-ordinary-sess.summary: The African Union will hold the sixth ordinary session of its technical committee on communication and ICT in Libreville from 26 to 29 October 2026. The committee, which meets every two years, feeds the Executive Council on the Commission's ICT programmes.

2026-10-09-ben-cadreco-cdsi-ia-talents.summary: Benin's public-sector digital chiefs met in Cotonou on 8 October 2026 at a conference now covering digital transformation and innovation, where an AI cybersecurity framework with four risk tiers, an AI officer and an ethics committee was presented. Officials cited shortages of staff, equipment, servers and funding in administrations, and the minister stressed developing local solutions and talent.

2026-10-09-bfa-lefaso-zama-tche-maisons-.summary: Burkina Faso's digital-transition minister said 80 citizen service houses have been launched on a FCFA 10 billion envelope, against a target of one in each of 351 communes by 2030. She put the two modular data centres at FCFA 15 billion and a national data centre at an estimated FCFA 20 billion, and said digital identity enrolment was due to start in October.

2026-10-09-bfa-refletinfo-750-villages-z.summary: Burkina Faso's digital transition minister, Aminata Zerbo, said on 8 October 2026 that 750 villages without network coverage will get calls, internet and mobile money by the end of 2026, and 750 more by 2028, with 25 billion FCFA mobilised by the state. She said 3,140 government buildings are now connected and the administration's bandwidth has risen from 9 to 20 Gbps.

2026-10-09-biometricupdate-nigeria-abis-.summary: Nigeria's electoral commission put the register at 103,428,715 voters after a biometric clean-up, with 10,772,421 new registrations since August 2025. Voter card collection began on 9 October, ahead of elections in January and February 2027.

2026-10-09-bnr-moves-to-tackle-delayed-e.summary: Rwanda's central bank said it is working with financial institutions on delayed and failed transfers on the national payment switch, with rejections below 2% by September. Active accounts rose from 2.03 million to 10.3 million in a year.

2026-10-09-caf-afriquesur7-russie-gouver.summary: The Central African Republic signed a five-year digital governance partnership with Russia, implemented through Moscow's HSE University, on 9 October 2026 at the Global Digital Forum in Moscow. It covers training for civil servants, joint research and case studies, and seminars. No cost or funding is stated.

2026-10-09-caf-alwihda-centre-donnees-cr.summary: The Central African Republic inaugurated a building housing criminal databases at the interior and public security ministry in Bangui on 8 October 2026, with equipment funded through the UN mission MINUSCA and the UN Office on Drugs and Crime. It will let the police and gendarmerie centralise records of offences and wanted persons.

2026-10-09-caf-icasees-mission-appui-ban.summary: A World Bank supervision mission led by statistician Gervais Chamberlin Yama visited the Central African Republic's statistics institute ICASEES on 7 and 8 October 2026 to review the HISWACA-SOP2 statistics project (P180085). Its specialists examined fiduciary management, environmental and social safeguards, monitoring and evaluation, statistical output and the institute's capacity, and followed up recommendations from the previous mission.

2026-10-09-caf-minusca-base-donnees-crim.summary: The Central African Republic inaugurated its first integrated criminal database, attended by President Faustin-Archange Touadéra, the UN mission MINUSCA announced on 9 October 2026. MINUSCA financed the centre, equipment and servers and UNODC provided training and connectivity; the database lets police and gendarmerie share information, with the judicial police and regions to be added next.

2026-10-09-civ-aip-artci-reseau-postal.summary: The director general of Côte d'Ivoire's telecoms regulator, ARTCI, Lakoun Ouattara, said on World Post Day, 9 October 2026, that the postal network should adapt to e-commerce, digital addressing and last-mile delivery. He said the 2013 Postal Code, law 2013-702, is being revised to cover new uses and operators. No timetable for the revision is given.

2026-10-09-civ-ecofin-afdb-fintech-suppo.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's finance ministry launched a Fintech Sector Support Project in Abidjan on 6 October 2026 through its financial inclusion agency APIF, with African Development Bank funding under a business-climate programme. It aims to build fintech firms' capacity and encourage services beyond payments; mobile money use reached 84.2% in 2024. The project's own budget is not stated.

2026-10-09-civ-koaci-journees-foncieres-.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's cadastre director, Bahi Apollinaire Boua, said at the Abidjan land days of 5–7 October 2026 that widening the property tax base is now a priority of the tax directorate. He cited the e-Cadastre platform as part of moving land procedures online to improve access to land information and tax collection.

2026-10-09-cod-l-adn-en-collaboration-av.summary: KADEA and ULB-Solvay Lifelong Learning, with DR Congo's Agence pour le Développement du Numérique, ran the first session of an executive programme in digital transformation and AI for senior officials from 30 public institutions on 28 to 30 September 2026. This session dealt with diagnosis and digital strategy through case studies and group work; later sessions are to cover AI, data, leadership and drafting a digital roadmap, under the DRC Digital Nation 2030 vision.

2026-10-09-cod-rdc-monde-dgi-facture-nor.summary: The DRC's tax directorate began nationwide checks of the standardised invoice on 5 October, after the moratorium ended. Consumers are asked to verify invoices by QR code in the official application, with rewards for verified reports of non-compliance.

2026-10-09-cod-zoom-eco-vodacom-670-mill.summary: Vodacom Congo said at a Kinshasa forum on 8 October 2026 that it plans a long-term US$670 million network investment programme, against an average of US$140 million a year. It reported 26.4 million subscribers, 4G coverage of 46.1 per cent and 10 million M-Pesa customers. Prime Minister Judith Suminwa said state and citizens' data must be hosted in the country.

2026-10-09-cpv-eeas-eu-cabo-verde-specia.summary: The 14th ministerial meeting of the EU–Cabo Verde Special Partnership, held in Brussels on 9 October 2026, reported Global Gateway digital projects in preparation: domestic and international submarine cables, better connections between the islands and access to European digital infrastructure. It also noted progress in EU support for Cabo Verde's national data and AI strategies. No amounts are given.

2026-10-09-cybersecurity-rwandans-urged-.summary: Rwanda launched its 2026 cyber security and data protection awareness campaign in Kigali, the ICT minister citing online fraud, phishing and identity theft. The government technology agency counts about 2,000 digital ambassadors to carry it to communities.

2026-10-09-dza-prixalgerie-digital-ident.summary: Algeria's digitalisation commission set out how the national digital identity is obtained: registration and an appointment at the commune, activation, then verification against biometric data. It also said a national data-governance system that classifies data sources against one reference is under way.

2026-10-09-ecomatin-cemac-mobile-money-4.summary: Central Africa's seven licensed payment institutions processed 4.6 billion operations worth FCFA 44,037 billion in 2025, against 3.4 billion operations in 2024, on the banking commission's annual report. Two Cameroonian operators' services held 65.4% of the sector's income.

2026-10-09-eth-biometricupdate-fayda-dev.summary: Ethiopia opened a public sandbox where developers and startups can test the Fayda digital identity's authentication interfaces before going live. Fayda counted more than 52 million registrations, 150 integrated partners and 208 million electronic verifications.

2026-10-09-eth-birrmetrics-banks-interna.summary: Ethiopia's Awash Bank, with Mastercard, and Oromia Bank, with Visa, launched eight internationally accepted payment cards between them on 8 October 2026. The launches follow the National Bank of Ethiopia's February 2026 rule change allowing banks to issue such cards to foreign-currency account holders. Awash said it processed over US$60 million in card foreign exchange last fiscal year.

2026-10-09-financialafrik-bceao-plafond-.summary: The West African central bank doubled the ceiling on electronic money one client may hold at one issuer to FCFA 4 million and raised monthly reloads from FCFA 10 million to FCFA 15 million. Issuers may go beyond them only with its prior authorisation.

2026-10-09-gab-gabonreview-etat-civil-at.summary: The workshop preparing Gabon's national civil-registration conferences closed with a diagnosis of badly kept archives, irregular data entry and a Civil Code dating from 1972. Its final report goes to the Interior minister, who sets the calendar.

2026-10-09-gab-gabonreview-poste-sa-akib.summary: Gabon's postal company presented Akiba, an application built and hosted in Gabon that combines payments, public services such as birth-certificate requests, postal services and insurance. A USSD version was announced; the app-store launch is still to come.

2026-10-09-gha-ghanaweb-nia-biometric-fr.summary: Ghana's National Identification Authority will begin Ghana Card registration of children aged 0-5 the following week, alongside the ongoing registration of 6-14 year olds, its deputy executive secretary Fred Bedzrah said at a forum at the University of Professional Studies, Accra. He presented biometric verification with liveness detection as the check against ghost names on government payrolls.

2026-10-09-gha-techafricanews-csa-reject.summary: A second account of the Ghana Cyber Security Authority's statement on Operation Blackout: it names the Ghanaian, British, American and Nigerian agencies that took part and says the operation ran under Ghanaian authority.

2026-10-09-ghana-csa-operation-blackout-.summary: Ghana's Cyber Security Authority said Ghana, not the FBI, led Operation Blackout, which arrested eight suspects and rescued 120 suspected trafficking victims at cybercrime centres in Greater Accra. It asked the FBI to correct its public account, saying foreign agencies have no police powers in Ghana.

2026-10-09-ghana-cybersecurity-essential.summary: Ghana's communications minister said the security of power, water, transport, health and financial services now depends on the control systems behind them, at a Cyber Security Authority workshop. He repeated that 13 critical sectors and about 200 institutions are designated.

2026-10-09-ghana-ghima-unlicensed-health.summary: Ghana's health information managers' association warned against unlicensed staff handling health records in facilities. It said the law requires a licence from the allied health professions council and that data quality and patient safety are at stake.

2026-10-09-ghana-miif-cyber-resilience-m.summary: The head of Ghana's minerals income fund called for stronger protection of the control systems that run mines, at a Cyber Security Authority workshop. She said an attack on them bears on safety, production and national revenue, not only on IT.

2026-10-09-gnq-realequatorialguinea-offi.summary: Equatorial Guinea's vice-president, Teodoro Nguema Obiang Mangue, named on X the alleged members of a network leaking official documents from the Presidency of the Government. He alleged that a registry official extracted several years of administrative files and handed a hard drive to a third party under the pretext of a project to digitise the Presidency's archives. The account is the government's; no court finding is reported.

2026-10-09-ken-radiogeneration-ntsa-auto.summary: Kenya's Senate ICT committee questioned National Transport and Safety Authority director general Nashon Kondiwa on 8 October 2026 about the Instant Fines Traffic Management System, including its legal basis and how offences are detected, notified and paid. The High Court halted automated penalties under the system on 12 March 2026, three days after its announcement, and the authority withdrew its launch notice on 27 March.

2026-10-09-ken-techafricanews-ict-state-.summary: Kenya's ICT principal secretary met Equity Group's chief executive on 6 October to explore working together on digital infrastructure, financial inclusion and regional trade. Nothing was signed.

2026-10-09-ken-techafricanews-kica-revie.summary: Kenya's ICT department told a National Assembly committee that the Kenya Information and Communications Act is under review and accession to the Budapest Convention on Cybercrime is advancing. Billing transparency for internet service was also discussed.

2026-10-09-lequotidien-taazour-sanad-dig.summary: Mauritania's national solidarity agency launched Sanad, a single digital platform for social assistance. It opens with transport costs for 11,656 pupils and students from households in the social registry, who are verified by facial recognition.

2026-10-09-linfodrome-artci-meta-monetis.summary: The head of Côte d'Ivoire's telecoms regulator received a Meta delegation to discuss paying Ivorian content creators on its platforms and the regulation of digital services. No decision or date was announced.

2026-10-09-lso-spaceinafrica-vodacom-les.summary: Vodacom Lesotho launched a managed satellite internet service for businesses and institutions built on Starlink, at an event in Maseru reported on 9 October 2026. It offers primary connectivity where there are no terrestrial networks, a backup option, and a combined satellite and terrestrial mode. Target sectors include financial services, health, education and public administration; no prices are given.

2026-10-09-malawi24-undp-printers-decent.summary: UNDP handed Malawi 152 printers to bring birth, marriage and death registration closer to people: 100 for registration offices at Traditional Authority level and 52 for health facilities. The minister said 180 health facilities are already digitalised.

2026-10-09-mar-nexus-core-systems-infras.summary: The developer of Morocco's planned AI compute platform states 500 MW of total planned capacity, a 40 MW initial deployment and a 12-hectare first site, on renewable power. The page gives no dates.

2026-10-09-mdg-fid-mobile-money-transfer.summary: Madagascar's development intervention fund FID is tendering for mobile-money providers to pay social cash transfers, in seven lots, under World Bank procurement rules. Bids close on 3 November 2026.

2026-10-09-midi-madagasikara-gouvernemen.summary: Madagascar scores 9 of 16 points against the 12 it needs to rejoin the Open Government Partnership, which it first joined in 2016. A colloquium is drafting commitments for a national action plan for 2026 to 2030.

2026-10-09-moz-mznews-atdi-x-road-traini.summary: Mozambique's digital transformation agency trained 25 technicians from nine public bodies on the X-Road data-exchange layer, among them civil identification, migration and tax. Estonian experts led the four days, under a World Bank project.

2026-10-09-moz-tridigital-maturity.summary: Mozambique's ICT institute, INTIC, has joined TriDigital, a project to build a common framework and bilingual platform for assessing the digital maturity of public institutions in Angola, Guinea-Bissau, Mozambique and São Tomé and Príncipe, with the United Nations University and Argentine and Portuguese partners. It runs from September 2026 to January 2028 with a budget of €124,030.

2026-10-09-mozambique-95-broadband-2030.summary: Mozambique's regulator validated its Internet for All strategy, which targets 95% broadband coverage by 2030, 12 million mobile internet subscribers and at least 60% of schools connected. It cited a programme to subsidise about 280,000 internet-enabled devices.

2026-10-09-mrt-ecofin-telecom-quality-ar.summary: Mauritania's regulator ARE released results on 7 October 2026 of a February–March inspection that found failings in voice and mobile data services at Mattel, Mauritel and Chinguitel, including call completion and drop rates in several towns and on main roads and weak 3G and 4G performance. Ecofin sets this against the government's plans for online public services, AI and e-commerce.

2026-10-09-mrt-wardip-csirt-soc-riad-ten.summary: Mauritania's WARDIP project unit at the digital transformation ministry issued a national tender on 9 October 2026 to set up a national CSIRT and a security operations centre for RIAD, the government's high-speed intranet, paid from World Bank credit IDA-7445-MR. Bids are due on 17 November 2026 with a 950,000 MRU bid guarantee. No contract value is stated.

2026-10-09-mus-pmo-cabinet-highlights-20.summary: Mauritius opened online applications for the State Age Pension from 7 October 2026, the Cabinet noted on 9 October, with a pension estimate app on the KOREK! government super-app. People with limited digital access can apply with help at 38 social security offices.

2026-10-09-nam-marketwatch-fibre-copper-.summary: Telecom Namibia signed a partnership with Demshi Investment Holdings to replace copper with fibre in areas hit repeatedly by theft and vandalism. Demshi builds and maintains the open-access network and Telecom Namibia sells service over it.

2026-10-09-nga-andersen-fhc-ndpc-pos-reg.summary: Nigeria's Federal High Court in Lagos ruled on 17 July 2026 that the Nigeria Data Protection Commission acted within its powers in designating point-of-sale operators as data controllers of major importance. Such operators must therefore register with the commission and pay its fees. A PoS agent had argued the requirement breached his constitutional right to privacy.

2026-10-09-nga-bpp-to-end-physical-biddi.summary: Nigeria's Bureau of Public Procurement plans to move federal bidding fully online through its e-GP system, so that contractors submit bids without meeting officials, its director-general said in Abuja. Submissions from the education ministry and federal universities already go through the PCOMS platform, and the bureau plans electronic audits of procuring agencies.

2026-10-09-nga-businesstech-one-regulato.summary: BusinessTech Nigeria explains the Nigerian Fintech Regulatory Commission Bill 2025 (HB.2389), which would create a single regulator to license and supervise fintech services now split between the central bank, the SEC and other agencies. The bill passed second reading in the House of Representatives on 28 October 2025 and had a public hearing on 2 March 2026; it remains pending.

2026-10-09-nga-opay-form-f-1-registratio.summary: OPay Limited, the Nigerian-operated payments company registered in the Cayman Islands with offices in Singapore, filed for an initial public offering with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on 9 October 2026, seeking to list American depositary shares on the New York Stock Exchange as OPAY. It reports 50.1 million monthly active users at 31 July 2026. A Standard Bank Group company has agreed to buy shares in a concurrent private placement of up to US$200 million.

2026-10-09-nga-securing-digital-trust-nd.summary: Nigeria's data protection commissioner visited the salaries and wages commission to press compliance with the 2023 Act and pay structures that keep data protection staff in the public service. He put the commission's revenue at more than ₦12 billion in 2026, against ₦7 billion in 2025.

2026-10-09-nga-standard-bank-opay-strate.summary: Standard Bank Group signed a subscription agreement to invest in Nigerian fintech OPay, to close with or shortly after OPay's proposed New York Stock Exchange listing, for which OPay filed with the US SEC on 9 October 2026. The two also plan to explore digital banking, merchant acquiring, lending and remittances. The release states no amount.

2026-10-09-nga-thestar-cbn-gftn-mou.summary: The Central Bank of Nigeria signed a memorandum of understanding with the Global Finance & Technology Network in Singapore to set a framework for cooperation between the two countries' financial-innovation sectors. It was signed during Governor Olayemi Cardoso's talks with the Monetary Authority of Singapore. The signing date is not stated.

2026-10-09-nilepost-museveni-orders-canc.summary: Uganda's President Yoweri Museveni ordered the cancellation of the government's agreement with Rowad Capital Commercial to revive Uganda Telecom at a State House meeting on 6 October 2026, according to unnamed meeting sources. The investor had not paid the initial US$25 million of a US$225 million package in four years. Ministries are to prepare a Cabinet paper on state funding for the revival.

2026-10-09-rwanda-ida-19m-digitalization.summary: Rwanda's parliament ratified EUR 17 million of World Bank financing for digital identity, public data management and cybersecurity, restoring part of US$20 million cut from the project in 2024. Delays to the government data hub have pushed the project's deadline to June 2028.

2026-10-09-sdn-alarabiya-bankak-app-outa.summary: Outages of Bank of Khartoum's Bankak app left Sudanese customers unable to reach or transfer money during cash and fuel shortages, Al Arabiya reported on 9 October 2026. Sudan's energy and oil ministry blamed fuel-station queues partly on slow banking apps, and a speaker warned of losses to government collection through the Eesaly system. The bank apologised and said its teams were working round the clock.

2026-10-09-sen-lesoleil-roa-bn-conseil-i.summary: Ten member states held the founding interministerial meeting of the West African Network of National Backbones, ROA-BN, in Dakar on 8 October 2026. Its founding texts, a 2026–2030 strategic plan and its bodies are still to be adopted. Senegal's telecoms minister Samba Diouf called for common rules on cross-border fibre and keeping West African data in transit within the region.

2026-10-09-sen-techreviewafrica-artp-new.summary: Senegal's new telecoms regulator chief said at his handover that he will move the authority toward data-led regulation, with real-time measurement of service quality. He named 5G, cloud, satellite broadband and digital finance as what it must anticipate.

2026-10-09-sle-truthmedia-cipher-launch-.summary: The Center for Information Privacy, Human-Centered Technology and Ethics Research (CIPHER), an independent research body, launched in Freetown, Sierra Leone, on 6 October 2026. Its chief executive, Cyril Foday-Kallie, said it will research mishandling of personal data, train people on data-subject rights and controllers' duties, and supply evidence for data-protection law and policy.

2026-10-09-southwood-africas-digital-lan.summary: An analyst updates his 2019 study of African online content: digital advertising's share of spend rose from 5 to 10% in 2019 to 45% in 2024. He finds video creators can be paid in only a handful of sub-Saharan countries, and payout services work in hard currency only.

2026-10-09-swz-eswatinipositivenews-post.summary: Eswatini's ICT principal secretary, Prince Mashishimba Andreas Dlamini, said on 9 October 2026, World Post Day, that the government plans to use post offices as community digital centres for public services. Eswatini Post would be brought into e-government work, supporting citizen authentication, document verification and digital payments in rural and underserved areas. No timetable or cost is given.

2026-10-09-swz-independentnews-ecot-miss.summary: An analysis of professional profiles presented at a skills workshop found 265 ICT professionals in Eswatini trained at Limkokwing and 152 at the University of Eswatini, and none visible from the Eswatini College of Technology. The presenter read it as a visibility problem for the college.

2026-10-09-swz-independentnews-eptc-post.summary: Eswatini's postal corporation said 34 of its branches now take payments for public services, in partnership with the revenue service. It is turning to government services to keep the network open as mail falls.

2026-10-09-tcd-camerpressagency-la-souve.summary: An unsigned CamerPressAgency editorial reports that a workshop to pre-validate Chad's National Artificial Intelligence Strategy opened in N'Djamena on 8 October 2026, aiming at what it calls ethical, frugal and sovereign AI. It links this to restructuring of the national postal company STPE under the Tchad Connexion 2030 plan, including a possible postal bank. No budget or timetable is given.

2026-10-09-tcd-lendjampost-e-visa-demand.summary: Applications on Chad's electronic visa platform have risen from under 10 a day to more than 100, the police official in charge said. The platform, launched in December 2024, has been the required route since 11 May 2026, though some embassies still issue visas.

2026-10-09-tcd-lendjampost-stpe-poste-ba.summary: Chad's telecoms minister set out a transformation of the state postal operator: a postal bank in the medium term, an integrated payment platform and post offices as one-stop counters. Its virtual-operator and internet-provider licences are to be put to use; no budget or date was given.

2026-10-09-tcd-tachad-tchad-le-ministre-.summary: Chad's digital minister Haliki Choua Mahamat told German, EU and GIZ representatives on 9 October 2026 that the country has about 6,000 km of optical fibre and aims for 14,000 km, citing the Trans-Saharan backbone and links with Libya and Nigeria. He also named a World Bank-funded project for uncovered areas and a national data centre, and said a digital code is still being drafted.

2026-10-09-tgo-tradefacilitation-plant-i.summary: The Global Alliance for Trade Facilitation launched a project in Lomé on 9 October 2026 to replace Togo's paper plant import permit with an electronic permit system for the Directorate of Agricultural Production. It is the Alliance's second digitalisation project in Togo after ePhyto, implemented through GIZ and funded by the European Union and the German government. No timetable is given.

2026-10-09-thisdaysl-sierra-leone-cybera.summary: Sierra Leone's communications ministry confirmed that 44 website addresses, one a government institution's, were hit on 25 September through the system that administers the national internet domain. Service was restored the same day; how the attackers got in has not been made public.

2026-10-09-tun-allafrica-lapresse-douane.summary: Tunisian Customs official Kais Ben Zayed said on 9 October 2026 that AI built by in-house staff will be added to the customs risk-management and selectivity system at the end of November 2026, to target high-risk declarations. He said nine or ten customs services have been digitised and more than 1.5 million declarations were examined in 2025.

2026-10-09-tun-lapresse-poste-inscriptio.summary: La Poste Tunisienne said about 1.57 million pupils, some 75%, and about 287,300 university students, some 76%, paid their 2026–2027 registration fees online using its free e-Dinar wallets. The post office also brought a new integrated ERP system into operation and launched the Universal Postal Union's Ecom@africa e-commerce exchange platform at Tunis-Carthage airport.

2026-10-09-tun-tunisienumerique-poste-tu.summary: Tunisia's communications minister, Sofiene Hemissi, said on 9 October 2026 that La Poste tunisienne's 2026-2030 strategy will integrate artificial intelligence and digital identity into postal services. Its chief executive listed five priorities, including financial inclusion and e-commerce logistics, and an enterprise resource planning rollout under way. The minister ruled out turning the Post into a bank.

2026-10-09-tza-dailynews-tcra-digital-in.summary: Tanzania's communications regulator (TCRA) said its project to adopt assistive technologies for people with disabilities is 80% complete, at a peer exchange of African regulators in Nairobi from 5 to 9 October 2026 under the iPRIS programme. TCRA's website accessibility work was recognised by the Tanzania Bureau of Standards under a new ICT accessibility standard.

2026-10-09-tza-digital-payments-now-a-bu.summary: Law firm FB Attorneys notes that Tanzania's Business Licensing (Amendment) Regulations, 2026, published as Government Notice 158N on 30 June and in force from 1 July 2026, require applicants for new or renewed business licences to show they can take digital payments, such as Lipa Namba or TANQR. Businesses in minerals, livestock, agricultural produce, timber and fisheries must also show a bank account.

2026-10-09-uga-monitor-ucaa-entebbe-ai-p.summary: The Uganda Civil Aviation Authority has upgraded the car parks at Entebbe International Airport with AI-assisted number-plate recognition, supplied through local contractor Samanga Utilities on Scheidt & Bachmann software, and mobile-money payment. The authority said it keeps vehicle registration records, timestamps and payment logs indefinitely and releases them to security agencies and police under statutory guidelines.

2026-10-09-uga-uganda-judiciary-digitise.summary: Uganda's Judiciary is digitising the Chief Registrar's records on advocates and bailiffs. When Chief Registrar Agnes Alum inspected the work at the Court of Appeal building in Kampala, all files had been scanned; capturing their data into a searchable system comes next, with the first phase due by the end of October 2026.

2026-10-09-unicv-cpv-dia-mundial-correio.summary: Cabo Verde's economy and digital transition minister, António Baptista, said at a University of Cabo Verde debate on e-commerce in Praia on 9 October 2026 that his ministry will run four national programmes, including digital and financial literacy. He said the Carteira Digital and 5G are in testing and a single government portal is in preparation.

2026-10-09-xaf-bank-of-china-ecobank-cip.summary: Ecobank, which operates in 34 African countries, said it would sign an agreement in China on 10 October 2026 to join China's CIPS interbank payment system for yuan transactions, chief executive Jeremy Awori told Reuters. It is also in talks with Bank of China to offer yuan settlement jointly. Rwanda's Bank of Kigali has joined CIPS and Angola's BFA plans to.

2026-10-09-za-ict-industry-redesign-ngca.summary: The president of Digital Council Africa told a Johannesburg conference that South Africa's ICT industry needs a full redesign of its regulation and physical infrastructure for AI. He said the country has very few specialists investigating and prosecuting cybercrime.

2026-10-09-zaf-itweb-woan-open-access-ma.summary: An industry opinion piece argues that South Africa's withdrawal of the wireless open access network direction leaves its principles in place: leasing of networks, wholesale capacity for other licensees and rural access. The author's case is for better use of infrastructure already built.

2026-10-09-zaf-presidency-keynotes-addre.summary: South Africa's deputy minister in the Presidency, Nonceba Mhlauli, marked 30 years of censuses by Statistics South Africa in Pretoria, in a speech published on 9 October 2026. She said Census 2031 is already in development, called statistical independence a constitutional safeguard, and said South Africa, as chair of the SADC Statistics Council, seeks to share experience with the region.

2026-10-09-zaf-sanews-sassa-steps-grant-.summary: The South African Social Security Agency defended its intensified grant reviews, eLife proof-of-life certification and beneficiary biometric enrolment as fraud controls on 9 October 2026. It rejected claims that they exclude eligible people, after media reports of 2025/26 payments to ineligible recipients and a parliamentary committee hearing on 7 October.

2026-10-09-zaf-techafricanews-kredete-ca.summary: Kredete acquired an entity holding a South African crypto asset service provider licence, to offer stablecoin remittances and payments. The regulator had approved about 310 of 533 licence applications by early 2026.

2026-10-09-zaf-techcentral-287154.summary: OPay, the Nigeria-focused fintech, filed on 9 October 2026 to list in New York; its registration statement shows Standard Bank's Stanbic Africa Holdings will buy up to $200 million of shares in a private placement alongside the IPO, with a 12-month lock-up. OPay reported 50.1 million monthly active users and $339.1 billion of transactions in the first half of 2026.

2026-10-09-zwe-heraldonline-zimsmart-con.summary: ZimSmart Villages is converting parts of Zimbabwe Postal Services offices into nurse-staffed digital health clinics with point-of-care diagnostics and small dispensaries, and uses container clinics where there is no post office. The company told a conference in Bulawayo it has 28 sites connected through Starlink and NetOne and has reached 118,000 people.

2026-10-10-bdi-burunditimes-eapss-paieme.summary: The East African Legislative Assembly's accounts committee reported that Burundi left parts of the regional payment-systems integration project unfinished when its grant closed in June. It recommends an audit and a costed completion plan; the central bank says it still intends to join the East African Payment System by December.

2026-10-10-caf-icasees-evaluation-mi-par.summary: The Central African Republic's statistics institute ICASEES held a mid-term review of the second national statistics strategy (2024–2028) in Bangui from 7 to 9 October 2026, funded entirely by the UN Development Programme. The strategy, adopted in August 2023 with a budget of nearly 60 billion CFA francs, is to be updated; a bill replacing the 2001 statistics law has passed technical validation and awaits review by the official-texts commission.

2026-10-10-citizen-za-proposed-road-traf.summary: South Africa's Department of Transport plans to amend the National Road Traffic Regulations so that Traffic Register Number certificates and learner's and driving licences can no longer be used as general identification. A 2023 check with Home Affairs of 1,072,258 TRNs found only 29,653 (2.7%) matched the national immigration identification system. The draft is to be published for 30 days' comment.

2026-10-10-cod-7sur7-copil-ptn-ptba-2026.summary: The steering committee of the DRC's digital transformation project met for the first time on 8 October and approved the 2026 work plan and budget. Members went through delays component by component and set priorities to 2027.

2026-10-10-cod-gachette-continuite-donne.summary: An economist's opinion piece starts from Google One refusing subscription renewals in the DRC and argues for data portability, trust standards for cloud services and enforcement of the 2023 digital code.

2026-10-10-gha-b2bgh-shaibu-fintech-open.summary: The head of Ghana's largest mobile-money fintech names AI, open finance, embedded finance, digital assets and instant payments as the themes that will shape the sector over the next two years.

2026-10-10-gha-ghanaguardian-agyeman-raw.summary: Visiting the Ghana Atomic Energy Commission on 9 October, the science and technology minister said the AI data centre it proposes must run under human oversight to protect sensitive nuclear information. She asked for governance arrangements to be written into the plan.

2026-10-10-gha-myjoyonline-us-seeks-chan.summary: Ghana's President John Mahama said the United States has asked to reopen talks on the roughly US$109m five-year health compact that Ghana's Cabinet rejected, with a view to amending or removing the disputed clauses. Ghana objected to provisions requiring it to give the US its pathogen profile and medical records, to counterpart funding and to limits on its Food and Drugs Authority.

2026-10-10-gin-mediaguinee-moussotech-10.summary: An NGO in Guinea launched MoussoTech on 9 October, an app in four national languages giving women information on health, rights and violence. A mobile operator is giving the first 100 participants a smartphone and a year of data.

2026-10-10-lagos-backs-ai-builders-over-.summary: Lagos State's special adviser on technology, Ganiyu Oseni, delivered Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu's address to the 11th Nigeria Innovation Summit in Lagos on 6 October 2026, saying Nigeria should build AI rather than depend on computing done in Europe. The address cited US$3.9 billion of venture capital in five years, more than one million connections on the state's fibre network and a planned innovation bill.

2026-10-10-lby-lana-al-baour-fcc-meeting.summary: The head of Libya's communications authority met officials at the US Federal Communications Commission in Washington, on licensing, spectrum, satellite licensing and the protection of subsea cables.

2026-10-10-lby-lana-wasl-digital-ai-empo.summary: Libya's Ministry of Social Affairs and the Minister of State for Digital Economy and Artificial Intelligence signed a memorandum launching the Wasl initiative at the Libya AI Forum in Tripoli on 10 October 2026. It has two tracks: digital and AI skills for social affairs staff, and digital access for persons with disabilities. No budget or timetable is given.

2026-10-10-mar-customs-ai-audits.summary: Moroccan customs are reported to have used AI and risk-analysis tools to audit imports worth about MAD 650 million and recover close to MAD 50 million for undervaluation. The account rests on unnamed sources, with no official statement.

2026-10-10-mdg-torohy-tax-corruption-pla.summary: Madagascar's tax directorate launched Torohy on 9 October, a platform for the public to report corruption in the tax administration. The head of state asked for the same at customs and the treasury.

2026-10-10-mli-icimali-conseil-des-minis.summary: Mali's Council of Ministers on 9 October 2026 took note of the country's fourth statistics master plan and its 2026-2030 action plan, presented by the economy and finance minister. It rests on four axes: managing the national statistical system, building its capacity, statistical production and analysis, and modernised dissemination. No cost is given.

2026-10-10-moz-techdisruptor-csm-tma-bei.summary: TradeMark Africa awarded India's CSM Tech a US$174,000 contract to build a Transport and Trade Observatory for Mozambique's Beira Corridor. The platform will combine port, road, rail and customs data into dashboards showing cargo movement and delays, be hosted in Mozambican data centres and run for about 18 months, starting with the Beira–Machipanda route.

2026-10-10-moz-techreviewafrica-sofala-c.summary: Mozambique's ICT institute held a consultation in Beira on 6 October to collect provincial input on the proposed national cybersecurity strategy for 2026 to 2030.

2026-10-10-mus-lexpress-ramtohul-discipl.summary: Mauritius's ICT minister, Avinash Ramtohul, told L'Express on 10 October 2026 about a two-day working session with Meta on content moderation, reporting and takedown requests. He cited about 20 abuse cases reported a day, a takedown agreement involving the national computer emergency team CERT-MU and Meta verification of MPs' identities, and said Meta could open an office in Mauritius.

2026-10-10-mwi-undp-printers-nrb.summary: UNDP's own account of the 152 printers handed to Malawi's registration bureau: 100 for registration at Traditional Authority offices and 52 for health facilities. It puts the Nzika registration application in pilot at 87 locations in five districts, with 250 planned by 2028.

2026-10-10-nam-bank-windhoek-face-id.summary: Bank Windhoek says it has recorded no fraud among customers using facial recognition. A quarter of its individual customers are now enrolled, up from 15% a year earlier.

2026-10-10-nam-namibian-marriage-records.summary: Namibia's home affairs minister, Lucia Iipumbu, told the National Assembly that some marriages remain unregistered because registers held by churches and magistrates' courts reach the ministry late or never. The gap came to light during records digitisation begun in 2021; the system relies on paper submission and does not track delivery, and some historical records are still in South Africa. Couples are urged to check their registration.

2026-10-10-nga-theafricanchronicle-stand.summary: Standard Bank Group has agreed to invest in the payments company OPay, which has filed for a New York listing. The amount is not disclosed, and closing depends on the listing and on regulatory approval.

2026-10-10-nga-theliberalist-nigeria-nee.summary: An opinion piece argues that Nigeria's data protection act and its implementing directive already regulate automated decisions, and points to the data protection commission's fines as evidence that a separate AI law is not needed.

2026-10-10-nga-timeexpressnigeria-gov-ra.summary: Katsina State and Nigeria's identity commission agreed a working group to link the state's identity management system to the national one, with a framework and memorandum due within eight weeks.

2026-10-10-nga-undp-cisco-networking-aca.summary: UNDP and Cisco signed a memorandum in Abuja on 9 October giving fellows of the Nigeria Jubilee Fellows Programme free access to the Cisco Networking Academy, with a target of up to 50,000 young people.

2026-10-10-sdn-alroya-bankak-ussd-1913-l.summary: Bank of Khartoum has opened a USSD transfer service on MTN lines, so customers can move money without a smartphone or a data connection. It comes as complaints about outages of the bank's app continue; the bank says more services will follow on the same channel.

2026-10-10-sdn-sudanhorizon-will-higher-.summary: A former banker argues that the Central Bank of Sudan's capital circular of February 2026 sets the same floor for digital banks as for commercial banks, and that the mergers it will force need scrutiny.

2026-10-10-sen-ledakarois-intrants-agric.summary: Senegal's agriculture ministry launched an app on 9 October for distributing subsidised seed and fertiliser nationwide. Producers get a text message before collecting, and the minister says the state now holds a digital register of who is entitled to what.

2026-10-10-sen-leral-pikine-guediawaye-a.summary: Senegal's justice ministry judged the first results of the pilot digitising judicial archives at the Pikine-Guédiawaye court satisfactory. Recruiting qualified staff and keeping the court platform fed are the open problems; other courts may follow.

2026-10-10-tgo-ancy-formation-cybersecur.summary: Togo's cybersecurity agency has been running the second phase of its national training programme since 7 September, for 350 public-administration staff. Training is free; trainees pay their own exam fees.

2026-10-10-tgo-atop-etat-civil-relecture.summary: A territorial administration ministry delegation consulted local officials in Avé 1 commune on 8 October as part of the review of Togo's 2009 civil status law. Participants raised the difficulty of deciding where a birth should be declared.

2026-10-10-tun-lapresse-plateforme-numer.summary: Tunisia's religious affairs ministry has launched a platform to manage mosque staff: it follows personnel files, shows vacant posts and links central and regional services.

2026-10-10-tza-eanso-cybercrime-fraud-le.summary: A second legal study judges Tanzania's Cybercrimes Act sound on paper and weakly enforced against mobile-money fraud. It calls for judicial warrants before communications are intercepted.

2026-10-10-tza-eanso-lga-cybersecurity-u.summary: A legal study finds that the security duties in Tanzania's e-Government Act are not tied to accountability in local government authorities, and that audits keep finding unauthorised access to council systems.

2026-10-10-tza-moh-data-use-partnership-.summary: Tanzania's health ministry describes its Data Use Partnership, a programme run with an international partner that has set up a digital health centre, a health enterprise architecture and an administrative-area registry covering more than 12,000 villages.

2026-10-10-tza-serikali-yawataka-wasafir.summary: Tanzania's Deputy Minister for Communication and IT, Switbert Mkama, called on parcel and express courier companies on 10 October 2026, World Post Day, to register and connect their tracking systems to national tracking and information-exchange systems. He commended couriers already linking to the Communication Monitoring System overseen by the regulator TCRA.

2026-10-10-uga-blogs-plan-now-for-infras.summary: Godfrey Mutabazi, director of Net Studios Africa, argues in a New Vision opinion column that Uganda needs a 10–15-year national compute and data-centre programme. He notes that the national backbone connects more than 1,600 government sites and that the 2025/26–2029/30 strategic plan provides for a third national data centre in Entebbe, with disaster recovery in Jinja.

2026-10-10-uga-eprc-ai-opportunities-fea.summary: A Ugandan think-tank blog weighs the risk that AI chatbots weaken learning against the risk of unequal access, and asks for an education chapter in the national AI strategy.

2026-10-10-uga-judiciary-cleans-case-rec.summary: Uganda's Judiciary is reconciling physical case files with its existing case administration system in nine courts, including Mpigi High Court, from 6 to 16 October 2026. The exercise prepares those courts to move onto the Electronic Court Case Management Information System (ECCMIS). No go-live date is given.

2026-10-10-xwa-seneplus-ia-afrique-franc.summary: A long read on the AI guidelines six francophone West African countries published together: seven principles and five ways of putting them into effect, with formal national adoption still to come. It notes that the size of the proposed AI fund is stated inconsistently.

2026-10-10-zaf-sundaytimes-2026-10-10-pu.summary: South Africa's universal service agency is consulting on whether to update the 2010 determination that defines universal access and universal service. Its discussion document sets out three options and leans towards a targeted revision; it creates no new funding or licence obligations.

2026-10-10-zaf-sundaytimes-usaasa-needy-.summary: The Universal Service and Access Agency of South Africa has invited public comment on a discussion document on who should qualify as a 'needy person' for subsidised access to communications services, who should apply and how subsidies should be paid, reported on 10 October 2026. The consultation, under section 88 of the Electronic Communications Act, sets no income threshold. No comment deadline is given.

2026-10-10-zwe-heraldonline-government-m.summary: Zimbabwe's ICT minister said the government is working to end fragmented digital systems across public bodies, and called for common standards so that citizens are not asked for the same information twice.

2026-10-11-ago-deliberacao-sobre-process.summary: Angola's data protection agency publishes its register of fines: 15 sanctions between 2022 and 2026, from US$75,000 to US$525,000, with banks, telecoms operators, the national airline and the Luanda water utility among those penalised. The largest 2026 fine was for storing personal data in a cloud abroad without authorisation.

2026-10-11-alchourouk-khadamat-app-app-s.summary: Tunisia's communication technologies ministry released its Khadamat public-services app on a second mobile platform, after an Android release at the end of August. It is reached through the e-Houwiya digital identity and covers civil-status records, driving licence and vehicle data, traffic fines, inspection bookings, health-insurance and social-security services and e-payments.

2026-10-11-bj-lanation-ia-images-retouch.summary: A learner prosecuted for circulating altered photographs of his teacher appeared before Benin's economic crimes and terrorism court on 8 October. The newspaper sets out the digital code's penalty for publishing a doctored image of a person without consent: five years in prison and a fine of FCFA 25 million.

2026-10-11-btw-afrinic-policy-petition-b.summary: An analysis of the second draft of AFRINIC's policy-process guidelines finds that its petition route, which lets the working group seek ratification of a policy, opens only when no operative Board exists. It needs 15 supporters from three subregions and still depends on a change to the Bylaws.

2026-10-11-caf-acdd-agence-presentation.summary: The Central African Republic's digital development agency sets out its own footing: a public industrial and commercial establishment created by a law of June 2023, with a mandate to implement the national digital strategy. The page gives no budget, staffing or activity figures.

2026-10-11-citizen-za-novazi-pay-or-cons.summary: A Stellenbosch law lecturer argues that South Africa's data-protection, consumer and competition laws are too fragmented to police platforms that make users choose between paying a subscription and surrendering personal data. The study, in a law review, calls for reform.

2026-10-11-cod-7sur7-gouvernement-annonc.summary: DR Congo's posts and telecommunications minister presented the commercial launch of 5G to the Council of Ministers on 9 October, as a new source of state revenue and a way to improve service quality. Deployment is to begin in urban areas; no operator, spectrum assignment or launch date was given.

2026-10-11-dza-lechodalgerie-plf-2027-e-.summary: Algeria's draft 2027 finance law proposes a 10% tax reduction until the end of 2028 for flat-rate and professional taxpayers who take at least half their receipts electronically. It would also require resident and non-resident e-commerce platforms to register with the tax authority and declare transactions yearly, on pain of a DA 1 million fine. The bill is not yet adopted.

2026-10-11-egy-vetogate-real-estate-regi.summary: Egypt's Digital Egypt platform now offers notarisation and real-estate registry services online. Citizens can draft powers of attorney, check the status of computerised transactions, look up registered contracts, book appointments at notary offices and request a mobile notary unit.

2026-10-11-gha-myjoyonline-bog-develops-.summary: The Bank of Ghana is drafting a directive on the use of artificial intelligence by financial institutions, its governor told the banks' annual meeting. The Bank will also run thematic reviews of how banks have implemented its revised cyber and information security directive.

2026-10-11-guardian-nga-postcode-next-di.summary: A commentary on Nigeria's new eleven-character postcode, switched on by the postal service on 1 October, reports early users finding it accurate for some buildings and missing for others. It argues the code could serve commerce, banking and lending as a proof of address if coverage is completed.

2026-10-11-mdg-2424-e-pasipaoro-online-p.summary: Madagascar's digital ministry said its online passport application portal is being tested. Applicants will be able to file, pay and track a first application, renewal or replacement online, while biometric capture and signature remain in person; no launch date was given.

2026-10-11-nga-thisday-galaxy-backbone-d.summary: Nigeria's state network operator said more than 30 federal ministries, departments and agencies have moved onto one platform for paperless approval of documents and memos, and promised wider adoption. It gave no list of agencies and no target; customers at the same event pressed for faster complaint handling.

2026-10-11-osiris-sen-marches-publics-ia.summary: An opinion article argues that Senegal should allow generative artificial intelligence in public procurement but require its use to be declared. The author says no Senegalese text now governs the use of artificial intelligence in public purchasing, and that the 2008 data protection law predates the technology.

2026-10-11-uga-how-scammers-are-stealing.summary: Uganda's financial services providers reported 6,533 fraud cases to regulators between January and August 2026, with about Ush23.5 billion lost of Ush67 billion targeted, on an industry consortium's figures. About 95% of reported cases involve mobile transactions, and few court cases end in conviction.

2026-10-11-uga-nilepost-land-titles-digi.summary: Uganda's minister of state for lands, Harriet Ntabazi, said new digital systems let land-title applicants enter their data at district level and have titles printed without travelling between offices. She said some landowners had paid more than Shs2.5 million to surveyors and land boards, and that surveyors will be registered in the ministry's database.

2026-10-11-world-bank-nga-2026-private-c.summary: The World Bank Group says it is helping mobilise up to US$5.79 billion of private financing in Nigeria in its 2026 financial year, through policy reform, investment platforms, guarantees and commercial lending. The national open-access fibre project is among the investments it names.

2026-10-11-xaf-atu-tespok-ixp-roadmap.summary: The African Telecommunications Union and the Technology Service Providers Association of Kenya (TESPOK) published a joint roadmap to strengthen internet exchange points in Africa. It builds on their assessment counting about 57 operational exchanges in 36 countries as of mid-2025, and proposes a continental coordination body, a model national framework and an IXP development fund. No funding amount is given.

2026-10-11-zaf-applesandoranges-agsa-sit.summary: South Africa's Auditor-General found that 2,076 of about 7,800 sites on the state IT agency's network ran below 10Mbps and that 294 government facilities were still on copper, in its audit of the communications department for 2025/26. The state broadband programme also fell short of its target of 14,742 sites for the year.

2026-10-11-zaf-dailymaverick-local-ai-po.summary: A commentary argues that South Africa's revised artificial intelligence policy must settle who controls data, computing capacity and models, and proposes pooling them regionally. It is opinion, written as AI systems become more autonomous.

2026-10-11-zaf-enca-creecy-trn-dormant-b.summary: South Africa's transport minister said 300,000 dormant traffic register numbers have been blocked, about half of those found to be fraudulent. Holders of the rest have been asked to verify their details with Home Affairs, and about 8,000 have come forward.

2026-10-11-zaf-sanews-asylum-court-guida.summary: South Africa's government will ask the courts for a supervisory order on implementing the Constitutional Court's July 2026 asylum judgment. Home Affairs is to introduce an online intention-registration and appointment system by 10 November 2026, with assisted registration at Refugee Reception Offices.

2026-10-11-zaf-sanews-home-affairs-biome.summary: South Africa's home affairs minister said a biometric online platform for asylum applications is to be operating by 10 November 2026, checking applicants' biometrics against earlier rejected claims and verifying their travel documents. He put the backlog of asylum appeals at about 120,000, a figure he said would be confirmed.

2026-10-11-zaf-sanews-transport-amend-re.summary: South Africa's transport department plans to amend the road traffic regulations so that traffic register number certificates, learner's licences and driving licences no longer count as identification. A traffic register number would be valid only as long as the passport and permit it was issued on, and the draft is to be gazetted for 30 days of comment.

2026-10-11-zwe-why-zim-needs-real-time-t.summary: An opinion article argues that Zimbabwe's telecommunications regulator should move from periodic audits of service quality, based on operators' submitted data and scheduled drive tests, to continuous automated monitoring. It says the regulator's quarterly reports show high compliance while users experience dropped calls and outages.

2026-10-12-agenceecofin-centrafrique-rdc.summary: The digital-economy ministers of the Central African Republic and DR Congo agreed in Moscow on 8 October on the need to carry out a fibre interconnection between the two countries, which would give the Central African Republic a third international route, toward the submarine cable landing at Moanda. No timetable or financing was announced.

2026-10-12-ago-minttics-apresenta-estrat.summary: Angola's telecommunications ministry presented the National Cybersecurity Strategy, approved by Presidential Decree 256/25 of 3 December 2025, at the CyberSecur Summit in Luanda on 12 October 2026. Policy director Hecdiantro Mena said a national commission will be formed to prepare, within 180 days, the conditions for setting up the National Cybersecurity Centre. No budget is given.

2026-10-12-ben-prix-simplification-commu.summary: Benin's government launched a presidential National Administrative Simplification Prize on 12 October 2026, inviting public servants, citizens and businesses to propose simpler procedures, including digitisation and data sharing between administrations. Submissions are open from 29 October to 12 November 2026. The prize supports Benin's target of having all procedures online by 2030.

2026-10-12-bwa-sundaystandard-hikvision-.summary: A newspaper investigation reports that two Chinese surveillance-camera makers have a substantial footprint in Botswana, from the police surveillance network to a nationwide banking CCTV system and public facilities. Only the opening of the article is held; the detail is behind a paywall.

2026-10-12-civ-senat-vote-electronique.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's Senate opened its second ordinary session of 2026 with attendance recorded in real time instead of a roll call, amendments filed online and proceedings archived automatically. Electronic voting was trialled the same day, with training for senators on 13 to 16 October.

2026-10-12-dza-agence-ecofin-fibre-optiq.summary: Algeria's fibre-to-the-home subscriptions passed 4 million in early October, from 53,000 in June 2020, on the posts minister's figures. The monthly price of an offer of 100 Mbit/s or more has fallen 76%, and the target is more than 4.4 million by the end of the year.
