2026-10-15-sen-us-health-agreement-perso.summary: Senegal's National Assembly is to examine the health memorandum signed with the United States on 13 March 2026, over the protection of personal data, under one of five parliamentary inquiries the prime minister announced. The US embassy says Senegal committed to co-invest US$27.3 million in health over five years under the agreement.

2026-10-15-senegal-targets-postal-sector.summary: Senegal's telecoms and digital ministry aims to restructure the postal sector by 2027 under its New Deal Technologique, refocusing the state-owned La Poste on digital and trusted services, e-commerce logistics and private partnerships. The minister set out the plan at World Post Day celebrations.

2026-10-15-shore-africa-ifc-proposes-35m.summary: The IFC disclosed a proposed sustainability-linked loan of up to $35 million to the wholesale operator WIOCC, for more subsea cable capacity, terrestrial fibre in Southern and West Africa and data-centre capacity. Board consideration is projected for 13 November 2026.

2026-10-15-sle-owlpress-national-id-card.summary: Sierra Leone MP Alpha Ben Mansaray, deputy parliamentary spokesman, asked the government on 15 October 2026 to implement the Tripartite Committee's recommendation 15 and subsidise national identity cards. The NCRA raised the standard card fee from NLe 145 to NLe 165 in February 2026; he proposes NLe 50, which he states is his own figure, not policy.

2026-10-15-south-africa-ai-policy-halluc.summary: One of the two South African officials suspended over the draft national AI policy that cited invented sources has resigned, and disciplinary proceedings continue against the other. The communications minister said cabinet will finalise a replacement before the end of March 2027, with public consultation expected from April.

2026-10-15-ssd-salc-oral-statement-cyber.summary: The Southern Africa Litigation Centre told the African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights that the region's decade of striking down sedition, criminal defamation and false-news offences is being reversed, through routine surveillance, new cybercrime laws and prosecutions under them.

2026-10-15-ssd-ssra-zambian-delegation-d.summary: A Zambian finance ministry delegation visited the South Sudan Revenue Authority to study its e-Tax, e-Customs and SSCAFFA revenue platforms, which the commissioner general credits with raising monthly collections. The platforms' technical contractor says it does not collect, hold or control government funds.

2026-10-15-tcd-aspa-internet-cher-fractu.summary: A Chadian commentary written during the Central Africa Internet Governance Forum in N'Djamena argues that the cost of getting online, not the official talk of digital sovereignty and AI, decides who takes part in the digital economy.

2026-10-15-tza-dailynews-pm-saccos-digit.summary: Opening the SACCA Congress in Dar es Salaam on 15 October 2026, Prime Minister Mwigulu Nchemba said Tanzania's SACCOS run 231 mobile-money agency arrangements and five offer mobile apps, with about 119,000 app and USSD users and 3.5 million transactions. He said only just over one in four SACCOS has a core banking system, and cited 72% adult mobile-money use from the 2023 financial inclusion report.

2026-10-15-tza-guardian-vp-govt-digital-.summary: Tanzania's Vice President directed the youth and labour ministries to merge the YES youth-enrolment system, the Ajira Portal and the Kazi Portal into one interoperable network, after hearing that YES had registered over 22,000 young people but listed only seven opportunities. He asked for an integration report within a week.

2026-10-15-uga-ict-ministry-koica-digita.summary: Uganda's ICT ministry and the Korea International Cooperation Agency discussed widening their digital-transformation partnership to ICT skills, local innovation and technology in public services. No new agreement or sum was announced.

2026-10-15-uga-mediacentre-ministry-of-t.summary: Uganda's trade minister Sanjay Tanna told a press conference on 15 October 2026 that his ministry will introduce a digital mark for online sellers to protect consumers, expected within a few months. The ministry is also building a database of sellers.

2026-10-15-uga-mediacentre-statement-afr.summary: Uganda's trade minister issued a statement ahead of a Kampala symposium on building Africa's digital single market, arguing that the country must help shape the rules for cross-border digital trade, payments and delivery. The symposium is set for 22-23 October 2026.

2026-10-15-xaf-ifc-sii-51853-cauris-thir.summary: IFC disclosed a proposed loan of up to US$7.5 million, capped at 10% of fund size, in the senior tranche of Cauris Finance's Third Wave Fund, a debt fund targeting US$75 million (hard cap US$100 million) that will lend to tech-enabled lenders in Africa's mobility and small-business markets. The loan is pending approval, with a board date projected for 30 November 2026.

2026-10-15-zaf-lifestyleandtech-telkom-i.summary: Telkom announced a R20 million partnership with South Africa's Electoral Commission to provide connectivity and technical support for the 4 November 2026 local government elections, carried on Openserve's national fibre network.

2026-10-15-zaf-pmg-nw5143-postbank-bank-.summary: In a written reply dated 15 October 2026, South Africa's Communications Minister said Postbank has been directed by the Prudential Authority to submit a new bank authorisation application, with no submission date set. The reply said Postbank paid grants to about 1.9 million beneficiaries as at September 2026, and that its SASSA agreement remains in force under Constitutional Court directions.

2026-10-15-zwe-hanyani-data-protection-a.summary: Panellists at a media policy dialogue in Zimbabwe said the Cyber and Data Protection Act, passed to curb cybercrime and protect women and children online, is being used against journalists.

2026-10-15-zwe-herald-potraz-critical-in.summary: Zimbabwe's telecoms regulator is developing a Cybersecurity Framework for Critical Infrastructure Protection, its draft regulation cited as a governance example at a regulators' follow-up meeting in Nairobi. The regulator also restated that data controllers must be licensed under the Cyber and Data Protection Act.

2026-10-15-zwe-herald-zimra-ataf-exchang.summary: ZIMRA's acting commissioner general told the continental exchange-of-information conference it co-hosted with ATAF in Victoria Falls that Zimbabwe deposited its ratification of the Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters on 31 August 2026, in force for it from 1 January 2027. He said ZIMRA is preparing for peer review and for automatic exchange of information.

2026-10-16-ago-pti-estado-da-nacao-telec.summary: In his State of the Nation address, President João Lourenço said Angola added more than 1,300 km of national broadband fibre between 2022 and 2026 and opened free Internet access points in all 18 provinces, reaching about eight million people. He also cited a National Cloud and government data centre, an approved National Cybersecurity Strategy, the World Bank-financed Angola Digital Acceleration Project (PADA), and a UN e-government score of 0.41 in 2024.

2026-10-16-agp-guinee-gbessia-sensibilis.summary: A sensitisation session on WARDIP, the 2023-2028 West Africa regional digital integration programme, was held at Gbessia town hall on 16 October 2026 under Guinea's digital economy ministry. Participants were told that the submarine-cable landing station and cable laying may affect all 13 communes of Conakry and the prefectures of Coyah, Forécariah, Dubréka and Boffa, and what is planned to limit environmental and social harm.

2026-10-16-atu-secures-endorsements-49-a.summary: The African Telecommunications Union says all 49 African Common Proposals for the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference in Doha (9-27 November 2026) now have the more than 15 country endorsements each needs, with Ghana making 23 endorsing states. The proposals cover affordable connectivity, cybersecurity, fair access to satellite orbits, AI for development and protection of submarine cables.

2026-10-16-bdi-iso-member-bbn.summary: ISO's member page lists the Bureau Burundais de Normalisation et Contrôle de la Qualité (BBN) as Burundi's member body. As read in October 2026, it participates in 11 ISO technical committees and observes 28.

2026-10-16-bdi-setic-services-institutio.summary: The home page of Burundi's government ICT secretariat, SETIC, sets out its role coordinating national ICT policy projects. Its listed services for public bodies include software development, cybersecurity, a network operations centre, hosting of national platforms and network maintenance.

2026-10-16-bdi-wearetech-strategie-natio.summary: Burundi's Council of Ministers adopted a National Cybersecurity Strategy on 14 October 2026, after work begun by a government commission in 2020 and a World Bank-funded PAFEN consultancy from 2023. The strategy provides for a legal and institutional framework, protection of critical infrastructure and public data, and a national incident-response team.

2026-10-16-bfa-aconews-gendarmerie-cib-a.summary: Burkina Faso's territorial gendarmerie brigades may now issue the AES biometric identity card (CIB-AES) and certify administrative documents. Enrolment still requires a birth-certificate extract or nationality certificate.

2026-10-16-bfa-insd-licence-donnees-ouve.summary: Burkina Faso's national statistics institute, INSD, publishes an open data licence granting free, worldwide, non-exclusive reuse of its data, commercial use included. Users must credit INSD, and the licence is governed by Burkinabè law.

2026-10-16-bfa-iso-member-abnorm.summary: ISO lists ABNORM as Burkina Faso's member body and sole national standards developer. It participates in 9 ISO technical committees and observes 5.

2026-10-16-bic-uemoa-8e-rencontre-annuel.summary: At the 8th annual meeting of the UEMOA credit information bureau, speakers said most microfinance institutions fall outside the duty to report to the bureau: in Burkina Faso, 20 of 120 licensed institutions met the FCFA 2bn threshold at the end of 2025. Panellists called for reporting by all microfinance institutions and wider use of client consent, which a banker said is now required for bureau access across the eight UEMOA states.

2026-10-16-biometricupdate-public-servic.summary: In an interview, ID4Africa chairman Joseph Atick argues that digital public infrastructure should be built as the delivery of specific public services demands it, not ahead of use on projected demand. He uses South Africa's social grant payments, which link Home Affairs, SASSA and the Reserve Bank, as his example.

2026-10-16-bj-tarification-des-actes-jur.summary: Benin's finance and justice ministers set fees for 109 documents issued by the courts and the justice ministry, now payable only online. A criminal-record extract costs FCFA 1,900 and a naturalisation application FCFA 50,000.

2026-10-16-caf-undp-ungm-fintech-platfor.summary: UNDP in the Central African Republic is seeking an individual consultant to write the functional and technical specification for POST CASH, a national fintech platform. The contract is 30 working days over two months in Bangui, and bids close on 25 October 2026.

2026-10-16-caf-wb-op00475730-mobile-mone.summary: A World Bank procurement notice dated 16 October 2026 invites bids for kits to set up mobile-money agent points in the interior of the Central African Republic. The goods tender, under the Public Sector Digital Governance Project, has an estimated value of USD 200,000 and a bid deadline of 13 November 2026.

2026-10-16-city-power-electricity-theft-.summary: Johannesburg utility City Power has put out a tender for near-real-time monitoring of prepaid electricity purchases, aimed at non-technical losses of R3.96bn in 2024/25, or 20.85% of electricity bought. Bidders may propose AI for theft prediction and customer risk scoring, but outputs must be explainable, auditable and compliant with POPIA, with humans making decisions and the data staying City Power's. Experts quoted say prepaid meters show token sales, not consumption, which limits what monitoring can find.

2026-10-16-civ-afrimag-ouattara-administ.summary: Afrimag reported on Côte d'Ivoire's digital administration plans to 2029. It cites a USD 195 million government digital services programme with 23 platforms, whose first phase closed in June 2026, and health information systems in 268 facilities. The figures are the outlet's own and are not sourced.

2026-10-16-civ-la-cote-d-ivoire-deploie-.summary: Côte d'Ivoire has deployed mHealth One, an AI version of its community health platform, in the five health districts of the Gontougo region, with UNICEF support; community health workers have used it since 5 October 2026. It gives workers offline treatment guidance, flags inconsistent data and inactive agents for supervisors, and lets officials query data in plain French.

2026-10-16-cmr-iso-member-anor.summary: ISO lists Cameroon's Agence des Normes et de la Qualité (ANOR) as a member body. As read in October 2026, it participates in 4 technical committees and observes 41.

2026-10-16-cmr-leconomie-e-gov-africa-su.summary: At the first e-Gov Africa Summit in Yaoundé, Cameroon's public service ministry reported that its AIGLE staff and payroll platform has processed over 342,049 promotion and tenure acts automatically since January 2025. It cited over 6.4 million logins, over 3 million payslip notifications and secure e-signature in 37 of 40 administrations.

2026-10-16-cmr-minfopra-aigles-egova-pap.summary: Cameroon's public service minister Joseph LE presented AIGLES, the state personnel and payroll system, at the E-GOVA Africa summit in Yaoundé on 15 October 2026. He said it is over 80% deployed and handles recruitment, careers, promotion, retirement and pay for more than 250,000 civil servants.

2026-10-16-cmr-orange-business-data-cent.summary: Orange Business Cameroon describes its data centre, open since May 2017, as Tier III+ with 340 racks in two server rooms. The company claims 99.82% availability and two separate medium-voltage grid feeds; no certification is named.

2026-10-16-cod-wearetech-plateforme-inte.summary: DR Congo's digital economy and foreign affairs ministers met on 14 October 2026 to speed up an integrated platform for processing electronic visas. The project is already in the government's 2026-2028 medium-term budget framework and is separate from the migration directorate's existing online visa application portal.

2026-10-16-cog-iso-member-aconoq.summary: ISO lists ACONOQ, created by a 2015 law, as the Republic of Congo's national standards body and ISO member. It is a member of ARSO and an Affiliate Plus of the IEC, and participates in 2 ISO technical committees.

2026-10-16-connectingafrica-demand-led-t.summary: At CollectiveXchange 2026 in Johannesburg, Sand Technologies CEO Fred Swaniker called for training scaled to what employers and the economy need, rather than tied to guaranteed jobs. Communications Minister Solly Malatsi put the digital economy at 7-8% of South Africa's GDP and said it could exceed 15%.

2026-10-16-dza-techreviewafrica-roblox-p.summary: Algeria has reached a preliminary agreement with Roblox on a programme to train Algerian video game developers, announced by Sid Ali Zerrouki. It comes with child-protection conditions: wider parental controls, fast-track reporting channels, and the platform's chat feature kept switched off in Algeria until safeguards are judged sufficient.

2026-10-16-eac-e-commerce-digital-trade-.summary: At a regional e-commerce meeting in Dar es Salaam on 13-15 October 2026, EAC Partner States updated the baseline data in the monitoring tool for the EAC E-Commerce Strategy. They also named priority regional actions on consumer protection, online dispute resolution and readiness for the AfCFTA Protocol on Digital Trade.

2026-10-16-fg-to-deploy-3700-telecom-tow.summary: Communications Minister Bosun Tijani commissioned the first tower of Nigeria's National Universal Communications Access Programme in Bende, Abia State, on 16 October 2026. The programme plans 3,700 towers to reach about 20 million Nigerians without phone or internet service, and the Deputy Speaker named 16 more Bende locations needing coverage.

2026-10-16-fpa-liberia-cybersecurity-tie.summary: Liberia was admitted to the African Network of Cybersecurity Authorities and SMART Africa, together with Malawi, Lesotho, Mali and Egypt, during Morocco Cyber Security Week in Rabat. Liberia's telecoms minister and the head of Morocco's DGSSI also agreed to pursue a memorandum of understanding on cybersecurity capacity building and technical help.

2026-10-16-fpa-naymote-urges-legislature.summary: Liberian civil society group Naymote, in a statement of 15 October 2026, urged the Legislature to tighten the proposed national ID agreement, which it values at US$52 million. It asks for full disclosure of financing, fees and contract terms, an independent value-for-money review, government ownership of identity data, free first-time enrolment and public hearings, and says the electoral commission must keep control of the voters' roll.

2026-10-16-gabon-aninf-octopus-2026-cybe.summary: A delegation from Gabon's digital infrastructure agency, ANINF, attended the Council of Europe's Octopus 2026 cybercrime conference in Strasbourg on 14-16 October. ANINF says it used the meeting to build expertise on electronic evidence and to look at Gabon joining the Budapest Convention on Cybercrime.

2026-10-16-ghana-2800-telecom-site-build.summary: Communications Minister Samuel Nartey George said Ghana will build 800 new cell sites and upgrade 2,000 more within the year across MTN and Telecel networks, with better coverage expected from late 2026 into early 2027. He also said more spectrum had been released in the past two years than in the previous two decades.

2026-10-16-gmb-gamtel-co-location-facili.summary: Gambian operator GAMTEL offers ISPs and small businesses space for servers and network equipment at its 43 sites and towers. Its listed prices include a GMD 3,000 installation fee and GMD 1,000 per square metre of floor space a month.

2026-10-16-gmb-gbos-downloads.summary: The Gambia Bureau of Statistics' downloads page indexes its GDP, price and trade series up to 2025 and its household, health, labour-force and SDG survey reports. Microdata are offered for several surveys, including the DHS and MICS.

2026-10-16-gq-gobierno-cnedoge-moderniza.summary: Equatorial Guinea's Vice-President Nguema Obiang Mangue authorised an upgrade of the systems at CNEDOGE, which issues identity cards and passports, after a report that much of its equipment dates from 2017-2018. Officials are to assess the installation with the supplier CETIS and cost the work, and CETIS was asked for new card and passport designs.

2026-10-16-gsma-madagascar-digital-refor.summary: A GSMA report launched in Antananarivo says four reforms could bring about 1.13 million more people in Madagascar onto mobile internet and add MGA 4.1 trillion to GDP by 2031: cheaper smartphones through lower levies and duties, a costed rural connectivity plan, lower sector taxes, and voice services in Malagasy. Unique mobile internet penetration was 14.3% in 2025. A companion GSMA report finds spectrum pricing and licensing reform across Africa could add more than US$120 billion to GDP between 2026 and 2035.

2026-10-16-itweb-digital-identity-failur.summary: This feature uses earlier incidents to show how identity verification failures can shut people out of several services at once: South Africa's Home Affairs reported failure rates of up to 50% in March 2025, and Nigeria's regulator ordered blocked SIM lines restored in July 2024. Practitioners quoted call for human review, ways to correct records across connected systems, and auditable AI decisions.

2026-10-16-itweb-ethiopia-cross-border-p.summary: Ethiopia has joined the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System, letting its financial institutions make instant cross-border payments in local currencies with counterparts elsewhere in Africa. The National Bank of Ethiopia reports that digital transaction volumes grew by 146% a year from 2020 to 2025, and the country received $8.2 billion in remittances in 2025/26.

2026-10-16-ken-education-data-systems-sw.summary: Kenya's Auditor-General found that the NEMIS learner database, replaced by KEMIS in September 2025, under-counted pupils in national schools and left them underfunded. A parliamentary committee resolved to summon the Education Cabinet Secretary.

2026-10-16-ken-iso-kebs-member-page.summary: ISO lists the Kenya Bureau of Standards (KEBS), set up under the Standards Act in 1974, as Kenya's member body. It holds one technical committee secretariat, participates in 129 committees and observes 177.

2026-10-16-ken-mombasa-tuk-tuk-fines-dig.summary: Two Mombasa tuk-tuk associations went to the High Court against the county's camera-based instant traffic fines, which block operators' stickers on the county portal until they are paid. They argue that no published law authorises the system or its capture of passengers' images; the case returns on 9 November.

2026-10-16-lbr-liberianinvestigator-dopo.summary: Liberian Senator Francis Dopoh, chair of the Senate Committee on Posts and Telecommunications, told the Senate on 15 October 2026 that the Executive is enforcing the new Cybercrime Law before setting up the Cybersecurity Council and specialised cybercrime team it requires. He asked the Senate to notify the Executive and demand corrective measures, following the reported arrest of a man accused of posting AI-generated images of the Vice President.

2026-10-16-lbr-liberiapublicradio-senate.summary: Liberia's Senate sent President Boakai's proposed US$52 million build-operate-transfer concession with Germany's OeSD International for a national ID, civil registry and vital statistics system (NIDCRVS) to three committees. They are to report to plenary within two weeks, before any vote on ratification.

2026-10-16-lbr-newdawn-house-scrutinizes.summary: Liberia's House of Representatives has sent a proposed US$52 million concession with OeSD International for a national ID and digital civil registry to a joint committee, which has two weeks to report. This account dates the President's communication to plenary on 15 October 2026 and says the build-operate-transfer system would hold demographic and biometric data on up to 10 million people.

2026-10-16-liberianobserver-house-review.summary: Liberia's House of Representatives referred President Boakai's proposed concession with OeSD International for a combined national ID and civil registration system to a joint committee, with 14 days to report; the referral is not ratification. Under the build-operate-transfer deal, OeSD would build and run a system issuing biometric ID numbers and cards and recording births, deaths and marriages, then hand it to the government.

2026-10-16-lso-beyond-the-harvest-can-ag.summary: The Reporter, on 16 October 2026, covered a weather-index agricultural insurance pilot in Lesotho during the 2025/2026 season, run by the agriculture ministry's SADP II with the World Food Programme, LNIG Hollard and African Risk Capacity. It covered maize and beans in Mafeteng, Mohale's Hoek and Quthing, with more than US$1.2 million in insured value reported.

2026-10-16-lso-iso-lsi-member-page.summary: ISO's record for the Lesotho Standards Institution shows it observing 2 ISO technical committees and 3 policy committees, as read in October 2026.

2026-10-16-lso-rsl-individual-taxpayer-r.summary: Revenue Services Lesotho's online registration form for individual taxpayers asks for the applicant's Lesotho identification number, its expiry date and a copy of the card. A passport or foreign ID can be given instead where the person has one.

2026-10-16-mar-crvslaws-vital-statistics.summary: A legal profile on the CRVS Laws database finds that Morocco's law gives vital statistics roles to the High Commission for Planning, the Interior Ministry and the Health Ministry. Its analysis notes that a 2022 decree lets the Interior Ministry produce statistics from civil status data or share that data with other bodies, but that it neither produces UN-standard vital statistics nor shares the data with the High Commission.

2026-10-16-mar-maroc-ma-nomination-nouve.summary: King Mohammed VI presided over the swearing-in of Morocco's new government at the Royal Palace in Rabat on 16 October 2026, according to the government portal. Ahmed Rahhou heads the ministry covering artificial intelligence and digital affairs, with Aicha Guellaa as delegated minister for administration reform.

2026-10-16-morocco-appoints-ahmed-rahhou.summary: King Mohammed VI swore in Ahmed Rahhou on 16 October 2026 as Minister of Artificial Intelligence, Digital Transformation and Administration Reform in Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri's new government. He replaces Amal El Fallah Seghrouchni, and the new ministry brings AI, digital transformation and administrative reform under one portfolio.

2026-10-16-moz-bnews-centro-pronto-vfs-g.summary: Mozambique's digital transformation agency ATDI opened the Centro Pronto service centre in Maputo in October 2026, built with India's VFS Global. It combines an online portal, self-service kiosks and assisted counters, initially for passports, identity cards, driving licences and foreigners' residence documents.

2026-10-16-mrt-iso-onanor-member.summary: ISO lists Mauritania's ONANOR as a correspondent member, participating in 5 technical committees and observing 10 as of October 2026. The page's description still names an older directorate under the mines and industry ministry.

2026-10-16-mus-pmo-cabinet-highlights-20.summary: Mauritius's Cabinet noted on 16 October 2026 that 162 Safe City cameras on 75 sites were damaged in the riots that began on 12 October. It also noted that the Mauritius Revenue Authority and ATAF will host the first Digital Tax Administration Conference on 19-21 October 2026.

2026-10-16-mus-topfm-sil-tcs-mou-digital.summary: Mauritius's State Informatics Limited and India's Tata Consultancy Services signed a memorandum of understanding on 15 October 2026 covering digital solutions, skills transfer and modernisation of public and private services. ICT minister Avinash Ramtohul presented it as part of Mauritius-India technology cooperation; no value or timetable was given.

2026-10-16-myjoyonline-bold-ambitions-fr.summary: In an opinion piece, cybersecurity and AI governance specialist Victor Awaga asks whether Ghana is ready for the risks of its push into AI and data centres, including the US$250 million AI Computing Centre announced in April 2026. He points to strain on the power grid, thin cybersecurity capacity, and data protection and cyber laws written before generative AI and large data centres.

2026-10-16-myjoyonline-ghana-hosts-un-ne.summary: Ghana will host the signing ceremony for the UN Convention on Negotiable Cargo Documents in Accra on 26 October 2026. The Ghana Shippers' Authority says the convention gives electronic bills of lading and similar documents the legal standing of paper ones, but that the benefits depend on ratification and readiness.

2026-10-16-nam-iso-nsi-member.summary: ISO lists the Namibian Standards Institution, set up under the Standards Act 2005, as Namibia's member body. As of October 2026 it participates in 21 technical committees and observes 23.

2026-10-16-nam-nampol-pushes-for-digital.summary: The Namibian Police has begun overhauling its E-Policing System after slow processing and intermittent interruptions, Acting Inspector-General Anne-Marie Nainda told New Era. The system, in use since 2014, spans 11 national databases including the N-ABIS fingerprint system, and no budget or timetable has been disclosed.

2026-10-16-nation-afyake-shutdown-65000-.summary: Murang'a Governor Irungu Kang'ata accuses Kenya's national government of switching off the county's AfyaKE hospital system ahead of the 30 October deadline to move to the national Tibabu system, leaving records for about 65,000 patients out of reach and stalling SHA claims. He says the system raised health revenue from Sh80 million to Sh800 million a year; the Ministry of Health says neither the county nor the developers applied for certification.

2026-10-16-nation-muranga-county-sues-st.summary: Murang'a County has petitioned Kenya's High Court against the Ministry of Health, the Digital Health Agency, the Health Cabinet Secretary, SHA and the Attorney-General after losing access to its Afya.KE health information system on 14 October 2026. It seeks orders restoring access and protecting clinical records across its more than 176 health facilities while the petition is heard.

2026-10-16-nigeria-phone-crackdown-ncc-c.summary: From 10 October 2026, Nigeria's communications regulator began texting owners of phones not verified under type approval that network access could be blocked after 30 days of active use. The checks run on the NCC's Device Management System against each phone's IMEI, and grey-market and overseas-bought phones are among those flagged. A registration route and official fees had not been clearly published by 16 October.

2026-10-16-odi-beyond-adoption-ai-produc.summary: In an ODI Global analysis, Alberto Lemma argues that AI may raise productivity in African firms while cutting the entry-level formal jobs that move workers out of the informal sector. He draws mainly on Kenya, where a World Bank survey estimates 42% of formal firms use some AI and call-centre work has been a first formal job for young people, and calls for targeted demand and training policies.

2026-10-16-rwa-ippis-developer-api.summary: Rwanda's public-sector HR platform, IPPIS, offers a REST API through which approved government partner systems can retrieve public servants' NID-verified profiles, education, work history and related records. Access requires partner credentials and bearer tokens.

2026-10-16-rwa-rsb-international-technic.summary: The Rwanda Standards Board lists the regional and international technical committees it sits on, including EAC standards committees. Among them, it is a participating member of the ISO/IEC JTC 1 subcommittee on IT service management (SC 40), an observer on JTC 1 and its security subcommittee SC 27, and a member of the EAC committee on IT standards.

2026-10-16-sadc-cyber-drill-cybercrime-c.summary: SADC, AfricaCERT and Angola's telecoms ministry held the seventh SADC Cyber Drill in Luanda on 5-9 October 2026, with 282 delegates testing incident response and cybercrime cooperation. The Secretariat reports that the number of operational national incident-response teams in the region has risen from 4 in 2018 to 13.

2026-10-16-sen-aps-e-osc-plateforme-ong-.summary: Senegal's Interior Ministry asked all NGOs and associations working in the country to register on its new e-OSC platform, which records their areas of work, projects, funding and beneficiaries. The ministry says the register will lead to NGO approval and association recognition being handled online, with training planned.

2026-10-16-sen-arcop-appel-eprocurement-.summary: Senegal's procurement regulator ARCOP told contracting authorities to load their 2027 procurement plans onto its APPEL e-procurement platform by 1 December 2026, ahead of general use from January 2027. It is training more than 325 contracting authorities and briefed ICT firms on the platform's electronic signature, encryption and timestamping.

2026-10-16-sen-kiriku-voice-challenge-ia.summary: AI Hub Senegal and the French embassy presented the results of the Kiriku Voice Challenge. It produced 210 hours of annotated Wolof, Pulaar and Serer speech and two openly published models, one for speech recognition and one for speech synthesis.

2026-10-16-sle-afcom-data-center-colocat.summary: Afcom describes its Freetown data centre as a privately owned, carrier-neutral Tier III facility offering rack, cage and cloud hosting. It claims 99.9% availability, with redundant generators able to run for two weeks without refuelling.

2026-10-16-sle-iso-slsb-member.summary: ISO lists the Sierra Leone Standards Bureau as a correspondent member since 2009. As of October 2026 it observes 7 ISO technical committees.

2026-10-16-sle-mof-dfmst-tier-iii-data-c.summary: Sierra Leone's Ministry of Finance set up its Directorate of Financial Management Systems and Technology in 2022 to run the ministry's ICT. The directorate operates a Tier III data centre that hosts ministry systems such as IFMIS and provides co-location for several financial-sector institutions.

2026-10-16-som-dalkom-colocation-web-hos.summary: Somali operator Dalkom offers colocation and hosting in its own data centres in Mogadishu and Nairobi, connected to a redundant 10 Gbps backbone. The company says it holds stakes in the EASSy cable and WIOCC.

2026-10-16-som-pch-soixp-directory-entry.summary: Packet Clearing House's directory lists the Somali Internet Exchange Point in Mogadishu as active, run by the National Communications Authority and established on 20 November 2018.

2026-10-16-som-wb-op00475480-api-gateway.summary: Somalia's Ministry of Communications and Technology is seeking expressions of interest from consulting firms to design and run a government API gateway, single sign-on and national digital government portal. The World Bank notice of 16 October 2026 falls under the Eastern Africa Regional Digital Integration Project, with responses due 29 October 2026.

2026-10-16-techcabal-hurdles-contactless.summary: This TechCabal feature asks why tap-to-pay has not caught on in Nigeria although electronic payments are widespread, starting from CashAfrica's 13 October rollout of mobile tap-to-pay across more than 350 Chicken Republic outlets. It sets that against earlier attempts such as PayAttitude in 2015 and Access Bank's Tap to Phone in 2025, and against the Lagos transport Cowry card, which works because tapping is built into boarding.

2026-10-16-techcabal-onafriq-shuts-niger.summary: Onafriq said on 16 October 2026 that it is closing Baxi, its Nigerian agent-banking business, after five years, citing inflation, naira depreciation, rising costs and the growth of instant account-to-account transfers. Baxi agents have been moved to another principal bank, and Onafriq will stay in Nigeria for payments and card issuing.

2026-10-16-techcabal-south-africa-digita.summary: At the CollectiveXChange 2026 summit in Johannesburg on 15 October, The Collective X, which coordinates South Africa's National Digital Skills Plan, reported R600 million mobilised in its Digital Skills Impact Fund and 4,000 beneficiaries so far, against a target of 500,000 young people in digital jobs by 2034. Yellowwoods estimated that reaching 20,000 more by 2028 would take R2.5 billion ($152 million) from existing skills funds, money not yet secured.

2026-10-16-techreview-crasa-smart-africa.summary: The Southern African regulators' association CRASA and Smart Africa have met to prepare a workshop in Gaborone on 20-22 October 2026 on implementing sub-regional roaming agreements and the One Africa Network. They also discussed capacity-building work with the Smart Africa Digital Academy.

2026-10-16-tgo-ecofin-voix-du-togo-colle.summary: Togo's digital transformation ministry launched Voix du Togo in October 2026, a three-year programme collecting voice and text data in national languages to train AI models, starting with Ewe, Kabiye and Moba. The target for each language is 50 hours of validated audio, 6,000 translated sentence pairs and at least 500 contributors; health, justice and administrative services are the intended uses.

2026-10-16-tgo-presidence-conseil-togo-c.summary: Togo and China signed thirteen agreements and memoranda in Beijing on 15 October 2026, two days after raising relations to a 'China-Togo community with a shared future for the new era'. They include cooperation on digital commerce and supply chains, an Authorised Economic Operator protocol between Togo's revenue office and Chinese customs, China Media Group partnerships with Télévision togolaise and partial cancellation of Togo's debt; a separate memorandum covers China's Global Security Initiative.

2026-10-16-thecitizen-uba-tanzania-launc.summary: UBA Tanzania has launched cross-border payments over the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System and says it is the first bank in Tanzania to sign up. Its customers can pay into other participating countries from shilling accounts at branches or through WhatsApp and Facebook, for a 2.5% fee capped at US$20, up to US$5,000 a transfer and US$10,000 a day.

2026-10-16-tun-datagovtn-portail-nationa.summary: Tunisia's national open data portal lists datasets by theme and publisher, with agriculture the largest theme, and shows nine recorded reuse cases. Its latest news item, from March 2026, is a workshop on the final draft of a national strategy for the governance and opening of public data.

2026-10-16-tun-innorpi-cooperation-inter.summary: INNORPI's own page sets out its international memberships: it represents Tunisia at ISO and the IEC and belongs to regional standards bodies including ARSO, AIDSMO, SMIIC and AFSEC. The page, which is undated, gives 20 ISO technical committees as a participating member and 148 as an observer.

2026-10-16-tun-iso-innorpi-iso-member-pa.summary: ISO lists INNORPI, which handles standards, certification and industrial property under Tunisia's industry ministry, as the country's member body. As of October 2026 it participates in 21 technical committees and observes 153.

2026-10-16-tun-leconomistemaghrebin-int-.summary: Tunisia's telecoms regulator INT found in its 2026 digital barometer that 85.9% of people aged 10 to 70 use the internet, 10.9 points more than in 2023, and that 47.9% of users use AI applications, ahead of e-commerce (36.9%) and online government services (26.5%). The face-to-face survey of 5,077 people ran from 15 May to 10 June 2026; fibre accounts for 4% of connections.

2026-10-16-tun-ooredoo-housing-data-cent.summary: Ooredoo Tunisie offers business hosting in a 188 m2 data centre it describes as built to the TIA-942 standard. Its stated provisions include two independent grid feeds, redundant UPS, generators with 50 hours' autonomy and a 99.95% availability guarantee.

2026-10-16-uga-monitor-uganda-champions-.summary: Ahead of a technology and intellectual property symposium on 22-23 October, Uganda's trade minister set out plans to back the AU's single digital market, including a trust mark for vetted online sellers and rules giving online buyers redress, to be rolled out in the EAC first. A Jumia-led e-commerce industry association and a call for a Consumer Protection Act were also presented.

2026-10-16-uga-watchdog-itms-preliminary.summary: Uganda's parliamentary physical infrastructure committee told Auditor General Edward Akol on 15 October 2026 to start a preliminary audit of the Intelligent Transport Management System digital number-plate project, run by a Russian firm, and report in writing the following Tuesday. Akol said he received the project agreement only on 13 October, and that the Office of the President calls the project an investor-financed pilot with no public funds spent.

2026-10-16-wearetech-afrique-du-sud-wise.summary: UK money-transfer firm Wise has received category 2 authorisation from the South African Reserve Bank to deal in foreign exchange and send money abroad under regulation. The approval date is not given; Wise already partners with Capitec.

2026-10-16-world-bank-cardip-265m-digita.summary: The World Bank is preparing CARDIP, a regional digital integration programme for the six CEMAC countries, with an estimated cost of $265.5 million and financing not yet approved. Appraisal is set for 3 November 2026 and board consideration for 12 April 2027, with CEMAC as the implementing body. The first phase would fund broadband and cross-border links in the Central African Republic, Congo, Equatorial Guinea and Gabon, alongside work on ID, payments and data exchange systems.

2026-10-16-xaf-gsma-spectrum-policy-in-a.summary: A GSMA Intelligence study finds African mobile operators held on average 570 MHz of spectrum below 7 GHz at the end of 2025, against 750 MHz elsewhere, and paid 24% more per unit. Only 9 of 54 countries have licences of at least 20 years or a published spectrum roadmap. It estimates pricing and licensing reforms could add more than $120 billion to Africa's GDP between 2026 and 2035.

2026-10-16-xwa-beninwebtv-bceao-fintech-.summary: The BCEAO opened applications for the first cohort of its Financial Innovation Laboratory, a regulatory sandbox set up on 8 April 2025, in a call published on 14 October 2026. UEMOA fintechs and licensed institutions can apply until 30 November 2026 for supervised tests of three to six months; crypto-asset projects are excluded and a successful test does not confer a licence.

2026-10-17-ago-governo-cria-equipa-para-.summary: Angola's Minister of State for Economic Coordination set up a technical group from ten state bodies, given 180 days, to build the central beneficial-ownership register (CRBE) required by the new beneficial-ownership law. The Justice secretary of state coordinates, with the Financial Intelligence Unit as deputy, as Angola remains on the FATF grey list it rejoined in October 2024.

2026-10-17-ben-ecofin-preuve-de-vie-pens.summary: Benin launched Preuve de Vie on 15 October 2026, a mobile app through which public-sector pensioners of the FNRB confirm they are alive using their NPI, pension booklet number and fingerprint, from Benin or abroad. Biometric kiosks taking the national ID card are an alternative, and the campaign runs to 15 November 2026.

2026-10-17-caf-icasees-lancement-deuxiem.summary: ICASEES launched the second collection wave of the Central African Republic's second harmonised household living-conditions survey (EHCVM2) at a press briefing in Bangui on 17 October 2026. The wave extends the survey to the Fertit region (Haute-Kotto, Vakaga and Bamingui-Bangoran), which the July-to-September first wave had left out for security reasons, and steps up household sensitisation; the survey runs under the World Bank-backed HISWACA-SOP2 project.

2026-10-17-cmr-declaration-de-yaounde-e-.summary: The Yaoundé Declaration, adopted on 17 October 2026 at the close of the E-Gov'A conference, is a non-binding statement by governments, institutions and companies under a "Local First, African First" approach to e-government and AI. It sets an aim of hosting all critical or sovereign public data locally by 2030 and creates an Observatory of e-Government and AI in Africa.

2026-10-17-cog-aci-arpce-livre-blanc-ind.summary: Congo's communications regulator Arpce presented the second edition of its white paper and a digital postal addressing project on 15 October 2026, the state news agency reported. Figures cited include internet penetration of 57%, mobile money use of 55.8% and 22 internet service providers.

2026-10-17-cog-adiac-arpce-livre-blanc-a.summary: Congo's regulator ARPCE presented the second edition of its Livre Blanc and a digital postal-addressing project in Brazzaville on 15 October 2026. The minister asked that addressing be built as public infrastructure that works with digital ID, the data-exchange platform and payments, and the Livre Blanc's conclusions go to the interministerial task force on digitalising the administration.

2026-10-17-cog-adiac-data-protection-com.summary: Opening the National Assembly's budget session on 15 October 2026, its president Isidore Mvouba asked the Congolese government to make the National Commission for the Protection of Personal Data operational promptly. He linked digital sovereignty to control over health, civil-status, education, tax and social-protection data.

2026-10-17-cog-adiac-digitalisation-admi.summary: The steering committee of Congo's task force on digitalising the administration, created by decree 2026-261 of 29 January 2026, met for the first time on 15 October 2026 and chose four priorities. They are e-visas and entry authorisation before visa-free entry for Africans from January 2027, digital criminal records and birth certificates, a clean-up of the civil-service personnel file, and data sharing between revenue agencies and land administration.

2026-10-17-dza-cnrc-creation-entreprise-.summary: Algeria's commercial register (CNRC) sets out the steps to create each type of company online, from reserving a name to registration. For a single-member limited company, it notes that the owner is liable only up to the share capital.

2026-10-17-dza-cnrc-portail-creation-ent.summary: Algeria's commercial register runs a single online portal for creating a company. One registration there covers every administration involved and issues a common identification number.

2026-10-17-eth-ombudsman-portal-landing.summary: The Ethiopian Institution of the Ombudsman's website says it has resolved more than 48,500 complaints of maladministration through 14 regional offices. It also reports 1.5 million public enquiries and a 96.4% compliance rate by institutions; the figures carry no date.

2026-10-17-gha-rural-telephony-contracto.summary: Ghana's communications minister Sam George gave Rural Telephony Project contractors 30 days to finish outstanding sites or face penalties, saying they have been paid in full, after touring sites in the Volta Region. He also said Ghana recorded more than 4,000 fibre cuts by June 2026 and operators spent over $20 million on fibre repairs in 2025.

2026-10-17-lesinfosdeguinee-guinee-forum.summary: The second International Forum of Government General Secretariats, on AI for government performance, closed in Conakry on 16 October 2026 with delegates from 14 African and European countries. Its recommendations cover responsible AI use in administrations, staff training and data governance, expanding the secretariats' network, and better law-making, including digital official gazettes and interoperable platforms.

2026-10-17-mdg-2424-conseil-etat-logicie.summary: Madagascar's Conseil d'État has given all magistrates software that removes litigants' personal data from case files before any AI tool is used, presented at an AI workshop at the Cour suprême on 15-16 October 2026. Built without public money, it is the first step of a Conseil d'État and ENMG programme training magistrates to use consumer AI tools, under the personal data protection law.

2026-10-17-mdg-dgi-nifonline-immatricula.summary: Madagascar's tax directorate lets taxpayers apply for a tax identification number online through NIFONLINE. The page lists the documents individuals and companies must then present in person.

2026-10-17-mdg-midi-smartphone-47pct-tax.summary: At the launch of a GSMA report on Madagascar's digital economy, operators said taxes make up 47% of the cost of an entry-level smartphone, including a 6% copyright duty. Mobile services also carry an 8% excise duty.

2026-10-17-mdg-parlement-consultations-p.summary: Madagascar's National Assembly runs an online portal for public consultations on bills. Past consultations include the 2026 electoral code reform, an environment bill and national budget priorities for 2026.

2026-10-17-mdg-refonte-de-la-liste-elect.summary: Madagascar's electoral commission has provisionally registered 7,163,714 adults on its rebuilt electoral roll, 93% of them through door-to-door visits. Missing identity cards and birth certificates are slowing enrolment, and the roll is due to be final by the end of April 2027.

2026-10-17-mdg-technologie-deux-malgache.summary: Only about two in ten people in Madagascar use the internet, although 3G and 4G networks cover more than 80% of the population. Operators blame the cost of handsets, and the 2026 finance law keeps the taxes on them.

2026-10-17-mwi-malawi24-paychangu-psp-li.summary: The Reserve Bank of Malawi issued fintech PayChangu payment service provider licence PSP-003/26 on 30 September 2026 under the Payment Systems Act 2016. It allows the firm to aggregate mobile money, card and bank-transfer payments on one platform.

2026-10-17-ner-amv-geoportail-adressage-.summary: Niger's urban modernisation agency runs an online addressing geoportal for Niamey. It is meant to give the capital a modern street-address system that residents, visitors and public services can all use.

2026-10-17-ner-rsu-presentation.summary: Niger's unified social registry, run from the Prime Minister's office with World Bank support, holds verified data on households that may qualify for social protection. Each household and member gets a unique identifier, which is shared with programmes so they can link it to their own systems.

2026-10-17-nga-nairametrics-cbn-nigeria-.summary: Central Bank of Nigeria governor Olayemi Cardoso said he met People's Bank of China governor Pan Gongsheng at the IMF-World Bank annual meetings to discuss cross-border payments, settlement, fintech and trade finance. He said Nigeria will pursue these on a coming visit to Beijing; no plans or timetable were disclosed.

2026-10-17-nga-nigerian-government-integ.summary: Nigeria's Border Control and Immigration Management System now holds more than 15 million migration records after integrating the earlier MIDAS system, Interior Minister Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo and Immigration Comptroller-General Kemi Nandap said in Abuja. They also described a system linking data across interior agencies and a data centre of more than eight petabytes.

2026-10-17-nga-punchng-nucap-3700-rural-.summary: Nigeria's communications minister Bosun Tijani commissioned the first of 3,700 rural sites under the Nigeria Universal Communication Access Project in Bende, Abia State, on 16 October 2026. IHS Towers subsidiary GICL is deploying the towers with public Wi-Fi and Smart Village kits, starting at seven locations across Abia, Delta, Enugu, Plateau, Katsina and Ogun.

2026-10-17-sdn-ozyr-284-arab-monetary-fu.summary: The Arab Monetary Fund agreed to include Sudan in its technical assistance on digital transformation in 2027. It will also support Sudan on securities and sukuk and offer more training places.

2026-10-17-sdn-tpra-universal-service-fu.summary: Sudan's telecommunications and post regulator describes its universal service fund, which pays for telecom and postal services in remote and rural areas to narrow the digital divide. The fund's stated purposes include extending coverage, improving e-services outside cities, and supporting research and capacity building.

2026-10-17-som-national-institute-of-tel.summary: Somalia's National Institute of Telecommunications and Technology, part of the communications ministry, launched a programme to build government employees' digital skills, opening with a workshop on data protection, information security and privacy. The ministry says it wants the institute to take the lead in training civil servants and building public institutions' capacity.

2026-10-17-swz-positivenews-hhukwini-elm.summary: Eswatini's health minister visited Hhukwini Clinic to review the eLMIS and CMIS digital health systems, which the ministry runs in 250 health facilities. The systems are interoperable and use national identity numbers to identify patients, according to Eswatini Positive News.

2026-10-17-tun-servicesgov-finances-serv.summary: Tunisia's national administrative services portal lists the tax and payment services citizens can use online. Among them are paying fines online or by USSD, estimating vehicle registration tax, and calculating and paying Tunis municipal building tax.

2026-10-17-tza-simu-za-mkopo-zilivyo-mat.summary: Tanzania's data protection commission said it is investigating complaints about how lenders selling phones on credit collect and use borrowers' personal data. Its director general called the misuse unlawful.

2026-10-17-uga-more-than-3mn-tax-records.summary: Uganda Revenue Authority had linked 2.13 million of its 5.41 million individual taxpayer records to National Identification Numbers by 30 September 2026, leaving about 3.27 million unmatched, the finance ministry told Parliament. Taxpayers with linked records are due to log in with their NIN from 1 January 2027, and no end date has been set for TIN logins.

2026-10-17-zaf-mps-raise-alarm-after-hom.summary: South African MPs found self-service kiosks that Home Affairs bought under a 2024 project still undeployed, while licence fees keep running. The briefing was postponed after the director-general and chief financial officer did not attend, and no total cost was disclosed.

2026-10-17-zaf-sarb-nps-regulation-page.summary: The South African Reserve Bank explains how its National Payment System Department regulates the payment system for safety, efficiency and stability, including the prevention of fraud and money laundering. It says consumer protection in payments is the job of the Financial Sector Conduct Authority.

2026-10-17-zaf-sars-client-information-s.summary: South Africa's revenue service says its Client Information System, introduced in 2014, lets taxpayers register for and manage all their tax and customs registrations in a single profile. SARS is now merging each client's tax, customs and excise records into one consolidated profile.

2026-10-17-zaf-sars-guide-to-payment-rul.summary: South Africa's revenue service sets out the rules taxpayers must follow when paying it, by each payment channel, so that payments are allocated correctly. It warns that payments that do not follow the rules may be rejected.

2026-10-18-bfa-digitalmagazine-faso-digi.summary: Burkina Faso's virtual Faso Digital 2026 fair opened on 17 October 2026 with 201 solutions, selected from 208 entries in its innovation competition. Rwanda is guest of honour, according to Digital Magazine BF.

2026-10-18-civ-cybersecurite-en-cote-d-i.summary: A profile of Côte d'Ivoire's national information-systems security agency, created by decree in October 2024 to take over the work of the former IT directorate and the national CERT. It sets out the cyber laws the agency applies, the Budapest Convention ratified in July 2024 and the Malabo Convention ratified in April 2023.

2026-10-18-cod-au-beach-ngobila-de-kinsh.summary: WHO's Regional Director for Africa, Mohamed Janabi, visited passenger screening at Kinshasa's Beach Ngobila river crossing on 18 October 2026, where the WHO-backed Preparedness Data Exchange platform supports Ebola surveillance. He said a similar electronic system would go live in Brazzaville the following week.

2026-10-18-gab-gabon-amendes-jusqu-a-50-.summary: Gabon promulgated by decree on 5 October 2026 a law ratifying its ordinance on social-network use, Gabon Media Time reported. Hosts or editors who fail to fight illicit content face a year in prison and fines of FCFA 5 million to 50 million, deepfakes are banned, and judges may order platform suspensions of up to 72 hours.

2026-10-18-gha-ghana-appoints-ai-focal-p.summary: Ghana's communications minister Sam George said every ministry now has an AI focal person and Cabinet ministers have been through an AI boot camp. A UNESCO-supported readiness assessment has mapped ministries and agencies, UNDP and UNESCO are training chief directors and directors, and cybersecurity and data protection laws are under review.

2026-10-18-gha-people-of-internet-biomet.summary: In an unsigned analysis, the outlet People of Internet argues that Ghana's plan to add biometric checks to SIM registration addresses a real gap but needs data safeguards written into the rules. It calls for purging legacy data, match-only queries, warrants for police access and a fallback when biometric reads fail. It draws on the communications minister's 7 September 2026 statement.

2026-10-18-gmb-undp-launches-e-monitor-p.summary: UNDP and The Gambia's Independent Electoral Commission launched e-Monitor Plus at Kololi on 13-15 October 2026, a platform pairing AI with human checking to track online misinformation, disinformation and hate speech before the 5 December 2026 presidential election. Civil society speakers warned that monitoring must not turn into censorship.

2026-10-18-ken-kna-tanui-iten-17000km-pu.summary: On 18 October 2026 the ICT Principal Secretary said a 17,000 km fibre project linking all public institutions is underway, run with the Communications Authority, ICT Authority and Kenya Power. A KSh13 billion private build of 27,000 km runs alongside it. The Elgeyo Marakwet governor said the county will waive all charges for companies laying fibre.

2026-10-18-ken-mps-probe-ai-classrooms-h.summary: Kenya's National Assembly gave its communication committee one month to report on how AI is used in education, health and the public sector, and on the rules that govern it. MPs said there is no national AI framework and are weighing a standalone AI law.

2026-10-18-lby-opening-of-ozone-telecom-.summary: Ozone (O3) Telecom Group opened in Benghazi and announced that the Medusa submarine cable has reached the city. It plans a 16,000 km fibre network, a Tier III data centre and a 5G trial by the end of 2026.

2026-10-18-ner-audience-du-president-du-.summary: Customs chiefs of the Sahel states confederation (Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger) and Togo's revenue office met in Ouagadougou on 15 October 2026 to review progress on interconnecting their customs IT systems and validated a draft decision on certifying confederal origin. They reported to Captain Ibrahim Traoré the next day while finishing the text to create a customs union.

2026-10-18-nga-customs-afreximbank-plan-.summary: Nigeria Customs Service opened talks with Afreximbank on modernising the Sèmè–Kraké and Mfum–Ekok border corridors with Benin and Cameroon. The plans include a system for exchanging customs declarations between the three countries on a common data model; no cost or loan has been agreed.

2026-10-18-nga-jamb-moves-to-rescue-grad.summary: Nigeria's admissions board launched a service that lets candidates correct their records to match their national identity data. It is meant to help graduates who have been barred from national service for years by mismatched records.

2026-10-18-nga-ncc-launches-internet-gov.summary: The Nigerian Communications Commission launched an Internet Governance Working Group at its first Internet Governance Symposium, held in Lagos on 15 October 2026. The commission called for wider cooperation on artificial intelligence, online fraud, privacy and child protection, and cited its Internet Code of Practice 2026 and a cyber resilience framework for the sector.

2026-10-18-sdn-sudandawn-commercial-regi.summary: Sudan's commercial registry has been almost entirely stalled for more than a week by a technical fault on the Baladna platform, which handles company and business-name filings, Sudan Dawn reported on 18 October 2026. Lawyers report a backlog of files and are calling for urgent intervention and a permanent fix.

2026-10-18-sen-diante-service-public-mod.summary: Senegal's civil-service minister said the physical and biometric audit of state employees, launched in June 2026, is still under way and has not yet confirmed any anomalies. He named e-Sénégal as the single access point for online procedures under the 2025–2029 public-service reform agenda.

2026-10-18-sle-sierra-leone-establishes-.summary: Sierra Leone has set up a national committee for UNESCO's Information for All Programme to align national policy with it, the Foreign Ministry announced. A UNESCO-government conference on information integrity held in Freetown on 28 September 2026 drew delegates from 41 countries.

2026-10-18-zaf-vodacoms-technology-chief.summary: Vodacom's group technology chief said the company will install its own GPUs first in its new Egypt data centre, then build a GPU-as-a-service node in Kenya, with South Africa last. The Egypt facility, built with Elsewedy Electric and Cassava, is expected to draw about $200m in its first phase.

2026-10-19-bfa-le-faso-digital-2026-l-ar.summary: Burkina Faso's regulator ARCEP reported about 3,514 white zones with no operator, nearly 40% of localities and some 4.7 million people, at the Le Faso Digital conference on 19 October 2026. Its figures at 30 June 2026 show about 30 million mobile subscriptions, nearly 20 million mobile-internet and 328,764 fixed-internet subscriptions.

2026-10-19-caf-developmentaid-pgnsp-mobi.summary: The Central African Republic opened an invitation for bids on 19 October 2026 for goods: kits to set up mobile money agents. The tender falls under the World Bank-financed Public Sector Digital Governance Project. No budget is stated and no award has been made.

2026-10-19-cmr-digitalbusiness-herve-tiw.summary: In an interview with Digital Business Africa, digital transformation and AI expert Hervé Tiwa argues that Cameroon has a legal gap on AI and should fill it. He favours a broader digital law that absorbs the cybercrime law rather than a separate law for each new technology, with clear prohibitions against misuse such as disinformation and deepfakes.

2026-10-19-cmr-itweb-camtel-socadel-infr.summary: Cameroon's Camtel and electricity utility Socadel signed a memorandum of understanding in Yaoundé on 16 October 2026 to study infrastructure sharing. It would pair Camtel's national fibre backbone with Socadel's poles and rights-of-way to extend fibre along overhead power lines. Feasibility studies and pilot sites come next.

2026-10-19-cod-who-deploys-pdx-preparedn.summary: WHO's Africa office has deployed its AI-based Preparedness Data Exchange in the DR Congo, the first country to get it, linking national epidemic intelligence to a regional platform for the 47 states of the WHO African Region during the Ebola response. Dure Technologies and WHO also installed the Voyage Santé digital entry-screening system at N'djili airport and the Nord Bangui border post.

2026-10-19-dza-mesrs-baddari-gpu-calcul-.summary: Algeria's higher-education ministry agreed on 19 October 2026 with public and private companies to set up a joint framework for drafting a 2030 roadmap to finance GPU-based high-performance computing and AI research capacity. Its four aims are company co-funding of GPUs, research steered to economic needs, a stronger national AI and data centre, and recruiting diaspora talent.

2026-10-19-gab-gabon-lidentification-for.summary: Gabon's law 003/2026 of 5 October 2026, published on 9 October, requires individuals and legal entities using social networks and online platforms to formally identify themselves. Gabon Media Time reports that article 4 does not say what documents are needed, how identity will be checked or how existing accounts are treated. It also does not make the personal identification number mandatory for this purpose.

2026-10-19-gab-gabon-securite-alimentair.summary: Gabon's food safety agency AGASA will launch Nexus, a digital platform for food and plant-health operators, on 2 November 2026. Operators will be able to apply remotely for approvals, import authorisations and health certificates, and track their files. Operators are asked to visit AGASA offices from 20 to 29 October with identity documents to update their data and get login details.

2026-10-19-gab-mediation-financiere-le-g.summary: Gabon's Comité national économique et financier (CNEF) was to launch financial mediation in Libreville on 26 October 2026, giving customers of banks, microfinance institutions and payment providers a free, confidential route to settle disputes, with agreements enforceable. The mechanism rests on a 2020 CEMAC consumer-protection regulation, a 2024 decree and two orders of January 2025; a complaint to the institution must come first, and Axcèle Saturnin Kissangou-Mouele was named mediator in June for a three-year term.

2026-10-19-gha-imani-africa-missing-plum.summary: John Sitsofe Mensah, an IMANI associate, argues that Ghana needs a whole-of-government data exchange to connect state databases, now that identity and payment systems are in place. He warns against agencies hosting core records on offshore cloud servers instead of the national government cloud run by NITA, citing legal, sovereignty and vendor lock-in risks. He also says a single exchange would stop citizens being asked for information the state already holds.

2026-10-19-lbr-biometricupdate-mps-scrut.summary: Liberia's House of Representatives referred a proposed $52 million build-operate-transfer concession for a national ID and civil registration system to a joint committee on 16 October 2026, giving it two weeks to report. The system would hold records for up to 10 million people, and civil society groups are asking for scrutiny of the financial terms and data protection. The National Identification Registry says fewer than 800,000 people hold a national ID.

2026-10-19-lby-techafricanews-o3-group-f.summary: Libya's O3 Group, a private telecoms company founded in 2024 and based in Benghazi, set out its infrastructure plans as the Medusa submarine cable made its first Libyan landing at Benghazi on 17 October 2026. The plans include a 12,000 to 13,000 km national fibre network, a Tier III data centre in Benghazi and a mobile service. A second Medusa landing is planned for Tripoli.

2026-10-19-le-gimac-et-papss-card-posent.summary: GIMAC, the Central African interbank card network, and PAPSS Card agreed the practical terms of a partnership at working sessions in Yaoundé on 13 and 14 October 2026, with a convention to be signed in the following days. The plan would let GIMAC cards issued by CEMAC banks be accepted across the PAPSS network and PAPSS cards be used in the CEMAC zone, and the sessions produced a roadmap of priority actions, owners and deadlines. GIMAC's interim director general Guy Noël Londongo tied the move to the BEAC joining the AU-backed PAPSS system.

2026-10-19-mastercard-moovn-five-year-ea.summary: Mastercard and Moovn Technologies signed a five-year agreement, announced on 19 October 2026, to add Mastercard prepaid cards, tokenisation, online acceptance, Pay Local and cross-border transfers to the MoovnPay wallet. Pay Local is to expand across Kenya and Tanzania, and the Shooga prepaid Mastercard portfolio is to launch next.

2026-10-19-moz-altas-taxas-cobradas-no-n.summary: Fees at Mozambique's new Centro Pronto document centre have drawn public anger, as the private centre adds its own fee and 16% VAT to the state fee. An adult identity-card renewal costs MZN 1,058.12 in total, of which the state fee is MZN 160. A driving-licence renewal costs MZN 5,201.84 and an express passport renewal MZN 10,725.10.

2026-10-19-moz-intic-eleito-comite-de-ge.summary: Mozambique's ICT institute INTIC was elected to the management committee of ANCA-CERT, Africa's network of cyber incident-response teams, for Southern Africa at the African Network of Cybersecurity Authorities meeting in Rabat on 12 October 2026. ANCA admitted five new members, taking it from 28 to 33 states, and Mozambique reported its cybersecurity and cybercrime laws in force since 29 September.

2026-10-19-mus-sil-tcs-mou-digital-trans.summary: Mauritius' State Informatics Ltd signed a memorandum of understanding with India's Tata Consultancy Services on digital transformation, technology cooperation and innovation. IT Minister Avinash Ramtohul said it would support knowledge transfer and local digital skills, and he pointed to the planned AI City and the automation of public-sector workflows.

2026-10-19-nga-techcabal-cheaper-fibre-f.summary: A TechCabal analysis of Nigerian Communications Commission portal data from July 2026 finds that state right-of-way fees do not neatly predict where fibre has been built. Ogun charges up to ₦6,600 per metre yet has 4,246 km of fibre, while Jigawa and Zamfara, which waive the fee, have 970 km and 1,101 km. The piece notes that construction costs and other factors are not captured in the portal data.

2026-10-19-nga-techcabal-onafriq-baxi-sa.summary: Onafriq had been negotiating the sale of Baxi, its Nigerian agent-banking business, before it announced a shutdown on 16 October 2026, according to UK-filed accounts approved on 29 July 2026. The accounts record a non-binding memorandum of terms for a full divestment, agency services revenue down 56% to $13.4 million in 2024, and ₦19.9 billion in overdrafts owed to Zenith Bank and Stanbic IBTC.

2026-10-19-sdn-suna-pm-forms-national-cy.summary: Sudan's prime minister issued a decision on 19 October 2026 forming a National Mechanism to Combat Informatics Crimes, chaired by an assistant attorney general. It is tasked with combating cybercrime and publications deemed harmful to the state and society, monitoring media and social platforms, and taking preventive and legal action, including lawsuits on the state's behalf.

2026-10-19-sle-statssl-mock-census-joint.summary: Sierra Leone's planning minister, the Statistician-General and UNFPA's country representative monitored the 2026 mock census enumeration at Hill Station, Freetown, on 19 October 2026. The mock census is testing census methods, the digital data-collection system and quality assurance ahead of the national census scheduled for December 2026, Statistics Sierra Leone said.

2026-10-19-som-biometricupdate-halmeel-u.summary: Somalia's Unified Public Service Delivery Center, known as Halmeel, plans to launch a unified digital government services platform by the end of March 2027, starting with about 70 services. The national ID will be the only accepted credential, its director general told Biometric Update. Halmeel, created by Cabinet resolution on 23 April, is integrating with the national ID agency NIRA, which had about 2 million people registered as of October 2026.

2026-10-19-som-developmentaid-eardip-api.summary: Somalia invited expressions of interest on 19 October 2026 for the design, deployment and operation of a government API gateway, a government single sign-on system and a national digital government portal. The work falls under the World Bank-financed Eastern Africa Regional Digital Integration Project.

2026-10-19-swz-govt-plans-ai-services-at.summary: Eswatini's ICT ministry presented a proposed platform for reaching government services and payments by mobile device at the Global AI & Digital Summit in Seoul on 19 October 2026. No implementation date was announced. The ministry also cited digital-skills targets of 300,000 citizens through a UAE partnership and 200,000 through a World Bank-supported initiative.

2026-10-19-swz-senators-back-e5m-fines-1.summary: Eswatini's Senate adopted the ICT portfolio committee's report on the Critical Infrastructure Bill No. 16 of 2025 on 19 October 2026. It backs fines of up to E5 million for companies, and E1 million or up to 10 years' imprisonment for individuals, for offences against telecom towers, fibre and energy lines.

2026-10-19-syc-seychelles-targets-2027-s.summary: Seychelles plans to begin implementing a digital human resource management system in 2027, Vice-President Sebastien Pillay announced after meeting Canadian vendor FreeBalance at State House on 14 October 2026. The system would cover employee records, payroll, performance management and workforce analytics. Pillay said technology alone would not improve efficiency unless administrative procedures are also reviewed.

2026-10-19-tcd-digitalisation-de-leftp-l.summary: Chad's higher-education ministry opened a workshop in N'Djamena on 14 October 2026 to validate a national strategy for digitising technical and vocational training, backed by the Francophonie's education institute IFEF. The strategy has three axes: data-driven governance, digital infrastructure in training centres, and digital skills and teaching quality.

2026-10-19-tgo-togo-signs-huawei-agreeme.summary: Togo and Huawei signed a memorandum of understanding in Shenzhen on 16 October 2026 covering energy, smart transport and smart customs systems. It includes technology transfer and local skills development, and was signed during Council President Faure Gnassingbé's visit to China from 9 to 16 October. No value was given.

2026-10-19-tun-tunisie-moins-de-paperass.summary: Tunisia's government told parliament its 2025-2027 programme to simplify some 2,250 administrative procedures is about 70% done, with around 80% of them to be digitised fully or in part. It opened 34 digital service houses in 21 governorates in 2026 and plans 68 more from 2027 to 2030.

2026-10-19-uga-43-000-elderly-ugandans-l.summary: Uganda's gender ministry said, as reported on 19 October 2026, that about 43,000 eligible older people cannot draw SAGE cash grants because the birth dates on their national ID cards make them appear too young. SAGE reaches about 318,000 of more than 2.4 million potential beneficiaries, and mobile-money payment is being piloted.

2026-10-19-xaf-au-innofest-26-youth-hack.summary: The African Union Commission convened the first African Community of Practice on Technology-Facilitated Violence Against Women and Girls and launched the SafeTech Africa HackLab for innovators aged 18 to 35. Both took place at AU InnoFest'26 in Addis Ababa on 29 and 30 September 2026, with UNDP, UNFPA, UN Women and the Spotlight Initiative.

2026-10-19-xaf-biometricupdate-sadx-ben-.summary: Benin, Ghana and Rwanda have connected their national identity systems through the Smart Africa Data Exchange and are moving toward real-world testing of cross-border ID verification, Biometric Update reported on 19 October 2026. Pilots are planned for Benin-Rwanda air travel and Ghana-Benin land crossings. No date for live testing has been announced.

2026-10-19-xea-mapping-digital-connectiv.summary: The African Development Bank built a digital intelligence platform using Ookla speed-test data to rank district-level connectivity gaps across 11 East African countries, reported on 19 October 2026. It combines 51 months of tests, January 2022 to March 2026, with data on 93,125 health and education facilities in 8,925 administrative areas.

2026-10-19-xgl-govinsider-jargon-problem.summary: Speakers at an Open Government Partnership webinar on 15 October 2026 said the label 'digital public infrastructure' keeps the public out of designing digital ID, payment and data systems, and urged governments to make clear where people can take part. Nigeria's open-government plan carries a DPI commitment led by NITDA, including a pilot of accessibility standards in 10 federal agencies.

2026-10-19-xwa-the-communications-direct.summary: The ECOWAS Commission's Communications Directorate held the second meeting of its Disinformation Working Group in Accra, Ghana, on 15 and 16 October 2026. The meeting brought together ECOWAS institutions and partners to plan a coordinated regional response to information integrity challenges.

2026-10-19-zaf-bma-vehicle-targeting-sys.summary: South Africa's Border Management Authority launched its Vehicle Targeting System at Lebombo Port of Entry on 18 October 2026. It reports 83 vehicles worth R46.6 million recovered in the six months since the system went live at land ports on 1 April 2026, with rollout to eight land ports planned by the end of February 2027.

2026-10-19-zaf-citizen-gauteng-egov-weig.summary: Gauteng's e-Government department said on 19 October 2026 it will decide whether to pursue criminal charges against student Joel Cedras, who exposed a flaw in the e-Panic Button app, once an investigation report due the following week is in. The DA's Michael Waters said the department had sought his prosecution, and that police advised the app's developers would have to open the case.

2026-10-19-zaf-electoral-commission-and-.summary: South Africa's Electoral Commission announced on 19 October 2026 a partnership with Google, Meta, Microsoft, TikTok and Moxii Africa to counter disinformation ahead of the 4 November 2026 local government elections. It follows a similar framework signed with the platforms before the 2024 national and provincial elections.

2026-10-20-ben-presidence-de-la-republiq.summary: Benin created a National Digital Committee under the President of the Republic by decree n° 2026-579 of 2 September 2026, reported on 20 October 2026. The head of state chairs it and it meets quarterly. It tracks digital projects through a quarterly dashboard from a permanent secretariat, and gives prior opinions on structuring digital projects and on technology partnerships that could affect national digital sovereignty.

2026-10-20-bfa-autorite-de-regulation-de.summary: Burkina Faso appointed W. Louis Modeste Ouédraogo, previously president of the Conseil supérieur de la communication, to head the new regulator formed by merging that council with the data-protection commission CIL. The decree is dated 16 October 2026.

2026-10-20-bfa-bulletin-agrometeorologiq.summary: Météo Burkina Faso publishes a ten-day agrometeorological bulletin covering rainfall, temperature and humidity anomalies and vegetation index data. The page seen on 20 October 2026 lists a latest update for 13 to 19 October 2026, describing monsoon winds with some harmattan incursions. Earlier updates cover periods back to early September 2026.

2026-10-20-bfa-les-regulateurs-du-numeri.summary: The second session of the UEMOA national digital regulators' committee (CRNN) opened in Ouagadougou on 20 October 2026 and runs until 22 October. The agenda covers regulation of digital financial services, sharing of telecoms infrastructure and community roaming. Burkina Faso currently chairs the committee, and the first session was held in Cotonou from 28 to 31 October 2025.

2026-10-20-cmr-donnees-modelisation-geom.summary: Cameroon's national climate observatory ONACC lists a library of 11 data, modelling and geomatics products on its website, seen on 20 October 2026. They include a national climate and geospatial database on PostgreSQL/PostGIS, risk maps, Sentinel satellite imagery, drought indices and web services. The page says connection to the database tables will be added later.

2026-10-20-cmr-modernisation-de-la-fonct.summary: Cameroon's public-service ministry MINFOPRA met on 20 October 2026 to validate the national public-services portal servicepublic.gov.cm and plan its rollout, and presented My MINFOPRA, an internal platform for staff to share documents and circulars. The portal is meant to be the single official source of information on administrative procedures, with a mobile app to follow.

2026-10-20-cmr-servicepublic-gov-cm-minf.summary: Cameroon's public-service minister Joseph Le reviewed the servicepublic.gov.cm portal on 20 October 2026 before its launch: it lists 1,250 procedures in 25 categories in French and English, with an app for offline use and a proposed 90-day publicity campaign across the ten regions. He asked for a new name and look for the portal and a review of the contract with its provider, ADWA SARL.

2026-10-20-dza-algerie54-solidarite-plat.summary: Algeria's Ministry of National Solidarity launched a digital platform on 20 October 2026 that tracks the progress and spending of the sector's investment projects nationwide through a dashboard for the central administration. For 2027 it plans an AI-built national map of persons with special needs and an AI system to detect fraud in solidarity schemes.
